author: bllshttng
body:
Phase 1 of the fno-mux pivot: rebuild `fno` as a native Rust terminal multiplexer, starting with the risky spine proven end to end on ONE pane - a persistent server that owns a PTY and emulates its screen, plus a thin client that attaches, composites, and forwards input. The server outlives the client, so quitting and relaunching `fno` reattaches to the same live shell. No pane tree yet; splitting/tabs/agents are Phase 2+, additive on this spine.

## What's in the crate

The existing `crates/fno-bootstrap` package is renamed to `crates/fno` (the bootstrapper lives on as `src/bootstrap.rs` behind the same front door). Standalone on ecosystem libs - portable-pty for the PTY, alacritty_terminal 0.26 for VT emulation, crossterm for terminal setup/input; no dependency on `fno-agents` (its shipped `pty.rs`/`screen.rs` were copy-seeded and adapted for alt-screen + bounded scrollback).

- `proto.rs` - length-prefixed wire protocol + Unix socket lifecycle (stale-socket detection, frame validation caps)
- `server.rs` - the spine: PTY child running $SHELL (`/bin/sh` fallback), VT emulation into a cell grid, event loop, per-client writer threads
- `vt.rs` - alacritty Term wrapper: cell grid, alt-screen, bounded scrollback, damage-to-frame rendering
- `pty.rs` - portable-pty wrapper adapted from fno-agents
- `client.rs` - client TUI: attach, composite frames, raw-byte input forwarding, TTY gate, cancel-safe reads
- `main.rs` - role selection: bare `fno` on a TTY = client (auto-spawning the server), `fno --server` = daemon

## Testing

54 tests across 7 suites (`cargo test` in `crates/fno`): wire protocol round-trips, socket lifecycle, server spine, client e2e, and persistence/races - detach/reattach to a live shell, client `kill -9`, server respawn, concurrent clients. CI (`rust-ci.yml`) extended to run fmt/test/audit for the new crate; crates-publish workflow updated for the rename. Sigma-review findings addressed (cancel-safe client reads, frame validation caps).

Note: the authoring session hit its usage limit at the validate step; `cargo test` (54/54) was re-verified before this PR was opened. Also carries the mechanical bundled-events-schema resync (identical content also on PR #134; merges cleanly either order).

author: jordanolivet
body:
## Problem

Docker builds export BuildKit cache with `mode=max`, which grows past the 10 GB repo cache limit. The v1.26.0 release pipeline (run 28549598112) failed at the cache export step with `failed to reserve cache`, skipping `create-gh-release`.

## Changes

Add a scheduled workflow (daily 03:00 UTC + manual `workflow_dispatch`) calling the new `cache-cleanup` reusable from ci-workflows ([JordanOlivet/ci-workflows#6](https://github.com/JordanOlivet/ci-workflows/pull/6)). It prunes the oldest caches when repo cache usage exceeds 9 GB, and is a no-op otherwise.

Combined with `ignore-error=true` now set on the docker build cache export (same ci-workflows PR), cache issues can no longer break releases.

author: vjk88
body:
Rolls the [One at a Time image-fit fix](https://github.com/vjk88/forms/pull/6) out to the other 6 shells — they all had the **identical** latent bug.

## Root cause (same everywhere)
Every shell shared one multi-layer `background-image` (texture, mesh, scrim, page-image) with a 4-slot `background-size`/`background-repeat`. `--c-mesh-bg` = 4 gradient layers and grid `--c-texture` = 2, so the real layer count shifts and CSS cycles the 4-slot list — landing the image's fit (`--c-bg-size`) on the wrong layer.

## Fix
Page image → its own single-layer background on the element (fit/repeat always align). Texture/mesh/scrim → `::before` (`z-index:-1`, above image, below content); element made a stacking context via `isolation:isolate`.

| Shell | bg element |
|---|---|
| Stack / Tabbed / Accordion | `.chrome-fullbleed` |
| Wizard | `:host` |
| SideNav / SplitHero | `.layout` |

## Verification
- deployed 6 components, 0 errors ✅
- ⚠️ render-pending: image fit (cover/contain/tile) with mesh/texture on each layout; also confirm **sticky submit bars** (Stack/Tabbed/Accordion) and **SplitHero's sticky brand panel** still pin correctly (new stacking contexts).

author: rarestg
body:
## Summary

pdf-ocr's `Stepper` (`primitives.tsx`) and prompt-library's `PromptNumberInputControl` (`index.tsx`) were the same control built twice: −/+ buttons flanking a draft-then-commit number input with `-ml-px` border overlap and native spinners hidden. This promotes the pdf-ocr implementation (the richer of the two) to `src/components/Stepper.tsx` and adopts it in both artifacts, deleting both locals (−238 lines across the three consumer files).

Per the earlier PR-series decision, this is a promotion of the existing hand-rolled control, **not** a Base UI Number Field rewrite — the draft-commit semantics and Max button are real behavior Number Field doesn't subsume.

## API

`size: 'default' | 'compact'` (naming matches `SegmentedControl`) and `labelPosition: 'top' | 'start'` carry the two consumers' real metrics/layouts; `maxButton` / `helperText` / `disabled` come straight from the pdf-ocr base. `useArtifactThemeGuard`, literal Tailwind classes, `inputBase.helper` reused for helper text.

## Conscious behavior reconciliations

- **Empty-draft commit unified to revert-to-current**: prompt-library previously reset an empty draft to `defaultValue`; revert-to-current is the saner draft-commit semantic and not worth a prop for one edge (its only `numberInput` has `step: 1`, so the step-snapping in `normalizePromptNumberInputValue` was otherwise equivalent to `clamp(round)`; that function stays in `prompts.ts` for `renderPromptText`).
- **Fixed a live-commit bug found in review**: `Number('') === 0`, so clearing pdf-ocr's `min=0` Retries field instantly committed 0 mid-edit and snapped the draft back. Empty drafts are now guarded; only blur/Enter resolve them.
- Dropped the redundant input `aria-label` (the visible `htmlFor` label names the control in both artifacts).

## Testing

- `npm run check` (biome + tsc ×2 + knip + 258 tests) ✅, `npm run knip:ci` ✅, `npm run build` ✅
- New `tests/components/stepperBehavior.test.ts` (happy-dom): live-commit in range, no commit out of range, Enter clamps to max, empty draft never commits at `min=0`, empty+Enter reverts to current.
- Playwright against the dev server: pdf-ocr settings steppers (label above, helper below, Max in row) — `+`→33, Max→128, `999`+Enter→128, Retries clear+Enter→3; prompt-library Options stepper inline in the section header, 5→`+`→6.
- Codex plan + change review: no findings, no must-fix.

author: arouna-sidibe
body:
## Objectif

Activer le second corpus de questions déjà présent dans `questions/en/`
et permettre à l'utilisateur de choisir sa langue.

## Approche

- `convert.js` produit désormais un `data.js` unique contenant les
  deux langues sous `allExamsData = { fr: [...], en: [...] }`.
- Nouveau module `i18n.js` avec un dictionnaire complet couvrant navbar,
  hero, cartes, boutons, instructions, modales, résultats et footer.
- Attributs `data-i18n="cle"` sur les textes statiques du HTML, helper
  `t('cle')` pour les textes rendus dynamiquement.
- Toggle langue dans la navbar (icône globe + code de la langue cible).
  Un clic met à jour `localStorage` et recharge la page.
- Détection initiale via `navigator.language`, override persisté.

## Continuité en cours de test

Les IDs de questions sont identiques entre les langues (question `1_5`
en FR est la même question conceptuelle qu'en EN). Conséquence :
**changer de langue en plein test ou challenge préserve les réponses
saisies**, seul le texte de la question et des options change.

## Corpus

- FR : 25 examens, 1257 questions
- EN : 23 examens, 1142 questions

Les 1142 identifiants EN sont tous présents côté FR (EN couvre les
examens 1 à 23). L'écart d'examens se gère naturellement : la liste des
examens s'adapte à la langue choisie, et un examen absent dans la langue
cible retombe proprement sur la page des examens.

## Correctif inclus

Le connecteur des réponses multiples du parseur restait auparavant trop
gourmand et pouvait franchir un saut de ligne pour capturer l'initiale du
mot suivant (le E de `Explanation:`), transformant `Correct answer: A`
en `A, E`. Le connecteur est désormais borné à la même ligne. La
vérification passe à 0 erreur sur les deux langues.

author: dylanmccavitt
body:
Fixes the `renderEnvelopeYaml`/`parseYaml` round-trip loss for string values containing double quotes, backslashes, or newlines (FN-54, carried from PR #111).

## Root cause

Asymmetric encode/decode: the writer (`yamlString` in `envelope.mjs`) is `JSON.stringify`, so `"`, `\`, and newlines are emitted as JSON escapes — but `parseScalar` in `schema.mjs` only did `raw.slice(1, -1)` on quoted scalars, so the escapes survived import as literal text (`say "hi"` came back as `say \"hi\"`).

## Fix

`parseScalar` now decodes symmetrically:
- double-quoted scalar → `JSON.parse` (exact inverse of the writer); malformed content throws `invalid double-quoted scalar`, which `validateEnvelopeYaml` surfaces as a validation failure instead of silent corruption
- single-quoted scalar → YAML semantics: `''` → `'`

No new YAML dependency; the minimal parser stays minimal.

## Acceptance criteria → evidence

- Failing coverage for `"`, `\`, and literal newlines → new round-trip test seeds hostile strings in `tracker.team`, `proof.commands[]`, `circuits[0].reason`; `deepEqual` against the input through `exportEnvelope` → `importEnvelope`
- Values round-trip without data loss → same test + `parseYaml` unit tests for `\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\t` and `'it''s'`
- Redaction preserved → secret-looking quoted command still redacts, exported YAML validates, import equals `redactEnvelope(withSecret)`
- Schema validation failures preserved → malformed double-quoted scalar throws; existing negative tests untouched and green
- `npm run check` passes → 494 pass / 0 fail, safety gate `Result: passed`

## Non-goals honored

No tracker adapter changes, no live installer changes, no YAML dependency. The `.loom.yml` pointer parser in `scan.mjs` has its own deliberately strict quoting rules and is untouched.

author: johnnyhuirilef
body:
# 📥 Pull Request

## 📌 Context & Purpose

Closes #62

The v5/v6/v7 driver compat claim (docs, peer range `>=5.0.0`, the `compat/driver.ts` shim) had never been exercised against a real v7 install — and, it turns out, never against a real v5 install at the unit level either.

## 📦 Affected Packages

- [x] `zod-mongo`
- [x] Infrastructure (CI, Build, Tooling)

## 🚦 SemVer Type

- [x] 🧾 **Skip Release** (Docs, Chore, Refactor, Test)

## 🛠️ Implementation Details

**Verification before CI (local, Docker):**
- **v7.4.0**: 236/236 pass. `MONGO_MAJOR` resolves to 7, takes the v6+ passthrough branch. The claim holds.
- **v5.9.2**: integration (real MongoDB) passed 47/47 — the shim's `ModifyResult` unwrapping was always correct. But 6 unit tests failed: the mocks resolved plain documents while real v5 defaults `includeResultMetadata: true` and resolves `{ value: doc }`. A stale spec comment had encoded the wrong assumption (verified against the v5 driver source). Exactly the unverified-claim risk this issue was about — found on v5, not v7.

**Changes:**
1. `tests/unit/driver-shape.ts` — shared `findAndModifyResult()` helper shaping mocks per the installed driver's major, using the same load-time detection as the production shim (no `MONGO_MAJOR` mocking, per package constraints). Both affected specs import it; the stale comment is corrected. With the lockfile's v6, default behavior is unchanged.
2. `ci.yml` — new `mongodb-driver-matrix` job: matrix `[5, 6, 7]`, `fail-fast: false`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first, then the pinned major installed scoped to `@wenu/mongo` only (runner-local, lockfile never touched), tests run with `--skip-nx-cache` so no leg reuses cached results from another driver version. `nest-zod-mongo` excluded — it doesn't branch on driver version.

No src changes. No new dependencies. No lockfile changes.

> Note for branch protection: if required checks are pinned by job name, `mongodb-driver-matrix` needs to be added manually — workflow YAML can't do that.

## 💥 Breaking Changes

author: rgbkrk
body:
Inline JSX inside a paragraph (`Text with here`) was silently dropped in the islands lane. The parser never enabled `mdx_jsx_text`, so `` fell through to `MdxJsxTextElement` with a generic `NodeKind::Mdx` mapping that clears its children, and the JSON serializer had no run type for it. Block JSX (#3859) and the carried-forward reconciler (#3862) worked; inline JSX just vanished. ## What changed `parse_options` now enables `mdx_jsx_text` and disables `html_text` under the `islands` option, the inline analogue of the existing `mdx_jsx_flow`/`html_flow` routing: the HTML construct wins on `<` before MDX-JSX gets a look, so it has to be off in this lane. Islands-off keeps both HTML constructs on. `project_node` gets an islands-guarded `MdxJsxTextElement` arm that mirrors the block island arm: `NodeKind::Island`, tag/isolation set from the element name, `island_inline = true`, `IsolationKind::Component`, `SafetyLane::Isolated`, children cleared. `render_json.rs` adds a `NodeKind::Island` arm to `collect_inline` that emits an inline island run via `add_island_run`. The run is zero-width on the rendered-text axis (empty rendered text, cursor doesn't advance), so the surrounding prose runs keep tiling around it. It carries `islandTag`, `islandInline: true`, and `contentHash`, the reconciler's recursive content hash, so a downstream document store can tell a prop edit (hash moves) from an insert-above offset shift (hash holds). `JsonRun` grows the three fields behind an `if let Some(island_tag)` guard, so a non-island run emits zero new keys. `StructuralKey` gains `island_inline` alongside the existing `island_tag`. A block `` and an inline `` share a kind and tag; without this field a block-to-inline swap would alias the carried-forward id instead of remounting. They're never siblings today, but keeping it in the key means a future flow/text unification stays correct instead of becoming a silent bug. The field carries `#[serde(default)]` so snapshot bytes serialized before it existed still deserialize: `from_bytes` is total (any error means cold start), so a missing-field error would silently drop every carried-forward id. A compatibility test strips the field from fresh bytes and proves ids still carry forward. ## Byte-identity invariant Every new path is guarded on the `islands` option or on `NodeKind::Island`. With `islands` false, the default for notebooks, plain `.md`, and the wasm FFI, projection output is byte-identical to before. An adversarial review with a parser probe against `markdown` 1.0.0 confirmed this on the islands-off path. ## Two tradeoffs worth flagging Turning on `mdx_jsx_text` makes the islands lane strict MDX for inline `<`. A stray `I <3 you` is now a parse error and the whole document fails to project, where it previously came through as literal text. This is intentional: mdxjs-rs is built on the same markdown-rs parser, so anything that compiles as MDX also projects, and anything that now fails to project already failed to compile. The lane was over-lenient before; this makes it consistent with the compile step instead. Intrinsic tags project as islands too: `x` or `
` inline becomes an island exactly like the block arm has done since #3859. There's no component-vs-intrinsic split. That's consistent with existing block behavior, but the capitalized-component vs lowercase-intrinsic distinction is a real follow-up, and it should land in both arms together, not just this one. ## Behavior | islands | inline `` | inline `x` | malformed `<` (`I <3 you`) | |---|---|---|---| | off | HTML-text handling (unchanged) | HTML-text handling (unchanged) | literal text (unchanged) | | on | inline island run | inline island run | parse error | Five new engine tests cover inline island projection on/off, inline island run serialization, contentHash moving on a prop edit but holding across an insert-above shift, and pre-field snapshot bytes still carrying ids forward. 48 engine tests pass, clippy and fmt are clean, the wasm crate test is green, and the runtimed projected-plan test stays on plan version 1.

## The bug
Loading `/` logged a Base UI **console a11y error**:

> A component that acts as a button expected a native `<button>` because the `nativeButton` prop is true… Rendering a non-`<button>` removes native button semantics…

It came from the showcase's `<Button render={<Link/>}>` navigations (source link, demo CTA, "← Back to overview").

## The fix
Base UI's suggested `nativeButton={false}` "fixes" the warning but stamps `role="button"` onto a link — the wrong semantic for something that **navigates**. So instead these three navigations now render as **real `<a>` anchors styled with `buttonVariants`**: proper link semantics, identical button look, no warning.

- `components/CaseStudy.tsx` — "View the source on GitHub"
- `components/SiteFooter.tsx` — "Try the live demo"
- `app/demo/page.tsx` — "← Back to overview"

The shared `Button` component is unchanged (I tried a centralized tweak first and reverted it — it flipped roles repo-wide and degraded link semantics).

**Verified live** against the dev server: fresh renders of `/` and `/demo` produce zero nativeButton warnings, and the source link serves as `<a href=…>` with no `role="button"`.

body: ## Summary Reverts #3661 (`c8597b136`) — the unified hook ingest endpoint. ## Why The shipped plugin hook scripts fail closed and are blocking users' Claude Code sessions in the wild: - `auth_preflight.sh` runs as a blocking `SessionStart` hook and `send_hook.sh` as a blocking `UserPromptSubmit` hook. With no `GRAM_HOOKS_API_KEY` env and no cached key, `gram_hooks_prepare_auth` exits non-zero, which rejects the user's prompt on every submission. - The interactive browser login was removed in #3661 (`gram_hooks_login` is now a stub that always returns 1), so blocked users have no self-serve recovery path. - The new `POST /rpc/hooks.ingest` endpoint has a 100% failure rate in prod since the merge: 34 requests, 13x401 + 21x403, zero 200s (nginx ingress logs, first 8h). Most rejections happen client-side before any request is sent, so server telemetry undercounts the impact. ## Problem

A clean-machine bootstrap of this repo fails today, verified end-to-end in a tart VM (macOS Tahoe base image, 2026-07-01):

1. **Hard blocker**: the locked nix-darwin (`f73cbf1`, 2026-06-11) runs `brew bundle --cleanup --zap`, which current Homebrew rejects (`requires --force, --force-cleanup or $HOMEBREW_ASK`). Any machine with an up-to-date brew fails activation — including the host on its next rebuild (currently on generation 69 from April, with `onActivation.autoUpdate = true`).
2. The README bootstrap steps don't work as written: `.ditto` flake ref typo, flakes not enabled by the official installer, `nix run nix-darwin` resolves upstream HEAD via the GitHub API (version skew + rate-limited on shared IPs), no mention of the first-activation `/etc` renames, and `just _rebuild alyssa@work` references a `darwinConfiguration` that doesn't exist (only `ditto` does).

## Changes

- **flake.lock**: pin `darwin` input to nix-darwin master `a1fa429` (2026-06-18), which passes `--zap --force-cleanup`. Note: this rev also changes the brew invocation to `sudo --user=<owner>` — the brew prefix must be owned by the configured user.
- **README**: rewritten macOS setup section with the VM-verified sequence, including the new Homebrew tap-trust prereq (`brew trust cirruslabs/cli getditto/build-infra`) and the private-tap auth requirement.

## Verification

- Clean tart VM: nix install → flakes → `/etc` renames → `nix build .#darwinConfigurations.ditto.system` → `sudo ./result/sw/bin/darwin-rebuild switch --flake .#ditto` → green (19/20 Brewfile deps; `tailscale-app`'s pkg scripts fail inside VMs — system-extension approval — expected to work on hardware).
- Reproducibility: the branch's pinned build produced a store path identical to the pre-tested override build (no new generation on re-switch).

## Before merging / before next host rebuild

- Run `brew trust cirruslabs/cli getditto/build-infra` on the host (both currently untrusted there).
- Fresh machines additionally need: the `alyssaevans` user to exist, brew prefix owned by that user, GitHub auth for the private `getditto/build-infra` tap.

body:
## Summary
Addresses Scott's 2nd-round beta feedback on the **BHS Beloit Clinic** run (over-counted gyp ceilings, stairs priced as finished, missed WC-1). Three flag-gated sub-gates inside `_enforce_ceiling_scope_gate`, all **default OFF**. A cross-job validation sweep (32 saved JSONs) reshaped the scope — see the pinned comment for data.

### Ship-ready
- **`NIGHTSHIFT_WALLCOVERING_RFI`** — when a `WC-x` code appears but no wallcovering area was quantified, promote a dedicated RFI (via `_gate_add_rfi`). Never fabricates area. Pure upside; validated safe across the sweep. Beloit: surfaces the WC-1 that was buried in notes.

### Experimental (default OFF, do not flip on prod yet)
- **`NIGHTSHIFT_COMMERCIAL_CEILING_GYP_GATE`** — **provenance-based**: demotes a commercial painted ceiling to ACT/not-painted + RFI **only** when the extractor marked its material `"<type> (assumed)"` (could not confirm the type from an RCP/finish schedule). **Fail-safe**: no marker → no-op (proven a strict no-op across all 32 saved JSONs). Replaces an earlier keyword-whitelist that over-demoted real ceilings on Honey/TSC/Dutchess (see comment). Requires a re-run to exercise end-to-end, since existing extractions predate the marker.
- **`NIGHTSHIFT_STAIR_FINISH_GATE`** — zeroes stair-room paint scope unless a note confirms the stair is finished. Same over-demotion risk observed in the sweep; held experimental pending provenance treatment.

## Root cause
The extractor labels ceilings `GYP / painted=True` when the RCP/finish schedule isn't legible; the existing ACT demote only fires on an ACT material string, so mislabeled-as-GYP ACT rooms slip into the gyp bucket. WC-1 *was* detected (A120 note) but never promoted to a formal RFI.

## Validation

author: lvanhouten
body:
## Verification result

The deferred DACL finding (`_docs/issues/2026-07-01-named-pipe-dacl-verification.md`) is **confirmed**. Connecting a read-only `NamedPipeClientStream` and calling `.GetAccessControl()` on a live board pipe shows the default DACL grants:

| Principal | Rights | Inject (write)? | Read output? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Everyone` | `0x120089` read-only | No | **Yes** |
| `ANONYMOUS LOGON` | `0x120089` read-only | No | **Yes** |
| owner / SYSTEM / Administrators | full | Yes | Yes |

Command/keystroke injection is default-denied (no `FILE_WRITE_DATA`), but on a multi-user box any local user could open a line's data pipe and read its PTY output — which can carry secrets.

## Fix — per-boot access secret

Node's `net.Server.listen` can't set a pipe security descriptor, so both planes are gated at the application layer (chosen over a native `CreateNamedPipe` rewrite of the vendored kernel):

- Board generates a random secret at startup, writes it to an owner-only file (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\agent-relay\board.<pipe-base>.secret`; the file sits inside the user profile, which other non-admin users can't traverse).
- Every connection must send `<secret>\n` first; a wrong/absent secret is dropped (control) or receives nothing (data), with a 5s pre-auth timeout.
- Centralized in `lib.js` (`connectPipe`/`connectControl` send it, constant-time verify in `board.js`) so web/`sb`/`patch`/`mcp` are all covered without per-caller code. Read fresh per connect, so clients survive a board restart.

## Verification

E2e on an isolated board (`AGENT_RELAY_PIPE`): legit client reads output; wrong-secret foreign reader gets **0 bytes**; silent reader dropped at the auth timeout; a rejected control client doesn't disturb the legit control path. Unit tests: `server/board/lib.test.js` (round-trip + constant-time compare). 50 server + 12 client tests pass.

## Note

author: damione1
body:
## Problem

The firmware formats belt telemetry floats with `%g`; a NaN/Inf belt reading prints the bare tokens `nan`/`inf`/`-inf`, which is not valid JSON. `parse_minfo` returned `None` on that line, and since the `maslow-info` event just stops firing when parsing fails, the belt panel silently froze on its last good values with no indication anything was wrong, and this could persist indefinitely (every subsequent poll with the same bad field keeps failing).

## Fix

- `parse_minfo` sanitizes bare `nan`/`inf`/`-inf` tokens (only outside string literals, via a small hand-rolled scanner since `regex` isn't already a dependency) to `null` before parsing.
- `MaslowInfo`'s four belt-length and four belt-error fields become `Option<f32>`, so a single bad reading degrades just that field to `None` instead of failing the whole parse; the other fields keep updating normally.
- `BeltControls.svelte` renders a `null` length/error as `?` with a distinct visual flag on that specific belt, instead of the whole panel freezing or disappearing.

Checked the blast radius: only `BeltControls.svelte` reads these fields elsewhere in the frontend.

## Checks

- `cargo test`: 63 passed (new: mixed nan/inf/-inf fields parse with only the bad ones becoming `None`; sanitizer leaves strings and normal numbers, including scientific notation, untouched)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets`: 0 warnings
- `npm run check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings

## Hardware validation

- A MINFO line with a NaN belt value shows `?` on that belt with a visible flag, not a silent freeze; the other belts keep updating.

body:
## What

Adds the `assess-abi-migration` skill (ported from [janeyx99/abi-stable-skills](https://github.com/janeyx99/abi-stable-skills)) — a read-only audit of a PyTorch C++/CUDA extension repo that determines stable-ABI migration readiness and emits an ordered migration plan as `.abi-migration-plan.json` plus a chat summary.

## Skill Checklist

- [x] Structure matches the scaffold layout intentionally
- [x] `SKILL.md` has YAML frontmatter with `name` and `description`
- [x] Directory name matches `name` field in frontmatter
- [x] `evals/eval.yaml` exists
- [x] The eval measures a real task outcome (correctness of the emitted plan JSON), not formatting
- [x] Deterministic checks used wherever possible (plan-JSON checkers; sha256 read-only enforcement)
- [x] `uv run validate-evals skills/assess-abi-migration` passes
- [x] Manual verification was run against the authored benchmark contract (see below)

## Test Plan

- `uv run validate-evals skills/assess-abi-migration` — passes
- All fixture C++/CUDA files verified to compile against real torch headers (`g++ -fsyntax-only` / nvcc syntax check) so the pre-migration code is genuinely valid
- Every checker exercised in both directions: passes on a hand-authored reference plan, fails on the bare fixture, and fails on 10 mutated bad plans (experimental file included in scope, dropped pybind concern, wrong dispatch order, wrong cadence, empty_like false-positive gap, missing TensorIterator gap, blocked empty_strided without workaround, empty blockers, scaffold present in one-shot plan, modified source file)
- `prek` hooks pass on all added files

## Eval Coverage

1. `full_repo_assessment` — realistic mixed-concern repo (pybind bindings, C++ Meta impls, C++ autograd Function, unstable CUDA APIs, an existing `register_fake`, an out-of-scope `experimental/` dir). Checker asserts per-file concern tags, experimental exclusion, existing-fake detection, and canonical `dispatch_order` for incremental cadence.
2. `coverage_gap_detection` — forces real header grepping against the installed torch: `at::empty_like` must NOT be reported as a gap (it exists in `stable/ops.h`), `at::TensorIterator` must be a structural gap, `at::empty_strided` must carry the documented workaround.
3. `no_tests_blocker` — repo with no tests: plan must flag a test-related blocker (SKILL.md Step 8).
4. `one_shot_readonly` — adversarial: one-shot cadence must omit `scaffold-stable-target`, and a sha256 manifest enforces that the skill modified no source file ("this skill does not modify code").

All four exercised via the checker verification above; full agent-in-the-loop harness runs pending (API rate limits).

## Why This Eval Is Credible

The coverage-gap case specifically punishes answering from memory instead of grepping the installed headers. The read-only case guards the contract that assessment never mutates the repo.

author: jeandm-isc
body:
An issue can happen when deserializing some requests taking no arguments (for example the configurationDone request). 
For such requests, the DAP specification doesn't clearly explain if they should have no 'arguments' field or an 'arguments' field with an empty object, so different tools might use different ways to do it: Neovim sends such requests using the first way but Zed uses the second way. Since the specs are not clear, both ways seem valid and so should be handled.

As of now for these requests, if the received message contains an empty 'arguments' field, deserializing will fail. That happens because the Command enum has a few variants taking no arguments, meaning serde_json::from_str() will expect no 'arguments' field at all for these commands.
Just adding an Option<EmptyArguments> for these variants is enough to make sure that both a message with no 'arguments' field or a message with an empty 'arguments' field can be deserialized by serde.

author: bbaaxx
body:
This PR optimizes the Admin Categories management page by consolidating the data fetching logic for categories and their move counts.

Previously, the page fetched all categories and then separately fetched move counts grouped by category ID, merging them in-memory using a JavaScript Map.

The new implementation uses a single Drizzle query with a `LEFT JOIN` on the `moves` table and a `GROUP BY` on `categories.id`. It utilizes `sql<number>count(moves.id)` to ensure that the count is accurate even for categories with no moves (which would return 0 instead of 1 if `count(*)` were used with a left join).

This change improves performance by offloading aggregation to the database and simplifying the server-side code.

Key changes:
- Refactored `src/routes/admin/categories/+page.server.ts` to use a single optimized query.
- Removed manual Map-based merging logic.
- Updated `.Jules/bolt.md` with learnings regarding JOIN vs Batching for aggregations.

author: dbtlr
body:
## Summary

`find` and `count` gain three anchored string operators on frontmatter fields — `--starts-with`, `--ends-with`, `--contains` (`FIELD:VALUE` tokens, repeatable, AND-composed like `--eq`). The headline job is namespace enumeration over tag conventions:

```bash
norn find --starts-with tags:release:     # every doc carrying a release:* tag
norn find --starts-with depends_on:NRN-   # matches stored "[[NRN-123]]"
```

## Semantics

- **Case-sensitive and literal.** Implemented with `instr()`/`substr()` rather than `LIKE` — BINARY collation, `%`/`_` are ordinary characters, no wildcard/escape surface, no regex (per the scope guidance: the anchored trio stays indexable for the Wave-2 EAV index).
- **Scalar + array-aware** with `[[wikilink]]` bracket collapse on both sides, mirroring `--eq`.
- **Faithful to source text**: booleans compare as `true`/`false`, needle whitespace is preserved (`'title:done '` keeps its trailing space), numbers compare in JSON canonical form.
- Empty values and missing colons reject at parse (exit 1, the `--eq` convention); `--contains` is frontmatter-scoped — body substring search remains `--text`.
- **MCP parity**: `vault.find` / `vault.count` gain `starts_with`/`ends_with`/`contains` params; handlers construct the shared `FilterArgs`, so evaluation cannot drift (adding the fields is compiler-forced by exhaustive struct init).

## Review catches folded in

An adversarial review confirmed three defects, fixed here: (1) SQLite's scalar rendering leaked into matching (`archived:true` matched nothing while `--eq` worked — booleans now render via `json_type`); (2) the parser trimmed needle whitespace, silently altering anchored predicates; (3) the MCP param-schema doc comments and `docs/concepts.md` didn't enumerate the new operators. Two structural cleanups from the same review: the triplicated array-aware WHERE skeleton is now a single `push_array_aware_clause`, and `find`'s missing-predicate gate compares `FilterArgs` against `Default` instead of a hand-maintained field list (this diff itself initially fell into that trap).

## Verification

- Quartet green: `cargo check --locked`, 1533 tests / 0 failed, `clippy -D warnings`, `fmt --check`, no `Cargo.lock` drift.
- Atlas dogfood: `--starts-with tags:source:` → 3 real docs (array namespace enumeration); `--contains workspace:nor` (277) exactly matches `--eq workspace:norn`; `--ends-with type:artifact` → 161 = known agent-artifact count; warm queries ~34ms.
- Dogfood by-catch filed separately: NRN-76 (dot-prefixed vault root scans as silently empty).

author: contexxto
body:
Tercera vuelta de feedback en vivo. Investigué la "tarjeta cortada" reproduciendo la MISMA conversación en una sesión compartida y midiendo el DOM real con JS.

## Diagnóstico real
El overflow medido es de solo **~50px** (una fracción de una tarjeta de 230px) — no una tarjeta entera perdida. Pero el carrusel **no tenía ninguna forma de desplazarse con un mouse normal**: sin trackpad/touch, `overflow-x:auto` no reacciona a la rueda del mouse, y no había flechas ni scrollbar visible. La última tarjeta no estaba "cortada por falta de espacio": era **inalcanzable**.

## Fix (`ResultCards.jsx`)
- **Flechas ← →** que aparecen solo cuando hay contenido oculto de ese lado (`canLeft`/`canRight`, recalculado con `ResizeObserver` + `onScroll`). Desplazan por "página" (85% del ancho visible).
- **Rueda del mouse**: si el gesto es predominantemente vertical y el carrusel tiene overflow, redirige el delta a scroll horizontal — no compite con el gesto nativo de trackpad.
- **Degradado sutil** (fade al color de fondo) en cada borde con contenido oculto: la señal honesta de "hay más", visible incluso sin hacer hover.

## Verificación (ejecutada en mi entorno)
- Reproduje la conversación real en la misma sesión del navegador conectado y medí con JS: `scrollWidth - clientWidth = 50px` — confirmado que el contenido faltante es alcanzable, solo faltaba la forma de llegar a él.
- `vite build` compila; `eslint` sin problemas nuevos.

## Summary

This adds a default-off diagnostic switch for the slow `repo_dependency` retract path:

- `ESHU_REPO_DEPENDENCY_RETRACT_STATEMENT_TIMING=false` keeps the existing grouped transaction behavior.
- `ESHU_REPO_DEPENDENCY_RETRACT_STATEMENT_TIMING=true` executes the existing `repo_dependency` retract statements separately so the logs can time `repository_relationships` and `evidence_artifacts` independently.
- The diagnostic path reuses the existing `shared edge retract statement completed` log shape instead of adding a new metric, queue, worker, lease, timeout, Cypher text, or backend branch.

author: henry40408
body:
## Summary

When a Lua handler is cancelled mid-flight (timeout, connection drop) while inside a `kv.update` transform or a `db.tx` body, three resources could leak or get poisoned instead of being cleaned up:

- `IN_KV_UPDATE` stayed stuck `true`, poisoning later `kv`/`db` calls on the pooled VM.
- A pinned SQLite connection was returned to the pool mid-`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.
- A pinned Postgres connection stayed idle-in-transaction, holding a `SERIALIZABLE` snapshot and row locks on the shared operator DB.
- `db.tx`'s `run_tx` deferred the rollback to Luau GC (via a shared `Arc`) instead of firing it synchronously on cancellation.

## Changes

- `IN_KV_UPDATE` restored via an RAII guard so every exit path (return, error, cancellation) resets it.
- SQLite: rollback-on-drop guard (`Drop for SqliteTransaction`) + `PinnedTx` wrapper for `kv_update`, best-effort rollback via a detached task.
- Postgres: mirrors the SQLite fix (`Drop for PgTransaction` + `PinnedTx`), plus a deterministic single-connection regression test in the `pg-serial` nextest group.
- `db.tx`: closures now hold `Weak` refs instead of cloned `Arc`s, so `run_tx` holds the only strong ref and cancellation drops the transaction (and fires the rollback) synchronously instead of waiting on GC.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated to document the rollback-on-drop invariant.
- Design doc and implementation plan under `docs/superpowers/plans/`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo nextest run` — 235/235 passed, including new deterministic single-connection regression tests for the SQLite, Postgres, and `run_tx` cancellation paths
- [x] `cargo fmt --all`

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Problem

The repository's `CONTRIBUTING.md` (line: `Sign-off (DCO \`Signed-off-by\`) is **not** required for this repository.`) and `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (line: `> Note: DCO \`Signed-off-by\` sign-off is **not** required for this repository.`) explicitly state that DCO sign-off is not required.

This deviates from the ROS2 ecosystem standard. The `ros2/ros2` meta-repo, Navigation2 (`ros-planning/navigation2`), and Autoware (`autowarefoundation/autoware`) all enforce DCO (Developer Certificate of Origin) — every commit must carry a `Signed-off-by` trailer (`git commit -s`). The rationale is documented in the ROS 2 Developer Guide (https://docs.ros.org/en/rolling/The-ROS2-Project/Contributing/Developer-Guide.html#developer-certificate-of-origin).

Those projects use the Probot DCO GitHub App at the organization level, but since this repository is a standalone repo outside the `ros2` GitHub org, that app is not available. The standard alternative for standalone repos is `KineticCafe/actions-dco@v3` (used by many orgs that cannot install org-wide GitHub Apps).

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Add `.github/workflows/dco.yml`

A new workflow that checks every pull request for `Signed-off-by` trailers on each commit:

```yaml
---
name: DCO

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  dco:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 2
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0  # v7.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: KineticCafe/actions-dco@<RESOLVE_SHA_AT_IMPLEMENTATION>  # v3.7.2
```

> **Note for implementer:** Resolve the SHA for `KineticCafe/actions-dco` tag `v3.7.2` by running:
> ```
> git ls-remote https://github.com/KineticCafe/actions-dco.git refs/tags/v3.7.2
> ```
> Replace `<RESOLVE_SHA_AT_IMPLEMENTATION>` with the full 40-character SHA and add a trailing comment `# v3.7.2`.

### 2. Add `.github/dco.yml`

Exemption configuration for bots and trivial changes:

```yaml
exempt-authors:
  - "dependabot[bot]"
trivial-pattern: "^(ci|docs|chore|typo|fixup!|squash!):"
```

### 3. Update `CONTRIBUTING.md`

Replace the line that says DCO is not required with instructions for contributors:

```markdown
## Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)

This repository requires all commits to include a `Signed-off-by` trailer
as per the ROS 2 Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) standard
([ros2.org](https://docs.ros.org/en/rolling/The-ROS2-Project/Contributing/Developer-Guide.html#developer-certificate-of-origin)).

To sign a commit, use `git commit -s` (or `git commit --signoff`).
Existing unsigned commits on a branch can be fixed with:

```sh
git rebase --signoff HEAD~N   # where N is the number of commits to fix
```

CI enforces this check on every pull request via `.github/workflows/dco.yml`.
Trivial changes (typo fixes, docs, chore) and Dependabot commits are exempted.
```

### 4. Update `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`

Replace the DCO-exemption note with a checklist item:

```markdown
- [ ] All commits include a `Signed-off-by` trailer (`git commit -s`)
```

Remove the line:
```
> Note: DCO `Signed-off-by` sign-off is **not** required for this repository.
```

## Rationale

- **Ecosystem alignment:** Every major ROS2 project enforces DCO. Accepting contributions without sign-off creates a legal chain-of-copyright issue for any future contribution that needs to be upstreamed or redistributed.
- **Low ceremony:** Adding a 2-minute CI job and a one-line `.github/dco.yml` is negligible overhead. Contributors already use `git commit -s` out of habit if they work in the broader ROS2 ecosystem.
- **Self-service fix:** If a contributor forgets, `git rebase --signoff` is a well-known fix, and the DCO check's failure message is clear.

## Prior Art

- `ros2/ros2` — DCO enforced at org level via Probot DCO app (no workflow file)
- `ros-planning/navigation2` — DCO enforced at org level via Probot DCO app
- `autowarefoundation/autoware` — DCO enforced at org level via Probot DCO app
- `KineticCafe/actions-dco` — the de-facto standard action for standalone repos that cannot install the Probot app: https://github.com/KineticCafe/actions-dco
- `jenkinsci/dco-check-action` — alternative with lower adoption

## Files Changed

author: skydoves
body:
## Summary

Fixes #863. When `ZoomablePlugin` is enabled, its double-tap detector consumes the pointer `down` on every tap, so a parent `Modifier.clickable` never fires. This is inherent to `detectTapGestures` (it calls `down.consume()` as soon as a pointer goes down, regardless of whether the gesture becomes a double tap), and the parent's `clickable` requires an *unconsumed* down. A single tap therefore cannot both drive zoom and bubble to a parent.

This PR exposes an `onTap` callback so taps can be handled at the plugin level, which is what the issue asks for ("provide a click callback within the ZoomablePlugin").

## Changes

- Add `ZoomablePlugin.onTap: ((Offset) -> Unit)?` and thread it through `ZoomableContent` (android/skia), `SubSamplingImage`, and `zoomGestures`.
- Install the tap detector when **double-tap zoom OR `onTap`** is set, and make `onDoubleTap` conditional on `enableDoubleTapZoom`. When both are off, no tap detector is installed, so a single tap stays unconsumed and reaches a parent gesture handler (previously the only workaround).
- Fix a stale KDoc example that referenced a nonexistent `ZoomablePlugin(config = ...)` parameter; configuration is supplied via `rememberZoomableState(config = ...)`.

The change is source-compatible: `onTap` defaults to `null`, and with it unset behavior is identical to before.

## Usage

```kotlin
GlideImage(
  imageModel = { imageUrl },
  component = rememberImageComponent {
    +ZoomablePlugin(onTap = { position -> openFullScreen() })
  },
)
```

## Tests

Adds desktop `runComposeUiTest` coverage in `ZoomGesturesTest` (runs on the JVM via `desktopTest`, no emulator):

- `doubleTap_zoomsIn_withDefaultConfig` and `doubleTap_whenZoomed_resetsZoom` — regression: existing double-tap zoom/reset still works.
- `singleTap_invokesOnTapCallback` — new: a single tap fires `onTap`.
- `singleTap_invokesOnTap_notParentClickable` — new: `onTap` fires while the parent clickable stays silent (documents the intended replacement).
- `singleTap_reachesParent_whenTapHandlingDisabled` — regression: with tap handling off, a single tap still bubbles to the parent.

All 5 pass locally. All targets (android/desktop/ios/macos/wasm) compile.

## Notes

- Adds `org.jetbrains.compose.ui:ui-test-junit4` and the host `skiko-awt-runtime` (classifier detected per host, so CI/Linux works) as `desktopTest`-only dependencies.
- Test compiles were excluded from explicit-API mode in the module build, matching `landscapist-core`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added optional single-tap handling to zoomable content, so apps can react to taps while zoom gestures are enabled.
  * Improved desktop UI test support across host environments and added compose UI test libraries.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Double-tap zoom behavior is now covered by tests, including reset behavior when zoomed in.
  * Tap handling now correctly prevents parent click targets from receiving taps when zoom gestures consume them.
* **Tests**
  * Added desktop Compose UI tests for tap and zoom interaction behavior.

## Resumo

Primeira fatia vertical da **migração completa do dump legado → core-api** (32 tabelas). Estende o ETL one-shot (`scripts/etl/`) — que cobria só suppliers, financiers, collaborators e users — para o módulo `programs`, espelhando o padrão já validado do `partners`.

Ticket: `PRG-ETL-BOOTSTRAP` (closed-green, W0→W3). Runbook operacional: `ERP-INFRA/docs/runbooks/dump-migration.md`.

## O que entrega

- **Proveniência:** `prg_programs.legacy_id` (INT NULL, UNIQUE) + migration `0001_grey_triathlon.sql` no journal próprio do módulo (`__drizzle_migrations_programs`). NULL = nativo; não-NULL = migrado.
- **Port de ETL na public-api:** `LegacyEntityStore<A,Ref>` genérico em `application/ports/`, adapter Drizzle com `provision` idempotente (SELECT `.for('update')` por `legacy_id` → INSERT ou skip `already-exists`, **nunca UPDATE**) e `public-api/etl.ts` (`buildProgramsEtlPort`) importado por path direto (ADR-0006).
- **Fatia no `scripts/etl/`:** reader/decode da tabela legada `programs` + mapper com **validação estrita via domínio** — `Program.create` revalida nome/sigla; `active=0` → `Program.deactivate` (estado sempre via transição); linha inválida → quarentena `DomainRejected` com `combine` acumulando erros (nunca INSERT direto).
- **Decisões travadas:** `legacyId = programNumber = row.id`; `logoKey = null` sempre (o `logo` legado é URL, não chave S3 — re-upload é fatia futura).

## Como foi validado

- W2 (code review read-only): APPROVED round 1/3 — adesão a ADR-0006/0014/0020 e ao padrão `partners`.
- W3 verde: `pnpm run typecheck` + `format:check` + `lint` + `pnpm test` (**3321 pass · 0 fail**); teste do mapper 7/7 isolado.
- W0 RED reproduzido genuinamente (mapper removido → `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`).

## Fora de escopo (fatias futuras)

- Re-upload do `logo` legado como `logoKey` S3.
- Asserções de `programs` nos testes de integração gated + execução real contra DB/Docker (fixture pronta em `tests/etl/fixtures/legacy-mini.sql`).

## Resumo

- **Tela de datas/preço** (`apps/mobile/app/reservas/checkout.tsx`): nova tela que espelha fielmente `_PriceCalc.tsx` (web) — tabs diária/semanal/mensal, DateTimePicker nativo, devolução calculada automaticamente, resumo de preço com descontos, teto R$ 500 (D2), nota ao proprietário, tratamento de erro `REGISTRATION_INCOMPLETE`.
- **Criar reserva**: `POST /api/bookings` via `apiFetch` (Bearer). Navega para `/reservas/[id]` após sucesso.
- **Checkout Mercado Pago** (`app/api/payments/mp/checkout/mobile/route.ts`): rota aditiva que aceita Bearer JWT (usa `resolveUserId` em vez de `auth()` cookie). Idêntica à rota web em lógica de negócio; `back_urls` usam deep-link `shareo://`. Flag `mercadoPagoEnabled` OFF → 404 → mensagem amigável no app.
- **Tela de item** (`apps/mobile/app/itens/[id].tsx`): substitui `Alert.alert("disponível no site")` por `router.push("/reservas/checkout")` com params de preço. Tap targets 44×44 px, acessibilidade.
- **Tela de reserva** (`apps/mobile/app/reservas/[id].tsx`): botão "Pagar reserva" visível quando `status=CONFIRMED && paymentStatus≠PAID`. Abre `init_point` via `Linking.openURL`. Trata todos os casos de erro da API.
- **`apps/mobile/lib/pricing.ts`**: espelho isolado de `lib/pricing.ts` (web) — `calcBookingTotal`, `fmtCurrency`, `addDays`, `CHECKOUT_MAX_CENTS`.
- **14 novos testes** em `lib/__tests__/pricing.test.ts`.

## Checagens

| Checagem | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @shareo/mobile test` | 28/28 passando |
| `tsc --noEmit` (mobile) | 0 erros novos (4 pré-existentes em `api.test.ts` não tocados) |
| `tsc --noEmit` (web) | 0 erros |
| ESLint rota nova | Sem erros |
| Flag `mercadoPagoEnabled` OFF | Inerte-seguro (404 → mensagem amigável) |
| Rota web `/api/payments/mp/checkout` | Não tocada |

## Necessidade de mudança no backend (para avaliar)

**Nenhuma mudança nas rotas existentes foi feita.** Um ponto para avaliação:

> `POST /api/payments/mp/checkout` usa `auth()` (cookie NextAuth) e **não aceita Bearer JWT do app mobile**. Por isso foi criada a rota espelho `/api/payments/mp/checkout/mobile` — aditiva, sem tocar na web.  
> Se no futuro quiser unificar as rotas, basta migrar `/api/payments/mp/checkout/route.ts` para usar `resolveUserId` (que já aceita Bearer e cai para cookie como fallback). Esse seria um PR separado pós-review.

## Plano de teste manual (APK)

1. Login com conta de locatário de teste
2. Abrir qualquer item disponível → tela mostra preços e botão "Reservar item"
3. Tocar "Reservar item" → abre `/reservas/checkout` com tabs corretas
4. Selecionar data + dias → devolução calculada, total exibido
5. "Solicitar locação" → cria reserva, navega para `/reservas/[id]`
6. Com `mercadoPagoEnabled=OFF`: botão "Pagar reserva" não aparece (status PENDING, não CONFIRMED)
7. Com reserva CONFIRMED (admin confirma no web): botão "Pagar reserva" aparece → toque → mensagem "pagamento indisponível" (flag OFF)

author: brunokohncontact-coder
body:
## O quê

Adiciona um nudge no Painel para a **antecedência de agendamento** (booking lead time): quando os shows vêm entrando na agenda com pouca antecedência mediana, o dashboard alerta *"Você fecha shows em cima da hora"* e sugere prospectar com mais folga.

Fecha o único item recente do eixo Shows ainda sem eco no Painel — a antecedência já tinha página, CSV (D185), recorte por ano (D186) e comparativo ano-a-ano (D187), mas nenhum nudge.

## Como

- **`src/lib/shows.ts`** — novo helper puro `bookingLeadTimeHeadline(report, shortDays=14, criticalDays=7)` + tipo `BookingLeadTimeHeadline` + constantes `LEAD_TIME_SHORT_DAYS`/`LEAD_TIME_CRITICAL_DAYS` (espelho de `paymentLagHeadline`). De uma `bookingLeadTime` já computada: `show` só quando a amostra é **confiável** (`reliable`, ≥ `MIN_LEAD_TIME_SAMPLE=3`) **e** a mediana cai a ≤ 14 dias; `critical` a ≤ 7. Ao contrário do card ano-a-ano (onde subir a mediana é melhora), aqui o alarme é a ponta **baixa**.
- **`src/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx`** — banner 🟠/🔴 logo após o nudge de funil por contratante, reaproveitando os `shows` já carregados (`createdAt` vem na consulta `include`, **zero I/O extra**), linkando `/shows/antecedencia`.
- **`src/lib/shows.test.ts`** — **+7 testes** cobrindo gate por amostra, faixas curta/crítica, limiares inclusivos e injetados.

## Por quê

A deferência anterior (D185(d)/D187(a)) tratava a leitura como "um retrato, não um alarme". Reavaliado: uma antecedência mediana **curta** é a mesma tese de "planejar com folga" que já sustenta os nudges de fins de semana livres e de sazonalidade — e tem precedente direto no DSO/prazo de recebimento (D70), também um retrato que ganhou card no Painel. O gate apertado (`reliable` + ≤ 14 dias) mantém o banner raro. Detalhes em **D189** (`DECISIONS.md`).

**Ressalva de dados:** herdada da D185 — `createdAt` só é fiel com cadastro perto do fechamento; seed/import distorcem.

body:
Closes #710
Closes #601

## Summary

- **#710 — Auto-generated MapLibre styles**: `GET /styles/{source-id}/style.json` now falls back to a generated MapLibre v8 style when no configured style matches but a vector source with that id exists. Since TileJSON `vector_layers` carries no geometry type, each source-layer gets fill + line + circle layers gated by legacy `$type` filters (z-grouped: all fills → all lines → all circles), deterministic per-layer HSL colors, `fill-outline-color`, and zoom-interpolated widths.
- **#601 — Composite tiles**: `GET /data/{a}+{b}+{c}/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf` fetches member tiles concurrently, decodes MVT, merges layers (name conflicts → append features), and re-encodes. Merged TileJSON at `GET /data/{a}+{b}.json` (vector_layers union, minzoom = max, maxzoom = min of members). Named composites via `[[composites]]` TOML config with their own TileJSON + tile endpoints (`data/configs/composite-demo.toml` example included).

## Implementation

- New pure modules `src/stylegen.rs` (style generation) and `src/composite.rs` (MVT decode/merge/encode via prost types) — no new dependencies.
- Route hooks: `routes/styles.rs` (style fallback), `routes/data.rs` (composite id resolution: configured `[[composites]]` entry wins over ad-hoc `+`-joined ids).
- Config: `[[composites]]` section + schema reflection; docs for both features in `apps/docs/content/`.

## Testing

- 75 unit tests in `stylegen`/`composite` (exhaustive per-variant coverage: geometry mapping, color hashing, layer z-grouping, merge conflicts, TileJSON union edge cases).
- 32 integration tests (`route_composite.rs`: 23, `route_style_autogen.rs`: 9) covering happy paths, 404/400, empty-tile members, zoom-range respect, and named-composite config.

## Qué

Cierra los incs 8-9 del spec [agio-hub-middleware.md](docs/specs/agio-hub-middleware.md) a partir del reporte del equipo Hub (su PR #204 en `agio-hub`, pendiente de merge de Carlos), aplicando las correcciones C1–C10 del contrato v0.2 que nos tocan.

### Desviación real corregida (código)

El seed del Hub escribe **`APP_TOKEN_FIREWALL_MONITOR_BATCH`** al `.env`, pero nuestro `config.py` solo leía `HUB_APP_TOKEN` → el token seedeado era invisible. Fix: `AliasChoices` en `hub_app_token` — lee el nombre del seed tal cual y `HUB_APP_TOKEN` queda como override manual (gana si ambos existen). Cubierto con 2 checks nuevos (suite 27/27).

### Inc 9 — verificado end-to-end contra el código real del PR #204

Levanté el Hub de la rama `feat/firewall-monitor-ingest` en un **worktree aislado** (sin tocar el clone ni la rama del otro equipo) con SQLite scratch y venv propio:

- Credencial `firewall-monitor-batch` provisionada (audiencia `firewall_monitor`).
- `scripts/smoke_hub.py` (nuevo, permanente): push real → `200 accepted=5` · re-push idéntico → idempotente · token inválido → `401 apps.invalid_token`. **3/3.**
- `sync_once` completo del orquestador → 15 filas en `fw_wan_metrics`/`fw_system_metrics`/`fw_internet_quality`, lotes solapados **deduplicados por llave natural** (9, no 14), origen derivado del `credential_id`, watermarks avanzados con 0 fallos.

Falta solo re-correr `smoke_hub.py` contra **prod** tras el merge del PR #204 + deploy (runbook §5 de su reporte).

### 🐞 Hallazgo para el review del PR #204 (lado Hub, no bloqueante aquí)

La ruta **create** de `seed_firewall_monitor_credentials.py` llama `AppsService.create_credential()` sin el argumento keyword-only `slug` → `TypeError` en la primera corrida sobre una DB donde la credencial no existe (exactamente el caso del VPS en su paso de deploy). La ruta *rotate* sí funciona — por eso no lo vieron. Fix de 1 línea: `slug=cred_name`. `seed_odw_credentials.py` arrastra el mismo problema latente. Documentado en el contrato §2.

### Docs

- [agio-hub-ingest-contract.md](docs/specs/agio-hub-ingest-contract.md) → **v0.2**: C1 (sin permiso IAM de ingesta), C2 (401 vs 403), C3 (**prod `HUB_URL` = `https://app.agiotech.mx/api`**), C4 (credencial con guiones), C5–C10, y las respuestas §7 (tablas espejo `fw_*`, retención 90d, tope 500, credencial-por-instalación).
- Spec: incs 8-9 marcados con su estado real; checklist de "done" — solo queda abierto el ítem del seed por el bug del `slug`.

## Validación

`test_hub_sync.py` **27/27** · `import app.main` OK · e2e real contra la rama del PR #204 como se describe arriba. El Hub quedó intacto (worktree removido, proceso apagado, su clone sin tocar).

author: surya-prakash-s
body:
### 🎨 Palette: Improve accessibility with automatic aria-invalid propagation

#### 💡 What:
I have implemented automatic propagation of the `aria-invalid` attribute from the `FormElement` container to its child form controls (`Input`, `Select`, `Textarea`, and `CheckboxPrimitive`). 

Previously, if a `FormElement` had `hasError={true}`, it would apply the error styling, but the screen reader wouldn't necessarily know the input itself was invalid unless `aria-invalid` was manually added to each individual input component.

#### 🎯 Why:
This solves the user problem of inconsistent accessibility reporting in forms. By making the propagation automatic, we ensure that every form element in an error state is correctly announced as invalid by assistive technologies, without requiring developers to manually sync state across multiple components.

#### ♿ Accessibility:
- **Automatic `aria-invalid`**: Screen readers will now reliably announce "Invalid entry" when a form field has an error.
- **Defensive Prop Logic**: The `Input` component now correctly honors an explicitly passed `aria-invalid` prop, falling back to inference only if not provided.
- **Fixed PropTypes**: Corrected an invalid `PropTypes.boolean` in `FormElementHelpMessage` to `PropTypes.bool`, which prevents runtime warnings and potential silent failures in prop validation.

#### 📸 Before/After:
*Visuals remain identical as the change affects ARIA attributes and underlying React logic, but the accessibility tree is now correctly updated during error states.*

#### 🛠️ Implementation Details:
- Added `displayName` to `Input`, `Select`, `Textarea`, and `CheckboxPrimitive` for robust component identification.
- Updated `FormElementControl` to use `React.Children.map` and `React.cloneElement` to inject `aria-invalid="true"` when `hasError` is active.
- Added a new learning to `.Jules/palette.md` regarding reliable component identification in React.

author: firestaerter3
body:
## Summary

Fixes concurrent playback sessions on the same channel killing each other.

**Root cause**: when two devices play the same channel, they share one `XtreamLiveStream` because both sessions return `MediaSource.Id = "xtream_live_N"`. Emby`s `MediaSourceManager` reuses the first live stream for the second session. When the first session stops, `RemoveConsumer` drops the count to 0 and closes the stream, killing the second session too.

**Fix**: append `XtreamLiveStream.UniqueId` (a per-instance GUID) to `MediaSource.Id` in `GetChannelStream`. Each session now gets a uniquely identified media source, so Emby treats them independently. Closing one session only affects that session stream.

**Evidence from the reporter logs**:
- Chrome and iPhone both play ESPN (stream 363)
- Both sessions share `LiveStreamId: 06044cf0...xtream_live_363`
- Chrome stops at 00:08:23.425 → `consumer count is now 0` → stream closed
- iPhone gets `IOException: Unable to read data from the transport connection: Operation canceled` at 00:08:25.429

The `XtreamLiveStream` already tracks consumer count correctly; the issue is that Emby assigns both sessions to the same stream object.

## Testing

- `dotnet test`: 344 passed, 1 skipped (unchanged)
- Added `ConcurrentSessionsGetUniqueMediaSourceIds` test verifying two instances for the same channel have distinct UniqueIds

  * Fixed a live streaming issue where concurrent viewers of the same channel could end up sharing the same media source identifier, leading to cross-session interference.
  * Each active live stream session now gets its own unique media source identifier to improve stability during parallel playback.
* **Tests**

- **root tsconfig**: `module` / `moduleResolution` を `NodeNext` へ移行し、`baseUrl` と `paths` を削除（`@nostr-cache/*` は npm workspaces の node_modules 経由で解決されるため `paths` は実際には使われていませんでした）
- **dexie を named import 化**: NodeNext では dexie 4 の CJS default import が型エラー（TS2507）になるため `import { Dexie } from 'dexie'` に変更（ランタイム動作も検証済み）
- **テストの相対 import に `.js` 付与**: cache-relay の統合テスト3ファイル（NodeNext は拡張子必須）
- **server tsconfig**: root と重複する `target` / `module` / `esModuleInterop` の上書きを削除
- **build 用 tsconfig の `types` を明示**: shared=`[]` / cache-relay・server=`["node"]`。TS 6 は @types の自動取り込みに依存できないため、3パッケージで扱いを統一
- **cache-relay の build から `src/test/**` を除外** し、build script で `dist` と `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` をクリーン（テスト補助ファイルが dist に emit され、incremental ビルドでは除外後も残存していたため）
- **doc/TODO.md**: web-client（Angular 製 POC）を**一旦すべて廃棄する方針**を明記（オーナー決定）。廃棄項目を新設し、E2E 配線デモは作り直すクライアントを前提とする注記を追加

## Notes / 補足

- **TypeScript 本体は `^5.0.0` のまま**です。web-client の Angular 19（`@angular/compiler-cli`）が TS `>=5.5 <5.9` を要求するため、モノレポで TS 6 に上げると npm の dedupe により web-client のビルドが壊れます（検証済み）。
- ただし **web-client は廃棄方針が決まった**ため、`packages/web-client` の削除が完了すれば Angular の TS 制約が消え、Angular アップグレードを待たずに TS 6 化が可能になります（doc/TODO.md に反映済み）。
- shared / cache-relay / server の build 設定は **TypeScript 6.0.3 でのビルド通過を確認済み**で、TS 側の移行障害は解消されています。

## Verification / 検証

- TS 5.7.3: monorepo-wide `npm run build` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint:check` / `npm test` all green
- TS 6.0.3: `tsc -b` on shared / cache-relay / server passes
- `examples/node-relay-demo.mjs` runs end-to-end (EVENT/OK, REQ/EVENT/EOSE, CLOSE)
- Clean build no longer emits `dist/test/**` in cache-relay

## Summary

Comax Secrets **M3 — GitHub Actions 통합 + 서비스 토큰 관리**. GitHub Secret을 키마다 등록하지 않고, admin이 발급한 **CI 토큰 하나**로 서버 시크릿을 워크플로 스텝에 주입한다. 기본은 process-env(자식 프로세스에만), 필요할 때만 github-env(job 전역)로 opt-in.

## Changes

- **서비스 토큰 관리** (admin-only): `POST/GET/DELETE /api/v1/tokens` + `secret token {create,list,revoke}` CLI. 발급 토큰은 항상 non-admin(유출돼도 추가 토큰 발급·회수 불가). `is_admin`/`revoked_at` 컬럼 + 기존 DB용 admin-backfill 마이그레이션.
- **Soft-revoke 양쪽 arm**: bearer(`ByHash` revoked 제외) + 대시보드 세션(`authSession`의 `RevokedAt` 체크로 401) 동시 종료 (R2-1).
- **secret export**: `dotenv` / `json` / `github-env`. github-env는 `$GITHUB_ENV` heredoc + 값별 `::add-mask::` (opt-in job 전역 주입).
- **composite action** (`action.yml`): 자격증명 one-shot `$RUNNER_TEMP` + `if: always()` cleanup (R2-2). process-env(`run`) 기본 / `export-to: github-env` opt-in. `action-smoke.yml`가 (a) process-env 격리·plaintext 미노출 (b) credential 비잔존 (c) github-env 마스킹 (d) soft-revoke 거부를 E2E 증명.
- **대시보드**: `/settings/tokens`(발급/목록/회수, 한 번만 표시 dialog) + `/integrations/github-actions`(스니펫 레퍼런스) 페이지.
- **문서**: `docs/github-actions.md` 신규, `docs/threat-model.md`에 M3 위협모델 + 정직한 한계(마스킹 best-effort, CI 토큰 read-scope 없음 M4 이연, revoke는 소급 아님).
- **보안 수정 (이 PR에서 발견·수정)**: login이 `$COMAX_TOKEN` env를 읽어 토큰이 argv/process listing에 미노출; 마지막 live admin revoke 거부(409); ghenv 키 개행 방어.

## Files Changed

- **Source**: `internal/store/{token_repo,migrate,store,session_repo,schema.sql}`, `internal/server/{handlers_tokens,router,middleware,validate}`, `internal/cli/ghenv/ghenv`, `cmd/cli/{cmd_token,cmd_export,cmd_login,cmd_pull,cmd_run,main}`, `pkg/client/client`, `action.yml`
- **Tests**: `handlers_tokens_test`, `token_repo_test`, `migrate_test`, `ghenv_test`, `cmd_token_test`, `cmd_export_test`, `cli_loadctx_test`, `cli_integration_test`, `.github/workflows/action-smoke.yml`, `web/dashboard` *.test.tsx + e2e
- **Dashboard**: `pages/{Tokens,Actions}.tsx`, `components/TokenRow.tsx`, `AppShell.tsx`, `router.tsx`, `lib/{queries,types}.ts`
- **Docs/plan**: `docs/{github-actions,threat-model}.md`, `README.md`, `.claude/{prds,plans,reports}/…`

## Testing

- `go build ./...` / `go vet ./...` / `go test` (ghenv·store·server·cli·client) — green. 신규 테스트 5건 포함(login env, 마지막-admin revoke ×2, ghenv 키 개행).
- `gofmt -l` clean, `golangci-lint run` 0 issues (변경 패키지).
- `action-smoke.yml` — composite action M3 acceptance (a~d) E2E.

## Related

- PRD milestone 3 (`.claude/prds/comax-secrets.prd.md`), plan (`.claude/plans/comax-secrets-m3-github-actions.plan.md`), report (`.claude/reports/…`).

## Design Review

impeccable `critique` + detector (Assessment B) — advisory.

- **Detector (deterministic slop scan)**: clean (`[]`, 0 findings) on Tokens/Actions/TokenRow/AppShell.
- **강점**: two-phase "한 번만 표시" 토큰 dialog(복사 + 재조회 불가 경고); `forbidden`을 에러가 아닌 "관리자만" 안내로 프레이밍; revoked를 색이 아닌 라벨 badge로 전달(색만으로 상태 전달 금지); empty/loading/forbidden/error 상태 모두 처리; 기존 Sessions 페이지 어휘(`.sessions-table`) 재사용으로 일관성 확보.
- **약식 heuristic**: ~34/40 (Good).
- **[P2] advisory**: `CreateTokenDialog.copyToken`가 클립보드 실패 시 사용자에게 안내가 없어 복사됐다고 오인할 수 있음 → 후속 개선 권장(review-only, 이 PR에서 수정 안 함).

## Codex Adversarial Review

- 호출: `codex-runner.js` → `codex-invoke.js adversarial-review --base origin/master` (v0.2.2 fail-closed wrapper)
- 라운드 수: 1 (수렴, cap=1)

- YAGNI Triage: 해당 없음 (findings 0).

- Cross-gate dedupe: skip_safe=false (선행 plan/implement-codex receipt 미수렴) → 전체 diff 대상 신규 리뷰.

### Security Reviewer

`mccp:security-reviewer` Task (diff가 auth/token/crypto/secret 민감 영역 접촉) — **APPROVED for merge**.

- 이번 세션 수정 3건 독립 재검증: **H1**(login `$COMAX_TOKEN` env, argv 미노출) / **L1**(마지막 live admin revoke 409 가드 + `CountLiveAdmins`) / **L2**(ghenv 키 개행 거부) — 모두 sound, 테스트 커버.
- 추가 경로 전부 sound: SHA-256 토큰 해싱(constant-time), 토큰 revoke 시 세션 종료(`authSession` RevokedAt), admin-backfill 멱등(NOT EXISTS guard), `if: always()` credential cleanup, credentials 파일 atomic write + 0600, 대시보드 세션 HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite, CSRF constant-time, github-env heredoc delimiter 충돌 방어.
- **신규 취약점 0건.**

## Accessibility Review

## Contexte

Chaque visite compte (trafic faible). Ces modifications visent à lever les frictions sur le parcours d'achat de la page photo individuelle, en particulier sur mobile.

- **Bloc confiance** sous le bouton d'achat : paiement Stripe crypté, fichier disponible immédiatement, RAW + licence personnelle

## Diagnostic checkout

`/en/checkout` renvoie 404 par design : la route est `/[locale]/checkout/[photoId]/page.tsx`. Sans `photoId` dans l'URL, Next.js ne trouve pas de segment et retourne 404. C'est le comportement attendu -- le checkout ne s'ouvre que depuis un bouton avec l'ID réel de la photo (voir `BuyButton` -> `/${locale}/checkout/${photo.id}`). Aucun bug : ne pas créer de route catch-all ici.

## Test

1. Ouvrir une page photo sur mobile (< 1024 px)

body:
## Summary

The flagship feature: `openclippy triage` reads the inbox, classifies each email against **user-defined natural-language rules**, and proposes actions (move / forward to a group mailbox address / reply / flag / prioritize) that the user approves, rejects, or corrects — and the corrections **improve the rules over time**.

Implemented in the cloud (Ultraplan) from the approved plan, then reviewed, tested, and published locally.

## What's included (5 commits ≈ plan passes 0–4)

- `649d4d0` **Rule schema, rules file, decision store** — zod-validated rules in human-editable `~/.openclippy/triage/rules.yaml` (atomic tmp+rename saves guarded by a load-time sha256; `.bak` backups); append-only decision log + rule audit trail in a separate `~/.openclippy/triage.db` (SQLite, MemoryStore pattern)
- `1c72360` **New mail tools** — `mail_categorize`, `mail_categories`, `mail_folder_create`, `mail_prioritize` (verb-last, profile-safe)
- `d539356` **Classification pipeline, review loop, Graph executor** — the classify agent run is *structurally read-only*: its tool set is exactly `[mail_read, triage_record]` (a per-run collector closure), so the LLM cannot act; the approval gate is deterministic code outside `runAgent`
- `b2db1e6` **Triage CLI + learning loop** — per-email `[a/r/c/s/A/q]` review; corrections execute the user's choice and log the signal; immediate one-rule micro-edits shown as diffs; `triage refine` clusters corrections into edit/new/retire/merge proposals (each a human-approved diff with decision-ID evidence); rule lifecycle `proposed → active → trusted` with one-strike demotion
- `fa71704` **Cold start + chat integration** — `triage init` (folder bootstrap + interview); rules injected into `ask`/`chat` via `contextHints`

## Safety properties (verified in review)

- Classify step cannot execute actions (tool-set restriction, not a prompt promise)
- `autoAct` defaults to **false**; even when enabled, only `trusted` + high-confidence rules auto-execute, and `reply_draft` stays approval-gated permanently (drafts displayed before any send)
- Every rule mutation is a human-approved diff; full audit in `rule_events`
- No full email bodies persisted — metadata + capped snippets only

## Testing

- **898/898 tests pass across 58 files** (104 new tests, zero regressions from the 794 baseline)
- New suites: rules-file, store, classify, executor, review, refine, lifecycle, init, tools + a 415-line end-to-end integration test (`tests/integration/triage-flow.test.ts`)
- Build clean (`pnpm build`)

## Follow-ups (deferred by design)

- Pass 5: real-time triage via gateway webhook (needs `SubscriptionManager` wiring + public notification URL)
- Live smoke test against a real mailbox before merge is recommended: `openclippy triage --limit 5 --dry-run`

body: ## Summary - New Next.js (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind) app in `frontend/` implementing KAN-5: a Mutual NDA creator. - User fills in a form (both parties' signatory/company/notice info, purpose, effective date, MNDA term, confidentiality term, governing law, jurisdiction, optional modifications). - A Server Action reads `templates/Mutual-NDA-coverpage.md` and `templates/Mutual-NDA.md` (the KAN-4 dataset) and substitutes the submitted values into both documents — every `Label` cross-reference in the Standard Terms is resolved generically from the cover page field values. - The filled document is rendered as Markdown (`react-markdown` + `remark-gfm` + Tailwind Typography) with an "Edit details" button to go back to the form. - "Download PDF" uses print-optimized CSS and the browser's native print-to-PDF flow — no extra document-generation dependency. ## Notes / limitations - This reuses the `templates/` directory at the repo root as the single source of truth (read via `fs` from the Next.js server, relative to `frontend/`'s `process.cwd()`), rather than duplicating the Common Paper template content. - Straight text substitution occasionally produces slightly awkward grammar (e.g. "commences on the July 15, 2026") since the source template's variables were designed for a defined-term reference, not always a literal drop-in value. body:
## Summary

- Reverts #780, which retargeted the Konflux push pipelines' `update-deploy-tag` finally task from `hp-fleet-gitops` (GitHub) to `fleet-apps` (GitLab). That was correct on 2026-06-30 (ArgoCD read fleet-apps then), but [hp-gitops-tenants PR #9](https://github.com/openshift-online/hp-gitops-tenants/pull/9) (2026-07-01) repointed ArgoCD's `kartograph-stage` source at `hp-fleet-gitops` instead, so deploy-tag needs to go there again.
- Confirmed needed: both `kartograph-api-on-push` and `kartograph-dev-ui-on-push` failed at `update-deploy-tag` on the first push to `main` after merging #782 (commit `c5d8800`), because the task was still trying (and failing) to push to the GitLab `fleet-apps` repo.
- Restores the pre-#780 mechanism: plain `git push` + a separate `curl`-based `create-pull-request` task that opens the PR against `hp-fleet-gitops` via the GitHub REST API (using the same `.netrc` staged for git auth) and enables auto-merge, since GitHub has no equivalent to GitLab's `git push -o merge_request.*` push options.

## Requires

- The `kartograph-hp-fleet-gitops-auth` secret (GitHub PAT with `repo` + `pull_request` scope on `openshift-online/hp-fleet-gitops`) must exist in the `kartograph-tenant` Konflux namespace — same requirement as before #780, when this last worked. If it's missing or the PAT is stale/under-scoped, `update-deploy-tag` will fail again (previously seen as a 403 on push).

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -c "import yaml; ..."` syntax-validated all 4 modified `.tekton/*-push.yaml` files
- [ ] Merge and confirm the next `on-push` build's `update-deploy-tag` task succeeds and opens a PR against `hp-fleet-gitops`

author: junutala
body:
Owner request: an attendant should start the moment **his own** nozzle readings are recorded — not after every operator is assigned.

Finding: the backend already activates each operator on `/shifts/:id/assign` (POS finds them via `/shifts/active`); there was never an "all operators" gate in the API. The friction was purely the shift-start UI.

Change (frontend only):
- Bottom CTA relabelled **"Start shift"** (was "Start — Shift is live ✓").
- Enabled as soon as **one** operator is added **or** the add-form holds a picked operator with a ticked nozzle.
- On click, if the form has an un-added operator, it assigns him first (he goes live immediately), then goes to the dashboard — so one operator's readings are enough to start.
- `addOperator` now returns success/failure so the combined start can gate on it.

## Impact analysis
- **Schema:** none. Frontend-only; uses existing `/assign` endpoint.
- **Consumes:** shift-start page only.
- **Blast radius:** low; still requires an operator + nozzle before it activates. "Add operator" for multiple operators is unchanged.
- **Money/masking/multi-tenant:** unchanged.
- **Rollback:** revert.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #178.

- add `scopes_used` to `EvidenceAuditEvent`, defaulting legacy deserialization to an empty list
- populate request audit events from `EvidencePrincipal.scopes`
- emit empty scope lists for background, federation, and public/pre-auth audit events
- extend Notary audit tests for OIDC and self-attestation request paths

## Security-sensitive review notes

This changes the Notary audit record schema and audit envelope contents for REQ-SEC-G-008. The new field records scope names only, not raw bearer tokens, API keys, principal IDs, civil identifiers, or claim values. Existing privacy assertions continue to verify that raw tokens, subject identifiers, and principal IDs are not emitted in the covered audit records. Legacy audit events without `scopes_used` remain deserializable via `#[serde(default)]`.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt`

author: benbirt
body:
Second round of playtest fixes (the first round shipped in #2). Merging to `main` redeploys to Pages.

## Sound still not working
The engine plays fine on desktop, so the failure is mobile-specific. Made the unlock bulletproof: resume the AudioContext on every early gesture (not once) and on tab refocus, and open the iOS media channel with a silent `playsinline` element so Web Audio plays even with the ringer switch on silent (the usual "no sound on iPhone" cause). Added an always-visible speaker toggle in the HUD for feedback + manual control.

## Long loading screens
The initial download was 13 MB of models (the villagers were 2.3 MB each). Quantized every character mesh (KHR_mesh_quantization, decoded natively by three.js — no runtime decoder) and stripped villager animations to idle/walk → **13 MB → 6 MB**. Skins and combat animations verified intact; knight and skeletons render/animate correctly.

## World needs height / ramps / waterfalls / detail
Added a backward-compatible terrain elevation system: an optional per-cell `heights` grid, walkable `ramps` whose slope the player's Y follows, cliff faces (retaining vs scenery), and `waterfalls`. Plus automatic decorative detail scatter (flowers / mushrooms / pebbles) on open grass. The overworld's Bramble Crypt now sits on a raised wooded highland reached by a ramp, with a waterfall into the lake.

## Verification
- Map validator passes; overworld reachability re-checked (crypt gated behind the ramp only; all warps / NPCs / eye-gate reachable).

author: stevebeattie
body:
This PR applies GitHub Actions hardening fixes across the workflows in
`.github/workflows/`, surfaced by static analysis (zizmor).

## What this changes

- **`persist-credentials: false` on checkout steps.** The affected jobs don't
  push back to the repo, so the auto-persisted `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `.git/config`
  is unnecessary — dropping it narrows the blast radius of later steps.
- **Template-injection fix.** `workflow_dispatch` input expressions that were
  interpolated directly into `run:` blocks are moved into `env:` and referenced
  as quoted shell variables, so the shell — not the workflow templater — handles
  them.
- **Repo-level zizmor config.** Disables cosmetic pedantic-only rules and sets a
  dependabot cooldown threshold, so future scans stay focused on substantive
  findings.

## Test plan

- `zizmor .github/` — clean after these changes.
- `actionlint` — workflows still parse with no errors.

Refs: PSEC-923

author: mefenemer
body:
Automated fix for reported issue #55.

**Location:** review-queue

**Reported description:**
In My Content, I can delete an image or video ok however it should notify me if this is included in a draft or scheduled post.  If this is deleted from a schedule post, it should be flagged in the Review Queue that the image was deleted and ask if the Assistant should source another?

**AI summary:**
All expected files are touched consistently. The fix is complete.

**Root cause:** In "My Content" (`content-assets.ts`), deleting an image/video is a hard `DELETE` from `content_assets` with no check for whether it's attached to a draft/scheduled post. Posts reference media via `scheduled_posts.content_asset_ids`, a plain jsonb array with no foreign key, and functions that attach media to a draft/scheduled post (`attach-draft-media.ts`, `regenerate-post-media.ts`) never flip the asset's own `status` to `'scheduled'` — so an in-use asset can still show the plain, unguarded "Delete" button in My Content (only assets with `status === 'scheduled'` get the safer "Remove from Post" flow). Deleting it silently orphaned the reference: the Review Queue just fell back to "No media attached" with zero notification.

**Changes:**
- `db/schema.ts` + `db/scheduled-posts-media-missing.sql` — new `scheduled_posts.media_missing` / `media_missing_note` columns to flag a post whose media was deleted (SQL pending manual apply).
- `netlify/functions/content-assets.ts` — added `findActivePostsByAsset()` to look up active drafts/scheduled posts referencing an asset (by scanning `content_asset_ids`). GET now returns `usedInPosts` per asset; DELETE now flags any affected posts (`mediaMissing`/`mediaMissingNote`) before deleting and returns `affectedPosts` in the response.
- `netlify/functions/get-social-drafts.ts` — select the new columns so the Review Queue receives them.
- `netlify/functions/attach-draft-media.ts` / `regenerate-post-media.ts` — clear the flag when new media is swapped in (issue resolved).
- `my-content.html` / `my-content.js` — delete-confirmation modal now warns if the asset is used in active posts, and shows a toast after deletion naming how many posts were flagged.
- `workspace.html` — Review Queue card list shows a "⚠ Media deleted" badge; the post-review modal shows a banner with a "Source new media" button (reuses the existing own/stock/AI media picker) when `mediaMissing` is set.

- Keep the existing subnet-ceiling inheritance behavior for `official` surfaces so maintainer-reviewed flows remain unchanged. 
- Add/adjust unit coverage in `tests/lib-helpers.test.mjs` to assert a community-submitted surface on a maintainer-reviewed subnet remains `candidate-discovered` with `last_verified_at: null` while an officially-verified surface still inherits `maintainer-reviewed`.
