body: ## Summary Fixes tracker item content rendering as raw JSON after closing and reopening an item in the Trackers panel. `updateTrackerItemContent` persists the item's rich-text body as `JSON.stringify(markdown)` in the `content` column. Two read paths returned that column value as-is instead of decoding it: `rowToTrackerItem` (used by `trackerToolHandlers.ts`, the MCP tool surface the AI agent uses) and `ElectronDocumentService.getTrackerItemContent` (used by `TrackerItemDetail.tsx` in the renderer). As a result, a tracker item's body rendered correctly right after creation, but showed literal quotes and escaped `\n` sequences instead of formatted markdown once the item was closed and reopened (fresh DB read). The fix decodes the JSON-encoded value on read in both places, falling back to the raw string when it isn't valid JSON (legacy/plain rows written before this encoding was introduced). ### Before ### After ## Related issue None filed — found while working in the Trackers panel. ## Testing - Added unit tests covering: JSON-encoded content decodes back to plain markdown, non-JSON content passes through unchanged, and null content stays undefined/null. - `npm run test:unit` passes for the touched files. ## Notes for reviewers Two call sites needed the same fix (`trackerToolHandlers.ts` and `ElectronDocumentService.ts`) since they read the same column independently — happy to consolidate into a shared helper if maintainers prefer not to duplicate the decode logic.

body:
## Summary

Release **v1.0.1** (patch) to npm. Merges `develop` into `main` with critical bug fixes shipped after v1.0.0.

After merge, push the tag to trigger CI:

```bash

git push origin v1.0.1
```

author: wrburgess
body:
## Summary

PR3 of the #103 sequence — **Work item 2: asset-delivery contract** (HC-ratified Option A: alias-only + cleanup). This corrects the engine's asset contract so a consuming app on the standard MPI pipeline (Propshaft + esbuild + dart-sass) can actually load the engine's JS and SCSS, and stops forcing an unused runtime dependency on every consumer.

Linked as **Part of #103** only — no closing keyword. The umbrella is finished by PR4 (README rewrite + `v0.2.0` tag), which is gated on #111 landing first.

## Changes Made

- **`lib/mpi_design_system/engine.rb`** — removed the dead `config.assets.paths` initializer. esbuild and the dart-sass CLI don't read `config.assets.paths`, so it delivered no component JS/CSS to any consumer and only implied assets "just work" once mounted. Replaced with a comment documenting why there is no initializer.
- **`mpi_design_system.gemspec`** — dropped the `bootstrap ~> 5.3` runtime dependency. Runtime set is now `{rails, view_component, stimulus-rails}`.
- **`Gemfile`** — removed the now-orphaned `gem "bootstrap", "~> 5"` (see "For the reviewer" below).
- **`app/assets/stylesheets/mpi_design_system/_tokens_values.scss`** (new) — dependency-free values module; every variable is `!default`.
- **`app/assets/stylesheets/mpi_design_system/_tokens.scss`** — now `@import`s the values module and layers the Bootstrap variable overrides on top (legacy `@import` output is byte-identical).
- **`AGENTS.md`** — documented the real install contract (Gemfile + esbuild alias + sass `--load-path` + `registerMpiControllers`, and both token entry points).
- **`package.json` + `spec/fixtures/scss/*` + `.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — new `build:css:compat` script + fixtures, wired into the CI `js-build` job.
- **`spec/packaging/engine_spec.rb`, `spec/packaging/gemspec_spec.rb`** (new) — Ruby guards for the contract.

## Technical Approach

- **Why remove, not scope, the initializer:** the engine images dir is empty and no template references an engine image; Rails' built-in `Rails::Engine` `append_assets_path` still contributes `app/assets/*` as static Propshaft paths (standard + harmless). The only *misleading* addition was `app/javascript` (JS source is esbuild-bundled, never Propshaft-served) — now correctly absent.
- **Why the values-module split:** `_tokens.scss` mixed raw MPI values with Bootstrap `$var` reassignments, which only work in the legacy pre-Bootstrap-`@import` position. Extracting a `!default` values module lets a modern `@use`-based app adopt the palette — and override it via `@use … with ()` — without double-compiling Bootstrap against its own `bootstrap@5.3.x`. `_tokens.scss` keeps the legacy path byte-compatible.

## Testing

- **`spec/packaging/engine_spec.rb`** — asserts no `mpi_design_system.assets` initializer exists and `app/javascript` is not on the asset path (fails if the initializer is re-added).
- **`spec/packaging/gemspec_spec.rb`** — asserts runtime deps are exactly `{rails, view_component, stimulus-rails}` and Bootstrap is absent (fails if a runtime dep creeps back).
- **`yarn build:css:compat`** (CI `js-build` job) — compiles three consumer models and asserts the expected primary color reaches the compiled CSS:
  - legacy `@import "mpi_design_system/tokens"` → `#2e75b6` (proves the split didn't change values)
  - modern `@use "mpi_design_system/tokens_values"` → `#2e75b6` (proves the palette feeds Bootstrap with no double-compile)
  - `@use … with ($mpi-primary: #0A5C2E)` → `#0a5c2e` (a `with ()` override of a non-`!default` var is a hard Sass error, so a clean compile proves the flags; the color proves the override wins)
- `bundle exec rubocop -a` → **0 offenses**. `bundle exec rspec` → **513 examples, 0 failures**.

## For the reviewer

- **Gemfile bootstrap removal is slightly beyond the literal "drop the gemspec dep" decision.** I removed `gem "bootstrap"` from the Gemfile too because it was unused (nothing Ruby-side loads it; CSS compiles against npm `bootstrap`), and leaving it would keep pulling an unused gem into the dev bundle. The bundle re-resolves cleanly (111 gems) and the full suite passes without it. Revert this one line if you'd rather keep it.
- **`@import` remains in the engine's own SCSS.** Migrating the engine off deprecated `@import` is out of scope; the values module gives modern apps the `@use` path without forcing that migration now.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass (`bundle exec rspec` — 513/0)
- [x] Linting passes (`bundle exec rubocop -a` — 0 offenses)
- [x] SCSS compat matrix (legacy `@import` + modern `@use` + `with()` override) green
- [x] `Part of #103` — not a closing reference (PR4 finishes the umbrella)

— Claude Code (Fable 5)

author: bsodium
body:
## The bug

`BootReceiver`'s KDoc claimed the mutable AI alarm was "intentionally NOT re-armed here — the next sensor event will trigger a fresh AI replan, which will re-arm it naturally." That assumption was broken: **nothing restarts `SleepSessionService` after a reboot.** The service hosts `ScreenStateMonitor` and `ActivityRecognitionMonitor` — the source of every sensor event that could trigger a replan — and neither `BootReceiver` nor anything else started it until the *next* evening plan trigger.

So after a mid-session reboot (e.g. 3 a.m.), there was no sensor monitoring, no sleep/wake detection, and no re-arm path: the user silently woke at the hard-latest safety floor with no attempt at the AI-planned wake time.

## The fix

When an active (non-Complete) session exists at boot:

1. **Restart sensing** — `context.startService(SleepSessionService.startIntent(context))`. This is a plain start intent (no `ACTION_EVENING_PLAN`), so `onStartCommand` only reconstructs the monitors; it never re-bootstraps a session or re-runs the evening-plan flow.
2. **Re-arm the planned alarm** — decode the session's persisted `currentInstruction`; a non-null `alarmTime` (SetAlarm sets it, DoNothing carries it forward, CancelAlarm clears it) is re-armed via `AlarmScheduler.schedule(...)`, gated on the target still being in the future. A null `alarmTime` keeps hard-latest-only behavior, matching the pre-fix semantics.

The existing hard-latest re-arm and evening-plan trigger re-arm are unchanged; the class KDoc now documents the corrected behavior.

## goAsync() budget

The added work is one Room row read (already there), one `startService` call, one small JSON decode, and one `AlarmManager.setAlarmClock` — all synchronous, non-blocking, and well within the ~10s `goAsync()` window. No network, no long-running work.

## Tests

New `BootReceiverTest` (Robolectric, production DB singleton wiped per test):
- active session + non-null `alarmTime` → hard-latest AND planned alarm armed, service started with a plain (action-less) intent
- active session + null `alarmTime` → hard-latest only, service still started
- Complete session / no session → nothing armed, service not started

`assembleDebug`, `lintDebug`, `checkFileLength`, `checkAnimationPreviews`, and the full `testDebugUnitTest` suite all pass.

author: jupiterv2
body:
## Problem

`convert()` aligns the balance store before applying each checkpoint:

```go
Align(ctx, ck.GetSequenceNumber()-1)
```

`GetSequenceNumber()` is `uint64`. For the **genesis checkpoint 0**, `0 - 1` underflows to `MaxUint64`, and `Align` treats that as a rebuild target:

- empty store → `!has` → `from = 0` → `rebuild(0, MaxUint64)`
- non-empty store → `current < MaxUint64` always holds → `rebuild(current+1, MaxUint64)`

Either way `rebuild` runs `pager.Walk(from, MaxUint64, ...)`, stepping ~5000 checkpoints at a time up to `MaxUint64` — an effectively infinite loop / hang.

This currently doesn't trigger in production because the balance store is enabled mid-chain (`enable = storePath != ""`), so the first enabled `Align` happens at a high checkpoint rather than 0. It's a latent landmine for any deployment that starts from genesis with the balance store enabled.

## Fix

Genesis has no predecessor to align to. Add `balanceController.ResetToGenesis`, which empties the store via `delAll` (that also drops the `current` cursor, so `getCurrent` reports `has=false`), and call it instead of `Align` when the sequence number is 0.

Besides avoiding the underflow, this preserves the retry-rollback contract: a failed `convert(0)` retry re-applies checkpoint 0 from a clean empty base rather than double-applying partial writes.

## Notes

- `bazel build //chain/sui/chv4:chv4` passes.
- Follow-up to the chv4 balance reorg review; separate from #362 (the reorg reload `<=` fix).

author: sidorovanthon
body:
## What

Rewrites merge-when-green **Step 1a** (added in #429): the base-freshness check now uses `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main <PR-head>` instead of `gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus` → `BEHIND`.

## Why

Live verification during the very next merges (#431/#430) showed `BEHIND` never fires on this repo: GitHub only reports it when server-side "require branches to be up to date" protection is enabled, which Phase 0 defers (GitHub Free + private, ADR-0008 §2.6). A stale branch here reads `CLEAN`/`UNSTABLE`, making the rule as written a no-op. The ancestry check is the signal that actually works (and is what was applied by hand to merge #431/#430).

Closes #432

## Notes

- docs-only; no runtime code, no UI (registry-research N/A).
- Pre-commit hook skipped (`--no-verify`): fresh worktree without `node_modules`, per the repo-conventions escape hatch for docs/config-only branches; CI re-runs lint/format.

author: jsonbored
body:
### Motivation

- A Postgres backup path passed the full database URL (which can include the password) to `pg_dump`, exposing credentials via process argv; this change prevents that leak while keeping backup functionality.
- The goal was to preserve the existing Postgres and SQLite backup behaviors but avoid placing secret data in command-line arguments.

### Description

- Parse the configured Postgres URL in `scripts/backup.sh` and export libpq connection pieces (`PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGDATABASE`, `PGUSER`) instead of passing the full URL on `pg_dump` argv. 
- When a password is present, create a temporary, 600-permission `PGPASSFILE`, populate it with an escaped entry, export `PGPASSFILE`, and register a `trap` to securely remove the file on exit. 
- Replace the vulnerable `pg_dump ... "$PG_DB"` invocation with `prepare_pg_env` + `pg_dump -Fc -f ...` so `pg_dump` runs with env-based credentials only. 
- Add a regression unit test `test/unit/selfhost-backup-script.test.ts` that fakes `pg_dump`, captures its argv/env, and asserts that neither the Postgres URL nor the password appear in process arguments while existing Postgres and SQLite backup behavior remains unchanged. 
- Modified files: `scripts/backup.sh` and `test/unit/selfhost-backup-script.test.ts`.

### Testing

- `sh -n scripts/backup.sh` returned successfully with no syntax errors. 
- Targeted unit tests were run with `npx vitest run test/unit/selfhost-backup-script.test.ts` and passed (3 tests), including the new regression that verifies credentials are not passed on `pg_dump` argv. 
- `git diff --check` passed locally. 
- Full local gate `npm run test:ci` could not complete in this environment due to network/actionlint setup issues (WASM fallback reported the repo's custom self-hosted runner label), and `npm audit --audit-level=moderate` returned `403 Forbidden` from the npm audit endpoint.

author: yeendj
body:
## Resumen

Este PR lleva a `main` la **primera versión completa de la plataforma Vuelo Carmesí**: portal web para experiencias agroecológicas con sabor a cacao (Colombia). Incluye el **sitio público** (landing, catálogo de experiencias con reservas y tienda con flujo de compra completo), el **panel de administración** protegido, y el **backend REST** con base de datos, notificaciones por email/Telegram, subida de imágenes y configuración dinámica del sitio.

**Alcance:** 138 commits desde el commit inicial · monorepo `front/` + `back/` con npm workspaces.

---

## 🏗️ Arquitectura

| Capa | Tecnología |
|------|-----------|
| Frontend | Next.js 14+ (App Router) · TypeScript · CSS custom properties con tokens de marca |
| Backend | NestJS · Prisma v7 (adaptador PG) · REST API con ValidationPipe global y CORS |
| Base de datos | PostgreSQL — modelos: `Experiencia`, `Reserva`, `Producto`, `Pedido` (+items), `Contacto`, `SiteConfig` |
| Servicios externos | Resend (email) · Telegram Bot (alertas al negocio) · Cloudinary (imágenes) |
| Testing | Vitest (front) · Jest (back) — tests de store, schemas, DTOs, servicios y controllers |

---

## 🌐 Sitio público

### Landing y marca
- Landing completa: **Hero con imagen dinámica** (administrable desde el panel), preview de experiencias destacadas **consumiendo la API real**, sección Sobre Nosotros, galería y **formulario de contacto** conectado al backend.
- Identidad visual implementada con **design tokens** (`tokens.css`): paleta carmesí/naranja/ámbar y tipografías de marca (Honey Lips para títulos, Bellota para cuerpo).
- Navbar con logo de marca y **badge de carrito en vivo**; Footer rediseñado con datos reales y redes sociales.

### Experiencias y reservas
- Catálogo de experiencias y **página de detalle** con hero, layout de 2 columnas y sidebar sticky.
- **Flujo de reserva completo**: formulario rediseñado con validación → confirmación → **notificación automática por email al cliente y Telegram al negocio**.
- Cambios de estado de reserva (confirmada/cancelada) disparan **emails HTML transaccionales** al cliente, con motivo de cancelación y escape de HTML en campos dinámicos.

### Tienda y flujo de compra
- Catálogo con **filtro de categorías dinámico** y badges **Nuevo / Destacado / Agotado** en las cards.
- Detalle de producto con **galería de imágenes, selector de cantidad, subtotal en vivo** y productos relacionados.
- **Carrito** con persistencia en `localStorage` (store compartido con tests), controles +/−, quitar y vaciar.
- **Checkout** validado con react-hook-form + zod (datos de contacto: teléfono, ciudad, código postal) → **pantalla de confirmación con número de pedido real**, persistente tras recargar.
- Indicador de pasos (carrito → checkout → confirmación) y toasts de feedback.
- Precios formateados en **COP (es-CO)** con helper compartido.

---

## 🔐 Panel de administración (`/admin`)

- **Autenticación por cookie** con guard de layout, página de login y logout seguro; route group `(protected)` para aislar las rutas.
- **Overview**: StatCards, gráfica de reservas y actividad reciente.
- **Reservas**: tabla con filtros (incluye **filtro por mes o rango de fechas**), cambio de estado con **modal de cancelación con motivo**, y drawer de detalle.
- **Pedidos**: tabla con filtros y drawer con **datos de contacto del cliente** (teléfono, ciudad, CP); actualización de estado vía PATCH.
- **Productos**: CRUD completo con modal, **edición de stock inline con alertas**, asignación de **badge Nuevo/Destacado** y filtro de categorías con datos reales.
- **Experiencias**: CRUD con toggle de destacada, archivado y **eliminación definitiva con modal de confirmación**.
- **Configuración del sitio**: página de config con **editor de recorte de imágenes** para Hero y Sobre Nosotros, persistido en `SiteConfig`.
- Componentes reutilizables: `ConfirmModal` (con manejo de estados async y errores), `ImageUploader` con preview y upload a Cloudinary, `StatusBadge`, `Toggle`, `StatCard`.

---

## ⚙️ Backend (NestJS + Prisma)

- **Módulos REST**: `experiencias`, `reservas`, `productos`, `pedidos`, `contacto`, `site-config`, `uploads`, `notificaciones`.
- **Validación exhaustiva con DTOs** (whitelist), incluyendo transiciones de estado de reserva, badge de producto y datos de contacto del pedido.
- **NotificacionesModule**: EmailService (Resend) + TelegramService, con envío **fire-and-forget** al crear reservas y pedidos (no bloquea la respuesta al cliente); templates HTML con escape de contenido dinámico.
- **UploadsModule**: `POST /uploads/image` con Cloudinary, protegido por **AdminGuard** junto con los endpoints de configuración.
- **Pedidos**: creación con items y validación de stock (protección contra race conditions); la actualización de estado devuelve el pedido con **items → producto** incluidos para el detalle en notificaciones.
- **Ordenamiento por destacada** y query `?destacadas=true` para la landing.
- **Cache invalidation on-demand**: cache tags en los fetches del front + Server Actions con `revalidateTag` disparadas desde el admin — los cambios se reflejan en el sitio público sin redeploy.

---

## 📄 Documentación y proceso

- `docs/specs/` y `docs/plans/`: cada feature mayor tiene **design spec aprobado y plan de implementación** (flujo de compra, notificaciones, cache invalidation, operación sin fricción, páginas de detalle, eliminaciones con modal).
- `handoff/`: handoffs de diseño del sitio público, panel admin y flujo de compra (HTML navegable, fuentes y screenshots).
- README con estructura, stack, setup e instrucciones de desarrollo.

## ✅ Testing

- **Back**: tests unitarios de servicios, controllers y DTOs (validación de argumentos, transiciones de estado, formato de dirección).
- **Front**: Vitest configurado; tests del store de carrito (persistencia, operaciones) y del schema de checkout.

---

## ⚠️ Notas de despliegue

1. **Migraciones de Prisma**: correr `prisma migrate deploy` contra la base de producción antes de levantar el back.
2. **Variables de entorno requeridas**:
   - Back: `DATABASE_URL`, credenciales de **Resend**, **Telegram Bot** y **Cloudinary**, y configuración de CORS con credentials.
   - Front: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.
3. **Licencia de fuente**: *Honey Lips* es "Personal Use" — verificar licencia comercial antes del lanzamiento público.
4. Fuera de scope de esta versión: pasarela de pago real, autenticación de usuarios finales e internacionalización.

body:
Stacked on #9. Dresses the logomark up for a season — like the app's Christmas hat — via a **`holiday` prop on `Logo.Logomark`** (no separate `Logo.Holidays.*` compound).

```tsx
import { Logo } from "@posthog/brand/logo"

<Logo.Logomark holiday="christmas" />              // 🎅
<Logo.Logomark holiday="halloween" />              // 🧙
<Logo.Logomark holiday="christmas" jumpOnClick />  // the hat jumps with the head
```

![Christmas and Halloween logomarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/brand/139b757779061a3b1dbd5738562367f945acdf82/holiday-marks.png)

The accessory is injected **inside the head part group** from #9, so it rides the head when the mark jumps:

![Jumping Christmas logomark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/brand/9898deae61cb1af5210b9535abb5ba2e29359ffc/holiday-jump.gif)

## What's in it

- **Christmas** — the Santa hat ported from the app (`frontend/src/lib/brand/Logomark.tsx`), re-fitted to this repo's head geometry, in the brand palette.
- **Halloween** — the app has no Halloween logo treatment, so this adds a hand-drawn witch hat (`purple.darker` cone/brim, `tangerine` band, yellow buckle), seated on the head's crown with a gentle tilt so it sits on the head rather than floating.
- Accessories keep their festive colors in every variant, including `mono` — the mark inherits `currentColor`, the hat stays festive.
- **Deliberately not date-driven** — the consumer decides when it's the season, as the app does with its holiday helpers + feature flags.
- Holiday section on the site's Logo page, tests, changeset (minor).

## API surface

- `holiday?: "christmas" | "halloween"` on `Logo.Logomark` (via `LogomarkProps`) — composes with `jumpOnClick` / `autoJumpMs`
- `LogoHoliday` type exported for typing the value

author: jsonbored
body:
### Motivation
- The per-PR regate path could unconditionally upsert a fetched live non-open PR payload and return, allowing a stale closed response to overwrite a concurrently-reopened stored row and cause a live-open PR to be skipped by future sweeps.

### Description
- Add a freshness guard in `reReviewStoredPullRequest` that re-reads the stored PR and only calls `upsertPullRequestFromGitHub` for a live non-open payload if the stored row is still `open` and its `updatedAt` matches the job's snapshot.
- This prevents a stale terminal upsert from winning a race against a concurrent reopen webhook while preserving the early-exit semantics for genuinely terminal PRs.
- Add a regression unit test that simulates a concurrent reopen webhook while the regate fetch returns a stale closed payload and asserts the stored PR remains open with the reopened head.
- Files changed: `src/queue/processors.ts`, `test/unit/queue.test.ts`.

### Testing
- Ran `npx vitest run test/unit/queue.test.ts -t "regate-terminal-exit"` and the targeted unit tests passed.
- Ran `npm run typecheck` and `git diff --check`, both succeeded.
- Ran `npm run test:coverage` with coverage enabled and the global coverage thresholds for the whole repo failed (expected given the focused unit change and repo-wide thresholds), so full coverage gate remains unsharded and must be green before pushing.

author: jiyunson
body:
Hey Randall -- just a tiny edit! Thanks as always for all your awesome work on mosaic/ggformula/etc.

## Summary

When `lm.args = list(formula = y ~ poly(x, 2))` is passed to `gf_lm()` or `stat_lm()`, the call to `do.call(stats::lm, c(base.args, lm.args))` fails with:

> formal argument "formula" matched by multiple actual arguments

because `base.args` already contains `formula = y ~ x` (the default), and `lm.args` adds a second `formula` key.

The fix is one line: drop `base.args$formula` before merging when `lm.args` already provides its own formula, so the user-supplied formula wins cleanly.

## Reproduction

```r
library(ggformula)
data(KidsFeet, package = "mosaicData")

# Before fix: error "matched by multiple actual arguments"
# After fix: draws a quadratic fit
gf_point(length ~ width, data = KidsFeet) |>
  gf_lm(lm.args = list(formula = y ~ poly(x, 2)))
```

Note: the `formula = y ~ poly(x, 2)` direct-param syntax already works; this fixes the `lm.args` path to be consistent.

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify `lm.args = list(formula = ...)` no longer errors
- [ ] Verify `lm.args = list(formula = ...)` produces the same fit as `formula = ...` directly
- [ ] Verify default behavior (`lm.args = list()`) is unchanged

## Summary

Adds an in-browser end-to-end test suite (Playwright, Chromium) covering the app's core user flows, plus CI wiring. Independent of the unit tests — nothing about the existing Vitest setup changes.

## What's covered (11 specs)
- **daily-action** — mark a day complete/failed, toggle-off to clear, save a note + calendar note indicator
- **calendar** — today highlight, completed-day color, future-day guard, month navigation
- **stats** — current streak across consecutive days, streak-break + success-rate math
- **habits** — create / switch / delete (handling the `confirm` dialog), per-habit data isolation, last-habit delete guard, custom labels
- **persistence** — state survives a page reload

## How it works
- `playwright.config.ts` starts the app via the Vite **dev** server (the PWA service worker is off in dev, so there's no cache to make tests flaky) on a strict port; Chromium at a phone viewport (390×844).
- A **frozen clock** (fixed "today") makes calendar layout and streak assertions deterministic across runs.
- Each test gets a fresh browser context → clean `localStorage`; a small init script suppresses the first-run onboarding toast.

## Test-runner separation
- Unit tests stay `src/**/*.test.ts` (Vitest); e2e are `e2e/**/*.spec.ts` (Playwright).
- Vitest is pinned via `test.include: ['src/**/*.test.ts']` so it never runs the e2e specs. `npm run test` is unchanged.

## CI
- New **independent** `e2e` job in `build-and-deploy.yaml` (PR + push to main): `npm ci` → `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` → `npm run e2e`, uploading the HTML report artifact. Does not gate the Pages deploy.

## App change
- One non-behavioral tweak: a `data-date` attribute on Calendar day cells so date selection is selectable from tests.

`npm run e2e`, `npm run e2e:ui`, `npm run e2e:report`.

- e2e: **16 passed** (Chromium, headless, ~2.4s)
- unit: **131 passed (18 files)** — unchanged, confirming runner isolation

author: rbbtsn0w
body:
## Summary

Adds OpenTelemetry attributes to the CLI's existing single process span (`gh-address-cr.cli`) so that AI-agent invocations of `gh-address-cr` are observable — without adding any new public CLI flag, changing exit codes, or touching the packaged skill's runtime behavior.

- **Execution forensics**: `process.executable.name/pid/exit.code`, plus a new `safe_command_args` full-argv redactor (previously only a single-label reducer existed). `error.type` is set **only on a genuine crash** (propagated exception), never on the CLI's normal non-zero *status* exit codes (e.g. `WAITING_FOR_EXTERNAL_REVIEW`) — avoids inflating observed failure rates.
- **Agent-session correlation**: `gen_ai.conversation.id` groups every CLI invocation from one agent session. `GH_ADDRESS_CR_CONVERSATION_ID` is the designed, vendor-neutral entry point (any agent can set it, zero new code per vendor); `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is a free, zero-config passive fallback. Guidance is surfaced through two independent channels so no agent misses it regardless of invocation path: `skill/SKILL.md` (for agents that load the skill) and `--help` (for agents that invoke the CLI binary directly).
- **GenAI tool vocabulary**: `gen_ai.operation.name=execute_tool`, `gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` (reuses the same sanitized argv, no second unsanitized copy).
- **VCS GitHub-PR mapping**: `vcs.change.id` (PR#) + `vcs.provider.name` in plain text; `vcs.repository.name` is a one-way hash of `owner/repo` — the plain owner/repo is also redacted from `process.command_args`/`gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` for PR-scoped runs, so no private repository identity ever leaves the process.
- **Fail-open throughout**: every context/session/VCS lookup degrades to "attribute absent" on missing or malformed input; telemetry never changes the CLI's exit code or behavior. Three candidate strategies for auto-generating a fallback session id when none is provided were evaluated and rejected on evidence (documented in `research.md` R-012), including a live cross-agent test that caught a `ppid`-derived id silently merging two unrelated Codex conversations.

Deferred (documented, not built): a `--traceparent` override flag and full `gen_ai.tool.call.result` capture — both would grow the public CLI contract or require CLI-internal result plumbing beyond this feature's scope.

author: moomindani
body:
Fixes a `TypeError` in `DatabricksSqlHook.run()` when a scalar handler is used and the query returns no rows.

DBAPI `fetchone()` returns `None` on an empty result set, and common.sql's `fetch_one_handler` is typed `-> tuple | None` accordingly (it also returns `None` for statements where `cursor.description` is `None`). The base `DbApiHook._make_common_data_structure` passes `None` through unchanged, and `DbApiHook.run()` is annotated `... | None`. The Databricks override, however, only accepted `Row` or `Sequence[Row]` and raised `TypeError: Expected Sequence[Row] or Row, but got <class 'NoneType'>`.

User-visible impact: `DatabricksSqlHook.get_first(...)` — which is just `run(handler=fetch_one_handler)` — crashed on any query returning no rows, where every non-overriding `DbApiHook` (postgres, snowflake, ...) returns `None`. With this change the Databricks hook follows the common.sql contract and passes `None` through.

(The odbc hook's override maps falsy results to `[]` instead; `None` is deliberately chosen here to preserve `fetchone` semantics — "no row" and "empty row set" stay distinguishable — and to match the base contract.)

Found while validating #39448 against a live Databricks SQL warehouse; verified there that with this change `run(..., handler=fetch_one_handler)` on an empty result returns `None` and serializes cleanly through XCom.

author: passcod
body:
🤖 Exposes the read-only MCP fleet-query interface (spec `MCP`) on the internet-facing server at `/mcp`, gated by admin-minted bearer tokens, so agents outside the tailnet — specifically Claude's admin Connections credential proxy — can query the fleet. The tailnet mount at `/api/mcp` is unchanged.

## What's here

- **`canopy-mcp` crate**: `CanopyMcp` moves out of private-server (which depends on public-server, so reuse had to go upstream). It now holds a `Db` instead of the private `AppState`; both servers mount the same service behind their own gates.
- **`mcp_tokens`**: named tokens following the `server_enrollment_tokens` pattern — 256-bit CSPRNG plaintext prefixed `canopy_mcp_`, shown once at minting, only the SHA-256 digest stored, whole-digest equality in SQL. Lifetime is fixed at one year in code; there is no way to mint longer.
- **Public `/mcp` gate**: missing, malformed, unknown, revoked, and expired tokens all collapse to one opaque 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge (new `auth-token-not-valid` error type); failed attempts rate-limit per source IP; successful queries are logged by token name and stamp `last_used_at` (throttled to one write a minute). The mount is composed in `main` rather than `routes()`, keeping it off the private server's `/public` nest and out of the device OpenAPI spec. No ingress change: client certs are already `optional_no_ca` at the edge.
- **Settings → MCP access**: admin-gated mint (copy-once dialog), list with expiry/last-used and status chips, revoke with confirm. Playwright-covered.
- **Rotation alert**: from 15 days before a token expires until it's revoked or replaced, the monitor loop raises a `canopy`/`mcp-token-expiry` issue on every group, severity Error so it pages. Recovers on revocation; the idle sweep writes nothing. *Note: the follow-up PR reworks this (and the preflight identity alert) into a single self-alert with its own Slack path and UI — the per-group fan-out pages N times for N groups, which is far too noisy.*

Auth scheme rationale: Claude's credential proxy documents exactly "Bearer token + Allowed websites" for MCP servers; its OAuth credential types aren't documented to work for MCP connections, and every available scheme parks a long-lived secret in Claude's credential store anyway — so the mitigations live on our side (hash at rest, revocation, rotation alerting, last-use visibility).

## Setting up the Claude connection

1. **Mint a token**: admin UI → Settings → MCP access → name it (e.g. `claude-connections`) → Mint token → copy the `canopy_mcp_…` secret now (it is shown once).
2. **Add the credential** in Claude admin → Connections → Credentials: type **Bearer token**, paste the secret, and set **Allowed websites** to the canopy public host (the device-API domain, e.g. `canopy.example.com`) so the credential can only ever be sent there.
3. **Add the MCP server** as a plugin whose `.mcp.json` points at `https://<canopy-public-host>/mcp`. The endpoint speaks streamable HTTP in stateless JSON mode, so no session affinity is needed.
4. **Verify**: a `tools/list` from Claude should show the 12 fleet queries; the token's "Last used" column in Settings updates within a minute of first use.

Rotation: tokens expire one year after minting. An alert fires 15 days out — mint a replacement, swap the credential in Claude admin, then revoke the old token.

author: guangyu-reflexio
body:
## Summary

Decompose `litellm_client.py` (`reflexio/server/llm/`, 2058 lines, core LLM adapter, ~102 importers) into a 312-line facade + 3 concern mixins + 3 leaf modules — behavior-preserving, **zero public-surface change**. Final Tier-2.5 decomposition; `litellm_client` stays the stable import point.

## Architecture (hybrid, state-driven)
`LiteLLMClient` is stateful, so self-bound concerns become **mixins composed into the client**; stateless parts become **leaves**:
- Mixins: `_litellm_text_generation.py` (generation + hard-timeout/subprocess orchestration + `_compute_cost_usd`), `_litellm_embedding.py` (embedding + token-budget), `_litellm_structured_output.py`.
- Leaves: `_litellm_types.py` (config/response/exceptions), `_litellm_json_extraction.py` (6 pure fns), `_litellm_subprocess.py` (worker + the 6 `_Completion*Snapshot` dataclasses).
- Per-mixin `TYPE_CHECKING` stubs type the cross-mixin edges (`_provider_response_format`/`_maybe_parse_structured_output`); no shared Protocol, no cycle.

## Behavior-preservation safeguards (this is core LLM infra)
- **Identity-preserving re-exports:** the facade re-exports every symbol by import binding (never redefines). A surface-completeness guard asserts all 5 public + 8 test-imported internals resolve, `__all__` equality, per-module cold-import, **object-identity** (`_TRUNCATION_WARNED_MODELS` + each snapshot class `is` its defining module's), and `hasattr(litellm_client, "litellm")`.
- **LLM-mock interception preserved:** moved code keeps `import litellm` + `litellm.completion(...)` module-attr calls; the facade retains `import litellm` + the `suppress_debug_info`/callbacks init (the ~40 `patch("...litellm_client.litellm.*")` sites depend on the shared module object). Multiprocessing start-method unchanged (fork); snapshot pickling survives via identity.
- **Patch-where-used repoints:** test patches of names that moved (embedding providers, `resolve_model_name`, `assert_provider_safe_schema`) were repointed to their new module — a re-export would have made them silent no-ops running the real embedder/network. `resolve_model_name` is repointed in both embedding + text-gen. Embedding tests assert mock call-counts.

## Test plan
- `tests/server/llm/` 488 passed / 60 skipped (incl. the identity surface guard + mock-count embedding tests); generation-service sample 375 passed; `import reflexio` boot OK; ruff + pyright clean; whole-branch `/review-loop` APPROVE (AST byte-identity confirmed on all moved bodies; all 112 importer sites resolve).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Phase 1 of Unified Update Platform (UUP) on-premises support: make go-wus **UUP-aware and correct** without changing offer/download behavior. UUP rides the same MS-WSUSSS/MS-WUSP protocols go-wus already speaks; the gaps were (a) nothing labeled an update as UUP, (b) `.wim` was served with the wrong MIME type, (c) `.wim/.esd/.psf` classified as `Unknown`. All changes are safe on legacy catalogs.

### What changed
- **Feature gate** `uup.enabled` (default **false**), env `WSUSGO_UUP_ENABLED`, wired into config/compose/env+config examples. Operator opt-in surface; see the deliberate deferral below.
- **Delivery-model detection** in the catalog parser, grounded in a **real Win11 UUP member revision** (verified from the operator's live catalog, committed as fixture `internal/catalog/testdata/uup_osinstaller.xml`). The parser now captures `Properties/@Handler` and `@LegacyName`; `detectDeliveryModel` keys on the authoritative handler signal, with payload shape as fallback:
  ```
  Handler endsWith "/UpdateHandlers/OSInstaller"    -> UUP
  || LegacyName startsWith "UUP"  (e.g. "UUPv1")    -> UUP
  || HandlerSpecificData.type == "OSInstallerMetadata" -> UUP
  else:  hasImaging(.wim/.esd) || (hasMsu && hasPsf) -> UUP
         else                                        -> Legacy
  ```
  Replaces the previously hardcoded `DeliveryModelLegacy`. The admin API (`delivery_model`) and console detail page already render this field — it was just always "Legacy" before.
- **Correct content types**: `contentTypeForKey` serves `.wim` -> `application/x-ms-wim` (Microsoft's documented UUP MIME type); everything else stays `application/octet-stream`.
- **File-kind classification**: `fileKind` now maps `.wim/.esd` -> `SelfContained`, `.psf` -> `Patch` (reuses existing enum; display/provenance only — download stays extension-agnostic).
- Tests: detector (handler signal + payload-shape fallback), real-fixture parse, `contentTypeForKey`, `fileKind`.

### Deliberately deferred
Offer/download **suppression** for UUP updates is *not* wired to `uup.enabled` yet. Detection is now grounded in real metadata, but bundle-parent label propagation and behavioral gating are validated end-to-end in Phase 2 (against a real Win11 client). The gate defaults **off**, so wiring suppression prematurely could regress legacy offers. This PR only **labels** — no behavioral change to existing legacy sync/offer/download/serve paths.

author: moonming
body:
## What

Two new upstream auth types for registered MCP servers, alongside `none`/`bearer`:

- **`api_key`** — the stored `secret` is sent as `x-api-key` on every upstream request (transport `custom_headers`; the value is marked sensitive so header-map debug formatting can't echo it; a non-header-safe key fails with a clean error, no panic).
- **`oauth2`** — OAuth 2.0 **client credentials** (RFC 6749 §4.4, the machine-to-machine grant, matching the MCP spec's OAuth direction for HTTP transports). New optional `McpServer` fields: `client_id`, `token_url`, `scopes`; the existing `secret` carries the client secret. The gateway mints its own access token and presents `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` — the caller's AISIX key is **never** forwarded upstream (the MCP authorization spec's no-token-passthrough MUST, unchanged).

## Token lifecycle (the load-bearing part)

- Process-global cache keyed `(token_url, client_id, sha256(client_secret))` — a **rotated secret can never reuse the previous token**; reuse stops 60s before the reported expiry (`expires_in`, default 3600s when omitted per RFC 6749 §5.1).
- **401 invalidation, wired and live-tested**: rmcp's reqwest transport surfaces a 401 in exactly two shapes (`AuthRequired` when `WWW-Authenticate` is present; `UnexpectedServerResponse("HTTP 401: …")` otherwise — matched **prefix-anchored** so an upstream body can't spoof it). Either invalidates the cache entry so the next attempt re-mints. Post-handshake ops need no separate hook: the production bridge reconnects per operation, so every rejected token funnels through connect.
- Token minting is bounded by the same per-upstream deadline as the handshake (one timeout envelope).
- **Secret hygiene**: client secret and minted tokens never appear in `Debug`, logs, or errors; token-endpoint failures report **status only** (an identity provider echoing request params can't leak the secret through us). Tests assert non-leakage explicitly.

## Design decisions

- **Schema stays flat + permissive on cross-field coupling** (no oneOf restructure of `McpServer`): the runtime degrades a mis-configured `oauth2` server gracefully — its tools drop out of `tools/list`, the failure is logged, nothing (not even the word "oauth") leaks to the calling agent (pinned by tests). This data plane's own Admin API enforces the coupling at write time (`api_key` ⇒ secret; `oauth2` ⇒ client_id + secret + token_url), and the control plane will enforce it strictly too.
- **Wire compatibility**: the three new fields are optional + skip-when-unset, so existing stored resources and older control-plane payloads keep deserializing.
- **rmcp reqwest split** (the one real trap): rmcp 1.8.0 links reqwest 0.13 while the workspace pins 0.12 — a naive downcast would silently never match. The 401 downcast names rmcp's own reqwest via a renamed dep (error **type only**, no second client); the live 401 tests fail loudly if cargo's unification ever stops holding.
- Concurrent cache misses may mint in parallel (each token valid, last insert wins) — documented, no single-flight machinery.

## Tests

- `oauth.rs`: 9 unit tests against a real local token endpoint — grant shape (urlencoded client-credentials, scopes space-joined), cache hit/expiry-skew/refetch, rotated-secret isolation, invalidate, 500/malformed/empty-token clean errors with non-leakage asserts, incomplete-config fails without network.
- Bridge/e2e (`upstream_roundtrip.rs`): api_key header actually enforced by a live upstream; oauth2 end-to-end (mint → handshake → tool call); both 401 shapes re-mint (token endpoint hit exactly twice across two attempts); mis-configured oauth2 fails cleanly without leaking.
- Gateway (`gateway_aggregation.rs`): a schema-valid but mis-configured oauth2 row degrades gracefully — snapshot loads, healthy upstreams unaffected, no hang, no credential/config leakage to the agent.
- Model/schema: serde round-trips, rejects-unknown, permissive-coupling pinned; admin write-path coupling tests.

`cargo fmt` / `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` / full workspace tests (941 passed) / `dump-schema` byte-stable / `dump-openapi` carries all four `McpAuthType` variant titles.

## Control-plane pairing (per the cross-plane rule)

This DP change is half the feature: the paired **AISIX-Cloud PR** (cp-admin.yaml enum + fields, Go model/validation/KV projection, dashboard auth subforms + i18n, e2e) follows immediately. **Deploy order: data plane first** — its `deny_unknown_fields` resource schema must know the new fields before the control plane projects them. Refs AISIX-Cloud#894 Revision C (Phase 2 item 1).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added support for `api_key` and `oauth2` authentication for upstream MCP servers.
  * OAuth connections now support token fetching and reuse, with automatic refresh when needed.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved validation so required credentials are checked based on the selected auth type.
  * Misconfigured upstreams now fail gracefully without exposing sensitive details.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated API and schema docs to reflect the expanded authentication options and required fields.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

---

## Independent audit response

A cold security-focused audit (verified against the vendored rmcp/reqwest/http sources) found **no HIGH**; it explicitly confirmed: **no secret-leak path under gateway control** (Debug redaction real; token-endpoint errors status-only with hostile echo-back tested; reqwest strips URL userinfo before send; the agent-visible error is a fixed string; rmcp never Debug-logs the auth header), the **version-split downcast robust** (traced the boxed type end-to-end in vendored source; cargo must unify the 0.13 line; the live 401 tests fail loudly if that ever stops), and the api-key `custom_headers` applied on **all three request paths**.

Three MEDIUMs, all fixed in `32a0a95`:
- **Hostile `expires_in` panic** — an IdP returning `u64::MAX` overflowed `Instant + Duration`, killing the connect task. Lifetime now clamped to 30 days; test pins `u64::MAX` minting + caching cleanly.
- **`scopes` missing from the cache key** — two servers sharing one OAuth client with different scopes would share a token (silent over-scoping / invalidation thrash). Scopes are now keyed, and every component is length-prefixed (also closing the LOW delimiter-ambiguity finding); test pins same-client/different-scopes isolation.
- **Token fetch followed redirects** — 307/308 re-POST the secret-bearing form cross-origin (headers are stripped on redirect, bodies are not; https→http downgrade possible). `Policy::none()`; test pins that a 307 fails without being followed.

LOWs: Debug redaction of every credential variant now **test-pinned** (it was the only guard and untested); connect error text sanitized (control chars stripped + truncated) so an upstream reflecting request headers into a 401 body can't plant them verbatim in gateway logs; the third 401 shape (JSON-RPC-parseable body → `JsonRpcError`, availability-only, bounded by expiry skew — spec-conforming servers send `WWW-Authenticate`, which IS matched) and the cache's no-eviction bound are documented; `client_secret_basic` interop filed as **#692**.

author: srnnkls
body:
## Problem

Bumping a source pin (e.g. `effect@3.9.2` → `effect@3.21.4`) fails the whole sync when the new commit drops a file the offer still admits:

```
error: sync error: selection: effect:effect:deno.json — a recorded artifact is no longer in the source's offer
matched against: the current offer of source `effect` in target `effect`
remedy: restore the artifact to the source's offer, or eject it before removing it
to debug: phora explain effect effect deno.json
```

The sealed-offer guard (D9) can't tell a *deliberate pin move that drops a file upstream* (routine) from a *silent narrowing under an unchanged pin* (the case it exists to catch), so it hard-errors on both.

## Changes

**`--fast-forward` flag** on `sync` and `update`. When a recorded artifact is no longer offered **and the resolved commit differs from the recorded one** (the pin moved), the artifact's deployed files are deleted and its record dropped — instead of erroring. A same-commit narrowing still hard-errors. Deletion runs before deploy through the same confinement checks prune uses.

```
phora sync --fast-forward     # or: phora update --fast-forward
```

**Clearer diagnostics.** The sealed-offer error now names the binding, the affected path, and the pin transition, and only advertises `--fast-forward` when the pin actually moved:

```
error: sync error: selection: effect:effect:deno.json — a recorded artifact is no longer in the source's offer
matched against: the current offer of source `effect` in target `effect`
binding: source `effect` → target `effect`
pin: recorded 5a0845d → now effect@3.21.4 (a1b2c3d)
path: resources/effect/effect/deno.json
remedy: re-sync with `--fast-forward` to drop it, or eject it before removing it
to debug: phora explain effect effect deno.json
```

**Per-binding pin reporting.** Every sync/update now prints, for each source→target binding, the current pin and where it is moving (`unchanged` / `new` / `old → new`).

## Tests

- `fast_forward_deletes_an_artifact_the_new_commit_dropped` — success, on-disk file gone, record removed.
- `fast_forward_still_seals_a_same_commit_narrowing` — same commit → still D9, and message must **not** suggest `--fast-forward`.
- Sealed-offer hard-error test now asserts the binding / pin / path detail lines and that a moved pin surfaces `--fast-forward`.
- `detail_lines_render_between_matched_against_and_remedy` for the new `SelectionDiagnostic.details`.

Full suite green (1346), clippy clean, fmt clean.

body:
Stacked on #402. Merges Clean `main` (#403, the witgen-IR migration) into the Orchard branch, brings the tree back to a fully green build, and ports witness generation from closure-based `witnessNative` to the new typed IR wherever the new IR can express it.

## Summary

**Phase 1 — get the build green again**
- Mechanical rename across `Clean/Orchard`: `witness`/`witnessField` → `witnessNative`, `Unconstrained` → `UnconstrainedNative`, `UnconstrainedDep` → `UnconstrainedDepNative`.
- `Field` → `FiniteField` wherever circuit `eval`/`Environment` machinery is used; added the concrete `FiniteField Fp`/`Fq` instances for the Pallas/Vesta fields (previously only `Field` was needed).
- Removed a stale custom `ExplicitCircuit` instance in `Explicit.lean` left over from the pre-merge API.
- Resolved a pre-existing kernel/heartbeat performance cliff in `Ecc/MulFixed/BaseFieldElem.lean` (predates this branch's merge with `main`, just tipped over the edge by it) — documented in `doc/performance-problems.md`. Fixed via an `elaborated :=` correction, extracting an opaque `prefixCircuit` to break a chained-`Circuit.foldl` kernel-size cliff, and replacing a manual 13-way lookup destructuring with the existing `CopyCheck.spec_telescope` lemma.
- Assorted proof-shape fixes where the new IR's `circuit_proof_start` normal form shrank or reshaped `Spec`/`ProverSpec` conjunctions (a recurring pattern — some circuit constructions now auto-discharge a conjunct that used to need an explicit proof term).

**Phase 2 — port witness generation to the typed IR**
Ported wherever the underlying computation is expressible in the new IR (`witness`/`witnessProgram`, `FExpr`/`NExpr`/`BExpr`): `Ecc/{Add,AddIncomplete}.lean`, all of `Ecc/Mul/*.lean`, `Ecc/MulFixed/Short.lean`, `Poseidon/*.lean`, `Sinsemilla/{Merkle,CommitDomain,HashToPoint}.lean`, `Utilities.lean`, `Action.lean`, and `Action/{NoteCommit,CommitIvk}.lean`.

Added `Clean/Orchard/witgen-ir-unsupported.md`, documenting every remaining `witnessNative` site and why:
- **Genuine external hints** (e.g. `WitnessPoint.lean`, `Action.lean`'s top-level private inputs) — nothing within the circuit to derive them from.
- **Fixed-base multiplication window tables** (`MulFixed/{FullWidth,BaseFieldElem}.lean`, `HashToPoint.lean`'s generator reads) — blocked on precomputed point tables that aren't materialized as concrete data anywhere in the repo yet; a real infrastructure gap, not a rename issue.
- **Type-level native by design** — candidates for a future `Unconstrained`/`UnconstrainedBool`/`UnconstrainedNat` (IR-backed hint) migration, e.g. `Mul/*`'s per-round scalar-bit hints and `Utilities.lean`'s `CondSwap.Swap`/`WitnessShort`, which are internal plumbing rather than genuine secrets but need a struct-shape migration beyond a routine per-file port.
- `Add.lean`'s `r`/`lambda`/`delta` — needs decomposing `ShortWeierstrass.add`'s pair-equality branching into the IR; attempted, hit an unresolved proof-shape mismatch, reverted rather than force it.

## Summary

Fixes #101.

When `ADMIN_KEY` was empty, `build_checkin_url` fell back to emitting `?token=<user_id>` and the frontend accepted that bare form — but Discord user IDs are public, so anyone in the server could forge another attendee's check-in link. - **`frontend/app/api/token.ts`** — `verifyToken` now rejects all tokens when `ADMIN_KEY` is unset, removing the keyless bare-numeric acceptance path.

Legacy signed `<user_id>.<sig>` tokens still verify; per the issue, retiring those is deferred until existing links expire.

author: joshsiv-mulga
body:
## Summary

`StopTask` marked a task `lastStatus=STOPPED` and released its capacity/ENI in the control plane, but nothing ever told the ecs-agent to kill the container. The container kept holding its host ports, so `DescribeTasks` reported a STOPPED task whose container was still RUNNING, and a replacement task placed on the freed capacity that rebound the same host port hit `EADDRINUSE`.

Observed on env19 validating siv-480: after `StopTask`, task `lastStatus=STOPPED` while the container was still RUNNING with no exit code; a nginx container kept host-netns `:80` and the next `:80` task hit `EADDRINUSE`.

Root cause — the agent had **no stop path**: `pollAssignments` only started new tasks, and `forceStopTask` flipped the task to STOPPED + released capacity + deleted the assign inbox (the only thing the agent polls). The design (ecs-v1.md:165) specified an agent-driven stop that was never wired.

## Changes

Wire the agent-driven cooperative stop, reusing the existing reap + report + release primitives:

- Per-instance **stop inbox** (`StopsPrefix`/`StopKey`) + `bus.StopDirective`.
- `requestStopTask` (cooperative): marks `DesiredStatus=STOPPED` and posts a stop directive, leaving `lastStatus`/capacity/ENI/targets untouched. Used by `StopTask`, `DeleteService`, and service scale-in. The heartbeat reaper and cluster/instance teardown keep the immediate `forceStopTask` since no live agent can reap.
- `PollAssignments` returns pending stops; the agent lists containers by `mulga.ecs.taskID` label, `Remove`s them (kill + delete, freeing host ports/netns), then reports STOPPED. `recordTaskState` performs the single capacity release on the agent's STOPPED report and reclaims the stop inbox.
- `listServiceTasks` excludes `DesiredStatus=STOPPED` tasks so a cooperatively stopped task drops out of the service's running total immediately.

`DescribeTasks` now keeps the task RUNNING with `desiredStatus=STOPPED` until the container is actually reaped — matching AWS ordering and eliminating the port race.

## Testing

- New unit tests: agent stop handler reaps labeled containers + reports STOPPED (incl. no-container case); poll dispatches stops before assigns and suppresses a same-poll assign for a stopping task; control-plane cooperative stop leaves capacity/targets untouched until the agent STOPPED report, which releases once and reclaims the stop inbox.
- `make preflight` green (diff coverage 78%).
- Verified live against a local single-node control plane driving the real ECS gateway API: `stop-task` returns `RUNNING`/`desiredStatus=STOPPED` with capacity held; a replacement placement on a full instance fails `RESOURCE:placement` until the agent reports STOPPED, then succeeds — proving the `EADDRINUSE` slot is not freed before reap. (Live containerd kill simulated via `SubmitTaskStateChange`; covered by unit tests.)

Plan: `docs/development/bugs/ecs-stoptask-container-reap.md`

author: tuxbook
body:
# fix: tolerate closed market data WebSocket in subscription requests

## Problem

Sending a feed subscription/unsubscription while the market data WebSocket is closed — e.g. during Tastytrade's nightly maintenance window (~2 AM ET), before `WebSocketClientWrapper`'s reconnect loop has re-established the connection — throws from the subscription callbacks registered with `LevelOneServiceManager`. `DataQueueHandlerSubscriptionManager` logs and **rethrows** (`Common/Data/DataQueueHandlerSubscriptionManager.cs`), so the exception propagates into the engine's live data feed and terminates the algorithm.

Observed in production (QC Cloud, live Tastytrade deployments) on **both** paths:

**Unsubscribe — option universe churn during regular hours:**
```
Runtime Error: The remote party closed the WebSocket connection without completing the close handshake. in LevelOneServiceManager.cs:line 226
 at System.Net.WebSockets.ManagedWebSocket.SendFrameFallbackAsync(...)
 at QuantConnect.Brokerages.Tastytrade.TastytradeBrokerage.a(IEnumerable`1 A_0)
 at QuantConnect.Brokerages.LevelOneOrderBook.LevelOneServiceManager.UnsubscribeCallbackWrapper(...) in Brokerages/LevelOneOrderBook/LevelOneServiceManager.cs:line 226
 at QuantConnect.Data.DataQueueHandlerSubscriptionManager.Unsubscribe(...) in Common/Data/DataQueueHandlerSubscriptionManager.cs:line 71
 at QuantConnect.Brokerages.Tastytrade.TastytradeBrokerage.Unsubscribe(SubscriptionDataConfig dataConfig)
 at ... UniverseSelection.RemoveSecurityFromUniverse(...)
```

**Subscribe — next trading day's contracts (~2 AM ET), fatal:**
```
Runtime Error: The remote party closed the WebSocket connection without completing the close handshake. in DataQueueHandlerManager.cs:line 139
 at QuantConnect.Lean.Engine.DataFeeds.DataQueueHandlerManager.Subscribe(...) in Engine/DataFeeds/DataQueueHandlerManager.cs:line 139
 at ... LiveTradingDataFeed.CreateDataSubscription(...)
```

In the second case the deployment's automatic restarts re-hit the still-closed socket during initialization, exhausted their attempts, and the algorithm stayed down through the next session.

## Root cause

`TastytradeBrokerage.Subscribe(IEnumerable<Symbol>)` / `Unsubscribe(IEnumerable<Symbol>)` call `webSocket.Send(...)` with no connection-state guard and no exception handling, and unconditionally `return true` — the `bool` failure contract of `DataQueueHandlerSubscriptionManager`'s callbacks is never exercised.

The recovery machinery already exists and is sound: `WebSocketClientWrapper.HandleConnection` reconnects indefinitely with backoff, and `MarketDataWebSocketClientWrapper` re-runs SETUP/AUTH/CHANNEL/FEED_SETUP and `OnReSubscriptionProcess` (full re-subscribe from `LevelOneServiceManager.GetSubscribedSymbols()`) on every reconnect. The only gap is the unguarded send throwing into engine threads before that recovery can run.

## Fix

Route both callbacks through a shared `TrySendMarketDataRequest`, which skips the send when the socket is not open and tolerates transport failures, always reporting success:

- **Why report success rather than `false`:** local subscription tracking must remain authoritative. Returning `false` from the subscribe path would drop the channel from `DataQueueHandlerSubscriptionManager` tracking and permanently exclude the symbol from `OnReSubscriptionProcess` — silent, unrecoverable data loss. The broker-side feed state died with the connection anyway; the next successful (re)connect rebuilds it exactly from local tracking.
- Serialization (symbol mapping) stays **outside** the guard so mapper faults still surface loudly; only transport delivery is tolerated.
- A send failure on a live-but-dying socket is likewise safe: the receive loop detects the dead connection, cycles, and the reconnect flow re-synchronizes subscriptions.

## Testing

- New regression test `SubscribeAndUnsubscribeDoNotThrowWhileMarketDataSocketIsNotConnected`: subscribing/unsubscribing on a constructed-but-never-connected brokerage must not throw and must return a valid enumerator. Fails on master (unguarded send throws through the rethrowing subscription manager), passes with this change.
- Plugin project builds clean; no behavior change on the happy path (open socket → identical single `Send`).

body:
## What
Fixes the \"Statement already delivered\" dead-end error in Tally Inbox when clicking \"Retry send\" on a row that was already emailed.

## Why
`inbox-send` sets `tally_delivered_at` (step 3) and then calls `setHandoffState` (step 4) as two separate operations. If step 4 threw after step 3 succeeded, the statement was left with:
- `tally_delivered_at` set (D3 gate armed)
- `handoff_state = "ready_to_send"` (UI shows "Retry send")

Clicking "Retry send" → `inbox-send` → D3 gate fires → 409 error with no actionable path.

Reproduced on TWV-BS-0094 (SD/A/26-27/14).

## How to test
1. Find TWV-BS-0094 in the Tally Inbox (currently showing "Retry send")
2. Click "Retry send" — should now get: *"Statement already delivered. Refresh the page and use the 'Resend email' button."*
3. Refresh the page — row should now appear in Closed tab with "Resend email" button
4. Click "Resend email" — GST invoice should be emailed successfully

author: modernn
body:
## What

Lands the deferred **child-side live TLS socket** for LAN transport confidentiality (issue #21, red-team TR1). The child control plane now serves over **HTTPS** instead of plaintext, with the TLS cert provenance **bound to the pinned child identity key** — so there is no trust-on-first-use window.

Recorded as **ADR-031 D8** (amendment; the engine choice is human-approved per the ADR, enforcement surface). This closes the D5/D7 trigger: #22 real identity key + parent pairing having landed, the deferred socket can now land.

## Why now

ADR-031 D5/D7 deferred the live socket because "the CIO server cannot easily terminate TLS." The D5 trigger (real `IdentityKeyProvider` via #22 + parent-kmp pairing) is met on `main`, so implementing it is consistent with locked canon.

## Changes

- **Engine:** Ktor `CIO` → `Netty` + `sslConnector` (CIO can't terminate TLS). Every existing route is unchanged; routes were extracted into a member extension `Application.configure()` to avoid re-nesting. Auth stays **app-layer + transport-independent** (ADR-031 D1).
- **`TlsLeaf`** (new): ephemeral self-signed EC P-256 leaf, BouncyCastle-minted into an in-memory PKCS12. Software key — TLS is confidentiality-only and the channel's trust is the identity-bound `SpkiAssertion`, so the leaf **never authenticates** (a leaf-key compromise is at most LAN-metadata confidentiality loss; ATTACKS §1). BC is JVM-portable, so the socket + handshake are **host-testable**, not device-only.
- **`GET /spki-assertion`** (new route): serves `SpkiBindingSigner.assertFor(leafSpki, identityKey)`. **Fail-closed (D4):** no identity key (pre-pairing / no StrongBox) → **204**, the parent rejects, **no TOFU**.
- **HTTPS-only, no plaintext fallback:** a TLS bring-up failure leaves the socket down; **policy enforcement is independent and unaffected** (the watchdog holds the baseline offline).
- **Deps (disclosed, enforcement surface):** `ktor-server-netty` (replaces `-cio`), `bcpkix-jdk18on` + `bcprov-jdk18on`. No SaaS/telemetry; BC already trusted in `parent-kmp` (D7 verifier).

## Tests (host/JVM, no device)

- `TlsLeafTest` — cert/SPKI extraction, SPKI is a real hashable SPKI, ephemerality.
- `ChildTlsSocketTest` — a **real Netty `sslConnector` handshake**: genuine assertion for the negotiated leaf verifies (accept); cert-substitution rejected (D2 c3); an assertion signed by the wrong identity key is rejected **over a fully-trusted socket** (D1); no-identity-key serves **204** (fail-closed, no TOFU).
- Full `:app:testDebugUnitTest` green; `:app:assembleDebug` green (Netty + BC package cleanly). Existing `SpkiBindingTest` unchanged.

## Bench-gated / deferred

- The **real StrongBox-signed** assertion is bench-Pixel-7-only (ADR-032); the emulator/host exercise the socket with the injected synthetic identity seam (as #22 shipped).
- **Still deferred (coordinated sibling PR):** parent-side mDNS discovery + SPKI-pinning TLS client that feeds `presentedSpkiDer` from the negotiated handshake leaf. Until it lands, the two-emulator demo is **intentionally down** (child is now HTTPS-only) — not a regression.

## Gating

`agent-blocked` (transport-trust / MITM, enforcement surface). Implemented **attended**; requires human merge approval. Non-negotiables held: no SaaS/telemetry, no content monitoring, fail-closed throughout.

author: jayden0701
body:
### Summary
`RMSReverseNormLayer::incremental_forwarding` previously assumed a
single-token decode step: it asserted `(to - from) == 1` and hardcoded
`to = 1`. This made multi-turn inference impossible when the prefill
phase (non-zero `from`) spanned more than one token.

### Changes
- Removed the `to - from != 1` assertion.
- Replaced the hardcoded `to = 1` with `to = to - from`, normalizing the
  range to 0-based while preserving the original step size.

### Rationale
This enables multi-turn / multi-token prefill, where the step size can
be greater than 1. The rest of the computation (weight multiply, RMS
norm, out_scale) already operates on the full `to - from` slice, so it
works correctly without further changes.

### Testing
Verified that single-token decode behavior is unchanged and that
multi-token prefill no longer throws.

author: tya5
body:
**[e2e-coder]** — construction-forwarding gap (tui S6 dogfood, primary evidence). Separate from the a359 arc. Off clean main. Small (1 forward + tests).

## The gap
A chat-router MCP tool returning a large `ImageContent` inlined ~400KB base64 into the LLM body. Root: `Session._make_router_op_context` → `build_router_op_context` **omitted `media_store`**, so the chat-router op context had `media_store=None` → the mcp op handler couldn't save images to `.reyn/media/` as path-refs → base64 inlined. The **public twin** `RouterHostAdapter.make_router_op_context` already forwards `self._media_store` (session.py:1826) — this is a parity gap in the private builder.

## Fix
Pass `media_store=self._media_store` in `_make_router_op_context` (the builder already accepts + forwards it to `OpContext`). Now a chat-router MCP `ImageContent` is saved as a `.reyn/media/` path-ref → `media_blocks` stays small → the offload/clean-payload gate works → the LLM gets a path-ref, not a base64 blob.

## Falsify (real Session, RED-verified)
- `test_make_router_op_context_forwards_media_store` — the ctx carries the session's `media_store` (sentinel), not None. Reverting the forward fails it (RED).
- `test_router_ctx_media_store_none_when_session_has_none` — faithful None (no fabricated store).
- tui's ~400KB image repro is the live back-test (image → path-ref, not inline base64).

## CI gates
- ruff clean · tier-audit OK · docstrings clean · 11 focused (router-ctx + mcp-multimodal) pass · full suite running.

## Test plan
- [x] media_store forwarded (real Session) + RED-verified
- [ ] full suite green (running)

author: vieiralucas
body: Awareness reconnect grace on top of the `AwarenessClear` wire message (#70). - `clock::{Clock, SystemClock, ManualClock}` — server wall-clock seam (millis), the analog of core's `Host::now` the runtime lacked. `ManualClock` drives presence expiry deterministically in tests. - Disconnect no longer clears presence immediately: a client holding awareness is marked stale with a `now + grace` deadline (default 5s). Reconnect (Hello) within the window cancels it. - `Registry::sweep` clears every past-deadline client and fans `AwarenessClear { channel, actor }` to each affected room's remaining subscribers on their own channel. - `Hub::clear_client_awareness` now returns the cleared `(room, actor)` pairs so the sweep can address the fan-out. Clock is read only when the client actually holds presence — the no-awareness disconnect never touches it (keeps the Miri-gated registry tests off the isolation-unsupported system-time call). - `#69`'s disconnect test revised to grace semantics; new `awareness_grace.rs` suite covers sweep-past-deadline clear + fan-out, retention within window, reconnect-cancels-clear, and no-op sweep. Deferred (KANBAN): per-entry TTL, throttle/coalesce, wiring a periodic `sweep` into the tokio runtime. Gate: `cargo test --workspace` + `cargo +nightly miri test -p crdtsync-server` green, `cargo fmt` clean. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a reconnect grace window for awareness by injecting a server clock and adding an explicit sweep that clears expired presence and sends `AwarenessClear` to room peers. This prevents cursor flicker on brief disconnects and makes time-driven behavior testable. - **New Features** - Added `clock::{Clock, SystemClock, ManualClock}` plus `Registry::set_clock` and `set_grace_millis`. - Disconnect marks clients with awareness as stale until `now + grace` (default 5s); a reconnect within the window cancels it. - New `Registry::sweep` clears past-deadline presence and fans `AwarenessClear { channel, actor }` to each room’s subscribers on their own channel. - `Hub::clear_client_awareness` now returns cleared `(room, actor)` pairs; no clock read on disconnects with no awareness. - **Migration** - Run `Registry::sweep` on a periodic timer in the runtime to expire presence. - Optionally adjust the window with `set_grace_millis` and inject `ManualClock` in tests. Written for commit 90115c898fea8c90bedbe2698e430487d162d197. Summary will update on new commits.

author: abedubas-alchemydev
body:
## Summary

Two features, built and reviewed together (plus one small ops-docs fix that rides along).

### 1. Banks vertical — bank charter database (FDIC/OCC)

- **Ingestion from official public sources only** (keyless APIs): FDIC BankFind (`ESTYMD` window + `/history` `CHANGECODE:110` corroboration) for newly opened insured institutions, and OCC CAS "New Bank Charter" filings/actions (Receipt → Approved → Consummated-Effective / Withdrawn) for pending national-bank / federal-trust applications. Opened OCC applications are reconciled onto their FDIC identity via the OCC national-by-name directory workbook (exact normalized-name + state, unique-match only). Digital-assets charter applications are tagged from the OCC digital-assets page — public-portion PDF **URLs** stored, never fetched.
- **Data + API**: `banks` + `bank_application_events` tables (Alembic migration `20260702_0001`, idempotent upserts, forward-only status transitions); read-only `GET /api/v1/banks` list/detail behind the new `banks` feature permission.
- **Watcher job**: `scripts/watch_bank_charters.py` (dry-run default, `--apply` to write, overlapping trailing-30-day window so re-runs are safe) deployed by CI as Cloud Run Jobs `fis-bank-charter-watch-staging` / `fis-bank-charter-watch-prod` — **inert until their Cloud Scheduler crons are created out-of-band**. Runbook: `docs/runbooks/bank-charter-watch.md`.
- **Frontend**: new Banks section (`/banks` list + `/banks/{id}` detail) with application timeline, digital-assets tag, charter-status pill, established-date filter, and official FDIC/OCC source links; sidebar nav entry; chatbot app-knowledge + internal-route support.

### 2. Dashboard: Deficiency card → "Pending Approval BDs" card

body:
## Баг с живой установки

На реальном `ONAPPINSTALL` (токен сохранился корректно) в логах всплыло:
```
[b24 events] enqueue failed: Custom Id cannot contain :
```
`joinId` склеивал части job-id через `:`, а BullMQ **запрещает** `:` в кастомном `jobId` (он неймспейсит ключи Redis двоеточием). Падал enqueue во **все** очереди — не только follow-up установки, но и крон `bank-fetch` (`DEMO_LOAD_N>0`), `file-parse`, `crm-sync`. То есть вся шина очередей молча теряла джобы.

## Фикс

- Разделитель `:` → `|`. `encodeURIComponent` экранирует `|` (`%7C`), поэтому ни одна закодированная часть не содержит литерального `|` → id остаются **детерминированными и без коллизий**, и при этом BullMQ-safe.
- Тесты обновлены под `|`; добавлен инвариант «job-id не содержит `:`» (на реальном member_id и значениях с `:` внутри полей).

Дедуп-семантика не изменилась (те же поля, тот же детерминизм).

`pnpm check` — чисто, **441 тест**.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

New verified gallery entry **hermite-sawtooth-identity-oq-01-oq-03**, directly answering the open question posed by the parent entry (`hermite-sawtooth-identity-oq-01`):

> *Extend the elementary power-sum route to m = 3, 4 (each a fixed Faulhaber identity), charting how far the generating-function-free method reaches before the algebra becomes unwieldy.*

**Result.** For every `n ≥ 1`, over ℚ:
```
∑_{k<n} B₃(x + k/n) = (1/n²) · B₃(nx)      (coefficient n^{1-3} = n⁻²)
∑_{k<n} B₄(x + k/n) = (1/n³) · B₄(nx)      (coefficient n^{1-4} = n⁻³)
```
proved by the parent's elementary, generating-function-free method.

## Proof architecture
- Evaluate `B₃(x) = x³ − (3/2)x² + (1/2)x` and `B₄(x) = x⁴ − 2x³ + x² − 1/30` explicitly, computing the Bernoulli numbers `b₃ = 0`, `b₄ = −1/30` via `bernoulli_eq_bernoulli'_of_ne_one` + `bernoulli'_three`/`bernoulli'_four`.
- Expand `Bₘ(x + k/n)` into a polynomial in `k`; distribute `∑_{k<n}` over the monomials.
- Replace each `∑_{k<n} kʲ` by its closed Faulhaber form: `∑k`, `∑k²`, `∑k³ = (n(n−1)/2)²` (Nicomachus), and `∑k⁴ = n(n−1)(2n−1)(3n²−3n−1)/30` (m=4 only).
- Close with a single `field_simp; ring`.

## Verdict on the open question
The elementary route extends cleanly to **every fixed m**: order `m` needs only the power sums up to `∑k^{m−1}` (all one-line inductions) plus a mechanical polynomial expansion. It never becomes genuinely unwieldy — only longer.

## Verification
- **0 axioms** (`#print axioms` on `raabe_three`/`raabe_four` → `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only), **0 sorries**.
- 10 theorems / 159 lines, Mathlib 4.26.0.
- Typechecked via `lake env lean`.

author: misosiruda
body:
# Sharpe 검증 schema 추가

## 개요

이 PR은 RH5 `Sharpe Statistical Validation`의 첫 번째 작은 범위로, Sharpe 계열 통계 검증을 report/dashboard에 연결하기 전 사용할 `sharpe_validation.v1` contract와 설계 문서를 추가합니다.

기존 상태:
- `performance_metrics.v1`은 return sample 기반 per-sample `sharpeRatio`를 계산합니다.
- 기존 Sharpe 값은 annualize하지 않으며 serial correlation adjustment, confidence interval, Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio, Deflated Sharpe Ratio를 계산하지 않습니다.
- RH5 milestone에는 Sharpe sample warning, non-IID, selection bias warning을 후속 검증 항목으로 정의해 두었습니다.

이번 변경:
- `src/analytics/sharpeValidation.ts`에 `sharpe_validation.v1` schema version, TypeScript contract, unavailable placeholder helper를 추가했습니다.
- `src/analytics/sharpeValidation.test.ts`에 unavailable schema default와 `NaN` 미포함 검증을 추가했습니다.
- `docs/sharpe-statistical-validation-contract.md`에 RH5 Sharpe validation 설계, warning code, 후속 연결 계획, safety boundary를 문서화했습니다.
- `docs/research-hardening-milestone-plan.md`와 `docs/historical-replay.md`에서 새 contract 문서를 RH5 기준으로 연결했습니다.

영향 범위:
- report/dashboard payload에는 아직 새 field를 연결하지 않습니다.
- live signal, live order routing, broker write path, 자동 sizing 경로를 추가하지 않습니다.
- DB schema 또는 migration 변경은 없습니다.

---

## 주요 기능

### 1. 기능 요약

- `SHARPE_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_VERSION="sharpe_validation.v1"` 상수를 추가했습니다.
- `SharpeValidationReport` contract를 추가했습니다.
- sample, distribution, metric slots, selection context, warning code를 구조화했습니다.
- unavailable 상태를 deterministic JSON shape로 만드는 `createUnavailableSharpeValidationReport()` helper를 추가했습니다.
- RH5 design 문서에서 calculator/report/dashboard 연결을 후속 PR 범위로 분리했습니다.

### 2. 세부 기능

AS-IS:
- `performance_metrics.v1`은 per-sample `sharpeRatio`와 warning string만 가집니다.
- Sharpe confidence interval, PSR, DSR 후보는 문서상 후속 후보였고, artifact field contract가 없었습니다.

TO-BE:
- `sharpe_validation.v1`은 다음 metric slot을 명시합니다.

```text
sampleSharpe
loAdjustedSharpe
probabilisticSharpeRatio
deflatedSharpeRatio
```

- unavailable state는 다음 정보를 `null` 또는 explicit status로 보존합니다.

```text
sample.returnSampleCount
sample.minimumSampleCount
distribution.meanReturnRatio
distribution.volatilityRatio
distribution.skewness
distribution.excessKurtosis
distribution.autocorrelation
selectionContext
warnings
```

- 계산기와 report/dashboard 연결은 이번 PR에 포함하지 않습니다.

---

## 데이터 모델

### 1. 모델 정의

DB schema 변경은 없습니다.

TypeScript contract 변경:

```typescript
export const SHARPE_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_VERSION = "sharpe_validation.v1";

export interface SharpeValidationReport {
  schemaVersion: typeof SHARPE_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_VERSION;
  status: "available" | "unavailable";
  sample: SharpeValidationSampleSummary;
  distribution: SharpeValidationDistributionSummary;
  metrics: SharpeValidationMetrics;
  selectionContext: SharpeValidationSelectionContext;
  warnings: SharpeValidationWarning[];
}
```

`SharpeValidationMetrics`는 다음 slot을 포함합니다.

```typescript
export interface SharpeValidationMetrics {
  sampleSharpe: SharpeValidationEstimate;
  loAdjustedSharpe: SharpeValidationEstimate;
  probabilisticSharpeRatio: SharpeValidationProbability;
  deflatedSharpeRatio: SharpeValidationEstimate;
}
```

### 2. 제약조건

해당 없음. 이번 PR에서는 DB 제약조건 변경이 없습니다.

### 3. 인덱스

해당 없음. 이번 PR에서는 인덱스 변경이 없습니다.

---

## API 엔드포인트

### 신규 API

해당 없음. 신규 API 엔드포인트가 없습니다.

### 변경된 API

API 엔드포인트 변경 없음. `HistoricalReplayReport`, `BatchReplayAggregateReport`, `ReplayResearchReport`, Local Operations API, Next.js dashboard payload에는 아직 새 field를 연결하지 않았습니다.

---

## 아키텍처 구조

### 레이어별 역할

- **Analytics Contract Layer**: `src/analytics/sharpeValidation.ts`가 RH5 Sharpe validation schema와 unavailable helper를 정의합니다.
- **Analytics Test Layer**: `src/analytics/sharpeValidation.test.ts`가 unavailable shape의 deterministic default와 JSON serialization safety를 검증합니다.
- **Docs Layer**: RH5 설계, warning code, 후속 calculator/report/dashboard 연결 순서를 문서화합니다.

### 의존성 흐름

해당 없음. 이번 PR은 기존 report builder나 dashboard ViewModel에 새 schema를 연결하지 않습니다.

### 설계 의도

`performance_metrics.v1`의 기존 per-sample Sharpe와 RH5 검증 layer를 바로 섞지 않고, 별도 `sharpe_validation.v1` contract를 먼저 둡니다. 이렇게 하면 후속 calculator PR에서 sample warning, serial correlation, PSR/DSR 후보, selection context를 하나의 schema에 채울 수 있습니다.

---

## 핵심 구현 내용

### 1. 비즈니스 규칙

- Sharpe validation은 paper-only 사후 검증 경고입니다.
- insufficient sample, zero volatility, non-IID, missing selection context는 metric을 pass처럼 보이게 하지 않고 warning/status로 남기는 contract입니다.
- PSR/DSR 후보는 calculator와 selection context 연결 전까지 `not_implemented` 또는 unavailable 상태로 둡니다.
- AI confidence를 sizing이나 live signal로 직접 연결하지 않습니다.

### 2. 주요 알고리즘 / 처리 흐름

이번 PR은 계산 알고리즘을 추가하지 않습니다.

추가된 helper 흐름:

1. `createUnavailableSharpeValidationReport()`가 return sample 수, minimum sample 수, reason code를 받습니다.
2. report status를 `unavailable`로 둡니다.
3. distribution, confidence interval, benchmark, selection context 값을 `null` 또는 explicit unavailable 상태로 채웁니다.
4. reason warning과 `SHARPE_VALIDATION_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` info warning을 함께 반환합니다.

### 3. 예외 처리

- unavailable helper는 계산을 수행하지 않으므로 numeric exception을 던지지 않습니다.
- test에서 JSON serialization 결과에 `NaN`이 포함되지 않는지 확인했습니다.

### 4. 트랜잭션 처리

해당 없음. 이번 PR에서는 명시적인 트랜잭션 경계 변경이 없습니다.

---

## 보안·동시성·멱등성 정책

### 1. 보안 정책

해당 없음. 인증, 인가, secret, 개인정보, 민감정보 마스킹 정책을 변경하지 않습니다.

Safety boundary 확인:
- live order surface 추가 없음.
- broker write path 추가 없음.
- raw command execution surface 추가 없음.
- 자연어 주문 surface 추가 없음.
- AI decision provider와 deterministic backend 책임 분리 변경 없음.
