author: fabeat
body:
## Problem

`PluginLoader` resolved the entry-point class via a redundant `require_once` of either a manifest-declared `file` path or `<plugin>/Plugin.php` by default. When neither matched — e.g. a plugin whose entry point lived at `src/Plugin.php` with no `file` key in `plugin.json` — `class_exists($fqcn, false)` returned `false` and the plugin was **silently dropped**. The empty result was then cached in `storage/.plugins_stamp`, locking the failure in across reboots.

This is the root cause of `spora-plugin-minimax` not appearing in the web admin UI after `bin/spora plugin:install` — the operator skeleton reports "Plugin install completed" in the log but `/api/v1/plugins` returns an empty array, the four MiniMax tools never surface in `/settings/tools`, and the cache holds `{"plugins":[]}` indefinitely.

## Fix

Make `class` the single source of truth for resolving the entry point. Drop the `file` field. Lean entirely on PSR-4 autoloading.

### `PluginLoader.php`

- **Drop `require_once`** in both `loadPluginFromManifest()` and `restorePluginFromSidecarEntry()`. The class is resolved via `is_a($fqcn, PluginInterface::class, true)` (PSR-4 autoloading, with the manifest's `autoload.psr-4` mapping registered by `registerManifestAutoload()` immediately above).
- **Replace the silent-drop gate** with a throw:
  ```php
  if (!is_a($fqcn, PluginInterface::class, true)) {
      throw new PluginLoadFailedException(sprintf(
          "Plugin manifest '%s' declares class '%s' but the class is not autoloadable "
          . "or does not implement %s. Check that the manifest's autoload.psr-4 entry "
          . "points to the right directory, and that the package's composer.json declares "
          . "a matching PSR-4 mapping.",
          ...
      ));
  }
  ```
  The exception message includes the manifest path and the declared FQCN, so a future failure is straightforward to diagnose from a log line.

### `plugin.schema.json`

- Drop the `file` property. `additionalProperties: false` on the manifest root means any leftover `file` key in a plugin's `plugin.json` is rejected.

### Tests

- **Delete** the obsolete `"file" key loads the plugin from the specified path instead of Plugin.php` test.
- **Flip** `manifest whose declared class cannot be resolved is silently skipped` to `toThrow(PluginLoadFailedException::class, 'Tests\\Fixtures\\Plugins\\DoesNotExist\\Plugin')`.
- **Add** `PSR-4 autoload resolves the entry-point class without a "file" key in the manifest` (positive test against the restructured `NamedPlugin` fixture).
- **Add** `manifest whose declared class is autoloadable but does not implement PluginInterface throws` (uses new `NotAPlugin` fixture).
- **Remove** all `symlink()` calls in the test bootstrap (now dead code under autoloading).
- **Restructure** `plugins_with_custom_file/NamedPlugin/`: drop `src/` subdirectory, drop `file` key from `plugin.json`. This is the only fixture that used the file override.
- **Register explicit PSR-4 mappings** for each fixture plugin in `tests/Pest.php` so `is_a(..., true)` can resolve them — the fixtures are organised by test purpose (`plugins_with_manifest/`, `plugins_inventory/`, etc.), not by namespace, so `Tests\` → `tests/` alone can't find them.

### Docs

- Drop `file` field from the optional-fields table and from the full example.
- Rewrite the "Manifest validation" section so the unresolvable-class case is loud rather than silent.

## Validation

Run from `vendor/spora-ai/spora-core` (or any checkout with the worktree's branch checked out):

```
composer test         # 2213 passed, 0 failed
composer analyse      # No errors
php-cs-fixer fix --dry-run --diff --config=.php-cs-fixer.php  # 0 of 469 files can be fixed
```

End-to-end against the operator skeleton with the local `spora-core` symlinked via path repository:

```
rm -f storage/.plugins_stamp storage/.plugins_stamp.cache.json
php bin/spora spora:install
curl -b cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/plugins | jq
# → "minimax" entry with bundledTools: [image, speech, music, video]
curl -b cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/tools | jq
# → 4 generation tools (MiniMax Image, MiniMax Speech, MiniMax Music, MiniMax Video)
sqlite3 storage/database.sqlite "SELECT migration FROM migrations WHERE migration LIKE 'minimax_%';"
# → minimax_000001_create_minimax_generation_log
```

## Followup (separate PR)

`spora-plugin-minimax` itself has a structural quirk unrelated to this fix: its entry-point class is `Spora\Plugins\MiniMax\MiniMaxPlugin` but the file is `src/Plugin.php`, so even with PSR-4 correctly registered the autoloader looks for `src/MiniMaxPlugin.php` and finds nothing. The old `require_once`-based loader accidentally supported this layout; PSR-4 does not. The fix in the minimax repo is one of:

- Rename `src/Plugin.php` → `src/MiniMaxPlugin.php` (recommended).
- Add `"classmap": ["src/Plugin.php"]` to the plugin's `composer.json`.

Without one of these, the minimax plugin still won't load after this PR merges. The end-to-end verification above was performed after applying the rename locally to confirm the rest of the fix works.

## Files changed

- `app/Plugins/PluginLoader.php` — refactor (drop require_once, throw on unresolvable class)
- `plugin.schema.json` — drop `file` property
- `app/Extensions/AppLoader.php` — incidental CS Fixer cleanup (ReflectionClass import)
- `tests/Pest.php` — explicit PSR-4 mappings for fixture plugins
- `tests/Unit/Plugins/PluginLoaderTest.php` — restructured tests (delete, flip, add, drop symlinks)
- `tests/Fixtures/plugins_with_custom_file/NamedPlugin/` — restructured (drop `src/`, drop `file` key)
- `tests/Fixtures/plugins_invalid_manifest/NotAPlugin/` (new) — autoloadable-but-not-a-plugin fixture
- `docs/07_plugins.md` — drop `file` references, update manifest-validation section

author: abkrim
body:
## Summary

Test-infra + migration consistency sweep for `lararoi` (AID-301, umbrella consolidation 2026-07-02). No functional code changes. Complements AID-263 (config consistency), different scope.

Both parts of the issue are coupled here because `lararoi` was **`.stub`-only** (no timestamped `.php`): the migrator globs `*_*.php` and cannot see a `.php.stub`, so `RefreshDatabase` needs a real migration first. Part B is therefore a prerequisite of Part A.

## Part B — schema package-managed (retire publishing)

- Rename `create_vat_verifications_table.php.stub` → `2025_01_01_000001_create_vat_verifications_table.php` (timestamped, 0 stubs).
- Service provider: `hasMigration()` → `hasMigrations([...])`.
- Matches the umbrella reference (laratickets AID-290 / lara-verifactu). Recommendation in the issue was to retire publishing for coherence — done.

## Part A — discover migrations in tests

- `tests/TestCase.php`: drop the hardcoded `include ... ->up()`; register the migrations directory via `afterResolving('migrator')` + `RefreshDatabase` (umbrella CLAUDE.md lesson 2026-07-02). Not `defineDatabaseMigrations()` (rollback in teardown).
- `tests/Pest.php`: apply `RefreshDatabase` to the suite.

## Verification (red → green)

- With the `.stub` still in place and the new TestCase, the suite goes **red** (`no such table: vat_verifications`, 29 failures) — proving the migrator does not see the stub.
- After renaming to a real timestamped migration, the suite is **green**.
- `composer quality` green: pint, phpstan (level 5), coverage **73.1%** (CI min 20).

## Installation contract change

Consumers now obtain the schema via `php artisan migrate` (package-managed) instead of publishing a stub. Verified safe: no umbrella consumer depends on lararoi's migration/model/service — `larabill` declares the dependency but imports nothing from `Lararoi` and ships its own `VatVerification` (its own duplication is the consumer's debt, not lararoi's).

Version bump / release is handled separately (P2).

Closes AID-301.

## Summary

Two cohesive TUI test-hardening follow-ups flagged by Sentinel CONDITIONAL reviews. No production code was changed — the underlying behavior was already correct; only the test oracles were too loose to catch a regression.

### #1743 — LeftNav active-route marker bound to the active row
`left-nav.test.tsx` previously asserted the `●` active-route marker appeared *somewhere* in the frame. Tightened it to assert the marker sits on the row matching `activeId` and is **absent** from every other row.

**Discrimination proof:** temporarily changed `LeftNav.tsx`'s `isActiveRoute` to `i === 0` (marker always on the first row regardless of `activeId`). The tightened test failed:
```
AssertionError: expected '   ▥ Panels' to contain '●'
```
The old loose assertion would have passed (marker was still present, just on the wrong row). Reverted the break; suite green again.

### #1744 — launchpad-home follow-ups (PR #1741)
Four Sentinel-flagged gaps, all addressed:

1. **Unsafe recent-session id regression test** (`home-screen.test.tsx`): added a test with `id = "s/1?x=y#z"` and a `LocationProbe` component (reads `useLocation().pathname`, since `useParams()` would decode the segment back and mask whether encoding happened). Asserts the route contains the `encodeURIComponent`-encoded id.
   **Discrimination proof:** reverted `HomeScreen.tsx` to `navigate(\`/sessions/${item.id}\`)` (no encoding) — the unescaped `#` broke route matching entirely (frame rendered empty), failing the assertion. Reverted; suite green.

2. **`isActive={false}` cursor/Enter inertness** (`home-screen.test.tsx`): the existing test only pressed quick-action letters (`c/e/p/,`). Extended it to also send `j/k`/arrows/`Enter` and assert the frame is byte-identical before/after (no cursor movement, no navigation).
   **Discrimination proof:** temporarily hardcoded the cursor-selection hook's `isActive` to `true` (leaving the quick-key hook untouched) — Enter navigated to `/panels/compose`, failing the new assertion, which the old test could not have caught. Reverted; suite green.

3. **Wall-clock `sleep(120)` → deterministic wait** (`council-tui.test.tsx`): replaced the fixed sleep before the Enter-navigation integration assertion with `vi.waitFor` (polls + flushes microtasks until the assertion passes or times out).
   **Discrimination proof:** delayed navigation to 300ms in `HomeScreen.tsx` — the *old* `sleep(120)` pattern false-failed (correct behavior, just slower), while the *new* `vi.waitFor` still passed. Removing navigation entirely still correctly failed (timeout) with the new pattern. Reverted; suite green.

4. **Docs**: added a `docs/designs/interactive-tui.md` §4.2 bullet documenting the Home launchpad's unified quick-actions + recent-sessions list, its cursor, and its independence from the left nav's own `j/k` focus.

## How each discriminates
See per-item "Discrimination proof" above — each was verified via a temporary production-code break (never committed), confirming the tightened/added assertion fails on the targeted regression, then reverted to a clean, green state.

author: nicklasskoglund
body:
## Syfte

Steg 5 — slutlig utvärdering. Jämför de två färdigtränade modellerna
(`baseline_model.keras` från Steg 3, `best_model.keras` från Steg 4) sida
vid sida på ett identiskt testset, utan omträning.

## Vad ingår

- **Nytt notebook:** `notebooks/04_final_evaluation.ipynb`
  1. Imports & konfiguration (RANDOM_SEED + `enable_op_determinism()`)
  2. Ladda & förbehandla data (samma 70/15/15-split som tidigare steg)
  3. Ladda båda sparade modeller från disk (ingen omträning)
  4. Utvärdera baseline-modellen på testset (153 samples)
  5. Utvärdera optimerad modell på samma testset
  6. Sammanfattande jämförelsetabell
  7. Diskussion av val/test-gapet
  8. Slutsatser & nästa steg

## Resultat

| Metric | Baseline | Optimerad |
|---|---|---|
| Test Accuracy | 0.6732 | 0.6601 |
| Test AUC | 0.7528 | 0.7594 |
| Val AUC (Grid Search) | — | 0.8895 |
| Val/Test AUC-gap | — | 0.1301 |

Alla resultat är verifierade mot tidigare dokumenterade siffror från Steg 3
och Steg 4 — matchar exakt (inom avrundning), vilket bekräftar att testsetet
och modellerna är identiska.

## Nyckelinsikt

Val/test-gapet (0.13 AUC) dokumenteras och förklaras som indirekt
overfitting mot valideringssetet vid Grid Search med litet dataset (48
kombinationer testade mot 153 val-samples) — inte klassisk overfitting.
Rekommendationer för framtida förbättring (k-fold, mer data, nested CV)
listas i notebookets sista cell.

## Notera

`reports/figures/*.png` och `reports/final_model_comparison.csv` genereras
lokalt vid körning men är gitignorade — de committas inte, i linje med
projektets etablerade konvention.

## Nästa steg

`05_story.ipynb` — datastory/presentationsunderlag baserat på dessa resultat.

author: simonbleher
body:
`buildBifrostEntry()` in `bin/install.js` writes `url: BIFROST_URL` — the value
resolved at install time — into `~/.claude/mcp.json`, while the `x-bf-vk` header
correctly stays the literal template `${BIFROST_VK}`.

This contradicts the README ("## What gets written to mcp.json"), which shows both
`url` and the VK header as `${...}` templates resolved at runtime. The
marketplace/.mcp.json path already uses `${BIFROST_URL}` (and works — Claude Code
expands it at runtime), so the installer path is the odd one out: it snapshots the
URL, going stale if the gateway URL changes without re-running the installer.

Fix: write the `${BIFROST_URL}` template, matching the VK header, the .mcp.json
path, and the README. Side effect: the installer's idempotency check no longer
rewrites the entry on every URL change.

author: tombeckenham
body:
Closes #871

## Summary

Adds **Gemini Omni Flash** (`gemini-omni-flash-preview`) — Google's multimodal video-generation model with conversational editing — to `@tanstack/ai-gemini`. Omni only serves the Interactions API (`generateContent` rejects it with a 400), so the video adapter now routes by model: Veo models keep the `:predictLongRunning` operations flow, while `geminiVideo('gemini-omni-flash-preview')` creates a background interaction, polls it by id, and returns the finished clip through the existing `generateVideo()` jobs API.

## What changed

- **Adapter** (`packages/ai-gemini`): Interactions-based job path — `interactions.create` with Step-list input, `response_modalities: ['video']`, `background: true`; `interactions.get` polling; inline base64 MP4 surfaced as a `data:video/mp4;base64,…` URL (Files-API URI delivery passes through). Usage maps from `output_tokens_by_modality`. `size` maps onto `response_format.aspect_ratio` (`'16:9' | '9:16'`) and `duration` onto `response_format.duration` — any value in the 3–10 second range (fractional seconds included), defaulting to a 10s clip when omitted. The range was verified against the live API (the docs do not publish the field; out-of-range values are rejected with explicit min/max errors, and a 3s request returns a 3.008s MP4 per ffprobe). Image **and** video prompt parts are sent as interaction content blocks in order (`data` sources inline; `url` sources pass through untouched — never downloaded). `modelOptions.previous_interaction_id` chains conversational video edits.
- **Model meta / options**: `GEMINI_OMNI_FLASH_PREVIEW` ($0.10/sec), `GEMINI_INTERACTIONS_VIDEO_MODELS`, `GeminiOmniVideoProviderOptions` derived from the SDK's `CreateModelInteractionParamsNonStreaming`, per-model input modalities (Omni: image + video).
- **Core type fix** (`@tanstack/ai`, patch): `generateVideo` / `getVideoJobStatus` constrained adapters as `VideoAdapter<string, any, any, any>`, which rejected any adapter with a narrowed per-model duration union (Omni's `10`, Veo's `4 | 6 | 8`) under strict contravariance. Constraints now span all six generics.
- **Dependency**: `@google/genai` floor `^2.8.0` → `^2.10.0` (Interactions API surface).
- **Example** (`examples/ts-react-media`): Omni text-to-video + image-to-video entries exercising all inputs — text, start image, attached reference/edit video clip (Omni-only), and an "Edit" box on completed videos that chains `previous_interaction_id`.
- **Docs/skill**: `docs/media/video-generation.md` Omni section (interactions flow, inline `data:` URLs, conversational editing), media-generation skill update.

## Testing

- **Live-verified against the real Gemini API**: generation (~45s, valid 2.6 MB MP4, usage `{promptTokens: 16, completionTokens: 58728, totalTokens: 59052}`) and edit chaining via `previous_interaction_id` (~60s, edited clip; prior video reported as input tokens). The issue's SDK-vs-REST 400 caveat is resolved — the typed `interactions.create()` works with Step-list input, no raw REST fallback needed.
- 17 new unit tests (request shape, status mapping, inline/URI extraction, usage, typed durations) — 40 pass in the video suite.
- New `interactions-video` E2E feature backed by a dedicated aimock mount at `/omni-video` (aimock's native interactions text handling untouched); all video + stateful-interactions specs pass.
- `pnpm test:pr` green (sherif, knip, docs, kiira, eslint, lib, types, build across 50 projects).

author: cmeier76
body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to the Docker build and development workflow for the project, focusing on increased flexibility in dependency management, enhanced configuration via environment variables, and updated documentation to reflect these changes. The most significant updates are in the `Dockerfile.zms`, `Dockerfile.fastapi`, and `compose.yaml`, allowing for more dynamic and customizable builds, as well as easier local development and debugging.

**Docker build and dependency management improvements:**

* Refactored `Dockerfile.zms` and `Dockerfile.fastapi` to support new build arguments (`ZMS_EXTRAS`, `FASTAPI_EXTRAS`, `UPDATE_DEPENDENCIES`, `UPDATE_EXTRAS`, and `PYTHON_VERSION`), enabling conditional installation of dependencies and extras, and allowing for more flexible and progressive dependency updates. The FastAPI image now uses the official Python base image instead of a custom one. 

* Updated `compose.yaml` and `versions.env` to add and propagate new build arguments for dependency and extras selection, aligning environment variable usage across the stack for easier customization and reproducibility.

* Improved local and container development setup by updating volume mounts, user configuration, and asset linking in `compose.yaml` and Dockerfiles, making it easier to synchronize code and assets for development and debugging.

author: pepebndc
body:
## Summary

Adds a **baseline documentation section for OpenZeppelin Contracts for Tron**, mirroring the structure of the existing Solidity contracts docs. Content is ported from the [`tron-contracts`](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/tron-contracts) and [`tron-contracts-upgradeable`](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/tron-contracts-upgradeable) repositories' AsciiDoc docs and converted to MDX, and is **aligned with the released npm packages**: [`@openzeppelin/tron-contracts`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openzeppelin/tron-contracts) and [`@openzeppelin/tron-contracts-upgradeable`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openzeppelin/tron-contracts-upgradeable) (currently `5.6.0-rc.1` on the `latest` tag).

The new section is available at `/tron-contracts`, selectable via the **Tron** entry in the ecosystem switcher.

## What's included

**16 pages** under `content/tron-contracts/`:

- **Overview**, **TVM Differences**
- Guides: Extending Contracts, Using with Upgrades, Backwards Compatibility, Access Control
- Tokens: TRC-20 (+ Creating Supply), TRC-721, TRC-1155, TRC-4626, TRC-6909
- Modules: Governance, Utilities, FAQ

**TRON branding** — official logomark icon, ecosystem tab, homepage ecosystem card + brand color (`#EF0027`), and full navigation wiring.

## Release alignment (second commit)

The pages were re-verified against both source repos at the 5.6.0-rc.1 release, covering the full audit-fix wave that landed after the original port:

- **Released and audited**: the library's audit completed in August 2026; the docs no longer carry "unaudited / active development" framing. The index links the published npm packages, ports the repo's versioning policy (minors track upstream, patches independent), removes bug-bounty claims, and points security reports at GitHub security advisories (per tron-contracts #140/#142).
- **Install**: `npm install @openzeppelin/tron-contracts` (tag `latest`, audited) and `@next` for release candidates. The `@dev` example was dropped: npm publishes no `dev` tag (the release-tag policy table itself is kept as published in the repo docs).
- **Audit-fix accuracy**: `SafeTRC20.safeTransferChecked` as the USDT-safe default (H-01, #131) including the TRC-4626 fee example; `trc7201Slot` (L-04, #115); TRC165/TRC1271 artifact renames (#126); TRON block-time governance arithmetic and TRC-6372/TRC-5805 (#116); AccessManager cancellation rights including role admins (#141); TimelockController self-administration; Tron Upgrades plugins recommendations (#132).
- **TVM differences**: P256 verifies in pure Solidity with the TIP-7951 precompile cited as specified-but-not-yet-active on mainnet (matching tron-contracts master; the precompile-only design is a separate open PR there); corrected EIP-7702 / ERC-4337 rows; new "Native TRC-10 assets" section (#130/#133) and a callout on 20-byte addresses inside `bytes` payloads (#117/#136).

## Notes / decisions

- **Examples are inlined** as Solidity code blocks, verified against the released `contracts/mocks/docs/` sources.
- **Placed as a flat, unversioned section** (like Sui/Stylus).
- Upstream follow-up flagged for the repo docs (not this PR): the repo's `index.adoc` still shows a `npm install @openzeppelin/tron-contracts@dev` example although no `dev` dist-tag is published.

## Validation

- `pnpm build` passes (full static generation).
- Branch rebased onto latest `main` (Tron + Canton ecosystem entries merged).

author: kamegoro
body:
## Summary

Deep dive into the plugin's core touchpoint — the suggestion float — against toast-notification conventions, the Clippy failure postmortems, and habit-loop (cue/routine/reward) design research. Full writeup is in #71; this closes it.

- **Fixed a real bug**: `ICON` in `ui/float.lua` was an empty string despite a comment claiming it was a nerd-font icon. The suggestion window has been rendering with no brand icon at all.
- **"Why now"**: `logger.lua` already threads the detected pattern name through `on_pattern`, but `suggest.lua`'s `M.queue(_, cmd)` discarded it one line before it could reach the display. Threaded it through to `ui.float.show`, added a reason line per pattern (34 × en/ja) plus a generic template for idle-triggered suggestions with no single trigger event.
- **Category color**: the border is now colored by category (motion/edit/search/window/fold/mark/macro) via new `TobiraSuggest*` highlight groups, so a returning user can recognize the kind of suggestion without reading.
- **No way to make it go away**: ambient (idle) suggestions never showed a mute hint — only `:Tobira` manual invocations did. Added a persistent, de-emphasized `:TobiraProgress x to mute` footer shown in both modes.
- **Reward loop**: `watch_adoption()` silently marked commands as adopted with zero user-facing feedback — the habit loop had a cue and a routine but no reward. Added a one-time `celebrate()` toast the first time a suggestion is ever adopted, tracked via a new `celebrated` field with a safe migration.
- **Duration**: auto-dismiss now scales with content length within the 6–9s toast convention instead of a fixed 10s for everything.
- **Docs**: fixed the README/vimdoc claim that suggestions route through `vim.notify`/nvim-notify — they never have; the window is always tobira's own float (nvim-notify only affects color matching).

## Why

Full research and reasoning in #71. Short version: the plugin's entire value proposition is "notices your habits and helps you improve" but the one feature people see every day never explained its own reasoning, had no way to be muted in-place, and gave zero feedback when it actually worked.

## Test plan
- [x] `stylua --check lua/ plugin/` — clean
- [x] `selene --display-style=quiet lua/ plugin/` — 0 errors/warnings
- [x] Full test suite (598 tests) — all green
- [x] Coverage — 100.00%
- [ ] Manual smoke test in a real Neovim session (GIFs/demo update as a follow-up if desired)

Closes #71

author: kbwen
body:
## What

Post-release hardening from a **5-simulation stability wave** on v1.8.7 (2× fresh-adopter deploy, hotfix e2e in an isolated worktree, 2× adversarial red-team, `/govern-audit` dogfood — all subagent-run; **every finding independently re-verified against the code by the primary** before action). Goal was to confirm v1.8.7 is stable for a month and fix anything real before it settles.

**Headline: no stability regression anywhere.** Every new v1.8.7 check is fail-safe in the regression direction; the adopter deploy is clean end-to-end and the deployed governance actually enforces (accepts a well-formed quick-win log, rejects a broken one); `/hotfix` §6 (added #309) and `/govern-audit` (#311) are both executable end-to-end from their own docs. This PR fixes the **two genuine correctness bugs I introduced this session** (both fail-safe) plus two triple-corroborated doc gaps.

## Fixes

| ID | Defect (verified both code sides) | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **F1** | `validate.ps1` D4 built the check's Python by interpolating the INDEX path into a raw single-quoted literal (`idx = r'...'`). A repo path with an apostrophe (e.g. `C:\Users\O'Brien\...`) → `SyntaxError` → empty child output → the default `PASS` silently masks a real dangling reference on Windows. `validate.sh` was always immune (argv). | Pass the path via `sys.argv[1]` (mirror of sh); empty/unrecognized child output now WARNs instead of defaulting to PASS. |
| **F2** | Both validators parsed only bold `- **Created Date**:`, but the template and **all 40+ real logs** use plain/backtick/table form → `created_date` always empty → the legacy gate-evidence exemption, and hence the **D5 tightening shipped in #308, never executed** (dead code). | Widen both parsers to list/bold/backtick/table (mirroring how sibling header fields are already parsed). Fail-safe: no existing log predates the 2026-03-25 cutoff → zero current verdict flips; the mechanism now works as its ship record claims. |
| **doc** | `templates/worklog.md` Phase Summary never mentioned the `⚡ ACX` sentinel that `validate.sh` checks for there (a WARN I hit all session). | +1 line stating the requirement. |
| **F3** | `/govern-audit` (shipped #311) was missing from the gate-parser's out-of-band support-workflow exclusion allowlist (`retro/research/brainstorm/decide/audit`) in **both** validators — its sibling `audit` had it. A stray `Gate: govern-audit` receipt would false-FAIL as illegal progression. Surfaced by the `/govern-audit` dogfood (which independently re-confirmed F1+F2). | Add `govern-audit` to both allowlists (defense-in-depth; parity with `audit`). |
| **doc** | `ship.md` step 3 never said archival is a MOVE not a copy (I made this exact mistake; the leftover copy WARNs + counts toward the active-log limit — flagged by 3 independent sims). | +clause: MOVE, delete the `work/` original (compressed to stay under the 355k token ceiling — deletion-funded, no bump). |

Both F1 and F2 touch `validate.sh` + `validate.ps1` with sh/ps1 parity; 2 structural lock tests added (`test_ps1_d4_passes_index_path_as_argv...`, `test_created_date_parser_accepts_non_bold_forms...`).

## Findings NOT fixed here (dispositioned, no release churn)

- **Backlog #113** (P2): `--no-python` gate-progression fallback checks receipt *presence* not *ordering/completeness*, so a feature skipping review/test/handoff prints "integrity check passed" — pre-existing reduced-assurance path (connects #103b).
- **Backlog #114** (P3): tiny-fix self-labeling has no validator visibility (no Work Log) — inherent honor-system limit.
- **Close-with-reason** (recorded in Work Log): fabricated-but-perfect chain = the documented honest ceiling (enforces sequencing, not truth-of-work); `/govern-audit` permitted-writes is prose-tier by design (real control = path-based guard, applies regardless of workflow); D4 `..`/non-JSON/duplicate all fail-safe; docs-pins has no coverage hole; 2 cosmetic `/govern-audit` doc ambiguities — marginal.

## Evidence

- `validate.ps1` (fixed): `pass=111 warn=5 fail=0`; D4 now reads via argv ("86 checked").
- F1/F2 structural lock tests + existing D4/D5: 4 passed.
- F2 sh parser extracts the date from list/bold/backtick/table forms (verified).
- Full CI-equiv sweep + `validate.sh` fail=0: in PR checks / Work Log.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. F1 = argv correctness; F2 = parser widening (fail-safe, activates a dormant-but-correct mechanism); docs = prose. No new gate, no engine change.

- **Ollama provider** — run agents against open-weight models locally (`/api/chat`, NDJSON streaming) or via Ollama Cloud (OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, SSE), auto-detected from the base URL, with tool calling in both modes. Point any agent at a non-default endpoint with the new `agent.BaseURL` / `micro.AgentBaseURL` option. (`ai/ollama/`, `examples/agent-ollama/`)
- **Retrieval-backed agent memory** — agents can recall relevant prior turns by similarity, not just the recent window, with a summarizer hook that compacts older history so long conversations stay in budget. (`agent/`)
- **Scheduled flows** — a flow can run an agent (or any step) on a cron-style schedule, with the dispatch traced end to end. (`flow/`)
- **Flow verification/grader loop** — a workflow can grade its own step output against a rubric and retry until it passes, plus run-trace analysis to surface where a flow spends its time. (`flow/`)
- **A2A streaming & continuity** — outbound agent streaming flows through the A2A binding (`message/stream`), with `tasks/resubscribe` and `input-required` handoffs for multi-turn interop. (`gateway/a2a/`)

##### Changed

- **Agent tool-call resilience** — opt-in retries around agent tool calls, and a fallback that executes tool calls emitted as text by weaker models so they still make progress. (`agent/`)
- **Hardened agent durability** — terminal failure statuses are classified and surfaced, and durable resume-after-restart is covered by tests. (`agent/`)

##### Documentation

- **"Your first agent" walkthrough** and a canonical 0-to-hero reference path, lowering the on-ramp from install to a running agent. (`internal/website/docs/`)
- **Discord** linked prominently across the README, website nav/footer, and docs. (`https://discord.gg/G8Gk5j3uXr`)

author: monkeytower
body:
## Summary

- **landr-db45** (Opus review #122 M1): App and CustomFormStep each fetched `public_get_product_flow` independently with no shared cache. If App's fetch produced the custom-form step but CustomFormStep's own separate later fetch transiently failed (or returned a flow missing the form key), CustomFormStep set `fetchError` and permanently disabled Continue — a forward dead-end under flaky networks (Back still worked; Continue never would).
- Fix: thread the already-resolved flow from App's `ensureProductFlow`/`withResolvedFlow` cache down into `CustomFormStep` as a new `flow` prop. The form def is now derived synchronously from the already-fetched flow on the happy path — no second network request, so it can never race into the dead-end.
- Consistent with the recently-merged `iyyf` work (widget#139): reuses the same `remoteFlow`/`clearProductFlowCache` cache rather than adding a parallel one. `flow === undefined` (prop genuinely absent — older/standalone callers) falls back to the original self-fetch behaviour unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `rm -rf node_modules/.tmp && npx tsc -b` — 0 errors, whole-project build
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm test` — 1037/1037 passed, including a new regression test (`Continue stays enabled even when a later independent getProductFlow call would fail`) that reproduces the original dead-end: App resolves the custom-form step, then simulates every SUBSEQUENT `getProductFlow` call rejecting, and proves Continue still works end-to-end (and that only 1 call to `getProductFlow` happens at all)

author: kuyziss
body:
## Summary

Enable tracing span attribute enrichment for OTLP log export.

The current OTLP log bridge only records event fields. When logs are emitted inside active `tracing` spans, span fields are not copied onto the resulting OTLP log record. This enables `opentelemetry-appender-tracing`'s `experimental_span_attributes` feature and switches the OTLP log layer to the builder API with `TracingSpanAttributes::all()`.

This intentionally does not include span-name enrichment; that depends on a separate upstream OpenTelemetry appender API (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-rust/pull/3466).

author: alevant1905
body:
## What this does

Full GUI overhaul to the **Midnight Glass** direction Alex chose from four interactive mockups: deep-navy night gradients, frosted-glass cards, electric blue→cyan gradient accents with soft glows, Space Grotesk display type — applied consistently across all 14 pages, on PC and iPhone.

## How it works

Every page already declared the same palette variables (`--cream`, `--paper`, `--ink`, …) in its own inline `:root`. `blue.css` now overrides them under `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, which out-specifies the pages' own blocks — so **midnight is the default everywhere at once**, with zero changes to most page markup. The existing floating toggle now switches to `data-theme="light"`, where every midnight rule stands down and the original cream styling shows through untouched.

**Vilda's kid chat is pixel-identical**: `blue.js` pins `body.kid` pages to the light theme and skips the toggle and nav drawer entirely.

## New site-wide navigation

`blue.js` injects a glass hamburger button + slide-in drawer on every page (except login and kid mode): sectioned links (Talk / Know / Robots), current page highlighted, 44px touch targets, safe-area insets for the iPhone notch. No more dead-ending back to the home page to move between sections.

## Stragglers brought onto the system

body:
## What Adds an `el-linear project-updates {create, list, read}` command group for Linear's native **project update** entity — the status posts that appear in a project's Updates feed, with a health color — via the `projectUpdateCreate` mutation. This is distinct from the existing `projectUpdate(id, input)` project-*edit* mutation (`projects` command); the naming collision in Linear's schema (`projectUpdate` the verb vs. `ProjectUpdate` the noun) is why this lives under its own `project-updates` namespace, mirroring `project-milestones`. ## Why Downstream, the `transcript-processing` skill posts a meeting note's summary to the relevant Linear project as a project update. There was no clean CLI path — only a raw `graphql` call or a mis-targeted project *document*. Per "strengthen the tool first", it belongs in el-linear as a first-class command. ## Surface - `project-updates create --project

--body|--body-file <…> [--health onTrack|atRisk|offTrack] [--diff-hidden] [-q]` - `--body`/`--body-file` mutually exclusive, exactly one required (mirrors `comments create`). - `--health` validated against the enum **before** the API call. - `-q/--quiet` prints ` `. - `project-updates list --project

[-l]` - `project-updates read ` A dedicated summary formatter renders health/author/created/url. Because a `ProjectUpdate` node carries `body` + `createdAt` + `user` like a comment, the summary inference heuristic keys on `health` and is **ordered before** the comment check — unit-tested both ways so a health-less comment still classifies as a comment. ## Testing - `src/queries/project-updates.test.ts` — GraphQL validity + variable/field assertions. - `src/commands/project-updates.test.ts` — create (body, health valid/invalid, `--body-file`, mutual-exclusion, missing-body, API failure), list, read (found/not-found). - `src/utils/formatters/summary.test.ts` — formatter output + the comment-vs-project-update inference disambiguation + `formatLine` quiet render. - Full suite green (1815 tests), typecheck + biome clean. - Live-verified against the real API: `list` on an existing project and a `create` smoke post both round-trip correctly. Refs DEV-5353.

body:
## Why (SUR-741)
`enqueue_book`/`enqueue_note` carried the SUR-724-era **partial** column sets, so native could round-trip-*preserve* a book's cover or a note's source-metadata but never **author** them. Those columns are already in `synced_schema()` — only the FFI was too narrow. Blocks 660/661 (which consume the FFI).

## What
Widen in place (recommendation, founder decision #1 — no shipped native hosts; an additive `_v2` doubles the surface for no consumer):
- `enqueue_book` += `isbn`, `cover_url`, `cover_source`, `cover_resolved_at`
- `enqueue_note` += `source`, `source_id`, `source_meta_json`, `chapter`, `image_path`, `ink_crop_path`

### Rules that carry the correctness
- **`None` → column omitted** (partial-patch): server `merge-duplicates` + local `stage_write` merge touch only supplied columns, so a `None` never clobbers a pulled-only column (the `enqueue_book_edit_preserves_pulled_only_columns` contract holds). **Consequence (founder decision #2):** native can't yet *clear* a field to NULL — tri-state deferred to a 660/661 follow-up, noted in the method docs.
- **`source`** is the one always-sent optional: `None` → `"manual"` (the PWA's `|| 'manual'`).
- **`source_meta_json`** (founder decision #3) is a JSON **object** string, parse-validated at enqueue → invalid JSON / non-object = `SyncError::Store`, **nothing staged** (atomic).
- Column names mirror surfc `upsertBook`/`upsertNote` exactly → no payload key outside `synced_schema()` (vendored-schema drift guard stays green).
- **Seal-at-write unchanged:** only `plaintext` is sealed (enc:v2, AAD = note id) + `content_tag` from plaintext; the new fields never touch the `Vault` (crypto-reviewer line).

## Tests (local: 87 lib tests + fmt + clippy green)
- **Unit:** author cover fields; author widened note + `source_meta` parsed to a JSON object; `source None→"manual"` + others omitted; invalid `source_meta_json` rejected atomically (nothing staged); note edit omit-preserves (`image_path`/`source_id`/`chapter`) while `source` resets; ciphertext + `content_tag` invariants on the widened path.
- **Integration** (`#[ignore]`, CI `sync-integration`): new `native_authors_cover_and_source_metadata_to_the_server` — native-authored book-with-cover + note-with-source-metadata round-trips to the server, with the note text still enc:v2 on the wire.
- **Bindings:** regenerated via `scripts/gen-bindings.sh` (the SUR-742 `bindings-drift` guard verifies — re-gen is byte-stable); Kotlin + Swift round-trip tests call a widened method incl. the invalid-JSON rejection crossing the FFI.

## Residual-doc cleanup (folded in, now that SUR-743 merged)
Removed the stale allocation-order caveats in `src/sync/http.rs` (`get_page`) + `src/sync/pull.rs` (module doc) and updated the CHANGELOG residual note to **closed** — surfc `0052` made `change_seq` commit-ordered.

## Sequencing
Branched off `main` **after** PR-B (#13, guard active — it verifies these regenerated bindings) and **after** PR-A/#335 (so the residual-doc cleanup is truthful). No stacked PRs.

## Gate
`touches-ffi` (nightly macOS Swift leg). `sync-reviewer` + `crypto-reviewer` + `naming-reviewer` + founder. Agent under the gate — not merging.

## Summary

The env expression itself (`github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'dev' || 'prod'`) was flagged in the issue as *possibly* confusing, but the issue author explicitly asked to "confirm it matches intent" rather than requesting a swap. author: herbert-consult-bot
body:
## Problem

Wenn Lena eine Mail mit `action='ablegen'` kategorisiert (`POST /api/lena/mail/categorize`), wurde die Mail nur mit dem Outlook-Tag `Lena: Ablegen` versehen — aber **nicht archiviert**.

Lena musste danach manuell `archive-by-category` aufrufen. Das hat sie vergessen. Resultat: Mails häuften sich mit der Ablegen-Kategorie im Posteingang an, bis Sven explizit "bitte alle Mails archivieren" sagt.

**Log-Beweis:** 3× `422 Unprocessable Content` auf `archive-by-category` (Lena hat versucht, es richtig zu machen, aber mit falschem Request-Body-Format), dann eine `200`-Erfolgsmeldung erst nach Svens explizitem Befehl.

## Lösung

`POST /api/lena/mail/categorize` mit `action='ablegen'` archiviert die Mail jetzt **sofort** via `PATCH parentFolderId` auf den Archive-Ordner — gleiche Logik wie `archive-by-category`.

- Kategorie wird gesetzt (bisheriges Verhalten bleibt)
- Danach direkt: Mail in Archive verschieben
- Bei Fehler beim Archivieren: geloggt, nicht als HTTP-Fehler zurückgegeben (die Kategorie wurde korrekt gesetzt, das Archivieren ist non-fatal)
- Response enthält neu: `moved_to_archive: Optional[bool]`

## Geänderte Dateien

- `api.py`: `LenaCategorizeResponse` + `lena_mail_categorize`

## Test

1. Mail im Inbox haben
2. `POST /api/lena/mail/categorize {"message_id":"...", "action":"ablegen"}`
3. Mail sollte sofort im Archive sein → Response enthält `"moved_to_archive": true`
4. Anderer action-Wert (z.B. `"antworten"`) → `"moved_to_archive": null`, Mail bleibt in Inbox

Fixes: HBE-1603 (wiederkehrende "Mails nicht archiviert"-Beschwerden)

author: mitsuru
body:
## 背景

セキュリティスキャナの指摘 (`c5b059c1`, high / attack-path high) への対応。

`crates/fulgur/src/gcpm/target_ref.rs` の `compute_first_letter()` が、対象テキストを `trim_start` した後に **全書記素を `Vec<&str>` へ materialize** してから、先頭の first-letter プレフィックス (`gs[..j].concat()`) だけを返していました。

攻撃者が制御できる巨大なテキストノードを持つ id 付き要素に対して、CSS の `target-text(attr(href), first-letter)` を向けると:

- pass 1 で対象要素のテキスト全体が `AnchorEntry.text` に格納される
- pass 2 で `compute_first_letter()` が呼ばれ、**返り値が1書記素でも全長分の fat pointer (64bit で約 16 bytes/byte)** を確保する

untrusted HTML/CSS をサーバサイドでレンダリングする脅威モデルにおいて、これは OOM / DoS ベクタになります（検証では 5,000 万書記素で `memory allocation of 536870912 bytes failed`、n=100 万で `peak_live=16777217` と入力に線形増加を確認済み）。

## 修正

`graphemes(true).collect::<Vec<&str>>()` をやめ、`grapheme_indices(true)` で**遅延イテレート**するように変更しました。

- 先頭の任意 punctuation 連 → 最初の letter → 末尾の punctuation 連、まで走査したところで **早期に打ち切る**
- 保持するのはバイトオフセット (`first_letter_end`) のみで、返却は `trimmed[..end].to_string()`
- 確保量が返却プレフィックス長に限定され、末尾に巨大なテキストがあっても走査・確保しない

## 挙動の等価性

`is_punct` / `is_letter` の判定は不変で、同じ書記素列に対して選択されるバイト範囲だけが問題になります。`idx + g.len()` は次の書記素の開始バイトオフセット（＝旧コードの `j` 境界）と一致するため、`trimmed[..first_letter_end] == gs[..j].concat()` が成り立ちます。既存の behavioral テスト（先頭 punct 保持、末尾 punct 取り込み、書記素クラスタ、通貨記号拡張、空文字ケース等）はすべて変更なしでパスします。

`Content` / `Before` / `After` は元々テキストをそのまま clone する（出力＝入力サイズ）ため増幅は無く、対象外です。この1修正で CLI / Python / WASM いずれの経路もカバーします（すべて `resolve_target_text` を経由）。

## テスト

- `cargo test -p fulgur --lib` … 1553 passed
- `cargo test -p fulgur --test gcpm_integration` … 13 passed
- `cargo clippy -p fulgur --lib` … warning なし
- `cargo fmt --check` … OK
- 回帰テスト `first_letter_large_tail_stops_early` を追加（先頭に letter + 100万文字の tail → 出力 `"H"`、早期打ち切りのオフセット経路を exercise）

Fixes fulgur-lfgg

author: jsonbored
body:
## Summary

Closes #2539.

An earlier roadmap item (#1941) collapsed most repeated check/status reads onto a shared per-request cache used by the readiness check, the maintenance planner, and the post-publish boundary. This issue identified two remaining call sites that bypass it: the staged-merge approval-queue acceptance path (`decidePendingAgentAction`) and the auto-maintain action executor's own pre-mutation re-check (`executeAgentMaintenanceActions`).

**This PR's history reflects a real correction, not just an implementation.** My first commit implemented a coalescing shortcut (`prefetchedLiveCi`) between these two call sites, on the assumption that they run "moments apart, in the same synchronous accept pass." The gate's own AI review correctly flagged this as unsafe. I traced the actual call chain and confirmed the review's finding — the assumption was wrong, and I reverted the shortcut in a follow-up commit. Both commits are visible in this PR's history for anyone who wants the full story.

## What the gate found, and what I verified

Between `decidePendingAgentAction`'s accept-time CI read and the eventual `mergePullRequest` mutation, there is real, non-trivial async work:

1. `Promise.all([isHoldOnly(env, ...), isCloseHoldOnly(env, ...)])` — two DB reads.
2. When a merge is staged and the author is close-eligible: `createInstallationToken(...)` + `resolveLinkedIssueHardRule(...)` — a live GitHub API call when hard rules are configured for the repo.
3. Inside `executeAgentMaintenanceActions` itself, before reaching the (previously coalesced) CI check: the freshness guard's `fetchPullRequestFreshness(...)` — an **unconditional** live GitHub call checking the PR's current head SHA.

That is exactly the window the executor's pre-mutation CI re-check (#2128) exists to catch a CI flip in — its own doc comment says so explicitly: *"Re-read live CI right before the mutation so a check that flipped in this narrow window is never acted on from stale information."* Reusing the earlier accept-time read defeated the guard it was reusing, on the merge/close actuation boundary — exactly the class of bug #4220 was about.

## What changed

- **Reverted** `prefetchedLiveCi` entirely: the field on `AgentActionExecutionContext`, its capture/thread-through in `decidePendingAgentAction`, and the reuse branch in `executeAgentMaintenanceActions`'s pre-mutation check, which now always fetches fresh again — byte-identical to before #2539.
- **Replaced** the 3 coalescing tests (which asserted the now-reverted behavior) with one regression test asserting the correct always-two-fetches behavior, so this specific unsafe shortcut can't be silently reintroduced.
- **#2539's other orphaned call site is unaffected and remains correctly coalesced**: the duplicate-sibling reconciliation and gate-override reads (`cachedFetchLivePullRequestState` / `cachedFetchLivePullRequestHeadSha`), already shipped in #2537 — those are genuinely non-authoritative reads, not the merge/close actuation boundary this PR is about, and don't share the same async-gap risk.

## Why this is still a legitimate resolution of #2539

The issue's own requirement was explicit: *"Preserve the requirement that these are act-boundary reads... this is a coalescing fix, not a staleness-tolerance fix."* Having verified that the ONE remaining orphaned pairing (`decidePendingAgentAction` ↔ `executeAgentMaintenanceActions`) cannot be coalesced without becoming a staleness-tolerance change, the correct outcome — consistent with how #2541 (review-enrichment cost-class parallelization) and #2543 (rate-limit-observation write batching) were also resolved in this same roadmap — is to document why, not force an unsafe implementation to satisfy the issue's original framing.

## Tests

- `test/unit/agent-action-executor.test.ts`: removed the 4 tests exercising the reverted `prefetchedLiveCi` reuse/mismatch/heuristic-close/no-prefetch paths.
- `test/unit/agent-approval-queue.test.ts`: replaced the 3 coalescing tests with one regression test asserting `fetchLiveCiAggregate` is called exactly twice for a full successful staged-merge accept (once for the #2126 accept-time re-check, once for the executor's #2128 pre-mutation re-check) — locking in the correct, non-coalesced behavior.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npx vitest run test/unit/agent-action-executor.test.ts test/unit/agent-approval-queue.test.ts` (118 tests pass)
- `npm run test:ci` (the full local gate, exit 0)
- `git diff --check`
- Diff-level coverage check: 100% of changed lines/branches covered per `coverage/lcov.info`

## Scope

- [x] Change is narrow and limited to the stated problem
- [x] No secrets, wallets, hotkeys, trust scores, or reward values added anywhere
- [x] No edits to `site/`, `CNAME`, `**/lovable/**`, or `CHANGELOG.md`

## Safety

- [x] No auth/session/CORS surface touched
- [x] The merge/close actuation boundary (#4220's own concern) is now verified, via a direct trace of the async call chain and a regression test, to always force-refetch live CI immediately before mutation

author: roninsightrx
body:
## Why

Part of the API cleanup (#223); collapses the model-constructor surface per the
naming rule + hard-break policy decided in #224. Two functions did overlapping
"give me a model" jobs: `ferx_model()` (wrap an existing `.ferx` file) and
`ferx_model_new()` (scaffold a new file from a template). One constructor,
`ferx_model()`, now covers both. This is the last of the #227/#230/#231
rename/delete blockers ahead of the file-split in #225.

## What changed

`ferx_model_new()` is **removed**. Scaffolding is now a mode of `ferx_model()`,
selected by `template =` (or `print = TRUE` to preview a skeleton without
writing a file):

- Old output arg `path` (1st positional) moves to the named `path =` arg.
- Scaffold mode returns a `ferx_model` **object** (not the file path), so it
  pipes straight into `ferx_fit()`.
- Template skeletons moved into an internal `.ferx_model_skeleton()` helper.
- Wrap mode (`ferx_model(data, model)`) and its back-compat arg-order shim are
  unchanged.

```r
# before
ferx_model_new("m.ferx", template = "1cpt_oral", edit = FALSE)
ferx_model_new(print = TRUE)

# after
ferx_model(template = "1cpt_oral", path = "m.ferx", edit = FALSE)
ferx_model(print = TRUE)

# scaffold + fit in one pipe (new capability)
ferx_model(template = "1cpt_oral", path = "m.ferx", edit = FALSE) |>
  ferx_fit(data)
```

## Alternatives considered

Keeping scaffold mode returning the path (faithful move) was the other option;
maintainer chose the unified object return so the result is pipe-ready and the
constructor has one consistent return type.

## Cross-repo dependency
| Repo | PR | Status | Must merge first |
|------|----|--------|-----------------|
| ferx-core (engine) | n/a | not needed | — |

## Breaking changes (R users)
- [x] Function signature changed
- [ ] Output column names / types changed
- [ ] New minimum ferx-core version required
- [ ] None

<details>
<summary>Migration notes</summary>

`ferx_model_new(path, template, overwrite, edit, print)` ->
`ferx_model(template = ..., path = ..., overwrite = ..., edit = ..., print = ...)`.
The output path is now the named `path =` argument, and scaffold mode returns a
`ferx_model` object instead of the path string (use `$model` to get the path).

</details>

## Tests
- [x] `testthat` tests added / updated (test-model.R, test-model-pipe.R; 335 pass, 0 fail via `pkgload::load_all` + `test_dir`)
- [ ] `R CMD check` passes (not run locally; CI to confirm)
- [x] Test against real ferx-core binary (not mocked)

## Example (user-facing features only)
- [x] `@examples` block added / updated in `ferx_model()` roxygen
- [ ] Standalone example added to `inst/examples/`
- [ ] Not applicable

## Docs
- [x] `roxygen2` docs updated (man/ + NAMESPACE regenerated, `ferx_model_new.Rd` deleted)
- [x] Vignette updated (`vignettes/articles/model-editing.Rmd`)
- [x] `NEWS.md` entry added

## Checklist
- [x] Not applicable (no ferx-core dependency change in this PR)

## Reviewer hints

Focus on `R/model.R`: the scaffold-vs-wrap mode branch at the top of
`ferx_model()` (triggered by `template =` / `print = TRUE`) and the extracted
`.ferx_model_skeleton()` helper. Downstream chains that fed the old path return
into path-taking fns (`ferx_model_show`, `ferx_model_set_section`) now take
`ferx_model(...)$model`.

## Open questions

None.

author: triplecitiestech
body:
## Summary

Adds a public, unauthenticated `GET /api/health` for external uptime monitoring (UptimeRobot). A homepage 200 only proves Vercel's edge served HTML — it doesn't prove the backend is alive. This verifies the **database is reachable**, which is the shared dependency behind the marketing site, admin portal, customer portal, and every API route.

## Behavior

- `SELECT 1` via the pg pool (`getPool()`), wrapped in `withTimeout(…, 5000)` so a hung DB can't hold the serverless function open.
- **200** `{ status: "ok", checks: { database: { ok: true, latencyMs } } }`
- **503** `{ status: "degraded", checks: { database: { ok: false, error } } }`
- Exposes no secrets, connection strings, or customer data — only up/down, a latency number, and a short error label.
- Not gated by middleware (the matcher excludes `/api`), so monitors can reach it unauthenticated.

## Why it also covers the customer portal

The customer portal (`/portal/[company]/dashboard`) can't load a company or a session if the database is down, so this DB check is the portal's backend readiness signal. The portal's public front door (`/portal`) is monitored separately as a Keyword HTTP check (UptimeRobot config, no code change).

## Testing

- `next lint` clean.

author: kcodea
body:
## What

Dragging a card to a new slot and dropping it — in **both** the warband and the shop — replayed the swap: the dragged card jumped back to its old slot and re-slid to the new one *after* the drop. This fixes it so the card settles in place while its neighbours glide, on both slow drags and quick flicks.

Regression from #131 (`commitMs 0 → 200`).

## How

On a reorder the neighbours slide aside live via CSS transforms while the dragged card holds its old slot invisibly (it rides the drag overlay). On drop the `reposition`/`reorderShop` dispatch reorders the array and the `flipKey` layout effect runs — but by then `dragRef.current.active` is already `false`, so it fell into the `commitMs > 0` branch and ran a whole-row `Flip.from` that animated the dragged card old→new = the replay.

Fix: route drag-drop commits through the same manual per-card FLIP that hand-plays already use, generalized to whichever row the drop landed in:
- At drop, snapshot the row's live card lefts **excluding the dragged card** (it's stale at its old slot). A new `handFlipSelRef` records whether the row is the warband or the tavern.
- Set the existing `handPlaySnapRef` for hand-play, board reorder, and shop reorder.
- The commit branch glides only the cards whose captured spot differs from their final slot; the dragged card, absent from the snapshot, just appears at its committed slot with no slide.

This handles both slow drags (neighbours already home → snap; dragged card excluded → no replay) and quick flicks (neighbours glide from their pre-slide spots), so it's strictly better than either `commitMs` value. `commitMs` now only governs genuine non-drag commits (summons / effects / auto-reposition).

Follow-up (not in this PR): board-*sell* drags still route through the `commitMs` Flip and could show a milder version of this on the gap-close.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — green
- `npm run lint` — green
- `npm test` — 460 passed
- `npm run build:web` — green
- Owner confirmed live in-browser on both rows: the drop settles with neighbours gliding and no post-drop replay.

author: kimbeomgyu
body:
## What

Promotes the per-call cost callback from a hidden, test-only internals param to a **public, documented `GuardOptions.onSpend`**. Every successful guarded call emits a `SpendEvent`:

```ts
guard(client, {
  project: 'my-app',
  dailyCapUSD: 50,
  onSpend: (e) => log(e), // { project, feature, model, usd, dayTotalUsd }
});
```

A hard cap *stops* the bleeding; `onSpend` lets you *watch* it — pipe per-call cost into logs, traces, or a dashboard.

## Why

Direct response to reader feedback on the launch article (dev.to, @raju_dandigam):

> "cost caps plus execution traces feel like two sides of the same safety story."

The `SpendEvent` primitive already existed internally — this just makes it a first-class feature.

## Changes
- `SpendEvent` moved to `types.ts` (re-exported from `guard.ts` for back-compat)
- `onSpend` added to `GuardOptions`; reads `opts.onSpend ?? internals.onSpend` (existing injection still works)
- README: new "See every call's cost (observability)" section + Options block now lists `onSpend`/`onExceeded`
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`; ROADMAP item ticked

## Behavior
- Fires **once per successful call**, synchronously, just before the response returns
- **Never** fires on a blocked (over-cap) call — spend is only recorded on success

## Verification (3-layer)
- ✅ 31/31 unit tests (added `onSpend` accumulation test)
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` clean
- ✅ Biome clean
- ✅ Tarball-install smoke in a fresh consumer: `onSpend` fires per call with accumulating `dayTotalUsd`; over-cap call throws `BudgetExceededError` and emits **no** event; `onExceeded` fires once

release notes 
## libmodbus 3.2.0 (2026-07-02)

- Add `modbus_proxy()` to bridge two Modbus backends (closes #70).
- Add termios2 support to allow custom baud rates (RTU).
- Return an exception response for READ EXCEPTION STATUS (0x07).
- Use `EMBXILVAL` instead of `EMBMDATA` for illegal data value errors.
- `modbus_reply`: reject NULL `req` and `mb_mapping` arguments.
- `modbus_reply`: validate request length before reading per-function fields.
- Fix signed integer overflow in `modbus_get_float_*()` (reported by Dominik
  Blain and Henrik Brodin).
- Fix signed integer overflow in the `MODBUS_GET_INT*_FROM_INT*` macros;
  `MODBUS_GET_INT16_FROM_INT8()` now returns a signed `int16_t` in every context
  (reported by Henrik Brodin - Trail of Bits).
- Fix strict aliasing violation in `modbus_set_float_*()` by using `memcpy`
  (reported by Henrik Brodin).
- Remove dead code (Coverity CID 561619).
- modbus-rtu: don't use `O_EXCL` when opening the device (#760).
- WIN32 compatibility for `setsockopt()` in modbus-tcp.c (#800).
- Check if `ai_list` is null before freeing it (#831).
- Respect user-provided CFLAGS (closes #836).
- Fix test to use `ctx` instead of `invalid_ctx` (closes #791, #792).
- Update documentation of float functions (closes #838).
- Fix documentation examples of `modbus_get_float_*` functions.
- `modbus_reply_exception`: reject a NULL request pointer.
- `modbus_mask_write_register`: validate that `ctx` is not NULL.
- `modbus_write_and_read_registers`: validate `src`/`dest` pointers and counts.
- `modbus_report_slave_id`: reject a NULL `dest` buffer.
- `modbus_get_*_timeout`: validate that the output pointers are not NULL.
- `modbus_mapping_new_start_address`: cap table dimensions.
- `modbus_mapping_new`: reject negative counts.
- `modbus_rtu_set_custom_rts`: reject a NULL callback.
- modbus-rtu: avoid integer overflow in the RTS post-send delay.
- modbus-rtu: check the return values of the RTS ioctl calls.
- modbus-rtu: check the return value when saving termios settings on connect.
- modbus-rtu: report a failure to restore termios settings on close.
- `modbus_new_rtu`: reject negative baud rates.
- modbus-tcp: guard `freeaddrinfo()` against NULL on resolver failure.
- `modbus_new_tcp`: NUL-terminate the IP string when `ip` is NULL.
- `modbus_reply`: validate FC22 request length before writing the register.
- modbus-tcp: keep `ctx->s` consistent across failed or repeated connects (no
  false success on a stale descriptor, no socket leak on reconnect).
- modbus-tcp: don't override the user error recovery mode in the flush overflow
  path.
- modbus-tcp: fully initialize the sigaction struct for the SIGPIPE handler on
  BSD.
- modbus-rtu: fix the Windows serial handle lifecycle (initialize the handle,
  guard close against a never-opened handle and reset it after close).
- modbus-rtu: sleep the RTS turnaround delay in chunks to stay portable with
  `usleep()`.
- `modbus_new_rtu`: validate `data_bit` and `stop_bit` arguments.
- `modbus_send_raw_request_tid`: reject NULL `raw_req` with `EINVAL`.
- `modbus_get_byte_from_bits`: remove an always-false assert and clamp `nb_bits`
  consistently in debug and release builds.
- Preserve errno across the Windows error-recovery paths.
- tests: don't kill the unit test server on RTU bad-CRC frames.
- tests: fix integer overflow in the bandwidth-client rate computation.

## New Contributors
* @micrictor made their first contribution in https://github.com/stephane/libmodbus/pull/831
* @desteemy made their first contribution in https://github.com/stephane/libmodbus/pull/800

author: mfw78
body:
## What

Gates the unauthenticated metrics-server debug routes behind a profiling build and bounds the pprof endpoint.

The `/debug/pprof/profile`, `/debug/memory` and `/debug/heap/dump` routes, their handlers and the `Query`/`Deserialize`/`profiling` imports they need now live in a `debug_routes` module compiled only under `any(feature = "profiling", feature = "jemalloc")`. A default build (bare client, the plain `http-server` recorder build) mounts neither the routes nor the handlers and advertises only `/metrics` and `/health` on the index, so an operator scraping metrics exposes no debug surface and no route the listener does not serve. Within a profiling build the pprof duration is clamped to sixty seconds and served one at a time behind a drop-guarded single-flight latch (the profiler is process-global and each run parks a blocking-pool thread), so the route can no longer be driven to exhaust the pool. The default metrics bind is already localhost (`127.0.0.1`, in the node CLI args), satisfying that acceptance criterion without a change here.

## Why

Closes #282 (part of the observability audit follow-ups). The debug routes mounted unauthenticated on the same listener as `/metrics` in every build, the index advertised them, and pprof accepted a caller-controlled unbounded duration: a denial-of-service lever and an allocator-stats fingerprint on any operator that bound the listener wide.

All three acceptance criteria are met: debug routes unreachable on the default bind in a default build (structural, via the cfg gate, proved by `default_build_index_advertises_no_debug_routes`); pprof duration bounded and concurrent profiles capped (`profile_duration_is_clamped_to_the_bound` plus the single-flight latch); metrics bind defaults to localhost (pre-existing).

## Testing

`cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy -p vertex-observability --features http-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `--all-features` (both cones clean; the gate means the non-profiling cone must compile with no debug machinery); `cargo nextest run -p vertex-observability` in both configs (5/5 non-profiling incl. the no-debug-routes index assertion, 6/6 all-features incl. the clamp and profiling-index assertions).

## Notes

The heap-dump predictable `/tmp` path (symlink and path-leak risk) is left as a residual: it is now reachable only in a heap-profiling build behind the gate, and tightening it (a process-unique directory, path not echoed) is a separable hardening better done with the launcher persistence seam. Flagged here so it is not forgotten.

## AI Assistance

AI Assistance: Claude Code (Fable 5) used for the analysis, implementation and this PR body.

author: markbkk
body: ## Summary Fixes a capture reliability bug where Stop/SubagentStop turn-complete hooks could be suppressed while an earlier detached transcript catch-up was still active. In that case, transcript items were captured, but the final agent-turn seal signal could be missed, leaving agent tool calls/results/final output pending instead of sealing into an embedded Memory Event. This does not change semantic chunking rules. Long agent turns can still roll over at `MEMORY_EVENT_MAX_TOKENS` with `seal_reason = token_limit`; this PR preserves the final Stop/SubagentStop signal for the remaining turn bundle. Root cause: signal-only foreground hooks normally queue detached transcript catch-up and return. The catch-up throttle treated an active earlier catch-up as enough, so a later Stop/SubagentStop hook could avoid queuing its own catch-up payload. Since Stop/SubagentStop is the turn-complete control signal, that left agent bundles waiting for another seal condition. Fix: - Treat Stop/SubagentStop as turn-complete signals that force a detached transcript catch-up even if another catch-up is active or recently failed. - Keep foreground capture from also persisting the same Stop/SubagentStop payload when detached catch-up owns it, avoiding duplicate raw hook payload rows. - Add regression coverage for the active-catch-up case. ## Related Issues None. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Maintenance - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Other ## Validation - author: michaeltrefry
body:
## What

F-017 (candle-gen full review, epic 8979): the shared `nn::linear` re-derived the `[in,out]` weight inside **every** forward via `w.t()?.contiguous()?`, materializing a fresh contiguous copy of the whole weight matrix on each call — ~10+ Linears × 32/36 DiT blocks per upscale step/tile, several GB of transient allocation plus extra kernel launches of pure overhead. The sibling `candle-gen-sam3` `Linear` already stores its weight pre-transposed at load; this closes that drift.

The transpose now happens **once at load**:
- `nn::linear(x, wt, b)` now takes the weight already in the `[in,out]` layout candle's matmul consumes (no per-call transpose/copy). New `nn::transpose_weight` helper produces it.
- `dit::Linear::Dense` and `vae::Linear` store the pre-transposed `wt` (transposed once in `load`).
- The DiT quant path recovers the torch-native `[out,in]` layout by transposing `wt` back **once** inside `quantize` (runs at most once per Linear, never per forward) — GGUF folding is unchanged.

## Why

Pure overhead removal on the hot path. The per-forward math is byte-for-byte the same `x·Wᵀ (+ b)`; only the redundant transpose+copy is eliminated.

## Tests

- **New** `nn::linear_pretransposed_matches_pre_fix_bit_identical`: asserts the optimized `linear` is **bit-identical** (`to_bits()` equality) to the pre-fix path for a 5-D (patchified-token-shaped) input across every leading dim, with and without bias; plus a shape assertion that `transpose_weight` yields exactly `[in,out]` (transposed exactly once, at load).
- Existing DiT quant round-trip tests (`q8_is_near_lossless`, `q4_stays_coherent`, `quantize_skips_indivisible_in_features`, `quantize_is_idempotent`) updated to the new field and still pass — they exercise the transpose-back quantize path.
- `cargo test -p candle-gen-seedvr2 --lib`: 29/29 pass. `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean.

## Validation

GPU-validated on Blackwell **sm_120** with real `numz/SeedVR2_comfyUI` 3B weights (`cuda_upscale_smoke`, bf16, seed 42, 256→1024 4× upscale):
- Coherent upscale, `corr_vs_bicubic=0.9943`, `grad_out=2.497` — identical metrics to the pre-fix baseline.
- **Output byte-identical**: built and ran the same smoke on the pre-fix parent commit; both output PNGs share SHA256 `0ce26432…e15f7` (`cmp` reports IDENTICAL). The refactor changed nothing numerically.

## AC coverage

- Weight transposed exactly once (at load), forward is a plain matmul with no per-call transpose/copy — done for both DiT (`Dense`) and VAE Linears.
- Numerical output preserved exactly (bit-identical unit test + byte-identical real-weight GPU render).
- Quant path preserved (transpose-back once at `quantize`).

## 요약

`automation/major-arcana/` 폴더 아래 YouTube Shorts 자동화 파이프라인을 추가합니다. Major Arcana 22장 덱 전용이며, `automation/multi-deck/`(다른 브랜치)과 파일 충돌 없이 독립적으로 동작합니다.

## 파이프라인 구조

```
node run.js --card "THE LOVERS" --question "Are we meant to be?"
```

한 명령으로 4단계가 순서대로 실행됩니다:

1. **record.js** — Playwright로 `index.html`을 `file://`로 직접 구동, Major Arcana 탭에서 22장 중 3장을 랜덤으로 뽑아 탭/플립/팝업 타이밍을 `metadata.json`에 기록 + 원본 `.webm` 저장
2. **edit.js** — 540×960 → 1080×1920 업스케일, `metadata.json` 타임스탬프 기반으로 캡션 오버레이(`drawtext`) + 탭 효과음(`tick.wav`) 믹싱 → `final.mp4`
3. **thumbnail.js** — `openCardPopup()`을 직접 호출해 목표 카드 팝업만 스크린샷 → 1080×1920 썸네일 (결과 스포일러 없음)
4. **meta.js** — YouTube 제목/설명/해시태그 생성 → `meta.json`

BGM 추가와 실제 업로드는 수동 작업으로 남겨둠 (핸드오버 문서 기준).

## 캡션 설계

- 오프닝 훅: "Starlight Tarot Challenge" + "if THIS card appears... it's a sign"
- 드로우별 리액션: 성공/실패/얼리힛 별도 문구 풀에서 랜덤 선택
- 결과: 성공 시 해당 카드 1줄 의미, 실패 시 마지막으로 뽑힌 카드로 피벗
- CTA: signal + nudge(~45% 확률로 attention word 접두) + action, 항상 bio+comments 언급

## 다른 자동화와의 관계

`automation/multi-deck/`(다른 브랜치)와 건드리는 파일 경로가 전혀 겹치지 않아 두 PR을 순서대로 머지해도 충돌이 없습니다.

## 테스트

- `--seed-success` / `--seed-fail` 플래그로 성공/실패 양쪽 브랜치 파이프라인 검증 완료

## What this PR is

Appendix C already tells teams how to turn repeated workflows into skills, but it stopped at “add it back to this library” and did not say where a skill should graduate once other PODs are expected to install or copy it. This adds a small, practical graduation check that points reusable skills toward the observed shared `razorpay/agent-skills` path, separates shaping from publishing, and calls out review gates for sensitive data workflows.

## Evidence

- Internal Slack signal from `#devex-skills` on 2026-07-02: reviewers discussed `razorpay/agent-skills` PRs, noted that some PRs are auto-reviewed/approved when checks pass, and explicitly required DevX + Security/AppSec review for `merchant-checkout-recovery` because it included restricted customer-contact export and anti-scrape guardrails.
- Existing playbook context already routes skill-authoring questions through [`#rzp-claude-skills`](https://razorpay.slack.com/archives/C0ABFFW6XNW) and [`#devex-skills`](https://razorpay.slack.com/archives/C0A8QFH9KEF) in `prologue/06-people-and-pocs.md`.
- External market signal: Cursor’s 2026-06-30 “MCPs and Organizations in Team Marketplaces” changelog says team admins can configure Team MCP servers once and distribute them across cloud agents, reinforcing that AI tooling is shifting from personal setup to org-distributed tools.

## What changed

- `appendices/C-skills-library/README.md` — adds a “Where reusable skills graduate” section with a copyable graduation check for local helpers, shared repo PRs, sensitive-data review, placement questions, and adoption announcements.
- `appendices/C-skills-library/README.md` — updates the maintenance step to include the distribution surface where other teams can find the skill.

## Why this and not something else

I considered using the same signal for a Black Belt governance update, but the exact review mechanics still appear to be settling. Appendix C is the safer fit: it teaches the PM/designer-facing habit that reusable skills need an owner, searchable shared home, and review path without over-specifying commands or repo layout.

author: ismael-benitez
body:
## Qué añade

Una **vista alternativa** de las escalas, conmutable con un toggle **Tarjetas | Cronología**, que responde a otra pregunta que las tarjetas no cubren: *¿cómo se reparte la entrada/salida en el tiempo y cuándo se satura el puerto?*

**Cronología = eje de tiempo vertical con scroll.** Cada escala se sitúa por su **ETA (▼ entra)** y su **ETD (▲ sale)**, agrupada por día. Cada cabecera de día lleva un **medidor de ocupación** (buques con estancia confirmada ETA+ETD que solapan el día) que **resalta el pico** → los horarios de mayor congestión se ven de un vistazo.

## Detalles

- **Sección "⚠ ATRASADO"** fijada arriba con las salidas demoradas (p. ej. Anna).
- Cada evento reutiliza los helpers existentes para sus chips: `▸ rumbo a Marín`, `⚠ retrasado/adelantado +Xh` (desvío de ETA AP vs AIS).
- **Clic / Enter / Espacio** en un evento abre la misma escala (drawer). Mismo patrón a11y de botón que las tarjetas (`role="button"`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`, foco visible).
- **Ocupación** sobre TODAS las escalas (estado real del puerto, ajeno al filtro); **eventos** sobre el conjunto filtrado → el filtro superior y la búsqueda componen con la vista. El mapa sigue visible en ambas vistas.
- Ocupación basada en estancias **con ETA+ETD confirmados** (no en las Previstas sin ETD, que aparecen como evento ▼): evita inflar el conteo con "llegadas que nunca salen".

## Verificación (Playwright, móvil 430px + escritorio 1300px)

- Toggle conmuta ida y vuelta; 12 tarjetas ↔ 12 eventos (11 próximos + Anna atrasada)
- Días: JUE 2 → JUE 9 JUL · ocupación **5 (pico)** / 3 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 0 / 0
- Sección ATRASADO con Anna (salida demorada); chips `rumbo a Marín` y `retrasado +2h` (Larixborg, Wilson Nice)
- Clic en evento → drawer; **sin overflow horizontal** en ninguna vista/viewport

Incluye el fix del mapa de #11 (rebasada sobre `main`).

author: badgerbees
body:
### What does this PR do?
This PR provides a small C++ micro-optimization for Diffie-Hellman key pair generation in `node:crypto` by removing a redundant runtime type check in `CryptoGenDhKeyPair.cpp`.

Previously, when generating DH parameters, `std::get_if<int>(&m_prime)` was called twice: once in the else if condition, and again inside the block to extract the primeLength value.

This change declares and initializes the primeLength pointer directly within the else if condition. This allows us to safely reuse the result of the `std::get_if` lookup inside the block, avoiding the overhead of querying the variant a second time.

### How did you verify your code works?
- Verified visually that the pointer initialization successfully scopes primeLength to the else if block.
- Confirmed that `paramCtx.setDhParameters` correctly dereferences the initialized *primeLength pointer without altering any of the underlying cryptographic logic.
- Ensured the C++ compiles cleanly and that existing Diffie-Hellman tests continue to pass with identical behavior.

author: thverg
body:
Two CI health fixes:

- **Deprecated actions:** the Build job used `actions/checkout@v2` and `actions/setup-python@v1`, which run on Node.js versions GitHub has deprecated on current runners (the Format job was on v3). All checkout/setup-python steps are bumped to the current majors (v4/v5).
- **Untested Python 3.9:** `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.9"` and carries the `importlib_metadata` backport dependency specifically for 3.9, but the CI matrix only tested 3.10–3.14. This adds 3.9 to the matrix so the claimed lower bound is actually exercised. (If 3.9 is no longer worth supporting, the alternative is bumping `requires-python` to `>=3.10` and dropping the backport shim — happy to rework the PR that way instead.)

Deliberately *not* included: bumping the black pre-commit pin (22.3.0). Every newer black release reformats existing files (black 24.x touches 8 files, 26.x touches 45), so that's better done as a standalone reformat commit to keep other PRs conflict-free.

author: shunsock
body:
## 概要

ドキュメントと実装の突き合わせ監査で見つかった「事実として誤っている記述」を修正する。ソフトウェアとドキュメントの乖離をバグとして扱い、実装が正しい箇所はドキュメント側を実挙動に合わせた。

## 背景

バグハントの一環で全ドキュメント(README / docs / docs/spec)と実装の全面監査を実施した。その結果、エラーメッセージの文言・型検査の挙動・AST 構造・拡張手順のファイルパスなど、実装と食い違う記述が 7 カテゴリ見つかった。

## 課題

誤った記述はユーザーとコントリビュータの双方を惑わせる:

- `2 + + 3` は「パースエラーの例」として掲載されているが、実際は単項プラスとして `5` に評価される
- エラープレフィックスが `type check:` と記載されているが、実際の出力は `type error:`
- `"hello" + 1` という例が載っているが、この言語に文字列は存在せずパース不能
- type_checker.md は「未知の関数名は Unknown として通過し評価器が捕捉する」と主張するが、実際は型検査時に `undefined function` で拒否される
- ast.md に `TypeCast` ノードと `postfix` 優先度レベルが無く、DateTime のフィールドも実在しない `offset_seconds: i32` と記載
- contribute.md の拡張手順が存在しないファイル(`evaluator/builtin.rs` 等)を指す
- `format_error.rs` の doc コメントが古いパースエラー例を複製

## 目標

### 必須項目

- 掲載されている全コマンド例・エラー例が実際の出力と一致する
- AST 仕様が `domain/src/ast.rs` の定義と一致する
- contribute.md の拡張手順が実在のファイルを指す

### 範囲外

- 未ドキュメント機能の新規記載(`**` 演算子・メソッドチェーン・`MM:SS` duration・`show builtin`・統計関数群)— 別 PR で対応
- コードの挙動変更

## 採用手法

各乖離について「実装とドキュメントのどちらが正しいか」を判定した。今回の 7 件はすべて実装側の挙動が合理的(例: 未知関数の早期拒否はエラーを早く・確実に返す)であるため、ドキュメント側を修正した。

### 検討した選択肢

| 選択肢 | 長所 | 短所 |
|--------|------|------|
| A: ドキュメントを実挙動に合わせる(採用) | 挙動変更ゼロでリスクなし。実装側の設計はいずれも妥当 | 無し |
| B: ドキュメントに合わせて実装を変更(例: 未知関数を Unknown 通過に) | ドキュメント不変 | 型検査の早期拒否という優れた設計を後退させる。エラー文言の変更は既存テストと衝突 |

### 採用理由

監査した全項目で実装側の挙動が設計原則(早期エラー・値オブジェクトによる検証)に適っており、ドキュメントの記述が古いか誤記だったため。

## 変更箇所

- `docs/example.md`: パースエラー例を `2 + * 3` に差し替え(`2 + + 3` は 5 に評価される旨を注記)、`type check:` → `type error:`
- `docs/spec/type_system.md`: `type check:` プレフィックス修正、パース不能な `"hello" + 1` 例を実例に差し替え
- `docs/spec/type_checker.md`: 未知関数名は型検査時に拒否される旨へ修正
- `docs/spec/ast.md`: `TypeCast` ノード追加、`postfix` 優先度レベル追加、DateTime の `offset: UtcOffset` へ修正、unary の繰り返し(`*`)へ修正
- `docs/contribute.md`: 拡張手順のファイルパス 3 件を実在のパスへ修正
- `ccc/usecase/src/format_error.rs`: doc コメントの古いパースエラー例を実挙動に更新

## 妥協と制限

無し(コメント以外のコード変更を含まない)。

## 検証方法

- 修正後の全コマンド例をビルド済みバイナリで実行し、出力がドキュメントと一致することを確認
- `cargo test --release` 全テストパス(doc コメント変更が影響しないことを確認)
- ast.md の Rust スニペットを `domain/src/ast.rs` の実定義と照合

## 確認事項

- ⚠️ 「未知関数の早期拒否」を仕様として確定してよいか(ドキュメント側を直したため、この挙動が正式仕様になる)

## 参考文献

- 関連 PR: #41, #42(同バグハントの挙動修正)
- docs/spec/ast.md, docs/spec/type_checker.md, docs/spec/type_system.md

body:
## What

Makes every post findable by family member, and by whether it has photos.

- `src/data/tags.ts`: the tag vocabulary. 24 people (you and your siblings, חיה and חיים צור, the grandparents, uncles and their wives, the stepsisters, cousins, your biological father, and the great-grandmothers) plus a `photos` topic. Each person carries the nicknames and role-words the blog used, as search aliases.
- `src/lib/tags.ts` and `src/components/TagChips.astro`: resolver and chip component.
- `/tags/` browse-all index, grouped into family and topics with post counts and an alias-aware search box (typing a nickname or name jumps to the right person), plus `/tags/<id>` listing pages.
- `tags:` frontmatter on all 182 posts.

## Why

חיה anonymised the family in the original blog, so searching a name returns nothing. Tags carry the post-to-person link that only the family knows, so each relative can pull up the posts about them. The person for each post was derived from role words, nicknames and blog-names in the text, then mapped to real names you confirmed one by one.

## Scope and verification

`npm run check` passes: build produces 219 pages, metadata OK (182 posts, 58 image refs base-prefixed and present). This repo has no linter or coverage tooling. Topic tags (treatment, trips, food, holidays, and so on) are intentionally left for a follow-up PR; this one is people plus photos.
