author: gokayfem
body:
## Summary

Third wave of fal-platform utilities, plus the pack's **first web extension**.

### Durable Job Inbox
Every async `Fal Submit` is journaled to the shared sqlite store, so queued jobs **survive ComfyUI restarts**. The new **Fal Job Inbox** node lists pending/collected jobs and outputs the newest pending `request_id` + `endpoint_id` — wire them into *Fal Result by Request ID* and collect yesterday's generations after a restart. Submit tonight, collect tomorrow.

### Provenance: every output is a receipt
*Fal Save Media from URL* now writes a `<file>.fal.json` sidecar and embeds a `fal_provenance` PNG text chunk (endpoint, request id, source URL — looked up from the result cache), and returns `request_id` as a second output (slot 0 unchanged). The new **Fal Provenance from File** node reads any saved file back into `endpoint_id` + `request_id` for **free re-materialization** months later. Existing PNG text chunks and ICC color profiles are preserved on embed.

### In-canvas cost UI (`web/` + `/fal_api` server routes)
- **Cost pills** rendered just above every fal node with published pricing ("≈$0.08/run"); free-typed endpoint fields (Any Endpoint, Submit, Cost Estimator) estimate live as you type (debounced).
- **fal sidebar tab** — session spend, account balance, and a live job list with copy-able request ids and per-job Cancel.
- **Endpoint search** — editing an `endpoint_id` field pops up catalog search with price labels; click to fill.
- All frontend features degrade silently on older ComfyUI frontends; all routes are exception-guarded, cached where hot, and leak nothing sensitive.

## Review
Adversarially reviewed; findings fixed: PNG embed now preserves source text chunks + ICC profile (regression-tested with a ComfyUI-workflow chunk), jobs route limit clamped.

## Test plan
- [x] 91 tests pass (15 new: job store lifecycle/persistence, provenance sidecar + PNG chunk round trip + wildcard-escaped URL lookup, server route pure functions incl. price filtering)
- [x] Full pack loads: 1,491 nodes + WEB_DIRECTORY; all `INPUT_TYPES()` valid; ruff clean; `node --check` on all JS
- [ ] Live smoke test with a real FAL_KEY: cost pill renders, cache hit on identical re-run, Submit → restart → Inbox → Collect cycle, sidebar balance/jobs, endpoint autocomplete

> ⚠️ Merging bumps `pyproject.toml` to 2.3.0 and auto-publishes to the Comfy Registry — do the live smoke test first.

author: abhiaiyer91
body:
## Summary

Resolves all 5 open CodeQL shell-command alerts (medium severity): `js/shell-command-constructed-from-input` #323, #571, #655, #714 and `js/shell-command-injection-from-environment` #399.

Each flagged path interpolated externally-influenced strings into a shell command. Fixes, by risk:

**mastracode login dialog (#655)** — the most meaningful one: the OAuth URL comes from the auth provider over the network and was interpolated into `exec(`open "${url}"`)`. A compromised/MITM'd auth endpoint could have injected shell commands. Now the URL is validated as well-formed http(s) and the browser is opened via `spawn` with an args array (`open` / `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler` / `xdg-open`) — no shell at all. Best-effort as before; the URL is still displayed for manual opening.

**packages/codemod (#399)** — `mastra codemod` built a jscodeshift invocation as one string and ran it through `exec`. Now it resolves `jscodeshift/bin/jscodeshift.js` via `createRequire` and runs it with `execFile(process.execPath, [bin, ...args])` — no shell, no `.bin` shim lookup. Side benefit: codemods now work on project paths containing spaces (previously broken).

**packages/cli `DepsService.installPackages` (#571)** — switched `execa` from a single interpolated string + `shell: true` to the `execa(pm, args)` array form. execa's cross-spawn still resolves `pnpm.cmd`-style shims on Windows, so no shell is needed.

**packages/deployer `createChildProcessLogger` (#714) + `getNpmArgs` flow (#323)** — this sink genuinely needs `shell: true` for package-manager shims on Windows, so instead args are validated against an allowlist (`/^[\w@%+=:,./^~-]*$/` — package specifier and CLI flag characters) and the call throws on anything containing shell metacharacters. All current callers pass `pkg@version` specs and `--cpu=/--os=/--libc=` flags, which pass validation.

## Test plan

- `tsc --noEmit` clean in all 4 packages (cli, codemod, deployer, mastracode)
- Tests: codemod 79/79, deployer services 4/4, cli services 11/11
- Manual end-to-end: built `@mastra/codemod` and ran `v1/mastra-core-imports` against a directory with spaces in its path — transform applied correctly

Closes all three 🔴 High priority items from the v2.4 roadmap.

---

### Feature #1 — D* band quantification (`peak_fitter.py` + `analyzer.py`)

- Added `"D_star": (1080, 1230)` to `PEAK_WINDOWS_532`
- D* is **dispersive** (same 53 cm⁻¹/eV as D band) — `get_peak_windows()` now shifts D* window with laser wavelength
- Single Lorentzian fit via `_fit_peak()` — standard SNR + R² gate applies
- New fields in `RamanAnalysis`: `IDstar_IG_height`, `dstar_co_note`
- `I_D*/I_G > 0.15` triggers a note: *"significant residual C–O groups / partial oxidation suggested"*
- Report table now includes D* row (shown before D)
- **Reference**: Lee et al. (2021) *Carbon* **183**, 814–822

---

### Feature #2 — B-doping fingerprint flag (`analyzer.py`)

New function `_check_boron_doping()` — all **three** criteria must be met simultaneously:

| Criterion | Threshold | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| G center | 1577–1587 cm⁻¹ | B-doping is hole-doping; no N-doping blue-shift (15–20 cm⁻¹) |
| I_D/I_D′ | 5–9 (target ~7) | sp³ substitutional B defects [Eckmann 2012] |
| I_D/I_G | > 3 | heavily defective lattice |

- New fields in `RamanAnalysis`: `boron_doping_flag` (bool), `boron_doping_note` (str with full evidence)
- Report shows `⚠ BORON DOPING FLAG` section only when flag is raised
- **Reference**: Kim et al. (2012) *ACS Nano* **6**, 8203

---

### Feature #3 — Fitting uncertainty via `pcov` (`peak_fitter.py`)

New helper `_pcov_stderr(pcov, idx)` extracts `√pcov[i,i]`, returning `None` if `inf` or negative (underdetermined).

All scipy-fitted peaks now populate:
- `center_stderr` — 1σ uncertainty on peak position (cm⁻¹)
- `fwhm_stderr` — 1σ uncertainty on FWHM = 2 × γ_stderr

Coverage:
- `_fit_peak()` — Lorentzian (indices 0, 2) and Pseudo-Voigt (indices 0, 2)
- `_fit_G_deconvolve()` — dual-Lorentzian (both G and D′ components)
- `_fit_D_G_Dp_global()` — triple-Lorentzian (D=0,2; G=3,5; D′=6,8)

Report output: `1234.5 ± 0.3` format for center and FWHM columns.

---

### Files changed
- `src/peak_fitter.py` — D* window, dispersive shift, `_pcov_stderr`, uncertainty in all fitters
- `src/analyzer.py` — D* ratio, C/O proxy note, B-doping flag, uncertainty in report formatter

author: gregahren
body:
## What

Three related upgrades to how big numbers read across the framework, driven by the ClickPy-style PyPI stats dashboard:

### 1. `format="compact"` (new)
- `formatValue` gains a `compact` case: `3,338,316,067` → **3.34B** (3 significant digits, locale-aware — `de-DE` → `3,34 Mrd.`; `decimals=` pins the fraction count instead).
- Works everywhere the shared formatter is honored (`<Counter>`, `<Value>`, `<Table>`, charts).
- On a `<Counter>` the exact thousands-separated value is one hover away via a `title` tooltip.

### 2. Chart value-axis ticks auto-compact
- Ticks compact once they reach 1,000 (`1,500,000,000` → `1.5B`) so a big-number scale stays readable instead of clipping or eating the plot. **Tooltips and data labels keep the exact format.**
- Applies to `number` / `currency` / unformatted value axes; currency ticks keep their symbol (`$1.2M`, ISO codes use the locale's compact currency form). An explicit `percent` or `format="compact"` passes through as the author's choice (`compact` then compacts tooltips too).
- Wired into all cartesian charts, scatter (both axes), boxplot, violin, candlestick, and both ComboChart axes (the right axis honoring its own `right_*` format).

### 3. Counter (KPI tile) polish
- Every tile top-aligns, so a KPI row mixing sparkline and plain counters keeps labels and values on one line (previously plain tiles centered and the row read ragged).
- The sparkline is now a **full-bleed background layer** pinned to the card's bottom edge behind the text — same card height as a plain tile, with a soft surface-color halo keeping the number legible, clipped to the card's rounded corners (the card itself can't take `overflow:hidden` — the "filtered by" tooltip pops above its top edge).
- The drawing is size-independent: normalized stretched viewBox + `non-scaling-stroke` for the line/wash, and the endpoint dot is an HTML span pinned in px to the right edge — correct through grid reflow, window resize, and print with **no ResizeObserver / redraw dependency**.
- Headline figures switch to proportional numerals (tabular digits only pay off in vertically stacked columns and make a large standalone value look loose).

## Verification

- Playwright checks: dot center sits exactly on the line endpoint (0.0px offset), text clears the trend layer, and an instant post-viewport-resize frame renders full-bleed correctly (the state that previously broke).
- Screenshots light + dark; axis ticks verified for `number` (`30M…150M`), `currency` (`$30M…$150M`), and unformatted (`20M…140M`) charts.
- `uv run pytest tests/` → **1373 passed, 24 skipped**; agent docs regenerated (freshness test green).

Docs updated: formatting page (format table + axis-tick note) and the Counter component page.

author: sleidig
body:
Part of the Sentry noise reduction effort: an error thrown repeatedly — e.g. on every change detection cycle — previously flooded remote monitoring without any client-side limit. The recent `NG0600` incident produced **20,797 events from essentially a single broken page** ([AAM-DIGITAL-720](https://aam-digital.sentry.io/issues/AAM-DIGITAL-720)), the largest noise source of the month.

## Changes

- The Sentry `beforeSend` hook now counts events by exception `type: message` (or plain message for `captureMessage` events) and **drops further occurrences after 5 per app session** (page load).
- Console logging is unaffected — only remote reporting is capped.
- The first 5 occurrences still reach Sentry, so issues are still created, alerted on, and carry representative context; only the flood is suppressed.
- Covered by unit tests (pure function, no mocks needed).

## PR Checklist

- [ ] manually tested (all) required functionality yourself and added comment with clear steps for manual testing
- [ ] reviewed the "Files changed" section of the PR briefly
- [ ] added label **"Final Review"** to trigger UI regression testing and CodeRabbit AI review
- [ ] marked each code review comment as resolved (or commented on it with a question, if unsure)

## Résumé
- Préserve les URLs SEO d’histoire pour les items fermés visibles lors d’une mise à jour parc.
- Allège la sonde frontend de disponibilité d’histoire avec un fallback items seulement en 404.
- Corrige les no-op ParkGraphUpsert pour ne pas réactiver le refresh SSR, et restaure l’axe mobile de la timeline.
- Clarifie les guides JSON sur `zoneId`/`manufacturerId` vs `zoneKey`/`manufacturerKey`.

## Pourquoi
Des commentaires de review restaient pertinents après les PR précédentes : certains items fermés pouvaient ne pas invalider/soumettre leurs pages d’histoire, l’appel frontend chargeait trop de timeline pour un simple booléen, et un no-op pré-exécution pouvait laisser `Refresh` à `true`.

body:
We add division code for `gr_mpoly`, ported from other mpoly modules. Only single-threaded heap algorithms; no "threaded" or "array" algorithms.

* `gr_mpoly_divides` (checked exact division)
* `gr_mpoly_div` (quotient part of divrem)
* `gr_mpoly_divrem`
* `gr_mpoly_divrem_ideal`
* `gr_mpoly_quasidiv`
* `gr_mpoly_quasidivrem`
* `gr_mpoly_quasidivrem_ideal`
* `gr_mpoly_div_weak`
* `gr_mpoly_divrem_weak`
* `gr_mpoly_divrem_ideal_weak`

With the exception of the `quasidiv` variants, this implements the same dot product optimizations as the multiplication code, so computing `(AB) / B` is roughly as fast as computing `AB`.

The "weak" versions implement the quasi-Euclidean division with remainder of `fmpz_mpoly_divrem`, with recursive division with remainder for nonexact coefficient quotients. I'm not sure how useful it is, but it requires little extra code to support.

The PR also adds dedicated squaring code, which is theoretically up to 2x faster than multiplication, though in practice usually much less than this unless one has big coefficients:

* `gr_mpoly_sqr_monomial`
* `gr_mpoly_sqr_commutative_heap`
* `gr_mpoly_sqr_commutative_heap_threaded`
* `gr_mpoly_sqr`

Plus a dispatcher in `gr_mpoly_mul` for aliased inputs.

Also adds `gr_mpoly_vec_t` and methods, for representing ideals.

Almost all code generated with Claude Opus 4.8.

Edit: renamed methods. Also renamed `gr_mpoly_mul_johnson` to `gr_mpoly_mul_heap`.

author: f33na
body:
<!-- No matching issue — fund-safety audit remediation. -->
Closes #

Closes six money-loss / double-pay hazards in the crypto custody + relay path found in a fund-safety audit of the on-chain rails (#20 BSC, #22 Tron, #23 TON). Every fix hardens an existing seam — no new rail, no wire change — and each is backed by a real-DB+TB test or a pure unit test. An adversarial multi-agent review pass over the diff found one bug this branch itself introduced (a TON same-amount double-settle), which is fixed and re-verified in the last two commits.

## Changes

**core (`fix(core)`):**
- **Refuse to broadcast when the clearing reserve never applied** (`relay.rs`) — the `Dispatched` broadcast op is the one relay op with no TigerBeetle leg to reject a double-submit, so a second withdrawal whose reserve *parked* (TB lagging the committed-but-undrained reserve lets the optimistic Read-First pass) could still hit the chain. The relay now Read-Firsts the reserve's `CLEARING_RESERVE` transfer in `saga_steps` before broadcasting and parks otherwise; `record_saga_step` failures are now load-bearing (`Outcome::Retry`, not best-effort). Exploit test `tests/broadcast_guard.rs`.
- **BSC treasury on-chain pre-check + free a rejected nonce** (`custody.rs`) — Read-First the treasury's USDT + BNB balances before allocating a nonce and signing; a first-send node `Rejected` now `discard_tx` (DELETE) frees the reserved nonce so the BSC sequence never gaps and stalls the pipeline.
- **Prove TON settlement and recover a stuck seqno** (`ton_custody.rs`, `ton_rpc.rs`, `ton_withdrawal_watcher.rs`, `main.rs`) — settle a TON withdrawal ONLY on a matching non-aborted outgoing jetton transfer (a bounce no longer false-settles on a bare seqno advance); `resign_stuck` re-signs an expired stuck send at the **same seqno** with a fresh `valid_until` (only one message per seqno can ever be accepted, so this can't double-send) to unfreeze the strictly-sequential wallet. `main.rs` shares one `Arc<TonCustody>` into both the custody registry and the watcher.
- **Require provable TRON death before re-signing** (`tron_custody.rs`, `tron_rpc.rs`) — only re-sign a TRON withdrawal once it is *provably* dead: the solidified-head timestamp is past the stored expiration + a 60s margin (all ms — units checked) AND no receipt exists; otherwise wait transiently rather than re-sign and risk a double-pay.
- **Close a TON double-settle from amount-only match** + **dedup TON settle candidates by tx hash** (`ton_withdrawal_watcher.rs`, migration `0018`) — the review-found bug: an amount-only match could attribute one on-chain transfer to two same-amount withdrawals. Replaced with a group-aware `plan_settlements` (a same-amount group settles only if it has ≥ as many distinct landed transfers as members — a bounce among them settles nobody), durable cross-scan dedup via `used_tx_refs`, tx-hash candidate dedup, plus a backstop partial `UNIQUE` index on `withdrawals.tx_ref`.

**signer (`feat(signer)`):**
- **Per-transfer USDT cap + optional destination allowlist** (`policy.rs` new, `service.rs`, `main.rs`) — an independent spend policy in the signer's own trust domain (a second gate if the hub is compromised): a per-transfer USDT cap (`SIGNER_MAX_TRANSFER_USDT`, scaled per-chain via `Usdt::to_onchain`) and an optional destination allowlist (`SIGNER_DESTINATION_ALLOWLIST`), enforced only on transfers **from the treasury wallet**. Both are no-ops until configured, so dev/CI and existing deployments are unaffected.

**docs:** the new invariants (broadcast guard, on-chain treasury pre-check, provable-death re-sign, TON settlement proof, no relay shutdown-cascade, signer spend policy) are recorded in `piggybank/core/PATTERNS.md`.

## How to test

- `cargo clippy --all-targets` — clean (only the pre-existing `evbanking_auth` large-`Err` warning).
- `cargo test -p piggybank-signer` — the policy cap/allowlist scaling + composition unit tests.
- Real-DB+TB suites (`nix run .#db` + `.#tb`, then `cargo test -p piggybank-core`) — `broadcast_guard` (a parked reserve is never broadcast; the claim is never over-spent), plus the existing `wallet_withdrawals`, `relay_recovery`, `relay_shutdown`, `relay_singleton`, `bridge_consumer`, `ledger_drift_guard`, `balance_allocations`, `health_readiness` all stay green.
- TON watcher unit tests (`ton_withdrawal_watcher`) — `same_amount_with_a_bounce_settles_none_of_the_group`, `an_already_used_transfer_is_never_re_attributed`, `a_duplicated_transfer_hash_backs_at_most_one_settlement`.

## Notes / residuals (documented, lower priority — not in this PR)

Reconciliation clearing-race window; single-RPC-endpoint trust; TRON static gas top-up; more DB constraints (`UNIQUE(network,nonce)`, FKs, CHECK state enums); `main.rs` TLS-by-URL-string to the signer; `Config` derive-`Debug` secret redaction (latent — no current print site); native/gas transfers not amount-capped by the signer.

## Checklist

- [x] Self-reviewed the diff (clippy clean, unit + real-DB+TB tests green, `cargo fmt`) + an adversarial multi-agent review pass that found and closed one self-introduced bug
- [x] Docs updated if behavior changed (`piggybank/core/PATTERNS.md`)

author: acryljonny
body:
## What

`FieldPatchHelper.add_tag` / `add_term` build a patch whose target array element is keyed by `fieldPath`. During patch merge, GMS rebuilds that element from the map value and does **not** re-inject the key. As a result, patching a tag or term onto a schema field that has no existing `editableSchemaFieldInfo` element fails server-side validation:

```
HTTP 422 - fieldPath is required
```

This affects any caller that adds field-level tags/terms via `DatasetPatchBuilder` when the field is not already present in `editableSchemaMetadata` (e.g. enrichment-only connectors that never emit the full schema aspect).

## Fix

Emit an explicit `fieldPath` add op once per field, before the first tag/term op, so the element always carries its key. The op is idempotent — a repeated add of the same scalar is a harmless no-op — so existing multi-op patches are unaffected.

## Testing

- Updated `tests/unit/patch/complex_dataset_patch.json` golden (semantic comparison via `check_golden_file`).
- `pytest tests/unit/patch/test_patch_builder.py` — 9 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests updated
- [ ] Breaking changes (none — additive, idempotent op)

author: krisoye
body:
## Summary

Part of EPIC #511. **Stacked on #529 (#514) — base branch is `feature/force-heart-loss-514`, not `main`, since #514 hasn't merged yet. Diff will show only this issue's changes once #514 merges and this PR retargets to `main` automatically.**

Today a WEAK catch fills no gauge at all (`BlockResolver.ts`'s WEAK branch pushes only the heart count). Under §7.1, a WEAK catch now fills the defending ring's own gauge at `1/def_force` — the same rate as a NEUTRAL catch — since the defender still committed that ring, even though it gave zero heart-mitigation credit (that's #514's existing WEAK heart formula, unchanged).

- `BlockResolver.ts` WEAK branch: copies the NEUTRAL branch's `blockGaugeDeltas` push loop verbatim, reusing `defenderTracked`/`trackedComponentsOf` (already `GAUGE_BEARING`-filtered) — no reimplemented filter.
- `hitGaugeElements` (attacker's-element gauge) untouched — still never fills on any catch.
- WEAK heart-loss formula completely unaffected — purely additive change.

Changelog fragment: `docs/changelog.d/515.md`

Closes #515

## Review

Escalated from the issue's stated `inline-checklist` to `spawn-reviewer` (opus) — the diff touches server-authoritative logic in `BlockResolver.ts` (safety backstop trigger). **APPROVE**, one P2 (missing changelog, fixed) and one P3 (a pre-existing doc-comment imprecision about STRONG parry vs STRONG block, tightened while already touching that comment). The reviewer independently verified `ElementSystem.resolve()` and confirmed a genuinely interesting finding: fusion defenders can never actually resolve WEAK (fusions have no weakness by design), making the issue's own "or a fusion with a tracked component" acceptance-criteria clause structurally unreachable at runtime — locked in as an invariant test rather than left as a silent gap.

## Testing

- **Unit**: `npx vitest run tests/unit/BlockResolver.test.ts --pool=threads` — 124/124 passing.
- QA wrote 2 phases (parallel-with-impl + implementation-aware): spec-driven adversarial (WEAK-vs-NEUTRAL rate-equality proof, Wind/Earth non-gauge-bearing cases, `hitGaugeElements` regression lock, `consumeUse=1` lock, xp=0 safety), implementation-aware (structural guards proving the WEAK branch genuinely reuses the shared `defForce`/`defenderTracked` rather than an independently-recomputed copy that could drift, plus an adversarial extreme-force-gap test guarding against a `1/atkForce` vs `1/defForce` mix-up).

## E2E

`npx playwright test gauge-four-case.spec.ts --project=pvp`: found and fixed one real test-setup bug along the way — the new WEAK-catch scenario's comment claimed the default loadout's D1 slot is WOOD, but the actual starter battle hand is all Wind/Earth (`D1=EARTH`). Since Earth defense is always Neutral (never WEAK), the exchange resolved NEUTRAL instead of WEAK. Fixed via the established `__testSetState` element-override pattern (matching how other specs in this file construct specific matchups). Re-verified: passes cleanly in isolation. The file's other 3 flaky results (EARTH non-triangle, strong-parry-resets, Tier-1-NEUTRAL) are the exact same pre-existing host-load-flaky tests already documented during #512's delivery — unrelated to this PR.

## Docs

- `docs/changelog.d/515.md` — user-visible mechanic change.
- `shared/types.ts` doc-comment updated and tightened (STRONG block vs STRONG parry distinction).

author: drhamilton
body:
Closes #24, step 1 (the "smallest change" path the issue recommends; roundness is step 2, deferred).

## What

A tree can now carry a `trunkFootprint` narrower than its canopy `footprint`. Fixes the gap the #22 review flagged: previously trunk and canopy shared one rectangle, so *any* tile under the canopy read as fully trunk-blocked at low sun — a tile at the drip line, nowhere near the actual trunk, went pitch dark instead of dappling.

- **Core** (`heightfield.ts`): `raiseObstaclesForObjects`/`opaqueSegmentTop` now classify each tile as inside-trunk vs canopy-only. Canopy-only tiles get no opaque segment (dapple through at any angle, from the ground up); trunk tiles keep the existing solid-below-`canopyBaseM` behaviour.
- **Shared helper**: `footprintContains` moved from `object-editor.ts` to `types.ts` (now used by both the editor's hit-testing and the heightfield's trunk classification, instead of two copies).
- **Editor default**: `placeObject` auto-computes a centred trunk footprint (~1/3 the canopy's size, min 1×1) for newly-placed trees — the only construction path new trees go through, so the feature is visible without needing new UI. Existing hardcoded demo-scene trees are untouched (no `trunkFootprint` → defaults to full-footprint, exactly matching #22).

## A design call worth flagging

The shadow pass has a special-cased **origin-tile self-check** (`shadow.ts:145-155`, unchanged by this PR) — a tile's *own* overhead object always dapples by transmittance, with no angle/height check at all. The existing comment there explains this was a deliberate workaround for trunk and canopy sharing one footprint.

I traced through whether a narrower trunk footprint should also make *that* self-check angle-aware (so a tree's own trunk tile reads as solidly blocked, not just dappled, at low sun). It's real physics — a ray leaving a point exactly at ground level starts below any trunk's height regardless of angle, so a naive fix would either always block (wrong — the existing #22 test expects a tree's own tile to dapple at *high* sun) or need a new "how far does this ray travel before it's clear of its own trunk" notion with no precedent in this codebase. Given the risk of regressing #22 and the issue's "smallest change" framing, I left it alone. **The off-origin ray-marching path — a *different* tile's ray crossing the tree's footprint on its way to the sun — already handles trunk vs. canopy correctly** once `opaqueTopM` is right per-tile, which is what this PR delivers, and it's what the acceptance criteria's headless test targets.

## Verification

- 4 new tests in `shadow.test.ts`, using a 2D grid where a due-east ray (zero north-south drift) isolates rows: a canopy-only row dapples, the trunk row blocks solidly, the far canopy-only row still dapples, and an object with `trunkFootprint` explicitly unset stays fully trunk-blocked on every row (matching #22 exactly). 106 tests total, all green.
- `CONTEXT.md` updated: reworded "Canopy base," added a "Trunk footprint" entry, cross-referenced from "Footprint."

## Screenshot

A 5×5 tree placed via the object editor (so it gets the auto-computed trunk) at low evening sun — the solid dark patch is the trunk's shadow; the dappled zigzag halo around it is the canopy-only shadow:

![trunk vs canopy dapple](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drhamilton/garden-sim/slice-24-tree-trunk-footprint/docs/screenshots/trunk-footprint/trunk-vs-canopy-dapple.png)

(The tree itself renders as one solid box — tree-shaped visuals are explicitly out of scope per the issue — so the shot is framed with open ground to the shadow's side rather than directly under the canopy, which the box hides.)

author: abhijeetnarvekar
body:
## Summary

- Copy buttons in the sidebar (e.g. **Copy workflow ID**) failed silently inside the VS Code webview: VS Code's Electron permission handler grants the async clipboard API (`clipboard-sanitized-write`) only to frames on the `vscode-webview://` origin, so `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` rejects in the cross-origin sidebar iframe even though the Permissions-Policy `allow` delegation is intact at every level.
- Adapter **1.3.2** added an optional `PluginInterface.copyToClipboard(text)` for exactly this case. This PR implements it: the webview host script relays the text over RPC to the extension host, which writes it with `vscode.env.clipboard.writeText()` — no permission or user-gesture constraints.
- Bumps the extension version to **0.3.2**.

## JIRA

https://markup-ai.atlassian.net/browse/INT-610

## Changes

- `package.json` / `package-lock.json` — `@markupai/sidebar-adapter` `^1.3.1` → `^1.3.2` (the version whose IPC layer registers the `copyToClipboard` receiver); extension version 0.3.1 → 0.3.2
- `src/webview/sidebarHost.ts` — `copyToClipboard` RPC stub on the plugin object
- `src/sidebar/sidebarBridge.ts` — `copyToClipboard` handler validating the payload and calling `vscode.env.clipboard.writeText()`
- `test/mocks/vscode.ts` — add `env.clipboard.writeText` to the mock
- `test/sidebarBridge.test.ts` — cover the happy path and non-string payload rejection

## Test plan

- `npm test` (79 passing), `npm run type-check`, `npm run lint:check`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run compile` all green
- Verified end-to-end against the dev sidebar (`Run Extension (dev sidebar)` launch config): clicking **Copy workflow ID** now copies — the webview console shows `SidebarIPCAdapter: Received copyToClipboard` and the pasted value matches
- Regression: sign-in (`openAuthUrl`), check, highlight, and apply-suggestion flows unaffected

author: jphein
body:
Fixes #1489

JP hit this live: an RSS feed's chapter list showed **empty with no error**, and chapter taps then hung on "Loading chapter…". Live probing (thanks @team-lead) found **multiple failure modes with distinct causes** — latency was a red herring. Every root cause below was confirmed against the code, and one against an on-device log.

## Repro 1 — `tricycle.org` → silent empty chapter list

Empty list, **no error**, yet backing out and re-entering loaded it. Three compounding causes:

1. **The empty chapter slot rendered nothing.** The screen gates its skeleton on `fiction == null`; once the (browse-cached) row lands it drops into the content branch and, with `chapters` still empty, drew a **bare empty list**. (It never reads `FictionDetailUiState.isLoading` — dead for this screen; left as-is, noted.)
2. **The refresh could silently no-op.** `FictionRepository.refreshDetail`'s #1314 stale-while-revalidate guard short-circuits to `Success(Unit)` **without fetching** when a row has `metadataFetchedAt > 0` but zero chapter rows and `force == false` → empty list, **no error**. Retry with `force = true` bypasses it — why re-entry "fixed" it.
3. **Homepage URL, no autodiscovery.** `matchUrl` only recognises feed-looking URLs; a bare homepage got fetched as HTML forever, `RssParser` threw, and the failure was swallowed to `null`.

## Repro 2 — reddit `.rss` → chapter tap hangs forever

`https://www.reddit.com/r/…/.rss` returns **HTTP 429** on the first request (reddit throttles the app's descriptive non-browser UA). Every tap re-fetched the whole feed (no cache) → instant 429 → mapped to a generic error → swallowed to `null`.

On-device confirmation (JP's phone): `E/PlaybackBindings: startListening: chapter … body not ready within 30s — aborting`. The abort was **log-only** — the reader never learned, so "Loading chapter…" spun forever; its own 30s wall couldn't help (the abort touches no playback state, and `retryLoading() = play()` can't recover a load the controller never received).

## The fix (one PR, bisectable commits)

1. **Chapter slot is a 3-state machine — never a bare list** (`FictionDetailScreen`): `refreshing` → spinner + "Fetching chapters…" · `empty && error` → themed `ErrorBlock` + Retry · `empty && no error` → "No chapters loaded yet." + Retry. Retry → `retryDetail → refreshDetail(force = true)`, **bypassing the #1314 TTL guard** — the in-place recovery for the "re-entry fixed it" report.
2. **`detailRefreshing` signal** — DEFAULT `flowOf(false)` (fakes untouched); `RealFictionRepositoryUi` flips a per-id `StateFlow` around `refreshDetail`; folded into the VM's combine tail as `chaptersRefreshing`.
3. **Feed cache for same-session tap latency** — a pure `TtlCache<V>(ttl, now)` (3 min) inside `fetchAndParse`. Plain-JUnit tested; `RssSource` builds it with `System::currentTimeMillis` (no Dagger seam, no Robolectric).
4. **Honest, typed fetch failures** — `RssFetcher` maps `429 → RateLimited` (parsing delta-seconds `Retry-After`); `fetchAndParse` returns `FictionResult<RssFeed>` and **propagates** `RateLimited`/`Cloudflare`/`NetworkError` through `fictionDetail`/`chapter` instead of collapsing to `null` (also stops discarding the #1443 `Cloudflare` signal). No browser-UA spoofing — the descriptive UA is policy (#1141).
5. **Feed autodiscovery** — on a parse failure, scan the HTML for `<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml">` (also atom+xml), resolve a relative href, follow **one** hop, remember the mapping in memory. `discoverFeedUrl` is a tolerant regex scan (not XML) so it survives messy HTML and stays plain-JUnit testable.
6. **Reader: surface the silent 30s abort** — `PlaybackControllerUi` gains `chapterStartFailures: Flow<ChapterStartFailure>` (DEFAULT `emptyFlow`); `AppBindings` emits at the abort instead of only logging; `ReaderViewModel` collects it (gated on `isLoading`) → drives `LoadingPhase.TimedOut` → the existing **"Couldn't start this chapter" + Retry** surface; `retryLoading` re-invokes `startListening` for the remembered ref. The abort site is app/-side, **not** core-playback.

## Timeouts (Part 3 — note, no change)

Already present + user-tunable: `RssHttpModule` sets connect/read/write from `NetworkPatience.Default` (10s/30s) + a per-call interceptor re-reading the user's patience preset (#597).

## Tests (all plain JUnit — no Robolectric, per project convention)

- `TtlCacheTest` (7) — hit, absent, TTL-boundary strictness, expiry, re-stamp, clear.
- `RssFetcherRetryAfterTest` (6) — delta-seconds, whitespace, null, HTTP-date → null, garbage → null, negative → null.
- `FeedDiscoveryTest` (8) — absolute/relative href, single quotes, no-feed, comments-feed skip, atom-only, rss-over-atom, non-feed `rel=alternate`.
- Real `tricycle-feed-snapshot.xml` **parked** in test resources with a note (no test): the parser was exonerated in production (re-entry loaded), so a real `RssParser` round-trip belongs in a future **androidTest**, not a Robolectric-free unit test.

UI/reader wiring is thin pass-through over the (default-safe) contract seams; per the `FictionDetailNotebookTest` rationale (the VMs have heavy, un-faked injection footprints) it's covered by compile + CI + on-device, not a full VM harness.

## Filed follow-ups (out of scope; core-playback frozen)

- **#1497** — persist RSS item bodies at refresh so cold-session taps never re-fetch (the cache only covers same-session; a cold tap on a throttled feed still can't fetch — correct, now that it's visible).
- **#1498** — decouple RSS subscription identity from fetch URL, so the autodiscovered feed URL can be **persisted** without changing the URL-hash `fictionId` and orphaning Room rows. (Why this PR keeps the resolved URL in memory only.)

## Scope

`source-rss/` + `feature/` + `app/` only — **`core-playback/` untouched** (plugin-dx epic freeze). Squash-merge collapses the commit sequence, which records the evidence-driven pivot from "latency" to "silent failure".

author: dancinlife
body:
## r7 — fused residual-add + LayerNorm epilogue (+ HexaVal carrier), opt-in default-OFF

Fuses a residual-add and its following LayerNorm into **one** launch — `_hx_cuda_kern_resid_layernorm_f32` computes `Y = LN(H + ADD)` and writes `H = H + ADD` in place, replacing the separate `_hx_k_residual_add_f32` + `_hx_k_layernorm_rows_f32` pair. Removes one `residual_add` launch per fused site.

This PR is the **hexa-side deliverable**: the CUDA kernel + byte-eq guard (from gemm-skinny's epi-fuse-r7) **plus the HexaVal carrier** that makes it callable from hexa/anima. The anima-side decode wiring (`r7-epi-wire`, gated `HEXA_EPI_FUSE` consumer) lands separately with the r6 anima car — this PR is the kernel + entry, not the consumer.

### BYTEEQ-NEUTRAL — the only bit-identical lever of the six
- **Guard PASS** (`tool/epi_fuse_guard.cu`, run on sm_120): `R=1/8/32 × C=1024` + `R=16 × C=4096`, all **`Y byte-eq=YES  H byte-eq=YES`** → fused == separate byte-for-byte.
- **In-situ DET |Δ| exact-match**: with `HEXA_EPI_FUSE=1` under `HEXA_DET=1`, worst |Δ| = `0.03330642419998142` — **identical to 17 digits** to r7-OFF. Same reduction order (same-thread write-then-read, LN passes verbatim).
- Byteeq-neutral → lands cleanest of the family; no argmax re-gate needed (unlike r1/r4/r6 which are argmax-faithful-but-bit-changing).

### Carrier (3-step, mirrors `farr_layernorm_f32_gpu`)
- `extern int _hx_cuda_farr_resid_layernorm_f32_gpu(h,add,g,b,y,R,C,eps)` fwd-decl + `HexaVal farr_resid_layernorm_f32_gpu(...)` wrapper in `self/runtime_emit_full.hexa` + tracked `self/runtime.h` prototype. 8 args (≥5 → transpiler direct-call).

### Effect / gate
- **+1.2% @N=1** (removes one residual_add launch/layer; part of the campaign's launch-fusion tail). Opt-in `HEXA_EPI_FUSE`, default-OFF byte-identical. Banner `[EPI-FUSE-FIRED]`.
- Rebased onto origin/main post-#4416 squash (attn-f32 family). Merge on required-summary + faithful-linux ×2 green (#4376/#4413/#4416 precedent).

author: abretonc7s
body:
## Summary

Three related deploy-node.sh bugs, fixed together:

**1. Missing workspace package (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`)**

`scripts/deploy-node.sh` hardcoded `@farmslot/protocol` as the only bundled workspace package. `services/node` now also depends on `@farmslot/capabilities` (`services/node/src/commands/screen.ts`, `fs.ts`), which was never synced. A fresh `farmslot node deploy <machine>` produced a node that crashed on startup with `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@farmslot/capabilities'`. Confirmed live — took down a node. Same class of bug as #233.

**2. Dev and prod node instances collide**

The deploy was single-instance: one `~/farmslot-node` dir, one launchd label (`com.farmslot.node`), one hardcoded gateway port (`7777`). A dev deploy and a prod deploy on the same machine overwrote each other's install dir and fought over the same service — the "keeps losing which gateway" symptom.

**3. Distless `dist/`-shipping packages silently "deploy" (found in review)**

The bundler only synced `dist/` if it already existed locally (`[[ -d dist ]] && rsync`). `@farmslot/protocol` resolves at runtime from `dist/`, which is gitignored and not produced anywhere in this script. On a fresh checkout, or after editing protocol without rebuilding, the deploy "succeeds" with nothing copied — then the node crashes at runtime with the exact `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` this script exists to prevent. Same root cause class as #233 and fix 1, one layer deeper.

## Fix

**1. Generic transitive workspace-package bundling** — resolver walks `services/node/package.json`'s `@farmslot/*` deps transitively (via each resolved package's own `dependencies`), so any future workspace dependency is bundled automatically. Syncs whichever of `src/`/`dist/` exist per package, handling both source-only (`capabilities`) and built (`protocol`) packages uniformly.

**2. `--instance dev|prod` (or `FARMSLOT_NODE_INSTANCE=dev`), default `prod`** — one `case` block is the single source of truth for everything that must not collide between instances on the same machine:

| | prod (default) | dev |
|---|---|---|
| install dir | `~/farmslot-node` (unchanged) | `~/farmslot-node-dev` |
| launchd label | `com.farmslot.node` (unchanged) | `com.farmslot.node.dev` |
| systemd unit | `farmslot-node` (unchanged) | `farmslot-node-dev` |
| gateway port | `7777` (unchanged, override `GATEWAY_PORT`) | `7801` |
| `MACHINE_NAME` | `<machine>` (unchanged) | `<machine>-dev` |

Also namespaced two `process.env` collision points inside `services/node` itself found while auditing, not on the original list: `FARMSLOT_HOME` (unused today, namespaced defensively) and `SCREEN_CONTROL_SOCKET` (`services/node/src/commands/screen-control.ts` defaults to a uid-only path — two instances on one box would fight over the same IPC socket). Both left unset for prod (byte-identical to today).

**3. Build dist-shipping deps before bundling** — the resolver now flags, per package, whether it ships from `dist/` (has a `build` script AND `main`/`exports` point into `dist/`) and `dist/` is currently missing. Before the bundling rsync loop, every flagged package gets built (`yarn workspace <name> build`); if the build fails, or `dist/` is still missing afterward, the deploy **fails loudly and exits** rather than silently shipping a distless package. Source-only packages (`capabilities`) are never flagged.

Prod output is byte-identical when `--instance` is omitted, and a package that already has a fresh `dist/` triggers no rebuild.

## Verification

I deliberately did **not** run the full script against the live machine — installing/reloading a real launchd service, or running a real `yarn build`, against the box this repo runs from is outward-facing and I'm not doing that without Arthur driving it directly. Everything below either exercises the real script's exact logic (extracted verbatim via `sed` line ranges — zero retyping, zero drift risk) or simulates the file-level effects in scratch directories:

- **Fix 1 (bundling):** simulated sync into a scratch `REMOTE_DIR`, confirmed both `capabilities` and `protocol` land correctly; built `protocol` for real and confirmed `tsx` resolves `@farmslot/protocol`, `@farmslot/capabilities/fs-watch`, `@farmslot/capabilities/screen-frame` from the synced tree; reproduced the original crash with protocol-only bundling for contrast.
- **Fix 2 (instances):** rendered both `--instance prod` and `--instance dev` plist/unit files from the real extracted fragments against fake paths — confirmed all 5 values differ and prod's render is structurally unchanged; verified `--instance` flag parsing (position, `=` form, env var, precedence, invalid-value rejection) with the real extracted parsing code; reran the bundling sim into both instance dirs concurrently and confirmed redeploying one instance leaves the other's directory (and a marker file placed in it) untouched.
- **Fix 3 (build-before-bundle), this round:** ran the real extracted resolver against the actual repo — confirmed `needsBuild=0` for both packages with `dist/` present. Removed `packages/protocol/dist` (gitignored, safe/reversible) and reran — resolver correctly flagged `protocol` (`needsBuild=1`), `capabilities` unaffected. Ran the real extracted build-loop against the live worktree: it invoked `yarn workspace @farmslot/protocol build`, `dist/` reappeared, and a re-run of the resolver flipped back to `needsBuild=0`. Ran the full pipeline (resolve → build-if-needed → bundle) end to end into a scratch `REMOTE_DIR` starting from a missing `dist/` — protocol was auto-built and both `dist/` and `src/` ended up correctly bundled; confirmed via `tsx` that runtime resolution succeeds. Separately simulated a genuine build failure (bogus workspace) and confirmed the loop fails loudly with a clear error instead of continuing.
- `bash -n` syntax check and pre-commit/pre-push quality gates (ESLint ratchet, type-escape ratchet, workspace structure/changelogs, import boundaries) passed after each commit, no new issues.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n scripts/deploy-node.sh`
- [x] Simulated `@farmslot/*` bundling (both source-only and built packages) into scratch dirs, verified `tsx` runtime resolution
- [x] Reproduced and confirmed the fix for the original `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (missing capabilities) crash
- [x] Rendered prod + dev plist/unit configs from extracted real script fragments, confirmed no collision across dir/label/unit/port/machine-name/FARMSLOT_HOME/SCREEN_CONTROL_SOCKET, and prod is unchanged
- [x] Verified `--instance` flag parsing and non-interference between simulated instances
- [x] Verified `needsBuild` detection flips correctly when `dist/` is removed/rebuilt, using the real repo's `protocol` package
- [x] Ran the real build-loop and confirmed it rebuilds `protocol` and dist reappears; confirmed it fails loudly on a genuine build failure
- [x] Ran the full resolve→build→bundle pipeline end to end from a missing-`dist/` starting state
- [x] Pre-commit / pre-push quality gates passed after every commit
- [ ] **Not done — needs Arthur or explicit go-ahead:** an actual `farmslot node deploy <machine> --instance dev` run against a real fleet machine, side by side with the existing prod node

author: mcb0035
body:
Documents ImgEdge's cryptography and network-protocol posture for the OpenSSF Best Practices **silver** criteria. **Documentation only — no behaviour change**; I audited the code first and it already complies.

All new content is in [`SECURITY.md` → Cryptography](SECURITY.md#cryptography) (three new subsections) with a CHANGELOG note.

### Criterion-by-criterion (suggested bestpractices.dev answers)

| Criterion | Answer | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Credentials/keys in separate files, updatable w/o recompile | **Met** | Token in its own `~/.imgedge_token` (`O_EXCL`, mode `600`) or `IMGEDGE_TOKEN`; never in logs/cache/config; `.crx` key only a transient CI secret; Sigstore is keyless → [SECURITY.md#credential--key-storage](SECURITY.md#credential--key-storage) |
| Secure network protocols; insecure off by default | **Met** | HTTPS-only pinned downloads; loopback-only API; public image fetch HTTP/HTTPS (`IMGEDGE_FETCH_HTTPS_ONLY` to require TLS); no FTP/telnet/SSH/SNMP → [#network-protocols--tls](SECURITY.md#network-protocols--tls) |
| Supports TLS ≥ 1.2 | **Met** | Platform default `ssl` context negotiates TLS 1.2/1.3; SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 not offered |
| TLS certificate verification by default (incl. subresources) | **Met** | Default verifying context; SSRF IP-pinning keeps `server_hostname` so chain+hostname are checked against the real host on the resource and redirects; verification disabled nowhere |
| Cert verification before sending private headers | **Met** | Token is sent only to the loopback API; external image fetches send no cookies/tokens/auth (neutral UA) — no private header ever crosses TLS; verification precedes every request |
| Multiple crypto algorithms (agility) | **Met** | TLS cipher negotiation (AES-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305…); app hashing via `hashlib` (SHA-2 224/256/384/512 + SHA-3); token via `secrets` → [#algorithm-agility](SECURITY.md#algorithm-agility) |

### Audit notes (why these are genuinely true, not aspirational)
- `download_models.py` refuses non-HTTPS URLs, restricts redirects to GitHub hosts, and SHA-256-pins every asset.
- `server.py`'s `_PinnedHTTPSConnection` wraps TLS with `server_hostname=self.host` — IP-pinning for SSRF **without** weakening cert/hostname verification.
- No `_create_unverified_context` / `CERT_NONE` / `check_hostname=False` / `verify=False` anywhere in `src/`.
- Crypto is HMAC-SHA-256 + SHA-256 + `secrets` — no MD5/SHA-1/RC4/DES.

author: thomaseizinger
body:
After a roam, iceless connections are soft-reset but all allocations are cleared. If the portal then hands out relays under new IDs, the connections stay pinned to relay IDs without an allocation: candidate events are routed by relay ID, so they never receive the newly gathered candidates and fan out re-key handshakes with zero pairs until the WireGuard tunnel expires (~20s) and the flow is re-created from scratch.

Queue connections for relay migration when soft-resetting them, so the existing migration machinery re-points them to a freshly sampled relay as soon as one is reachable and candidates then stream in via the regular allocation events. Migration seeds the full candidate set since a roam wipes the agent's locals.

This only surfaces for iceless connections because those are retained during roaming.

Related: #13088

## What

The public face of `robogeosociety.xyz` is now a **blank 404**, everywhere. Cloudflare Access is **retired** — the backend Worker is its own auth boundary. Stacked on #120 (Phase 1).

**The wall**
- `backend/src/auth.ts` — Access-JWT identity model → a pre-shared key (`X-RGS-Key` / wrangler secret `RGS_KEY`, constant-time compare; key = admin). Unset key (local `wrangler dev`) = wall open.
- `backend/src/index.ts` — wall middleware returns a blank 404 for any request without the key, before routing. **One carve-out** (registered first): `POST /discord/interactions` (Ed25519-verified — Discord's servers still reach it).
- `backend/wrangler.toml` — apex + `www` zone routes so the wall covers the whole domain, not just `api.*`.

**Consumers → `X-RGS-Key`**: `web/vite.config.js` (+ `.env.local.example`), `nomad/serve_web.py` + run script (the tailnet `/api` proxy).

**Infra teardown**
- `infra/access` — delete the backend + 4 frontend Access apps + the dev service token (kept the account-level GitHub/Google IdPs).
- `infra/dns` — drop the `campsites.`/`collectors.` Pages CNAMEs; add proxied apex + `www` parking records (the Worker route answers).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` — stop deploying the frontend to Pages (UI is on the tailnet now); deploy the backend Worker only.

## Verified live (already applied)

| From a stranger | Result |
|---|---|
| `robogeosociety.xyz` / `www` / `api` | **404** (blank — no Access redirect, no team-name leak) |
| `campsites.` / `collectors.` | NXDOMAIN |
| `atlas.` (public travel wiki) | 302 (untouched) |
| key bearer (`rgs-admin`, tailnet app) | 200 / `role: admin` |

Worker `e4819cde`; Access destroyed via **targeted** apply (a full `infra/access` apply would stomp the IdP client secrets in state).

## S55 T7 — P1.5 : durcissement des Edge Functions restantes

Ferme la vague **P1.5 (T7)** de l'audit `docs/workplan/audits/2026-06-27-audit-integral-par-module.md` (§4 P1). Trois axes : idempotence des annulations/remboursements, sortie du PIN de remise des arguments SQL, et défense-en-profondeur `REVOKE`.

### 1. Idempotence void / cancel via `x-idempotency-key`
- **`void_order_rpc_v4`** (`_082`) — replay idempotent via `refunds.idempotency_key` : un retry (réseau instable, double-clic, retry React-Query) renvoie le résultat du premier appel au lieu de doubler le void/refund.
- **`cancel_order_item_rpc_v3`** (`_083`) — replay idempotent via `order_items.cancel_idempotency_key`.
- Les Edge Functions **`void-order`** et **`cancel-item`** lisent désormais l'en-tête HTTP **`x-idempotency-key`** (`getIdempotencyKey` du helper `_shared/idempotency.ts`) et le propagent en `p_idempotency_key` aux RPC v4/v3.
- Côté POS : **clé stable par modal** (UUID v4 en `useRef`, survit aux re-renders) sur les flux void/cancel — `VoidOrderModal`, `CancelItemModal`, hooks `useVoidOrder`/`useVoidServerOrder`/`useCancelOrderItem`.

### 2. PIN de remise hors des arguments SQL (table nonce)
- Nouvelle table **`discount_authorizations`** (`_085`) : nonce d'autorisation de remise, isolée, single-use, avec expiration.
- **`complete_order_with_payment_v16`** (`_086`) — le PIN de remise ne transite plus comme argument de RPC (risque de log PostgREST/pgaudit) ; il est remplacé par un `p_discount_auth_id` (nonce) consommé atomiquement côté serveur (`consumed_at` + `consumed_order_id`), avec contrôle que le nonce a été émis pour le manager déclaré.
- **Raccordement money-path EF** — l'Edge Function **`process-payment`** est repointée `v15 → v16` : elle **vérifie le PIN de remise dans l'EF** (parité avec void-order/cancel-item/refund-order, pattern S25 « le PIN ne voyage que via `x-manager-pin` »), contrôle la permission `sales.discount`, **frappe le nonce** dans `discount_authorizations` (service-role) et le transmet en `p_discount_auth_id`. Plus aucun `p_manager_pin` dans les arguments du RPC ; le fallback `record_pin_failure_v1` (S38) est remplacé par `recordManagerPinFailure` in-EF.

### 3. Sécurité — `REVOKE` defense-in-depth
- `REVOKE EXECUTE` des reversal **v4 / v3** pour le rôle `authenticated` (`_084`) + rafraîchissement de la suite de régression `reversal_rpc_revoke`.

## 概要

作業員請求書の作成画面で、**出面×単価からの自動生成が全く効かず、空の明細1行しか表示されない**不具合を修正します。原因を握りつぶしていたため画面上は「なぜ空なのか」が分からず、`請求書に作成できる明細がありません` とだけ出る状態でした。

## 根本原因

`workerInvoice.getMyDraft` の自動生成が、以下のいずれでも**黙って空を返して**いました。

1. 本番でV2テーブル（`monthly_closing_v2_*`）が未マイグレーションだと `select` が例外を投げ、自動生成（出面×単価）が丸ごと失敗する
2. 月締めの提出レコード（`closing_submissions`）が未作成だと `NOT_FOUND` で打ち切られ、プレビューが出せない
3. 例外を `catch {}` で捨てていたため、画面には理由が出ない

出面の有無判定（overview）は `attendance` テーブルだけを見るため「対象あり＝フォーム表示」になり、一方で自動生成側が上記で失敗 → **フォームは出るのに明細は空**、という食い違いが起きていました。

## 変更内容

- **`server/db.ts`**: `getMonthlyClosingV2WorkerSubmission` / `getMonthlyClosingV2ExpenseLinesByWorkerMonth` を防御的に（try/catch）実装。V2テーブル未整備でも `undefined` / `[]` を返し、出面×単価の自動生成を止めない
- **`server/routers.ts` `getMyDraft`**:
  - 提出レコードが未作成でも自動生成する（プレビュー用途）
  - 保存済み明細があればそれを優先して返す
  - 自動生成に失敗／該当なしのときは**理由を `warnings` に載せて必ず返す**（黙って空にしない）
  - 返却形状を1つに正規化
- **`client/src/pages/AppMyClosing.tsx`**: 自動生成の成否・警告をフォーム上に表示（緑＝自動計算済み／黄＝警告・原因）

## 期待される効果

- 出面と単価が設定済みなら、締め提出前でも**明細が自動生成される**
- 出面が見つからない・単価未設定などの場合は、**その理由が画面に表示される**ので原因を切り分けできる

author: dealvz
body:
## Why

The Campaign Manager is meant to fulfill the Campaign Story through chat, not just recite the week. Until now, opening the manager chat always played the generic "here are the two or three things that matter this week" intro, even for a candidate who hasn't written their story yet. That candidate has nothing to prioritize against and no path into the story from the manager.

This makes the manager's opener story-aware. When the Campaign Story is unfinished, opening the chat (via "meet your campaign manager" or a fresh conversation) plays an opener that introduces the manager (or welcomes them back) and asks the first still-missing question, so it picks up where they left off instead of restarting the intake. Once the story is complete it falls back to the standard intro.

Completeness is computed client-side against the same three gates the Story page uses, so the manager never disagrees with the Story page or the generation gate:

- **why** = website bio (`getBioPlainLength`)
- **background** = campaign story field (`isStoryFieldAnswered`)
- **positions** = website issues

The opener wording mirrors the server-seeded greeting (`buildStoryGreeting` / `STORY_QUESTION_PROMPTS` in gp-api) so the two surfaces read the same; a comment on each marks the hand-kept sync. The status hook stays `ready: false` until both the story and website have loaded, so a candidate whose story is actually complete never sees a flash of the intake.

This is the frontend companion to the backend story-intake work; the backend seeds the same resume-aware greeting when the chat has no history.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> UX and display copy on the campaign-manager dashboard only; no auth, payments, or persistence changes beyond existing story/website reads.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Campaign Manager chat** now uses a **resume-aware opener** when the Campaign Story is incomplete, instead of always showing the generic weekly-priorities intro on “meet your campaign manager” / fresh greet flows.
> 
> `useCampaignStoryStatus` loads story + website and applies the same three gates as the Story page (bio → **why**, story **background**, website **issues** → **positions**). Until both sources are loaded it stays not `ready`, so completed stories don’t briefly see intake copy. When `ready` and fields are missing, `buildStoryOpener` builds intro + “First/Next” question text aligned with gp-api `STORY_QUESTION_PROMPTS` (hand-synced). `CampaignManagerHome` passes that as `intro` for `opener` and `defaultIntro` when greeting; otherwise it keeps `CAMPAIGN_MANAGER_INTRO`.
> 
> Unit tests cover `buildStoryOpener` (fresh vs resume vs partial progress); the home smoke test mocks the status hook to loading.

author: chadac
body:
Makes the AWS permission-request flow actually usable. Three fixes:

## (2a) A pending request survives a page reload

**Bug:** the AWS approval interrupt vanished on reload. `raiseInterrupt` emits a `RUN_FINISHED` with `runId "ext-<id>"` that is **not tied to the goose run**; the still-live goose run then emits its own `RUN_STARTED`/`RUN_FINISHED` (no interrupt), and the UI reducer (`integrityAgent.trackInterrupt`) cleared the pending interrupt on those run boundaries. So after reload, the replay ended on a plain run-finish → nothing rendered, even though the broker request was still `PENDING`.

**Fix:** track **external** interrupts (`ext-*`) in a separate keyed set that run boundaries never touch. They're settled **only** by a matching `PERMISSION_RESOLVED`. The per-connection replay rebuilds the set from scratch, so a still-open request reappears after reload and a resolved one stays gone.

## (2b) The agent knows its own conversation and can link to it

**Bug:** the agent didn't know the AWS approval surfaces in *its own* conversation, and had no shareable URL.

**Fix:** the provisioner injects `CONVERSATION_URL = <publicUrl>/?thread=<id>` into each sandbox (`platform.nix` sets `PUBLIC_URL` from the ingress host, gated on the ingress being enabled). `scooter-aws request` now sends `conversation_url` (so the approval UI/requester can jump to it) and reports **auto-approved** vs **"a human must approve in this conversation — share this link"**. New `scooter-aws` skill explains the whole flow.

## (2c) Read-only requests auto-approve (opt-in)

**Bug:** every request — even a pure `s3:GetObject` read — needed a human.

**Fix:** `policy.is_read_only_policy()` (all actions `Get*`/`List*`/`Describe*`/… ; a wildcard is **not** read-only) + a per-account **`auto_approve_read_only`** registry flag (documented in `broker.nix` with an example). `service.request()` grants a pure-read inline policy (no managed ARNs) immediately via a shared `_provision()` path with a synthetic `system:auto-approve-read-only` approver, instead of notifying a human. Writes / managed ARNs still need a human. **Default off** — nothing auto-grants unless the deployment opts in per account.

### itops example
```nix
broker.aws.accounts.readonly-sandbox = {
  account_id = "123456789012";
  broker_role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/agent-token-broker-base";
  enabled = true;
  auto_approve_read_only = true;   # pure-read requests skip the human
};
```

## Tests
- broker: policy `is_read_only_policy` (×5), service (auto-approve / write-still-pending / no-opt-in-stays-pending), cli (`conversation_url` passthrough + auto-approve messaging) → **81 passed**
- ui: `integrityAgent` — ext-interrupt survives a concurrent goose run; `PERMISSION_RESOLVED` settles it → **6 passed**
- agent-host **167**, full Tier 1 **180**, `just ci` green.

body:
## Summary

Implements the triage decision on #52: the per-star `sky` column is **deleted** rather than repaired. It under-reported the per-pixel sky by the Bayer fill factor (~2.7x low on TR, ~5x on TG, ~2.3x on TB — full geometric circle in the denominator instead of the mask-overlap aperture area) and was collapsed by an axis-less `np.mean` to one frame-wide scalar. Corrected, it would be byte-for-byte identical to the existing `bkgd_count`, so the duplicate goes away:

- `src/bandaid/photometry.py` — the `data["sky"]` computation is removed from `build_photometry_table`.
- `src/bandaid/scripts.py` — the QA manifest's `sky_median` is now `float(np.median(representative["bkgd_count"]))`: correct values, and finally an actual median (matching the existing doc description).
- `src/bandaid/writers.py` — the advertised writer-contract column list swaps `sky` for `bkgd_count`.
- `docs/outputs.md` — the custom-writer / in-memory examples use `bkgd_count` as the diagnostic column.

Dropping the column also fixes the latent staleness noted in triage: `calculate_l4_quantities` never stripped `sky` (unlike `fluxes`/`total_bkg`/`bkgd_std`), so the recombined L4 table used to carry a stale full-frame value.

## Expected output changes

- The `sky` column **disappears** from all photometry tables (in-memory results and anything a custom writer sees). `.star` files are unaffected — they never read `sky`.
- QA manifest `sky_median` values **change**: they are now a true median of the per-star, per-pixel annulus background (`bkgd_count`) instead of a fill-factor-deflated frame-wide scalar (previously ~4x low on a TR representative, i.e. whenever `--no-append-l4`).

## Tests

Regression tests adapted from the issue repro, integrated into the existing suites (test-first; all failed pre-fix for the stated reasons):

- `TestBuildPhotometryTable`: uniform frame → `bkgd_count` equals the true per-pixel sky on TR/TG/TB/L4 and no `sky` column exists; sky gradient → per-star (not frame-wide) values.
- `TestCalculateL4Quantities`: the recombined L4 table carries no `sky` column.
- `TestProcessBatchToDisk`: QA `sky_median` is the median of the representative table's `bkgd_count`.

Full suite: 239 passed, 1 skipped. `pre-commit run --all-files` green.

Fixes #52

The sixth UNICHARSET leaf: `direction` + `mirror` — the first columns read PAST the bbox+stats CSV, proving the CSV-skip and completing the varied-field surface of the character set.

## What ships (one commit, `cc76557`-rebased)

- `UniCharSet::{get_direction, get_mirror}` + `dump_direction`/`dump_mirror`, backed by `directions`/`mirrors: Vec<i32>` parsed by continuing the per-line token walk (the bbox+stats group is ONE whitespace token, so columns land at fixed offsets across all 5 of tesseract's istringstream fallback tiers — no bespoke tier detector).
- Faithful C++ semantics: `direction` load default `U_LEFT_TO_RIGHT` (0) vs out-of-range `U_OTHER_NEUTRAL` (10) — two distinct defaults for two distinct conditions (`unicharset.h:712`); `mirror` clamped like `other_case`, out-of-range → `INVALID_UNICHAR_ID` (`unicharset.h:721`).
- `examples/unicharset_dump.rs` gains `direction|mirror` modes (reproduces the parity diffs).

## Proof

**Byte-identical 112/112 each** vs tesseract's own `get_direction`/`get_mirror` on real `eng.lstm-unicharset`, via the self-validating oracle (bijection half re-proves the 5.5.0-header/5.3.4-lib layout before the new field is trusted). Direction is genuinely varied on eng (55× LTR, 33× OTHER_NEUTRAL, plus 2/3/4/6 codes); mirror has 10 real bracket/paren pairs — the parse is exercised, not just defaults.

With this, **every UNICHARSET field that varies on real eng data is transcoded and parity-proven** (E-CPP-PARITY-1..6). bbox/stats/normed are deferred with reason (uniform on LSTM data = weak falsifier; gated on a legacy unicharset).

## Robustness

This commit has survived **six rebases across ~240 commits of main churn** (V3 substrate, CanonHigh flip, #624–#632) with parity re-verified green each time. Current base: post-#632, **795 contract lib tests**, clippy `-D warnings` + fmt clean on touched files.

Board hygiene in-commit: EPIPHANIES `E-CPP-PARITY-6`, LATEST_STATE branch-work + `D-UNICHARSET-DIR-MIRROR`, TECH_DEBT `TD-CONTRACT-NOT-FMT-GATED`.

## What & why

Implements **spec-449** — removes the draft/approved status concept from **Standards**. A Standard is now in force the moment it exists. The status it inherited from the shared `documents` model gated nothing for standards and was half-built (no agent verb to change it, no browse-surface badge, no audit event on change). Ratification stays where it already lived: the **Drift Inbox** (`flag_drift` / `propose_standard_change`), not a status field.

The shared `DOC_STATUSES` enum is **untouched** — Specs (phase machine) and Execution plans (`approved` terminal state) genuinely depend on `draft`/`approved`, so only Standards stop treating status as meaningful.

## Changes

**Server**
- Standards born `approved` on every create path (`createDocDraft` docType branch + the `createStandard` service insert).
- Guard in `updateDocStatus`: rejects a status change when `docType==='standard'` (blocks both the `update_doc` tool and REST `POST /:id/status`); a no-op set is allowed. Specs/plans unaffected.
- Idempotent backfill migration `0123` normalizes existing standards → `approved` (standards-only; no column/CHECK change).
- Bootstrap guidance prose reconciled to born-`approved` + Drift-Inbox review.

**UI** — no draft/approved badge for a standard on **any** surface it can render:
- standards detail page (`Standard.tsx`)
- the generic `/docs/:id` page (`DocDocument.tsx` — a standard can open there; not redirected to `/standards`)
- the ⌘K search palette (`SearchPalette.tsx`)

Execution plans and free-form documents keep their status pill.

## Cross-spec note
Supersedes **spec-438 ac-10** (bootstrap standards born `draft`). spec-438's real ratification mechanism is the Drift Inbox (ac-11/ac-5), which is **unchanged**; the born-`draft` marker had no promotion path and is what this Spec removes. spec-438 ac-10 updated in Memex to record the supersession.

## Testing
- New server integration suite: born-approved (both paths), the guard, migration idempotency (run inside a rolled-back tx), enum-intact.
- UI: badge-absence tests on the detail page + search palette; `DocDocument` suite green (92) after the badge-condition change.
- Extended `journey-12` e2e to assert no status on the `/standards` and `/docs/std-N` paths — **run at the `make e2e-cold` PR gate** (couldn't run the cold-DB harness locally).

author: mgoulart
body:
## Problem

`arc` randomly dies with `Segmentation fault: 11` under PHP 8.5 (observed on 8.5.7, macOS arm64). Crash reports all show the same stack: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS at 0x18` inside `ZEND_DO_FCALL_SPEC_*_TAILCALL_HANDLER` while iterating `FutureIterator` — an engine-level null dereference in PHP 8.5's new tail-call VM dispatch, triggered when a userland **SIGCHLD** handler is delivered mid-dispatch.

`FutureIterator::waitForSockets()` installs a dummy SIGCHLD handler whose only purpose is to make `stream_select()` return early when a subprocess exits. On PHP 8.5 that handler turns every subprocess exit (every git command `arc` runs) into a potential engine crash. Large repos run many more futures, which is why the crashes cluster there.

## Fix

Don't install the handler on PHP >= 8.5. SIGCHLD's default disposition is ignore, so the only behavior change is that `stream_select()` waits out its timeout (bounded at 1s) in the rare `(sleep 60 &) &` edge case the existing comment describes, instead of returning early. PHP < 8.5 keeps the current behavior.

## Verification

Deterministic reproducer: a loop resolving three `ExecFuture`s via `id(new FutureIterator($futures))->resolveAll()` with `pcntl_async_signals(true)` (as `bin/arc` enables), under PHP 8.5.7:

- **Unpatched:** segfaults within ~10 iterations, on every run (5/5), with the exact stack from the field crash reports.
- **Patched:** 500+ iterations clean across repeated runs.
- PHP 8.4.22 never crashes either way, hence the version gate.

The underlying bug should also be reported to php-src; this is a workaround so arcanist runs safely on 8.5 today.

Dead onboarding components** — deleted all 6 files after verifying (repo-wide grep for filenames, exported component/prop names, barrel files, test/story files) they have zero references anywhere, including the live wizard. `app/(onboarding)/onboarding/page.tsx` only imports `OnboardingPreview`/`TEMPLATES` from `onboarding-preview.tsx` (kept — still used) and implements all wizard steps inline.

**2. Dead crash-recovery code** — deleted `RecoverFromCrash` and its 3 dedicated tests (`TestRecoverFromCrash`, `TestRecoverFromCrashNoExecID`, `TestRecoverFromCrashTransientInspectError`), left a comment pointing at `Server.recoverOrphanedRuns` as the actual boot-time recovery path, per the scope constraint on this PR did **not** touch `server_lifecycle.go` (owned by two in-flight recovery PRs).

   **Known gap, not wired in as a fix (flagging per instructions):** `recoverOrphanedRuns` does a DB/journal-only sweep — any run whose trace lacks a terminal `journal_entries` row at boot is unconditionally marked cancelled and its agent reset to `IDLE`, with no check of whether the underlying container exec might still genuinely be alive. `RecoverFromCrash` additionally called `ExecInspect` against the live container and explicitly left ambiguous/transiently-erroring runs untouched rather than declaring them dead. This is a real behavioral difference worth a follow-up decision, not something this PR resolves.

**3. Issue #618 doc/schema accuracy** (findings posted as a comment on the issue, not closing it):

Converted to `agent_run`, mirroring the same conversion already documented in `docs/manifest/routine.md`.

No UI dropdown exists for step-type/runtime selection (routines are authored via free-text chat or a raw JSON/YAML editor), so there was no dropdown to hide — the fix was aligning the docs/schema/examples that do advertise runtime availability.

author: robtfm
body:
Migrates realtime avatar movement — position, velocity, rotation, animation state, emotes, and profile-version announcements — from the LiveKit data channel onto the server-authoritative **Pulse** transport (UDP/ENet natively, WebTransport on wasm; server-quantized deltas over a per-subject sliding-window baseline). The rest of the client is untouched: every Pulse `PlayerState` is reconstructed into an `rfc4::Movement` and pushed through the existing `global_crdt` / `foreign_dynamics` pipeline, so nothing downstream learns Pulse exists.

## Highlights
- **Native ENet driver** (`rusty_enet`) with the full connection lifecycle: signed-auth handshake, teleport, and reconnect.
- **WebTransport driver for wasm** (`crates/comms/src/pulse/wasm.rs`) — the browser speaks Pulse over WebTransport (HTTP/3 / QUIC): a length-framed reliable bidi stream plus sequenced/unsequenced datagrams, matching the server's framing exactly. Native and wasm share the byte-boundary `PulseDriverChannels` seam; only the driver differs.
- **Proto-driven quantization ABI** — the dequantize/quantize accessors are generated from the pulse `.proto` field options (`build_quant.rs`), so the client can't silently drift from the C# server's `protoc-gen-bitwise` constants. Tracks protocol #431 (power-law velocity) and the quantized `PlayerState`.
- **Foreign-avatar smoothing** — position deltas are treated as a ±half-step *box* and dead-reckoned within it rather than snapped to the quantized centre, killing low-speed jitter. Head yaw/pitch preserve sign across the unsigned `[0,360]` quantizer.
- **Scene-driven animation decoupled** from movement (rides its own packet; animation stays on LiveKit).
- **Pulse gated to the realm island** — scene rooms stay on LiveKit; no double-delivery.

## ⚠️ Do not merge until the Pulse WebTransport server is deployed
Both drivers now exist — native (UDP/ENet, port 7777) and wasm (WebTransport, port 7443). The remaining gate is server-side: the Pulse server's WebTransport endpoint must be deployed to the target realms before the web client can connect. Until then the wasm build's Pulse transport won't establish (the default targets `pulse-server.decentraland.org:7443`), so a web client on a Pulse realm has no working movement transport. Draft until the server's deployed.

author: dkayiwa
body:
## Description of what I changed

Saving a drug order whose duration units concept carries the current SNOMED CT minute code fails with HTTP 500: `Unknown code 1156209001 for SNOMED CT duration units` (`org.openmrs.Duration:104`). SNOMED CT inactivated the legacy minute code `258701004` ("min", ambiguous) in its 2021-07-31 release, and dictionaries that track SNOMED CT releases now map their minutes concepts to the active code `1156209001`. CIEL's Minutes (1733) today carries SAME-AS mappings to *both* SNOMED codes, plus UCUM `min`.

The 500 is a symptom of three related defects in how core resolves duration units:

1. **Validation and execution disagree.** `SimpleDosingInstructions.validate()` and `DrugOrderValidator` accept a units concept if it has *any* SNOMED CT SAME-AS code, while `Duration.addToDate()` requires the code to be on a hardcoded list. A concept mapped to a real-but-unrecognized code passes validation and then throws at save time, surfacing as an HTTP 500 instead of a validation error.
2. **Resolution is nondeterministic.** `Duration.getCode()` returns the first SNOMED SAME-AS code in mapping-set iteration order. With CIEL's Minutes now carrying two SNOMED SAME-AS codes, whether an order saves depends on which mapping happens to be returned first.
3. **The hardcoded code list ages.** Core only knew the pre-2021 SNOMED codes, so every vocabulary change breaks order saving platform-wide until core chases the new code.

**The fix** introduces one deterministic resolution, `Duration.getDuration(Integer duration, Concept durationUnits)`, shared by auto-expiry derivation and both validators. Callers go straight from the order fields to a `Duration`; reference term codes stay entirely under the hood.

- It considers **all** SAME-AS mappings of the concept to the SNOMED CT and UCUM sources (each matched by its HL7 code or its source name), not just whichever mapping iterates first.
- Codes resolve to a unit through source-scoped registries (one per vocabulary, so a code can never resolve through the wrong source) that also know the current SNOMED CT minute code `1156209001` and the UCUM time codes `s`, `min`, `h`, `d`, `wk`, `mo`, `a`. UCUM codes are stable by design, which makes resolution robust against future SNOMED code churn instead of chasing codes one release at a time.
- SNOMED CT mappings take priority: the first SNOMED CT mapping carrying a known code resolves the concept, and UCUM is consulted only when no SNOMED CT mapping does. Per review, refusing to resolve when SNOMED CT and UCUM mappings disagree would have imposed a consistency rule on data that was valid while UCUM was ignored; with source priority, every concept that resolves today keeps resolving identically however its UCUM mappings are curated, and UCUM strictly extends resolution to concepts that previously resolved to nothing.
- `BaseDosingInstructions.getAutoExpireDate()`, `SimpleDosingInstructions.validate()` and `DrugOrderValidator` all use it, so an unresolvable unit is rejected at validation time with the existing `durationUnits` field error, and auto-expiry derivation can no longer throw for dictionary data. `Duration.getCode()` is deprecated with behavior unchanged (fhir2 still calls it), and `addToDate(...)` keeps accepting bare codes for API compatibility.

**Behavior compatibility:**

- Concepts mapped to the legacy SNOMED codes (existing working deployments): unchanged.
- CIEL-current dictionaries (the reported failure): orders save, deterministically.
- Concepts mapped only to UCUM: previously rejected by validation, now work.
- Concepts whose SNOMED SAME-AS code is unknown to core: previously passed validation and then failed with a 500 at save; now rejected at validation with a meaningful message.

## Verification

- `258701004` inactive since 2021-07-31 and `1156209001` active, confirmed against a SNOMED terminology server (tx.fhir.org `$lookup`).
- dev3 (platform 2.8.7, current CIEL): Minutes is the only duration unit whose SNOMED mapping changed; it carries both SNOMED codes as SAME-AS plus UCUM `min`. Most units in the "Duration units" set (CIEL 1732) also carry their UCUM code; Hours (1822) carries a malformed UCUM mapping (`h57.1`, reported upstream), which resolution skips as designed, so Hours resolves through its still-active SNOMED code and has no UCUM fallback until the CIEL mapping is fixed.
- `DurationTest`, `SimpleDosingInstructionsTest` and `DrugOrderValidatorTest` pass locally, with cases for the current minute code, the UCUM codes, multi-mapping concepts, unknown codes, the SNOMED CT preference when a UCUM mapping disagrees, the UCUM fallback when the only SNOMED CT code is unknown, case-insensitive UCUM source names and source filtering.

## Issue I worked on

see https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/TRUNK-6674

## Checklist: I completed these to help reviewers :)

- [x] My IDE is configured to follow the code style of this project.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [ ] I ran `mvn clean package` right before creating this pull request and added all formatting changes to my commit.
- [x] All new and existing tests in the touched test classes pass locally; full suite left to CI.
- [x] My pull request is based on the latest changes of the master branch.

Opened as an independently derived fix at the maintainer's request, without consulting the other open PRs for this report, so the approaches can be compared.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)





## Alternatives considered

- **Runtime-configurable code registry** (global property or metadata mapping): would let admins add codes without a platform release, but it moves a semantic-correctness decision ("this code means days") from compile-time review into runtime config, where a typo silently changes when medications auto-expire. For codes that have changed once in roughly a decade, that trades a rare, loud, reviewed failure for a rare, silent, config-shaped one. The existing split is kept deliberately: implementations configure *which concepts* are orderable duration units; the platform owns *what the codes mean*.
- **Terminology-server lookup** (ask SNOMED CT whether a code denotes a unit of time): adds a runtime dependency and offline failure modes, and still would not supply the calendar arithmetic each unit needs.
- **UCUM as the only vocabulary**: closest to durable, since UCUM codes are stable by design and FHIR's `Timing.UnitsOfTime` hardcodes the same seven, but every existing dictionary carries SNOMED mappings, so SNOMED stays first-class with UCUM alongside as the stable rail.
- **Repurposing `SNOMED_CT_MINUTES_CODE` to the new value** instead of adding a constant: public String constants inline at compile time, so modules compiled against older core keep the old value until rebuilt and then silently flip behavior; fhir2's translator map is the concrete casualty.

What makes the compiled-in registry safe, and must be preserved when extending it: entries are additive and never removed or repurposed; concepts that resolve to nothing fail as validation errors, never a save-time 500; and two vocabulary rails, with SNOMED CT taking priority and UCUM filling gaps, mean no single SNOMED inactivation is load-bearing. This rationale is also summarized in the `Duration` class Javadoc.

## Inhalt der AGB (SaaS/Freemium-Bausteine)
- Anbieter/Geltungsbereich · Leistungsbeschreibung mit **Freemium-Vorbehalt** (künftige Bezahltarife; Datenzugang/-export bleibt).
- **„Keine Steuer-/Rechtsberatung"** als eigener Abschnitt — NK-Abrechnung, Anlage V, AfA, Kalkulatoren und Auto-Fristen ausdrücklich Rechenhilfen ohne Gewähr. Für dieses Produkt die wichtigste Klausel.
- Registrierung/Vertragsschluss · Nutzerpflichten (Nutzer = Verantwortlicher für Mieterdaten → AVV; Freigabelink-Verantwortung; Datensicherung/§ 147 AO) · Verfügbarkeit ohne Quote im Gratis-Umfang.
- **Für spätere Bezahltarife vorbereitet:** Preise/Zahlung (USt./Kleinunternehmer-Platzhalter), Verbraucher-Widerruf inkl. Erlöschenshinweis § 356 Abs. 5 BGB.
- Laufzeit/Kündigung (Nutzer jederzeit via „Konto löschen"; Anbieter 4 Wochen beim Gratis-Dienst; außerordentlich bei Missbrauch) · Nutzungsrechte · Haftung (Kardinalpflichten) · AGB-Änderungsverfahren (4-Wochen-Ankündigung + Widerspruch) · Schluss (dt. Recht, ODR-Link).

- **Login-Consent** nennt jetzt „AGB + Datenschutzerklärung + AVV" (Fehlertext angepasst); Login-Footer + Einstellungen → Daten & Recht verlinken `/agb`.

## Summary

Adds an interactive 3D browse mode to the generated HTML diagram. It is opt-in (`--3d`), lazy-loads Three.js + 3d-force-graph from CDN only when the mode is entered, and leaves the 2D Viz.js path untouched.

- Force-directed 3D scene with level-of-detail labels, click-to-open state cards (property / action grids), tag filtering mirrored from 2D, and `?mode=3d` URL state
- Two theme sets — `botanical` (default) and `cosmos` (`--theme cosmos`)
