- Settings flyout (S key) with sliders persisted to localStorage; `prefers-reduced-motion` honored
- Demo pages (amazon / bookstore / lms) regenerated from the current generator

## Supersedes #252

The head of #252 (`02f1bd6`) is an ancestor of this branch, so this PR contains all of that work. Both actionable findings @coderabbitai raised there are fixed here (`39b7535`):

- `refreshGraphData()` keyed its fast path on the tag selection alone, so replacing `window.alpsData` under the same tags kept the previous nodes, links and stats. The document identity is now part of the cache key.
- `open3D()` only moved focus to the exit button after the CDN libraries resolved, leaving focus on the now-inert background during the load, and on the failure path entirely. The dialog is focused as soon as the overlay goes up.

The third finding (3D palette diverging from the canonical descriptor colors) was withdrawn as an intentional WebGL/emissive design choice; the 2D diagram, legend and table keep the canonical colors.

author: turnipdabeets
body:
## Problem

The credential used for local feature flag evaluation and remote config accepts **either** a Personal API Key (`phx_...`) **or** a Project Secret API Key (`phs_...`), but the config field is named `personalAPIKey`. That name is misleading — it implies only a personal API key is valid.

## Change

Add a new canonical `secretKey` argument to `PostHog::init()` and `Client::__construct()`, and keep `personalAPIKey` as a **deprecated, backwards-compatible alias**. This is **non-breaking**:

- The effective credential resolves as `secretKey ?? personalAPIKey`. When both are provided, `secretKey` wins.
- The resolved value is stored on the new `secretKey` field and mirrored onto the existing `personalAPIKey` field so all internal reads (and any reflection-based access) keep working.
- `personalAPIKey` is marked deprecated in phpdoc, pointing users to `secretKey`.
- New `secretKey` param/field carries a tooltip-friendly doc comment (accepts a Personal API Key or Project Secret API Key, defaults to null, used for local flag evaluation and remote config).
- Public API snapshot (`api/public-api.json`) updated for the new trailing optional param on both entry points.

Tests cover: `secretKey` sets the credential, `personalAPIKey` still works as an alias, and `secretKey` wins when both are set.

## Context

From Slack + PostHog/posthog-js#4046, this is the rename item only, part of a coordinated rename across backend SDKs. Mirrors the change already merged as draft in posthog-python (PR #727).

author: tylerwashington888
body:
## Purpose

Remediates Wiz SAST finding **WS-I002-JAVASCRIPT-00027** (Disclosure of Error Details and Stack Traces) in the Bedrock Content Generator app.

Passing raw error objects to `console.error` can expose internal stack traces, error messages, and implementation details in production logs, which may leak sensitive information.

- **ACT ticket**: https://contentful.atlassian.net/browse/ACT-3524
- **Wiz issue**: https://app.wiz.io/p/production/issues#%7E%28issue%7E%2746da7ad8-bbed-4019-8e22-cd7bb62cfc88%29

## Approach

Single-line change in `CommonGenerator.tsx` at line 75.

**Before:**
```typescript
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error);
}
```

**After:**
```typescript
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Generation failed:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error');
}
```

The raw error object is replaced with a controlled string. The `error.message` is included (not a stack trace) for debuggability, guarded by an `instanceof Error` check to avoid leaking non-Error throw values.

**Validity assessment**: VALID — line 75 is a textbook match for WS-I002 (`console.error(error)` with raw error object in a catch block, in a non-test file). Confidence: HIGH.

Note: Wiz API was unavailable (`WIZ_API_TOKEN` not set); the fix was inferred from the rule ID and direct code inspection. The pattern is unambiguous.

## Testing steps

1. Open the Bedrock Content Generator app in a Contentful space.
2. Trigger a generation failure (e.g., disconnect network or use an invalid locale).
3. Verify the console shows `Generation failed: <message>` instead of the raw Error object.
4. Run unit tests: `npx nx test bedrock-content-generator`

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a one-line logger message change with no behavior impact on the happy path.

## Dependencies and/or References

- ACT-3524: https://contentful.atlassian.net/browse/ACT-3524
- Wiz issue 46da7ad8-bbed-4019-8e22-cd7bb62cfc88: https://app.wiz.io/p/production/issues#%7E%28issue%7E%2746da7ad8-bbed-4019-8e22-cd7bb62cfc88%29
- Rule: WS-I002-JAVASCRIPT-00027 — Disclosure of Error Details and Stack Traces

## Deployment

No deployment concerns. Logger-only change, no schema or API impact.

Fresh-eyes pass over the repo. State found: 255 tests green across both apps, `tsc --noEmit` clean, both `next build`s pass, lint has 0 errors (2 pre-existing warnings). The project is live on 4 surfaces and well past shippable; the handoff/tix hygiene is genuinely good. ## The bug

`formatSol` truncated to 4 decimal places with no small-amount fallback, so a **real claimable drip below 0.0001 SOL rendered as flat "0"** on `/vaults` while the Claim button stayed live — e.g. 0.01 SOL on the hourly 1-week preset drips ~0.0000595 SOL per reload. This is exactly the bug class fixed on the EVM side in `582f983` (`format.ts` significant-digit fallback); the Solana formatter never got the fix, and it was duplicated in two page files.

## Changes

- **fix(sol)**: extracted `formatSol` / `parseSolAmount` / `formatCountdown` from the duplicated page copies into `packages/app-sol/src/lib/format.ts`; sub-0.0001 amounts on a zero whole part now fall back to two significant digits. Output stays plain-decimal and comma-free because Max feeds `formatSol` output back into `parseSolAmount`. 19 new tests, including the Max round-trip invariant `parseSolAmount(formatSol(x)) <= x` and truncate-never-round (a claimable must not overpromise).
- **test(app)**: `formatTokenAmount` (every displayed EVM amount routes through it) had zero tests — pinned 2-dp trim, thousands separators, 18-dp BNB USDC, the sub-cent drip fallback, boundary rounding, and the `maxFractionDigits` override.

author: shuddery
body:
## Beauty Salon Appointment Scheduler Implementation

### Overview
This PR implements a comprehensive appointment scheduling system for a beauty salon in New York, providing robust date/time parsing, validation, and formatted descriptions for customer appointments.

### Key Features
- **Appointment Parsing**: Converts textual date descriptions to `LocalDateTime` objects using flexible formatting
- **Appointment Validation**: Checks if appointments have already passed
- **Time Classification**: Identifies afternoon appointments (12:00 - 18:00)
- **Formatted Descriptions**: Generates human-readable appointment descriptions with proper date/time formatting
- **Anniversary Tracking**: Returns the salon's anniversary date (September 15th) for the current year

### Technical Details
- **Java Time API**: Uses `java.time` package for all date/time operations
- **DateTimeFormatter**: Pre-compiled formatters for consistent and efficient parsing/formatting
- **Locale Support**: English locale for proper date and time formatting
- **Immutable Design**: All methods work with immutable `LocalDateTime` objects

### Implementation Highlights
- **Single Responsibility**: Each method handles a specific scheduling concern
- **Performance Optimization**: Formatters created once as static constants
- **Type Safety**: Proper use of `LocalDateTime` and `LocalDate` for date/time operations
- **Readable Code**: Clean separation of parsing, validation, and formatting logic

### Example Usage
```java
AppointmentScheduler scheduler = new AppointmentScheduler();

// Parse appointment
LocalDateTime appointment = scheduler.schedule("7/25/2019 13:45:00");

// Check if passed
scheduler.hasPassed(appointment); // => false

// Check if afternoon
scheduler.isAfternoonAppointment(appointment); // => true

// Get description
scheduler.getDescription(appointment); 
// => "You have an appointment on Thursday, July 25, 2019, at 1:45 PM."

// Get anniversary
scheduler.getAnniversaryDate(); // => 2026-09-15

## Summary
Addresses the calibration issue from real-world testing (Schlafzimmer, window open): TTS volume stayed close to `min_vol` even with audible street noise, because the -50/-25 dBFS default threshold range didn't match observed ambient levels (open window ≈ -40 to -50 dBFS).

- Lower default thresholds: `quiet_db` -50 → **-55** dBFS, `loud_db` -25 → **-38** dBFS (15 dB range instead of 25 dB → more aggressive scaling)
- Add `Volume Curve Exponent` number entity (default 1.0 = linear; values < 1.0 apply `ratio ^ exponent` for a steeper ramp-up at moderate noise levels)
- Add `Ambient Noise Level (Fast)` sensor (1s update) alongside the existing 5s sensor, for watching values change live while opening/closing a window
- Extend the TTS log line with the full calibration breakdown: `TTS volume → 0.72  (ambient -42.3 dBFS, quiet=-55 loud=-38, ratio=0.48)`

author: akiomik
body:
## Summary

There was no built-in way to observe where a tears app spends time or why a subscription/command behaves unexpectedly. This PR adds `tracing` instrumentation to the runtime's hot paths, so they can be inspected with the standard `tracing` ecosystem.

This is the first of two PRs for backlog task **S3** (measurement foundation). The criterion benchmark baseline is a separate follow-up PR.

## Changes

- Add `tracing` as a normal (always-on) dependency
- Emit events at the runtime hot paths:
  - `tears::runtime`: message batch processed (with count), subscriptions updated (with count), command spawned, frame rendered, runtime started / shutting down, quit signal received
  - `tears::subscription`: subscription started / stopped
- Document observability in the crate-level docs and CHANGELOG
- Add a contract test (minimal counting `Subscriber`) proving instrumentation actually fires

## Design note

`tracing` is always-on rather than feature-gated, matching ecosystem-standard crates (tokio, hyper, reqwest). Events are inert unless a subscriber is installed, so the overhead without one is a cached atomic load per callsite — this avoids the cfg/no-op-shim complexity of feature-gating.

## Notes

- Additive / non-breaking: one new dependency, no public API signature changes. No version bump (handled at release time).

## Testing

- `cargo test` — 120 lib tests pass, including the new `test_process_message_batch_emits_tracing_event`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` — clean
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean

body:
## Description

Replaces all uses of std::unordered_map/set with boost unordered_flat_map/set, and replaces std::unordered_multimap with boost::unordered_multimap. This provides a nice speedup on the purplebench suite locally (though results were noisy on my laptop so take this with a grain of salt). I'd appreciate a benchmark run on the dedicated machine.

The only real risk here is flat_map's reference (in)stability across inserts. I don't see any cases where this is currently a problem. There may be some instances where unordered_map is better than flat_map, eg where the value type is large, or in cases with a lot of updates. I ran the BalancerV3Vault benchmark case, flat_map vs unordered_map for these instances locally and flat_map was never worse, but this could use more testing:

(these are cases where the value is non-trivial (eg std::set), and/or there's potentially a lot of mutation)
CommonSubexpressionEliminator.h:172
ControlFlowSideEffectsCollector.h:130
CommonSubexpressionEliminator.h:66
DataFlowAnalyzer.h:184
SSACFGBuilder.h:159

author: abpai
body:
## Summary

- Adds `generate` wrapper mode for Codex as an **implementation candidate** in dual-candidate orchestration loops (e.g. Fable orchestrates, Codex + Opus each implement, parent compares and synthesizes).
- Ships `generate.md` workflow, `candidate-report.schema.json`, and a phased improvement plan in `references/implementation-candidate-plan.md`.
- `generate` defaults to `workspace-write` + `high` reasoning and captures post-run git artifacts (`changed-files.txt`, `workspace.diff`, `workspace-diff.stat`, `workspace-status.txt`).

## Plan (phased)

| Phase | Scope | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | `generate` mode, workflow doc, report schema, SKILL/README updates | This PR |
| **2** | `codex-workspace.sh` for branch/worktree prepare/finalize/cleanup | Future |
| **3** | Dual-candidate orchestration reference kit for parent agents | Future |
| **4** | `--validation-cmd`, `--base-ref` diff capture, integration tests | Future |

## Dogfooding & fixes

Hardened by dogfooding the skill with Claude subagents (2 review, 2 dual-candidate `generate` given the same brief in separate worktrees), each driving the skill unaided and logging friction.

- **Critical fix:** the bundled `candidate-report.schema.json` was invalid under OpenAI strict mode (`notes` in `properties` but not `required`), so **every default `generate` run failed ~5s in with `invalid_json_schema`**. The `--dry-run` test path never calls the API, so it shipped green. Fixed (`notes` nullable + in `required`) and verified end-to-end (exit 0, valid structured report).
- **Regression guard:** `scripts/check_strict_schema.py` now lints every codex-exec output schema in `validate-skills.sh`/CI so this class of bug can't ship silently again.
- **Wrapper default:** `generate` now instructs Codex not to commit/push (was caller-only); verified Codex leaves an uncommitted diff.
- **Docs from friction logs:** how to background the wrapper (it doesn't daemonize), bounded `run_dir_file` poll, `state=` completion signal, `user-prompt.txt`, explicit `--uncommitted`, and an `invalid_json_schema` troubleshooting entry; `git worktree add` example + per-candidate scratch isolation in `generate.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n codex-exec/skills/codex-exec/scripts/codex-run.sh`
- [x] `codex-run.sh generate --dry-run --prompt-file …` in skills repo — confirms mode routing and prompt wrapper
- [x] Live `generate` run with authenticated Codex CLI against an isolated worktree — exit 0, valid structured report, Codex leaves an uncommitted diff (dual-candidate dogfood + direct repro)
- [ ] Parent orchestrator compares Codex `workspace.diff` against an Opus candidate diff (dual-Codex candidates were exercised; Codex-vs-Opus comparison is Phase 3)

body:
## ⚠️ Stacked on #684 (which stacks on #680) — merge those first
Based on `fix/audit-flag-collapse`; heavy overlap in `app/home/`. After #680 → #684 merge, this diff collapses to its own changes.

## Summary
Sixth slice of the audit remediation: **-5,938 lines** (net -5,801) of maintained-but-unshipped code. Every deletion was verified zero-production-consumer by repo-wide reference search (including templates, scripts, workflows) before removal. Tests that existed only to keep dead code green were deleted; tests carrying live contracts were retargeted at the live surfaces (e.g. the permalink-less-program feed test now runs through `day_groups`, the civic-tier contract pins `sandstone._event_tier`).

**What's gone (highlights):**
- **Track-A chat residue in `app/core`** — `conversation_copy.py`, ~330 lines of `slots.py` (kept `extract_date_range`, which the classifier uses on every request), the session flow/await state machine, and 4 orphaned helpers.
- **Pre-v4 home sediment (~1,900 lines)** — `today_feed.py`, `algorithmic_picks.py`, `snowbird_panel.py` (never wired), the BUILD.md-era home builders in `queries.py`, ~530 lines of window-feed/tonight-card builders in `home/router.py`, the retired "Places & Ongoing" surface, `calendar_view.build_calendar` (route-less after #684).
- **Computed-per-request-but-rendered-nowhere** — `primary_nav`/`mega_columns`/`service_tiles` context (built with DB queries on `/gas`, `/movies`, `/provider/*`, category pages, events-ui, mode landings — no template renders them), `explore_tiles`/`directory_primary_tiles`, the lake mode-landing config (`/lake` has 301'd since IA v2).
- **Orphaned helpers** — 2 unused event-dedup functions, unused photo-URL plural/wrapper functions, `photos/schemas.py`, `r2_client.delete_object`, 2 categories helpers, `LhusdEvent.dedupe_key`, halt3's provably-dead mentioned-name filter.

**Deliberately kept (with in-code notes):** `llm_cache.lookup/store` (39 tests need a real port to the `_with_embedding` variants — goes with the tier-2 consolidation PR); the `GENERIC_CATEGORY` placement regime (a complete, tested feature blocked on a documented classifier-wiring decision — deleting it forecloses the BACKLOG'd monetization option); `category_cards` (its liveness-dampener tests need porting onto `category_listing` — goes with the placement-helper consolidation).

Also surfaced in passing: the legacy `/calendar`'s free-text "for seniors" filter had **no v4 equivalent** — it was never served in prod, but if you want that filter on the v4 calendar it's a small new feature (noted in `calendar_view.py`).

## Gates
- `pytest -q`: **12,274 passed, 13 skipped**
- `ruff check .` clean, `mypy app` clean

body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements and refactoring to the benchmarking and modules API, with a focus on supporting material consumption data, improving code organization, and enhancing API versioning support. The changes add new structures and logic to handle material benchmarks, refactor module parsing and insertion, and introduce versioned endpoints for module creation and retrieval.

**Benchmarking Enhancements:**

- Added support for material consumption in benchmarking data structures and logic, including the new `material` field in `BenchmarkData` and `BenchmarkSeries`, and updated all related functions and handlers to process and return material data. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4R37-R46) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4L52-R68) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4R82-R107) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4R121-R150) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4L142-R186) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4L160-R201) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4L181-R222) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4L203-R240) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-b57da4af7d96abc4e646ef06bba86220282fd0b993e60fbe5a48aa1a2608b0d4L214-R251) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-2a0f7488f8833a1dc2bd19db31648cfc9eee662e53a24e4bc4f53822c4df9263L99-R108)

**Module API Refactoring and Versioning:**

- Refactored module parsing logic by splitting it into `parseModulePayload` and `parseModuleFromPayload`, and introduced a centralized `insertModule` function to handle validation, calculation, and persistence. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5448ab82aeca81db5c1c19de8bca10dbf30606a3a4326f44d27ee63cfb2b5a7bL15-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5448ab82aeca81db5c1c19de8bca10dbf30606a3a4326f44d27ee63cfb2b5a7bR50-R81)
- Added versioned handlers for module creation and retrieval (`createModuleV1Handler`, `readModuleV1Handler`) to support both legacy and new API formats, with appropriate validation and response shaping for each version. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5448ab82aeca81db5c1c19de8bca10dbf30606a3a4326f44d27ee63cfb2b5a7bL118-R244) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5448ab82aeca81db5c1c19de8bca10dbf30606a3a4326f44d27ee63cfb2b5a7bR254-R268) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5448ab82aeca81db5c1c19de8bca10dbf30606a3a4326f44d27ee63cfb2b5a7bL195-R362)
- Updated module duplication logic to include material totals and ensure all relevant fields are copied and processed. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5448ab82aeca81db5c1c19de8bca10dbf30606a3a4326f44d27ee63cfb2b5a7bR114) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5448ab82aeca81db5c1c19de8bca10dbf30606a3a4326f44d27ee63cfb2b5a7bR130-R140)

**Material Consumption Backfill:**

- Introduced new functions to backfill missing material consumption data for modules (`syncMissingModuleConsumptions`, `backfillMissingModuleConsumptions`), and triggered this process during application startup. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-097729c5adafafaebcb6e494d0a995012f93f29514ab908291bc13d3899cb146R1-R68) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ae22ad1e20b89eaefa8e09e4ed89443ac10fdc555b9767625f3866e3853100afR108-R120) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ae22ad1e20b89eaefa8e09e4ed89443ac10fdc555b9767625f3866e3853100afL128-R141)

These changes collectively improve the robustness, maintainability, and extensibility of the benchmarking and modules APIs, while ensuring compatibility with both current and legacy clients.

author: sethkarten
body: ## Summary - Route scheduled heartbeat and RLM heartbeat jobs through hidden custom context messages instead of visible user follow-up prompts. - Keep heartbeat contexts counted for internal busy/coalescing logic while excluding them from visible queue previews and session list pending counts. - Add tests for hidden heartbeat queueing, delivery, and daemon cron routing. ## Tests - `npm run check` - `npx tsx ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/suite/agent-session-queue.test.ts test/daemon-mode.test.ts` - `npx tsx ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/daemon-session-list.test.ts test/agent-connection-in-process.test.ts test/daemon-session-summarizer-lifecycle.test.ts test/agents-view-state.test.ts` --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches daemon cron scheduling, session queue draining, and busy/shutdown semantics; behavior changes when heartbeats fire during streaming, bash, or agent-message flows, though coverage is added in queue and daemon tests. > > **Overview** > **Heartbeat cron delivery no longer shows up in the chat queue.** Scheduled heartbeat and RLM heartbeat jobs are wrapped as hidden `heartbeat_context` custom messages (`display: false`) and queued via new `queueHeartbeatContext` / `runHeartbeatContext` on `AgentSession`, instead of visible `followUp` text or RPC prompts with a `heartbeat:` coalescing key. > > **Pending counts split for UI vs internals.** `visiblePendingMessageCount` excludes heartbeat-only queue entries; snapshots, agent-observe summaries, and daemon deferral for heartbeats use that visible count so users do not see a fake queued prompt. Full `pendingMessageCount` still includes hidden heartbeats for coalescing, post-bash drain, and **session `isBusy`** so heartbeat-only work keeps sessions marked working and blocks unsafe daemon shutdown. > > **Daemon cron routing** runs idle heartbeat jobs through `runHeartbeatContext` under an agent-message target lock (skipped when locks or agent-message accept/prepare are active). Post-bash drain now also waits on bash and re-queues heartbeat custom messages on prompt failure. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit cfbfb425abac5950cd1fae86e908bc619b7c56ee. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). > [!NOTE] > ### Hide heartbeat prompts from the visible chat queue using hidden context messages > - Heartbeat cron jobs are now delivered as hidden custom messages (`HEARTBEAT_CONTEXT_CUSTOM_TYPE`) via `session.runHeartbeatContext()` rather than as visible follow-up prompts, so they do not appear in the chat queue. > - Adds `visiblePendingMessageCount` to `AgentSession` that excludes hidden heartbeat contexts; snapshots and summaries use this for displayed pending counts. > - Busy detection (`isSessionBusy`, `isActiveSessionBusy`) now also checks `summary.isBusy`, which is set when hidden heartbeat work is in-flight even if visible pending count is zero. > - Heartbeat delivery is skipped (not queued) when the target session is locked or already processing an agent message. > - Behavioral Change: `pendingMessageCount` in agent connection snapshots and daemon summaries now reflects only user-visible queued messages, while internal busy state still accounts for hidden heartbeat work. > > > > Macroscope summarized cfbfb42. > >

## Summary

Implements #32 — the library-owned contract consumer control planes attach through, designed against [agent-control-plane-core](https://github.com/AlexanderMattTurner/agent-control-plane-core) as the reference consumer (its `bin/*-hook.mjs` clients forward normalized `ToolCallEvent`s to a consumer gate service and render the returned `Verdict` natively; this PR provides the rendezvous, readiness, and egress plumbing that gate needs).

## Changes

- **Schema** — optional `control_plane` object: `require` (ready-marker names, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`) and `egress_grants` (`{uid >= 1, hosts[]}`, IP literals rejected at schema level since draft-07 `format` is annotation-only).
- **Rendezvous volume** — new `control-plane` named volume, mounted read-only at `/run/control-plane` in the workload (`CONTROL_PLANE_DIR` exported); consumer `--extra-compose` services mount it read-write to publish `<name>.ready` markers and rendezvous config (e.g. `gate.addr`). Rendezvous is by static IP on the internal net — `.5`–`.9` reserved for consumers — because the workload's DNS is pinned to the firewall's resolver, so compose aliases do not resolve (`docs/control-plane.md`).
- **Ready barrier** — `_stack_wait_control_plane_ready` blocks after `up`, before seed/exec, until every required marker exists (bounded by `AGENT_SANDBOX_READY_TIMEOUT`, default 60s); timeout fails closed with teardown, naming the missing markers. A tool call can never race an un-ready gate.
- **Egress grants** — `stack_export_control_plane_grants` validates (uid integer ≥ 1, hostname-shaped hosts, duplicate-uid rejection — a duplicate would wipe the first grant's fresh ipset) and exports `CONTROL_PLANE_EGRESS_GRANTS` to the firewall; `render_control_plane_grants` (init-firewall) creates a `cp-grant-<uid>` ipset per grant via the existing batched resolver, pins hosts in a refresh-surviving dnsmasq conf-dir file (the allowlist conf is rewritten wholesale each refresh cycle), and appends `-m owner --uid-owner <uid>` ACCEPT on 443 — **before** the OUTPUT chain's final REJECT and before dnsmasq starts (an append after the REJECT can never match; dnsmasq reads `address=` only at start). Grant hosts never enter squid's allowlist or the workload-reachable set: resolution is not reachability. Fail-closed on any resolve/ipset/iptables failure; firewall-side re-validates the raw env.
- **Audit relay topology documented** — the consumer gate mounts `audit-secret` read-only and relays records; the workload never holds the secret, preserving the tamper-evidence boundary.
- New `firewall_cp_grant_applied` trace event; `docs/control-plane.md` is the contract doc.

## Testing

- `tests/test_control_plane.py` (19 tests: barrier satisfied/timeout/absent, grants export/refusals, grant rendering with exact iptables argv, fail-closed resolver) + 18 new schema cases in `test_workload_schema.py` — all pass, plus the neighbor suites (`test_stack_seams`, `test_stack_secrets_tty`, `test_stack_services`, `test_launcher`, `test_lifecycle_verbs`, all `test_firewall_*`).
- Bash non-vacuity by hand-mutation (no CI mutation gate for bash): grant port 443→80, swallowed resolve failure, dropped barrier call, empty-grants export flip — each turned exactly its covering test red; restored byte-identical.
- `bash -n` / `shellcheck` / `shfmt` clean on all touched bash.

Closes #32.

author: cneckar
body:
## Summary

Closes the last gap in the serverless steering flow: `SteeringEffect` resolved its vector directory from a hardcoded `"outputs/steering_vectors"`, so vectors regenerated to the network volume were **never read at inference** — the worker kept loading the committed (wrong-dim for gpt-oss) vectors from the ephemeral container.

`vector_dir` now resolves as **explicit arg > `STEERING_DIR` env > repo default**, matching the handler's `STEERING_DIR`. Setting `STEERING_DIR=/runpod-volume/steering_vectors` on the endpoint makes the regenerated gpt-oss vectors actually apply and persist across scale-to-zero. Added the missing module-level `import os`. Deploy README updated to note `STEERING_DIR` is dual-purpose (job writes there **and** inference loads from there).

Pre-existing `BaseEffect` F821 lint reds in this file are unrelated (they're the known `main` CI state); the change itself is flake8-clean.

author: nabinhait
body:
Adds unit tests for the **Accounts Payable Summary** report, which had none.

The report is a thin wrapper over `AccountsReceivableSummary` with `account_type=Payable`. The tests lock the supplier-side output that was previously untested:

- Invoiced -> advance -> partial-payment progression for a single supplier (advance shown in its own column, ageing bucket rolls down as the balance shrinks).
- `supp_master_name = Naming Series` adds the supplier-name column.
- `show_gl_balance` adds the GL-balance / difference columns and reconciles to zero.
- `show_future_payments` adds the remaining-balance column.
- A fully-paid invoice drops the supplier out of the summary.

## How to test
1. Create a supplier and submit a Purchase Invoice against it.
2. Open **Accounts Payable Summary**, filter by that supplier -> confirm invoiced/outstanding and the ageing bucket.
3. Record a partial Payment Entry -> outstanding and the bucket shrink; an unallocated payment shows under **Advance Amount**.
4. Tick **Show GL Balance** and **Show Future Payments** -> the extra columns appear and reconcile.
5. Pay the invoice in full -> the supplier disappears from the report.

author: dapperdivers
body:
Unblocks #3548's dead-man's switch (follow-up in the #3541 series).

The `alertmanager` ExternalSecret was still on the broken `find: path:` pattern — both lookups return nothing since the Infisical folder reorg, so the ES had been silently coasting on its last good sync. Adding `HEALTHCHECK_HEARTBEAT_URL` to the template turned that latent breakage into a hard `SecretSyncedError` (template references a key the finds never fetch).

Verified against live Infisical with a throwaway probe ES: `find.name.regexp` returns all three keys (`PUSHOVER_USER_KEY`, `ALERTMANAGER_PUSHOVER_TOKEN`, `HEALTHCHECK_HEARTBEAT_URL`); `find.path` returns none of them. This is the same migration already applied to the volsync component and the postgres apps.

Verification after merge: ES goes `SecretSynced=True`, `alertmanager-secret` gains `HEALTHCHECK_HEARTBEAT_URL`, and healthchecks.io starts receiving Watchdog pings every ~5m.

body:
## Summary

For v0.1, production inference will load the champion model via a plain `save`/`load` from a directory baked directly into the Docker image at build time — no MLflow client, run ID, or cache lookup on the runtime path. Previously the design (and the `production_model_run_id` setting) assumed production would call `BaseForecaster.load_from_mlflow(run_id, cache_base_path)`, relying on its local-disk cache for MLflow-outage resilience. That's unnecessary complexity for v0.1: if the model is already baked into the image, there's nothing to cache.

- Removed the now-unused `Settings.production_model_run_id` field (only ever referenced in docs, never read by real code).
- Updated `Settings.model_cache_base_path`'s docstring — it's still used, but only by the CV pipeline now.
- Updated `docs/architecture/ml-orchestration.md` and `docs/roadmap/live-service.md` (requirements, the `live_forecasts` asset design, the "Production model artifacts" decision, the container-build implementation notes, and the promotion runbook) to describe the simpler v0.1 flow, and to flag that we'll need `load_from_mlflow`'s cache again once production switches to dynamically fetching the champion model from MLflow (planned alongside the XGBoost quick-wins work).
- `docs/roadmap/index.md` map table / v0.1 milestone bullet updated to match.

**Not touched:** `BaseForecaster.load_from_mlflow` and its local-disk cache remain exactly as they were — `cv_power_forecasts` still uses them to load a fold's freshly trained model back from MLflow mid-experiment, which is unrelated to production resilience.

- [x] `uv run ruff check` / `uv run ty check` pass
- [x] `uv run pymarkdown scan -r docs README.md CLAUDE.md metadata/README.md packages/*/README.md` passes

body:
## What

The list endpoints paginated and filtered but had a fixed order. They now accept `?sort=<field>&order=asc|desc`.

- **`sortOrder(c, SORTABLE)` helper** — parses `?sort=&order=` against a per-route `SORTABLE` whitelist into a Prisma `orderBy`, or `undefined` so the route keeps its default order. `order` defaults to `asc`; an unknown sort field or a bad `order` value → `400`.

| Endpoint | Sortable fields | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/fish` | `id`, `commonName`, `family`, `creditsPerKgUnique`, `monsterTargetWeight` | `id` asc |
| `/api/locations` | `id`, `name`, `region`, `waterwayType`, `unlockLevel` | `id` asc |
| `/api/biting-preferences` | `fishId`, `depthZone` | `fishId` asc |
| `/api/fish-locations` | `fishId`, `locationId`, `specificSpot` | `fishId`, `locationId` asc |

Not breaking — defaults are unchanged, and `sort` is optional. Composes with the existing filtering and pagination. Documented in README + CLAUDE.md.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm test` — 75 passed (default order, whitelisted field+direction, order-defaults-asc, and the two 400s)
- **End-to-end against a live stack** (6/6): `asc`/`desc` ordering verified on real rows, default order (id asc), `sort` without `order` defaulting to asc, and `400` on a non-whitelisted field / invalid order.

Example: `GET /api/fish?sort=commonName&order=desc`.

author: fukusaka
body:
## Motivation

`NioEventLoop`'s loop selected with `selector.select()` and then iterated
`selector.selectedKeys()`. On the JDK's platform selectors that populates
a `HashSet` per ready event and walks a fresh iterator per wakeup — JFR
attributes `HashMap$Node` 12.2% plus `HashMap$KeyIterator` 2.3% of the
`/hello` allocation pressure to exactly these two mechanisms (the only
larger selector-side class, the JDK-internal `Integer` fd boxing at ~29%,
cannot be removed from keel). The JDK 11+ `select(Consumer)` variants
exist precisely for this: the platform selector invokes the action
directly per ready key and never touches the selected-key set.

## 動機

`NioEventLoop` の loop は `selector.select()` の後に
`selector.selectedKeys()` を iterate していた。JDK の platform selector
ではこれが ready event ごとに `HashSet` を populate し、wakeup ごとに
iterator を歩く — JFR は `/hello` の allocation pressure のうち
`HashMap$Node` 12.2% + `HashMap$KeyIterator` 2.3% をまさにこの 2 機構に
帰属させる（selector 側でこれより大きいのは JDK 内部の `Integer` fd
boxing ~29% のみで、keel からは除去不可）。JDK 11+ の
`select(Consumer)` 変種はまさにこのためにあり、platform selector が
ready key ごとに action を直接呼び、selected-key set に一切触れない。

## Modification

- The loop's three select calls (`selectNow` / untimed / timed) now pass
  a pre-allocated `Consumer<SelectionKey>` field; the former
  `processSelectedKeys` iterator loop becomes the per-key action
  `processReadyKey`, with the dispatch logic unchanged (per-direction
  callback snapshot, interest-bit clearing, stale-interest guard).
- The per-key `try/catch` now also serves the Consumer contract: an
  exception escaping the action would be relayed out of `select`,
  aborting the remaining ready keys — so it must not escape.
- The action field is deliberately declared **before** the `init` block
  that starts the loop thread, with a comment pinning the constraint:
  Kotlin initialises properties in declaration order, and on a cold JVM
  the freshly-started thread reaches its first select before the
  constructor finishes late-declared fields — it then reads a null
  action, dies on the NPE, and every registration on that loop hangs.

### Design decisions

- The Consumer contract was verified against the JDK javadoc before the
  switch: cancelling keys, changing interest sets, and closing channels
  are explicitly permitted inside the action; the only hard prohibition
  is a reentrant selection operation, which nothing reachable from the
  callbacks performs. The action runs while the selector holds its own
  monitors, which is moot here because every selector / key mutation is
  already funnelled to the loop thread (`setInterestCallback` /
  `removeInterest` dispatch, queued registrations).
- The action may be invoked more than once for one key with a subset of
  its ready ops; the existing per-direction handling processes subsets
  naturally, so no logic change was needed.

## 変更内容

- loop の 3 つの select 呼び出し（`selectNow` / 無期限 / timed）に
  事前確保した `Consumer<SelectionKey>` field を渡す形にし、旧
  `processSelectedKeys` の iterator loop を per-key action
  `processReadyKey` に変換（dispatch ロジックは不変 — per-direction
  callback snapshot、interest bit clear、stale-interest guard）。
- per-key の `try/catch` は Consumer 契約も兼ねる: action から例外が
  逃げると `select` の外へ相搬され残りの ready key が中断されるため、
  逃がしてはならない。
- action field は loop thread を起動する `init` block より**前**に意図的
  に宣言し、制約をコメントで固定: Kotlin は property を宣言順に初期化
  するため、cold JVM では起動直後の thread が constructor の後方 field
  初期化より先に最初の select に到達し、null action を読んで NPE で
  死に、その loop への登録が全て hang する。

### 設計判断

- 切替前に Consumer 契約を JDK javadoc で確認済み: action 内での key
  cancel / interest set 変更 / channel close は明示的に許可され、唯一の
  hard prohibition は再入 selection operation で、callback から到達する
  コードはこれを行わない。action は selector が自身の monitor を保持
  したまま走るが、selector / key の変異は全て loop thread に funnel
  済み（`setInterestCallback` / `removeInterest` の dispatch、queue 経由
  の registration）のため問題にならない。
- action は同一 key に対し ready ops の subset で複数回呼ばれうるが、
  既存の per-direction 処理が subset を自然に扱うためロジック変更不要。

## Test plan

- Red-Green on the initialisation-order hazard: with the action field
  declared after the thread-starting `init` block,
  `NioEngineConcurrencyTest` fails deterministically (3/3 runs — the
  first engine on a cold JVM hangs in `bind`); declared before it, 3/3
  runs pass plus the full `keel-engine-nio` suite.
- Both-host pre-merge gate green (aggregate, `-Ptls -Pbenchmark`,
  detekt + tests + Dokka on the Linux and macOS gate hosts).
- A/B (`pipeline-http-nio` — the engine the original JFR attribution was
  measured on; local M1, `BENCH_RUNS=3` median, `BENCH_TEMP_CAPTURE=1`):

| metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| JFR `HashMap$Node` share (`/hello`, 10 s) | 12.19% | gone (residual `HashMap$Node[]` 0.16%) |
| JFR `HashMap$KeyIterator` share | 2.29% | gone |
| JFR `Integer` (JDK-internal, not removable) | 29.0% | 26.2% |
| `GET /hello` (wrk 4t/100c) | 151.1K rps / p99 0.85 ms | 152.0K rps / p99 839 µs (+0.6%, tied) |

The JFR view is the direct evidence: both selected-key-set allocation
classes disappear, and throughput is flat-to-slightly-up (the removal is
a GC-pressure lever, not a latency lever, at this scale).

Closes audit 2026-07-02 §3.1 #5 — the LAST open VIDA-high of the §3.1 list (docs/audits/AUDITORIA-END-TO-END-2026-07-02.md).

## Descripcion / Description

**Bug:** the SOS outbox retries on transport failure. When the first POST reached the server (alert doc written, fan-out fired) but the RESPONSE was lost (flaky mobile network — the normal case in faenas), the retry created a SECOND `emergency_alerts` doc and re-fired pushes/emails to the whole supervisor roster. `sosOutboxClient.ts` even documented the gap: "no clientEventId idempotency yet".

**Fix (surgical):**
- `POST /api/emergency/sos` now runs behind the existing `idempotencyKey()` middleware (Stripe pattern, same as `/notify-brigada`; import already existed). A replay returns the recorded 2xx — same `alertId` — without re-running the handler.
- `sendSos()` sends `Idempotency-Key: <clientEventId>` — the orchestrator already generates and preserves this UUID end-to-end; it just never left the device.

**Safety semantics on a life-critical route (each pinned by a test):** header absent → passthrough (legacy clients unaffected); cache-read failure → handler runs anyway (fail-open: a SOS is never blocked by its own safety net); only 2xx cached (a failed SOS stays retryable); same key + different body → 422 (Stripe fingerprint); keys scoped per-uid. Zero-reach policy UNCHANGED (UI-layer tel: fallback) — this PR only makes transport retries safe.

body:
## What
GP already derives **coarse location (country + region)** from the client IP via GeoIP at telemetry ingestion — city and raw IP are never stored — but it was only used for promo geo-targeting and never shown in the dashboard. This surfaces it in analytics, both per-user and in aggregate.

## Per-user
- `GET /admin/user/{id}` returns `user.location` = `{country, region}` (the user's latest geo-tagged telemetry), rendered as a 📍 chip in the user-detail header.
- `GET /admin/users` adds a per-user `location` (latest non-null country/region — same un-app-scoped "latest telemetry" pattern already used for device/locale) and a sortable **Location** column in the Users table.

## Aggregate
- `GET /admin/telemetry/rich` adds a `by_location` rollup — distinct devices / users / events by country + region, honoring the Telemetry tab's existing filters — rendered as a **Users by location** table in the tab.

## Privacy
No new collection, no change to the privacy posture: country + region only (never city), raw IP is never stored (only `ip_hash`). Null location (geo DB not installed, or a ping predating geo capture) renders as an em dash and is excluded from the aggregate.

## Tests
`tests/test_location_analytics.py` (4): latest-location on user detail, null-when-no-geo, users-list location, telemetry geo breakdown (counts, geo-less rows excluded, ordering). 10 pass alongside the existing dashboard suite (no regression to the user/users endpoints touched).

author: dennisduong
body:
cleanSearchObject was never exported from index.ts and never called anywhere in src/ — its docstring claimed it ran "before stringifying search state for URL updates," but stringifySearchWith does its own (shallow) undefined-stripping and never called it. Its two sole helpers, isEmptyObject and isRecord, existed only to support it and were themselves unused elsewhere.

Deleted rather than wired in: routing it into stringifySearchWith would have changed public stringify output beyond simple undefined-removal (JSON.stringify already strips undefined) — it also drops resulting empty objects out of arrays, e.g. {arr: [{x: undefined}]} would serialize as arr:[] instead of today's arr:[{}]. That's an unrequested, semver-relevant behavior change, not a dead-code cleanup.

author: m3rcey
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #27 (the setup wizard). Every onboarding blocker hit during testing traces back to one thing: a **mandatory email-verification step in front of onboarding**. It causes:

- Supabase's built-in email **rate limit** (`email rate limit exceeded`) during any repeated signup.
- The **PKCE verify link bouncing to `/login`** — `exchangeCodeForSession` fails when the email is opened in a different browser/app than signup (no `code_verifier`), which is the common case (desktop signup → phone email, or in-app email browsers). Real new artists hit this, not just testing.
- **"Invalid credentials"** on manual login — Supabase silently no-ops a repeat signup on an existing email and does **not** update the password.

Pre-PMF, that gate costs more artists than it protects. The plan is to **turn off "Confirm email" in Supabase**, which removes the entire class of failures and logs new artists straight in.

## What this PR changes (code side of that plan)

With confirmation off, `signUp` returns a live session immediately — but `AuthForm` always showed the "Check your email" screen and never routed the user in. This fixes that:

- **`AuthForm`**: after signup, check for a session. If present (confirmation off) → route into onboarding via `onSuccess`. If absent (confirmation on) → show the confirmation screen exactly as before.
- **Signup page**: that success now goes to `/welcome` (onboarding), not `/home`.
- SW cache `v112 → v113`.

**No behavior change if email confirmation is left ON** — with no session, the confirmation screen still shows. So this is safe to merge independently of the Supabase toggle.

## Required config change (your side)

**Supabase → Authentication → Providers → Email → turn "Confirm email" OFF.** After that, signup → `/welcome` → `/setup` with no email step. Reversible anytime; if you later want verification back without the cross-device breakage, the durable path is the `token_hash` + `/auth/confirm` route pattern (happy to implement separately).

## Testing

- `npm run build` passes clean.
- Manual: with confirmation off, sign up a fresh email → should land on `/welcome` → Artist → `/setup` with no email/verify step.

author: jkamsker
body:
## Bug

`EventQueryJson` is the public JSON round-trip surface for `EventQueryDocument` and `QueryProjection` structural strings. Event names, member projection paths, and construct projection field names can contain malformed UTF-16 such as `prefix-\uD800-suffix`; serialization currently succeeds and deserialization returns a different string containing `U+FFFD` instead of preserving the public value or failing closed at the JSON boundary.

## Red test

Added `EventQuerySerializationTests.Structural_strings_round_trip_valid_surrogate_pairs` and `EventQuerySerializationTests.Structural_strings_round_trip_without_utf16_replacement` in `tests/DotBoxD.Kernels.Tests/Queryable/Serialization/EventQuerySerializationTests.cs`.

The red theory covers `EventQueryDocument.EventName`, `QueryProjection.Member` path, and `QueryProjection.Construct` field names with a lone high surrogate. It allows either explicit `JsonException` / `InvalidOperationException` rejection that names malformed UTF-16/surrogates or exact code-unit round-trip equality. The valid surrogate-pair test pins the supported Unicode case.

## Expected failure

The focused test currently fails all three malformed structural string cases with `Assert.Equal() Failure: Strings differ` at position 7. `EventQueryJson.Serialize` succeeds, but the restored value has replacement `U+FFFD` where the original string contained lone surrogate `U+D800`.

## Duplicate check

author: luuuc
body:
## Problem
Three inaccuracies in the index misled an AI reading Sense's output:
1. Summary "hub symbols" counted low-confidence bare-name collision edges that
   the resolver keeps below blast's floor, manufacturing nonsense hubs (a generic
   `get` reported with 8019 callers).
2. Committed Next.js build output (`_next/`) was indexed as source, flooding the
   index with thousands of minified-bundle symbols and polluting orientation
   (they even surfaced as "entry points").
3. The Python and JS/TS extractors emitted every attribute/member call at full
   confidence even when the receiver type was unknown, so an unverified `x.save()`
   was surfaced as a confident caller and could bind to an arbitrary same-named
   symbol.

## Summary
Three targeted accuracy fixes to the summary, scanner, and extractors so Sense's
orientation and edge confidence reflect what it actually resolved.

## Changes
- **summary**: hub-symbol ranking now counts only edges at or above blast's
  confidence floor (`ConfidenceUnresolved`), so bare-name collision guesses no
  longer manufacture nonsense hubs. Language-neutral.
- **scan**: add `_next/` to the default ignore patterns. Next.js build output is a
  directory named `_next` whose chunks are `<hash>.js` (not `*.min.js`), so it
  escaped the existing filters. Removes the minified-bundle symbols with no
  collateral on real source (the Next.js source repo itself has no `_next/`).
- **extract (python, tsjs)**: rate an attribute/member call by receiver knownness.
  `self`/`cls`/`this` and Capitalized (class/constant) receivers stay fully
  confident; a lowercase-variable or chained (unverified) receiver emits at the
  unresolved-confidence tier, mirroring the Ruby extractor's existing
  constant-vs-identifier distinction. 9 golden fixtures regenerated
  (confidence-only diffs).

## Architecture Highlights
- The extract change re-rates emission only; it is the first, foundational step of
  a broader effort to make call-edge confidence reflect receiver certainty, and
  deliberately does not yet demote or drop generic-name guesses (a follow-up that
  requires benchmark calibration).
- The two receiver helpers are kept duplicated in the `python` and `tsjs` packages
  by design, since the receiver node shapes differ (`self` identifier vs `this`
  node), rather than hoisted into a shared helper.

## Test Plan
- [x] Behavior-named unit tests per fix: hub confidence filter, `_next` match +
      negative cases (real source not matched), receiver-confidence table
      (self/Constant to full; lowercase/chain to unresolved).
- [x] 9 golden fixtures regenerated; confidence-only diffs verified as correct
      demotions (`order.save`, `db.query`, `obj.method`, `d.greet`).
- [x] Benched on the frontier model (Opus 4.8, x2) across four repositories: no
      cited-recall regression. Three held or improved; the fourth's dip in the
      dependent-recall metric is run-to-run variance, structurally confirmed not
      caused by this change (its gold dependents connect via reference edges this
      change does not touch).
- [x] `make ci` green (per-file coverage >=92%, lint, complexity ledger 0).
- [x] sense binary builds cleanly.

author: pmcfadin
body:
Closes #1283

## Summary
Consolidates the two overlapping SSTable integrity paths to a single source of truth (follow-up from #1236). `verify::verify_sstable` is the authoritative engine; `reader/integrity::perform_integrity_check` becomes a thin projection over it (Option A, owner-approved).

Design-driven — OpenSpec change `consolidate-verify`, capability `integrity-single-source`.

## What changed
- `perform_integrity_check` now calls `verify::verify_sstable_generation(&self.file_path, Full, …)` (a new **additive** verifier entry point that targets the reader's **exact** generation) and projects `VerifyReport → IntegrityCheckResult` (findings ⟹ `Corrupted`, else `Healthy`). The old independent Data.db block-walk is gone — no more divergent verdicts.
- Removed the dead computation behind `IntegrityStatus::Degraded` (`checksum_mismatches` was never incremented). Kept the variant + field as `#[deprecated]` (never produced) to avoid a breaking public-API removal.
- `verify_sstable`'s existing signature and the `cqlite verify` CLI text/JSON/exit-code contract are **byte-unchanged** (pinned by #1236) — only additive.

## Why it matters
Before: `perform_integrity_check` only walked Data.db blocks, so a corrupt Index.db / Digest / Summary / Filter / out-of-order keys read **`Healthy`** while `cqlite verify` correctly FAILed — two "integrity" APIs disagreeing. Now there is one engine.

## Quality
- `scripts/agent-gate.sh`: **RESULT: PASS** (17 components, clean tree).
- `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features`: clean.
- Intent audit (spec-auditor C): PASS (all 4 requirements). roborev (`--base origin/main`): clean (3 rounds — fixed a wrong-generation bug + path edge cases it surfaced, each with a regression test).
- New tests: digest-corruption-not-healthy (divergence gone, fails pre-change), reader's-generation-not-first-sorted (multi-generation), verifier path-tolerance + relative-path.
- #1236 parity oracle (`sstable_parity_corruption_verify`, `issue_1000_verifier`) untouched + green.

Note: `CQLITE_ALLOW_FILE_GROWTH=1` acknowledged for the already-over-threshold `verify.rs` (split is epic #1116 scope).

author: slepp
body:
## Summary

Codegen hand-mirrors several runtime-owned `#[repr(C)]` structs it can't link against, and only some had structural guards. This adds offset-parity guards — each independently reconstructs the LLVM struct shape and asserts every field's offset plus total size via `offset_of!` over the real `hew-cabi`/`hew-runtime` structs — for `HewVecElemLayout`, `HewMapKeyLayout`, `HewMapValueLayout` (both construction sites; these two deliberately invert `clone_fn`/`drop_fn` order, a copy-paste trap with no structural test until now), `HewTypeLayout`, and the dyn-trait vtable prefix.

Along the way, the vtable prefix type gained a single authority helper (`dyn_vtable_prefix_ty`) consumed by all three production construction sites (write-side emission, drop-read view, and the dispatch-site view), making write/read divergence impossible by construction. The emitted IR is unchanged, pinned by the crate's exact-IR-text assertions. `hew-cabi` is scoped to dev-dependencies since only `#[cfg(test)]` code uses it.

## Verification

- Negative probes on the Map value-layout and vtable guards: planted field-order swaps caught with exact field/offset diagnostics, reverted after confirming.
- Full `hew-codegen-rs` suite: green (nextest, one tautological test removed by design during revision).
- Workspace clippy and fmt: clean.
- Full preflight: green.

## Out of scope

- Mailbox/envelope structs and `CoroFramePrefix` — different risk classes, left for follow-up (#1878 tracks the full set; this PR covers the `HewVecElemLayout`/`HewMapKeyLayout`/`HewMapValueLayout`/`HewTypeLayout`/vtable-prefix subset, not `CoroFramePrefix` or mailbox/envelope).
- Already-guarded structs (`HewActor`) untouched.
- #1882's other three guard categories (FFI ABI-width table parity, suspend per-exit drop-equivalence, native/WASM behavioural parity) are unaddressed here.

author: andrei444-andrei
body:
## Зачем (продолжение расследования «скринер vs портфель»)

Сверка показала: у «металлов просадки» лаг входа ~1.9 т.д. до границы недели съедает **76% альфы** (+1.20 пп t=3.37 → +0.29 пп t=0.88), а у части сетапов лаг безвреден. Запрос пользователя: **«нужна статистика при создании для учёта лагоустойчивости сигнала»** — чтобы это было видно сразу в скринере, а не постфактум через сверку.

## Что добавлено

**Движок панели** на каждую сделку теперь считает **лаг-исходы**: доходность и превышение vs SPY при входе через **+1/+2/+3 торговых дня** после сигнала (удержание — тот же горизонт). В строке панели они едут **хвостом после факторов** — раскладка исходов/факторов не сдвигается, старые тесты/потоки не тронуты; `panel.lags=[1,2,3]`.

**В сводке скринера** — строка **«Лаго-профиль (vs SPY)»**: `+0д +1.20пп (t 3.4) · +1д … · +2д … · +3д …` + вердикт:
- 🛡 **лаго-устойчив** — на +2д остаётся ≥75% эджа и t ≥ 2 → переживёт недельный ребаланс;
- ◐ **частично устойчив** — ослаблен, исполнять быстрее;
- ⚡ **требует входа в день сигнала** — на +2д теряется >50% эджа или t < 1.5 → недельная ротация эддж не соберёт.

Профиль **живой** — пересчитывается мгновенно при изменении условий, как вся сводка.

**Снимок сетапа** получает `lag1Exc/lag2Exc/lag3Exc + lagVerdict` — лагоустойчивость сохраняется с сетапом (для библиотеки и будущего выбора исполнения в «Портфелях»).

## Пайплайн изменений

`studies.ts` (лаг-исходы в `forward_extras` + хвост строк + `lags` в ответе) → `screenAssemble.ts` (split/assemble переносят хвост, `TickerPanel.lags`) → `screenPanel.ts` (кэш **v10**, колонка `lags` само-миграцией) → `panel/route.ts` (прокидывает lags) → `screen.ts` (`Deal.lagRet/lagExc` из хвоста, обратная совместимость: панель без `lags` → полей нет) → `page.tsx` (мемо + строка в сводке + снимок).

## Тесты

author: vibhujawa
body:
## Summary

Adds a focused NeMo Curator image-to-Lance tutorial workflow for retry-aware WebDataset-style tar inputs.

- builds one immutable source manifest and deterministic snapshot ID
- uses stable `(shard, tar_id)` file partitions across attempts
- selects one URL winner by resolution, then newest attempt, then stable source order
- streams tar ranges through fsspec without staging or re-uploading source bytes
- writes image payloads as Arrow `large_binary` with MD5/SHA-256 and winner provenance
- packs work near 1 GiB and preserves logical Slurm-array shard identity for sparse retries
- uses matched one-CPU materialization/Lance writer stages so Ray can fuse them
- documents the retry locality requirement and Slurm-array submission flow

## Why

The image corpus contains repeated download attempts and needs deterministic, resumable distributed ingestion. A stable manifest and partition contract let Slurm arrays and Curator checkpoints retry exactly the failed logical work while keeping URL winner selection local to each stable tar partition.

## Scope

This PR intentionally contains only the reusable core workflow and tutorial. Production-specific validation, cleanup, benchmarks, compaction, indexing, credentials, paths, and dataset state are excluded.

## Validation

- Ruff format check
- Ruff lint
- 4 tutorial workflow tests
- Python compileall
- shell syntax check
- CLI help smoke test
- `git diff --check`

author: 2pacalypse-
body:
Second PR of the game/player reporting stack — **stacked on #1331** (base branch `game-reporting-migrations`). Implements the server-rs GraphQL surface on top of PR 1's schema, modeled on `news.rs`.

## Mutations

- **`reportGame`** (any logged-in user) — validates no self-report, the Other-requires-details rule, and details length; enforces the `reporting` restriction and a 10/hour anti-spam cap (`MAX_REPORTS_PER_HOUR`); authorizes that both the reporter and the reported player were in the game via a single `games_users` query; inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` so a duplicate surfaces a typed `ALREADY_REPORTED` error.
- **`resolveGameReport`** (`manage_game_reports`) — records outcome + resolver + notes idempotently (`WHERE resolved_at IS NULL`), distinguishing `ALREADY_RESOLVED` from `NOT_FOUND`.

## Query

- **`gameReports`** (`manage_game_reports`) — keyset-paginated `Connection`, unresolved queue newest-first by default, with a `GameReportFilter` for including resolved reports or filtering by reported user.

## `GameReport` resolvers

- `reporter` / `reportedUser` / `resolver` via `UsersLoader`; `game` via `GamesRepo`.
- `replay` — best (longest) replay as `{ replayFileId, hash (hex), url }`; admin-only, so it skips the per-user replay ACLs. Needs the new **`FileStore.signed_url_with_disposition`** so the download URL carries a proper `.rep` filename (Spaces sets `response-content-disposition`; the local dev store no-ops it).
- `reporterStats` / `reportedUserStats` — derived credibility counts (actioned/dismissed/abusive/duplicate/pending), not a stored score.

`reason`/`resolution` map to their `TEXT` columns via explicit `to_db`/`from_db` (no PG enum, matching the schema decision — there's no TEXT-backed sqlx enum precedent in the codebase).

## Verification

- `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace -D warnings` (online + offline `.sqlx`), `cargo fmt --check`, `tsc`, `eslint` all clean
- Regenerated `schema.graphql`, `client/gql`, and `server-rs/.sqlx`

body:
### Overview
This Pull Request integrates new, algorithmically verified benchmarks generated by the Extended Music Benchmarks (`emb`) project to test temporal localization in Audio LLMs. It
  adds tests for **temporal meter shifts** and **temporal key modulation**, allowing models to be tested on when a musical transition occurs.

These additions are completely additive and preserve the existing codebase structure of the baseline MUSE repository with zero friction.

### Changes Included:
  *   **New Runners (`Gemini/`):**
      *   `temporal_meter_Gemini_runner.py`: Evaluates LLMs on detecting shifts from 4/4 to 3/4 meter (early vs. late transitions).
       *   `temporal_key_Gemini_runner.py`: Evaluates LLMs on detecting key modulations from C Major to G Major (early vs. late transitions).
   *   **New Stimuli (`stimuli/emb_extension/`):**
       *   Adds 8 synthesized `.wav` audio clips representing the meter shift and key modulation trials (early shifts, late shifts, and steady tracks).
       *   These stimuli were programmatically generated as MIDI files, verified using `emb`'s internal solvers, and synthesized using FluidSynth and the default `FluidR3_GM.sf2`
  SoundFont to output realistic grand piano audio.
  *   **Documentation:**
      *   Adds a dedicated `README.md` under `stimuli/emb_extension/` explaining the generation method, runner details, and references to the sibling `emb` repository where the
  source MIDI files reside.
        *   Updates the root `README.md` task list and repository layout directory structure to register these extensions.

author: jonaprieto
body:
The bindings tests fork a node per chain. Unlike the generic-call-forwarder fix (#26), these can't drop forking: the protocol adapter constructor calls into the risc0 verifier router (`isEmergencyStopped`), and the execute test sends a real transaction against the deployed adapter, both of which need a forked node.

Anvil only reports ready after it fetches fork state from the RPC, so a slow or rate-limited RPC blows past anvil's 10s startup default and the test panics with `Timeout` (and it gets worse as chains are added). Raise the fork startup timeout to 120s.

body:
## Summary

Add a documented, dated grype `ignore` for **GHSA-fxhp-mv3v-67qp / CVE-2026-50163** (oras-go tar-extraction hardlink escape, High) so `make scan` / `make qualify` is unblocked while no fixed upstream release exists.

## Motivation / Context

`make scan` (`grype dir:.`) fails on GHSA-fxhp-mv3v-67qp in `oras.land/oras-go/v2 v2.6.1`. Investigation:

- **Reachable in AICR** — `aicr evidence verify` pulls an OCI bundle via `oras.Copy` into a `file.Store` that unpacks the gzip-tar layer to disk (`pkg/evidence/verifier/fetch.go`). This is the exact hardlink/relative-`Linkname` CWD-escape path the advisory describes, so a `not_affected` suppression would be false. Exploiting it requires an operator to verify a hostile/attacker-crafted bundle (CVSS `UI:R`).
- **No fixed v2 release exists** — `v2.6.1` is the latest tag and is affected; the fix (`b11f777`) is only on the `main`/**v3** module line (`github.com/oras-project/oras-go/v3`), which itself has only a `v3.0.0-dev` pre-release. The advisory declares the v2 patch as `v2.7.0`, but it is not tagged yet.

Given no fixed v2 artifact and no drop-in v2 commit, an accepted-risk-with-tracking grype `ignore` is the correct mechanism. **OpenVEX is not usable here**: `.openvex.json` is only wired into the image scans (via the `vex:` input), not `grype dir:.`, and all its statements are `not_affected`, whereas this CVE is reachable/affected.

Fixes: N/A
Related: GHSA-fxhp-mv3v-67qp, CVE-2026-50163

## Type of Change

- [x] Build/CI/tooling

## Component(s) Affected

## Summary

MIR drop-admission decided "does this binding's type oblige drop elaboration" through 12 inline copies of the same `ValueClass` comparison scattered across `lower.rs` — including one on the consume side whose silent divergence from the seed side would be a double-free. author: lukeevanstech
body:
## What

Second prowler fix, uncovered by #3390. Fixing broker auth revealed the next failure: the worker now connects to Dragonfly, then exits 1 ~3 seconds after `mingle: searching for neighbors` — no traceback, every restart, at any log level.

## Diagnosis (debug pod against the live broker, same image + secret)

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| defaults, concurrency 24 (2Gi pod) | OOMKilled in 12s |
| concurrency 2, with mingle | exit 1 at mingle |
| concurrency 1, DEBUG, with mingle | exit 1 at mingle, still silent |
| `--without-mingle --without-gossip` | runs cleanly, warm shutdown on SIGTERM |
| final command (concurrency 4, `-E`, all queues, no mingle/gossip) | ran full 90s, 845Mi |

Two independent problems:

1. **Celery 5.6 mingle/gossip are fatally incompatible with Dragonfly's pub/sub fanout** — the worker dies silently at startup. Both features exist only for multi-worker coordination; this deployment runs a single worker, so disabling them loses nothing. The image entrypoint hardcodes its celery flags, so the HelmRelease now invokes celery directly, mirroring the entrypoint's `start_worker()` (same queues, `-E`, `--max-tasks-per-child 1`, `DJANGO_APP_COMPONENT=worker` for pg application_name).
2. **Prefork pool defaults to `os.cpu_count()` = 24** on these nodes — 24 Django children idle at ~4GB, which is why the old worker sat at 98% of its 4Gi limit. Same class as the existing `DJANGO_WORKERS: "4"` gunicorn fix; prowler exposes `DJANGO_CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` for exactly this.

`$${DJANGO_LOGGING_LEVEL:-info}` is `$$`-escaped so Flux passes the literal through to the shell.

## Verification

- flate test security namespace: 7/7 passed
- Exact production command validated in a debug pod: worker ready, events on, consumed queues, clean warm shutdown, 845Mi footprint

body:
The RSRCC text field escapes newlines as literal `\n` two-char sequences, so `_parse_text`'s `rsplit` on real newlines never matched — 21,950/21,999 `rsrcc_test` prompts ended with `**Answer:** X` right before asking the model to answer. Apertus 8B scored 98.4%, which is answer-echo, not change understanding.

**Second commit (after xhigh review of the logged reruns):** the gold-answer extraction itself mis-scored 507/39,115 docs (1.3%) — trailing-junk golds (`B)`, `Yes.`, `B)Item`) never match a clean prediction, and `**Answer: B**`-style markers (matched by the split but not the old extraction regex) yielded empty golds that scored free points for unparseable predictions. Now: split and extraction share one grammar, the gold is the first alphanumeric token after the marker (rescues every observed format), `is_mcq` routes off the parsed question block, and docs whose gold still can't be parsed are dropped in `process_docs` with a loud warning (mirrors the geobench xBD filters). Verified against all 16 distinct gold forms observed in the 39k logged samples.

author: yperbasis
body:
Every new eth protocol version copied ~14-entry message-id map blocks into three hand-maintained tables: `eth.ToProto`, `eth.FromProto` (its inverse), and `libsentry.ProtoIds`. eth/68→71 accumulated four copies in each.

Now: `ToProto` is a literal eth/68 base plus per-version deltas (3/2/2 entries for 69/70/71); `FromProto` is derived by inversion with a collision panic; `ProtoIds` is derived in libsentry from the `FromProto` keysets. The one deliberate asymmetry is preserved and pinned: `FromProto`/`ProtoIds` omit `STATUS_69` for eth/69+ (status is handshake-only; `SendMessageById` must not emit a status frame) — `TestFromProtoOmitsStatus` derives the omitted set from goldens and asserts it exactly. wit's single-version tables get the same inversion treatment.

Golden tests were committed and verified green **before** the refactor: three external-package test files pin the exact pre-refactor content of all three tables with literal version keys (+325 test lines). One derivation is left unpinned: `ethProtocolsByVersion` becomes sorted `UintToProtocolMap` keys instead of a hand-written ordered literal, and its only consumer `MinProtocol` has no test — equivalent for 68<69<70<71, but unguarded.

Structural note: the import graph pointed the wrong way for a single-copy derivation (`eth` imported `node/direct` for the version constants). The version constants `ETH68..ETH71` move into package `eth` (where the protocol lives), `direct` re-exports everything as aliases so its ~109 external usage sites are untouched, and the version↔`sentryproto.Protocol` bridge maps live once in libsentry. The alias direction makes a future `eth → direct` re-import a compile error.

The cost of that flip, measured across all 451 packages: `libsentry`'s transitive internal dependency closure grows 10 → 85 packages and `node/direct`'s 14 → 89, because deriving `ProtoIds` makes libsentry import the protocol packages. Every other package in the repo grows by ≤4, and `eth`/`wit` each shrink by 6 (they drop `node/direct`). The lasting constraint is that nothing inside that closure — `db/*`, `execution/*`, `cl/*`, `p2p/protocols/*` — can import `libsentry` or `node/direct` without a cycle.

Net −72 production lines. eth/72's message-id mapping becomes a single delta instead of three ~14-entry copies, but the per-version registration points remain (`ETH72` const, `ProtocolToString`, `ProtocolLengths`, `libsentry.UintToProtocolMap`, the `direct` alias, `nodecfg`'s version list), and each of the three golden tables needs a new block — so the copy-paste partly relocates from production into tests, where a wrong entry fails loudly instead of misrouting silently. Verified: goldens pre/post, `go test ./p2p/... ./node/direct/...`, scoped `golangci-lint` clean (×2), `make erigon`.

Part of a dedup series; siblings #22165–#22174.

body:
## Start here — what this is, in plain terms

**What we built:** the first two rounds of the 10-round deep review you asked for. Each round re-examined one overnight phase — the config **reader** (Round 1) and the report **writer** (Round 2) — against its full history, re-ran its proofs fresh today, and wrote the three formal records the OpenGSD workflow expects and the overnight run skipped: a verification report (what's proven, with receipts), a validation map (what's tested vs what's honestly untested), and a learnings file (decisions, lessons, patterns, surprises — the "learning component" you correctly suspected was missing).

**Why it matters to you:** these records are honest by construction — each one opens by declaring it's *retroactive* and citing exactly where its evidence comes from (the original PR, the build summaries, and a fresh re-run today). Nothing is back-dated or invented. And the review caught two real things the tests didn't.

**How to review it (~6 min):**
1. Open [`01-LEARNINGS.md`](https://github.com/johnair01/newsletters/blob/loop/2026-07-02-deep-review/.planning/phases/01-swim-lane-binding-traced-yaml-loader/01-LEARNINGS.md) and [`02-LEARNINGS.md`](https://github.com/johnair01/newsletters/blob/loop/2026-07-02-deep-review/.planning/phases/02-module-scope-report-composer/02-LEARNINGS.md) — the distilled lessons; each item cites its source. Ask: *do these match what you'd want a future collaborator to know?*
2. Skim the two findings in "What we learned" below — both are recorded-not-fixed, per the loop's own rule (review never edits code).

This pull request adds some code to work around the bug where Spore can give the camera a NaN value.

author: wtokarzewski
body:
## What

Prevents two gateway instances from running against one workspace, and guarantees a shutting-down gateway actually exits. Also carries the post-merge doc updates for #224 and #225 (CLAUDE.md, FEATURES.md, docs/ROADMAP.md).

## Why

The 29–30.06 logs pinpointed the real root cause of the reminder outage: **two gateway processes on the same workspace**. The half-dead one (channels/lanes gone, cron alive) polled the shared `cron_jobs` table, claimed each due job first, and published it into a bus nobody consumed — the healthy instance saw `next_run_at` already advanced and never fired. Evidence in the logs:
- `Rozkręcanie aparatu ortodontycznego` fired **twice**, 22s apart (30.06 15:18:06 + 15:18:28) — two schedulers
- `Gateway: config reloaded` logged **twice** per change — two processes watching janus.json, appending to the same log file
- the 15:18:28 run was consumed with `active=0/3` and an **empty** cron queue, while the 08:15/14:20 fires never appeared in any lane — their messages went to a different (dead) bus

## How

- **`utils/instance-lock.ts`** — `.janus/gateway.pid`. Stale lock (dead pid, unreadable file) is taken over; a live holder is retried for ~30s (self_update spawns the new process moments before the old one exits), then startup is refused with instructions. Released only by its owner.
- **gateway** — `SIGTERM/SIGINT` path gets a 15s force-exit backstop (unref'd timer) so a wedged teardown can't linger; clean teardown ends with an explicit `process.exit(0)` so a leaked timer/handle can't keep a half-dead instance alive running cron.

## Testing

- [x] `npm test` — 741 passed (68 files), incl. new `instance-lock` tests (acquire, stale takeover, refuse on live holder, owner-only release)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes

author: westbridgeinc
body:
Master-plan gap **T2-D** — `Item.stockQuantity` was inert (checkout never decremented; real overselling risk). Now it's a real inventory engine.

## Behavior
- **Atomic sell-down at checkout** — conditional `WHERE stockQuantity >= qty` decrement inside the order transaction: overselling is impossible under concurrency, the losing checkout gets `409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK` and its whole transaction rolls back
- **Auto-hide at zero** — `isAvailable=false` + `autoHiddenAt` marker (distinguishes engine hides from the owner's own toggle)
- **Low-stock alerts** — new `Item.lowStockThreshold` + `LOW_STOCK` notification type; fires **once at the crossing**, not on every order below it; sold-out sends its own alert
- **Restock on cancellation** — every CANCELLED source state precedes physical handover, so tracked stock goes back and pure auto-hides un-hide. FAILED handovers deliberately do NOT auto-restock (returned food is the vendor's call)
- **Cart + checkout first-pass** friendly early errors
- **Vendor item update** — restocking above zero un-hides an auto-hidden item; an explicit owner toggle always wins
- **Mobile** — threshold field in the item editor + out-of-stock / low-stock badges in the menu list

## Tests
inventory.test.ts (8): last-unit race → exactly one 200; rollback leaves stock untouched; crossing alert exactly once; cancel restores + un-hides; manual hide survives restock; untracked items untouched. **API 423/423**, mobile 13/13, type-check + lint + expo export clean.

Consolidate repeated inline style literals across survey phase components (PhaseA, PhaseB, PhaseF, QuestionField, and StudioShell) into a shared `surveyStyles.ts` module. This eliminates duplication, improves maintainability, and establishes a single source of truth for the survey UI palette and component shapes.

## Key Changes

- **New module:** `packages/studio/src/survey/surveyStyles.ts`
  - Re-exports color constants from `ui/theme.ts` (BG_PAGE, BG_CARD, BORDER, ACCENT, TEXT_DIM, TEXT_MAIN, FONT, BLUE_ACTION)

author: jeffrymorris
body:
Runs the ContosoUniversity MVC sample end-to-end through an Aspire AppHost: it
provisions the Couchbase cluster, bucket, scope, and collections, creates the
query indexes, and seeds the example data on each run — so `dotnet run --project
samples/Contoso.AppHost` gives a working app with a populated database.

### What changed

**Aspire orchestration**
- New `Contoso.AppHost` project: adds a Couchbase cluster resource, the
  `Universities` bucket, and the `Contoso` scope with one collection per entity;
  references the web app and `WaitFor`s the bucket before it starts.
- New `couchbase-dotnet-ef.ServiceDefaults` project (health checks, OpenTelemetry,
  service discovery); package versions moved into central package management.

**ContosoUniversity app**
- `Program.cs` reads the Aspire-injected connection string, configures
  `UseCouchbase` from it, creates a primary index per collection at startup (the
  hosting DSL has no index primitive), then seeds via `DbInitializer`.
- Removed the circular `Contoso.AppHost` project reference (broke restore) and the
  app-inappropriate `Aspire.Hosting.Testing` / `Couchbase.Aspire.Client` packages.
- Fixed the hand-written SQL++ queries left over from the SQL Server original
  (`HomeController.About`, `DepartmentsController.Details`): they used the wrong
  keyspace/casing and PascalCase fields. Both now derive the fully-qualified
  keyspace (and PK column) from the model and use the camelCase field names the
  provider stores. Couchbase keyspaces are case-sensitive.
- `Program.cs` sets `ScanConsistency = RequestPlus` for read-after-write: the app
  seeds then immediately queries, and controllers query right after writes.
- Null-guarded the manual course lookup in `InstructorsController` so a missing
  related document can't NRE the page.

**Read-your-writes investigation (context for the RequestPlus change)**
Pages initially read stale data right after the seed. Investigation confirmed this
is **not** data loss and **not** a provider defect: documents are always present in
KV, and on a properly-built index both `RequestPlus` and `AtPlus` return every
write. The provider already applies the configured scan consistency — the app was
just defaulting to `NotBounded`. Added regression tests:
- read-your-writes on a freshly-built primary/GSI index returns all writes under
  `RequestPlus`/`AtPlus`;
- concurrent inserts into a just-created collection all persist (KV durability);
- a unit test asserting `QueryOptions.ScanConsistency` mutates in place.

### Verification
Fresh AppHost run: cluster provisioned, all collections + indexes created, all
example data seeded (all 7 courses), and every page renders (About, Departments,
Instructors, Courses, Students) with real data. Full solution builds clean.

### Notes
- Transitive NuGet vulnerability warnings (OpenTelemetry, MessagePack) are
  inherited from the Aspire templates — non-blocking; can be bumped separately.
- Sample only — no changes to the provider itself.

author: felixgeelhaar
body:
Improvements surfaced by **Senat-OS** wiring mnemos as per-org worker memory (on the Postgres provider, schema-per-namespace).

## Added
- **`Memory.RememberClaimWithEvidence(ctx, text, evidence, validFrom)`** — convenience over `RememberEvent` + `RememberClaim` for the common "statement + the references backing it" case. One observation event per non-blank evidence string, then a fact claim linking them; same fail-closed rule (≥1 non-blank evidence). Removes boilerplate every consumer (incl. Senat's `Store.Remember`) was rewrapping.
- **`Memory.Info() Info`** — backend / namespace / mode / embedder / actor, so operators can confirm a deployment is backed + isolated as intended (e.g. semantic vs lexical recall).
- **ADR 0007 (Proposed): per-tenant scoping within a namespace** — design for a fine-grained in-namespace tenant boundary (one pool/schema, many tenants) instead of a store/namespace per tenant. Motivated by Senat's per-org store-cache workaround; deliberately a design doc, not a rushed impl (isolation is the one thing not to rush).

## Changed
- **Postgres provider: `search_path` pinned per connection** via a pgx stdlib `AfterConnect` hook, so every pooled/lazily-created connection resolves to the namespace schema — not just the first. Closes the follow-up the provider's own comments flagged.

## Fixed
- **`WithSQLite` relative paths** — resolved to an absolute path before building the `sqlite://` DSN, so `./data/x` is no longer mis-parsed as a URL host into `/data/x`.

## Docs
- Removed the stale "postgres provider is a scaffold" comment (`cmd/mnemos`) and deprecated the `ErrNotImplemented` sentinel — the provider is **production-ready**, verified against pgvector pg17 (Senat runs it in prod).

## Tests
New: `RememberClaimWithEvidence` (incl. fail-closed cases), `Info`, `WithSQLite` relative-path. Full unit suite + Postgres integration (with the new AfterConnect path) + `go vet` green.

## Note
Additive + backwards-compatible (interface methods added — pre-1.0, minor bump). Releasing ripples to other consumers (nomi, pet-medical, decisionkit, iris) — leaving the tag/release to you.
