author: kaustabhinand
body:
So, I had looked at the Asm.flex file, and your problem was this: 

You had defined the char_literal like this: - **\' ( [^\\\'] | \\[^] ){1} \'**
Now, this had caused problems as, in the ca65 syntax, **' ' '** - represents ' (a single quote).
But the present rule had never included it as a character, so the match fails (the char literal is never seen).

And for this case: **' \ '** the \ is being represented as an escape character, so it takes in the **'** as well, needing one extra **'** to close the character, which in this case, is not present. 

The fix I did was just one line - I replaced the current rule with this: **\'[^\r^n]\'** - this can ensure that now any character in the quote is matched as a character literal, including the single quotes and backslashes. 

Please review and let me know if there are any other changes to be made :)

author: xcarter93
body:
This pull request introduces a new AI-powered assistant feature to the web application, enabling users to interact with a conversational assistant that can answer questions about their business data (clients, schedule, invoices, etc.). It includes backend support for the assistant, frontend UI components for interacting with it, and updates to dependencies to support markdown rendering and agent integration. The most important changes are: **Assistant Backend Integration:** * Added a new `assistantAgent` using the Convex Agent SDK and OpenAI's GPT-4o-mini model, with custom instructions, tool integration, and token usage tracking in `assistantAgent.ts`. * Implemented a usage handler and mutation to record assistant usage statistics for analytics and cost control. **Frontend Assistant UI:** * Added `AssistantSheet` component to provide a chat interface, conversation history, and markdown-formatted assistant responses using `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm`. * Integrated the assistant UI into the main layout (`sidebar-with-header.tsx`), including assistant triggers in both mobile and desktop headers, and managed assistant dialog state. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7388cefef474d5707b023f9396fa362c4c76add5d552b4a363785612b6e66ddfL3-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7388cefef474d5707b023f9396fa362c4c76add5d552b4a363785612b6e66ddfR52-R84) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7388cefef474d5707b023f9396fa362c4c76add5d552b4a363785612b6e66ddfR93-R94) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7388cefef474d5707b023f9396fa362c4c76add5d552b4a363785612b6e66ddfL84-R108) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7388cefef474d5707b023f9396fa362c4c76add5d552b4a363785612b6e66ddfR133-R142) **Dependency and Configuration Updates:** * Added new dependencies: `@convex-dev/agent`, `react-markdown`, and `remark-gfm`, and updated `ai` package version to support the assistant and markdown rendering. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8L69-R70) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8R99-R102) * Updated `.mcp.json` to include a new plan configuration for agent-native integration.

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces an org-scoped AI chat assistant backed by the Convex Agent SDK (GPT-4o-mini), wiring together a new backend layer (thread management, 16 read-only tools, token usage tracking, cascade deletion) and a streaming frontend sheet component with markdown rendering. - **Backend**: `assistantChat.ts` handles thread lifecycle and auth; `assistantTools.ts` wraps existing org-scoped queries so all tools inherit org isolation without rebuilding it; `orgCascade.ts` is updated to clean up thread metadata and usage records when an org is deleted. - **Frontend**: `AssistantSheet` streams responses with `useSmoothText`, renders markdown via `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`, and exposes thread history. The trigger is added to both the desktop header and mobile floating pill. - **Tests**: `assistantChat.test.ts` covers cross-org and same-org-different-user isolation at the mutation/query level.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The thread ownership checks and read-only tool isolation are solid, but the retry flow in the chat UI has a real defect and there is no rate limiting protecting OpenAI costs in production. Two issues stand out. First, if streamResponse fails after sendMessage succeeds, the error handler restores the prompt for retry — but the next retry calls sendMessage again, inserting a duplicate user message into the conversation thread permanently. Second, streamResponse has no per-user or per-org call rate limit; the rate-limiter component is already available in the app but not applied here, leaving API costs unbounded for any authenticated user. assistantChat.ts (streamResponse — no rate limiting) and assistant-sheet.tsx (handleSend retry path — duplicate user message on streamResponse failure)

author: dgkenn
body:
**Root cause of "bed temp frozen / heating-cooling looks broken."**

The live daemon was crash-looping every few minutes on the Windows host. `live_daemon._log` did `print("⚠ thermal: …")`, but the console/redirect defaults to cp1252, which **can't encode `⚠`** → `UnicodeEncodeError` killed the control tick. The crash handler then logged the exception repr (which still contained `⚠`) and **crashed again**, taking the whole daemon down. The watchdog restarted it, it ran one cycle, hit the thermal log, and died again (confirmed in the live watchdog log: dying every ~5–6 min all afternoon).

Because the daemon never survived a full cycle, `runtime_state` telemetry (`bed_temp_f`, `device_level`) **froze** and the controller never ran steadily — even though the Pod itself was cooling (per the official app).

Fix:
- `run_daemon.main()` reconfigures `sys.stdout`/`stderr` to **UTF-8 (`errors="replace"`)** at startup — the single entry point for both daemons — so a log line can never raise on any code page.
- `live_daemon._log()` gets a defensive ASCII-safe fallback and can no longer raise.
- Regression test: `_log` with an unencodable char against a strict-ASCII stdout must not raise.

Tests: engine 690 passed/1 skipped; API 598 passed (incl. new regression test).

## DEF-004 (MEDIUM) — Runner creation does not validate the model against the chosen provider

### Repro
`POST /api/fleet/runners {"provider":"gemini","model":"opus-4.8"}` returned **200** and created a nonsensical runner (`opus-4.8` is a Claude model; gemini offers `gemini-3-pro | gemini-3-flash`). The same gap applied to `PATCH /api/fleet/runners/:id` when changing the model.

### Fix
- Both `POST /api/fleet/runners` and `PATCH /api/fleet/runners/:id` (in `apps/server/src/api.ts`) now validate the requested `model` against the selected provider's model list. Invalid pairing → **400** with a clear error. On PATCH the check runs against the runner's existing provider.
- Existing provider-enum validation (zod contracts) is kept.
- The provider catalog stays the single source of truth: validation reads `store.listProviders()` (what `GET /api/providers` serves) and delegates to a new pure `modelValidForProvider()` helper in `@skynet/shared` — no duplicated provider→models map.

### Tests
New deterministic regression `tests/runner-model-validation.test.ts`:
- invalid pairing (`gemini` + `opus-4.8`) → rejected
- PATCH-style model change to a foreign provider's model → rejected
- valid pairings (`gemini`+`gemini-3-pro`/`gemini-3-flash`, `claude`+`opus-4.8`) → accepted
- unknown provider → rejected

author: tbolis-at-mulesoft
body:
## Summary

New split-model PDK policy for MuleSoft Flex/Omni Gateway: **A2A Agent Card Skill Governor**. An outbound, response-shaping policy that governs the `skills[]` array of an A2A Agent Card in-flight, before the card reaches the caller. It reshapes the advertised skill set per caller identity (extended card) or globally (public well-known card), driven by operator config.

Two mechanisms (Model C hybrid):
1. **Visibility** — first-match allow/deny gate per skill.
2. **Skills upsert** — rewrite an existing skill's fields or inject a new one, keyed by `skill.id`.

Governs all three A2A card surfaces (public well-known GET, extended JSON-RPC V1/Legacy, extended HTTP+JSON). Identity comes from the Anypoint `Authentication` injectable only — no raw token parsing.

## Key decisions

- **Body-only fail-closed.** The response filter uses the split headers→body flow because the PDK combined headers+body state (`into_headers_body_state`) *hangs* on the response leg on Flex 1.12.1 (Envoy 504). On the split flow `:status` is committed before the body is read, so a body-content-dependent status change is impossible. Fail-closed therefore replaces the card **body** with a surface-appropriate error envelope and leaves the upstream status. Security property holds: ungoverned skills never leak because the body is always replaced.
- **SLA tier channel.** `tier`-audience rules read the caller's tier from the `Authentication` custom property `sla-tier-name` / `sla-tier-id` (written by the `rate_limit_sla` policy); legacy spellings are probed as fallback. Requires an upstream SLA-tier policy; absent it, tier rules gracefully no-op.
- **Disclosure ≠ authorization.** Hiding a skill removes it from discovery, not from invocation. Documented prominently; invocation-time authz is out of scope.

## Testing

- Unit: 20/20 (`make test-unit`) — rule engine + pure `transform_card_body`.
- Integration: 12/12 live on Flex 1.12.1 (`make test`) — all three surfaces, passthrough, and body-only fail-closed.
- Clean `make build` to `wasm32-wasip1`.

## Notes for reviewers

Two working-tree artifacts are **gitignored** and won't appear in a fresh checkout:
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-02-a2a-agent-card-skill-governor-design.md` — full design spec (§7 body-only amendment).
- `a2a-agent-card-skill-governor-flex/.claude/test-a2a-agent-card-skill-governor-locally/SKILL.md` — local `make run` + curl recipes.

Tracked equivalents live at `docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/implementation/IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

Known accepted item: the `pdk-test` harness cannot inject an SLA tier, so `tier`-audience matching is not covered end-to-end — confirm against a live deployment behind an SLA-tier policy.

author: mattmillerai
body:
## ELI-5

The errors panel had the same little "locate this node" button copy-pasted in four places, with tiny inconsistencies between the copies. This pulls it into one small reusable component so every locate button is defined once and behaves identically.

## Summary

Extract the duplicated locate icon-button (`variant="textonly" size="icon-sm"` with a `lucide--locate` icon) from the errors panel into a single `LocateNodeButton.vue`.

## Changes

- **What**: New `src/components/rightSidePanel/errors/LocateNodeButton.vue` (prop `label` for the accessible name, emits `locate`). Replaces the four byte-identical `<Button>` locate sites — `ErrorNodeCard.vue`, `TabErrors.vue`, and two in `MissingPackGroupRow.vue`. Standardizes two prior inconsistencies across those sites: the decorative icon now always carries `aria-hidden="true"` (previously omitted in ErrorNodeCard/TabErrors) and the click handler always uses the `.stop` modifier (previously plain `@click` in MissingPackGroupRow, which sits under no ancestor click handler so behavior is unchanged).
- **Breaking**: None. The rendered markup, classes, accessible name, and each parent's existing `locateNode` emit are unchanged.

## Review Focus

- **Prop is named `label`, not `ariaLabel`** as the grooming note suggested: a prop named `ariaLabel` collides with the native `aria-label` global attribute, so `vue-tsc` captures the kebab binding as a fallthrough attr and the required prop goes unresolved (real type error). `label` is unambiguous and maps cleanly onto the button's `aria-label`.
- **Text-button unification is intentionally out of scope.** The grooming note's second sub-claim (promote `packTextButtonClass` to a shared const and replace the two inline text-button strings) is gated on a design decision: those strings diverge in font size — `ErrorNodeCard` uses `text-sm/relaxed` while `TabErrors`/`packTextButtonClass` use `text-xs/relaxed` — so unifying them changes ErrorNodeCard's rendered text size. That needs a design call on the intended size and is left for a follow-up rather than guessed at here.

## Tests

New `LocateNodeButton.test.ts` covers accessible name, `locate` emission, and click-propagation stopping. Existing `ErrorNodeCard`/`TabErrors`/`MissingPackGroupRow` suites pass unchanged (61 tests). `pnpm typecheck`, `eslint`, and `oxfmt` clean.

author: jiyuuchc
body:
**Alternative implementation of #295, to compare against #299.** Same goal — a remote-proxy source must read on the upstream's native chunk grid, not the over-amplified 64 MB default (#295) — but a much simpler mechanism.

## Insight

The *only* consumer of a proxy's `get_chunk_size()` / `get_read_plan()` is the `get_flight_info` RPC (`server.py:1170`); `precache.py` is the only other caller and it now skips remote sources (#303). So there is no need to probe the upstream for a grid and re-plan locally — just forward the plan.

## Change

`RemoteTensorAdapter.get_read_plan()` forwards one `GetFlightInfo` to the upstream (same `slice_hint`/`scale_hint`/`reduction_method`) and returns **its** endpoints, rewriting each `chunk_id`'s `array_id` upstream→local. The proxy becomes a true pass-through — its stated design: *"re-derives no chunk grid; only understands the array_id rewrite."* Native grid, scaled `chunk_id`s, and slice bounding all come from the upstream verbatim. The rewritten `chunk_id`s round-trip, since `do_get` already forwards back via `resolve_chunk_data`'s array_id swap. Falls back to the local planner only if the upstream call fails.

## vs #299 (the probe approach)

|  | #299 (probe `get_chunk_size`) | this PR (forward `get_read_plan`) |
|---|---|---|
| Code | ~90 lines: `get_chunk_size` override + `_upstream_chunk_shape` + `_probe_upstream_chunk_shape` + `_mirrored_ndim` + memo dict/lock | ~30 lines: one `get_read_plan` override + helper |
| Grid source | probe upstream for `chunk_shape`, **re-plan locally** with it | upstream's **actual** endpoints, verbatim |
| Correctness | native grid; scaled/slice reads re-derived locally | native grid + scaled/slice/non-uniform grids straight from upstream |
| Upstream RPC | 1 bounded (1-endpoint) probe per tensor, **memoized** | 1 full-endpoint `GetFlightInfo` per client `GetFlightInfo` (not memoized) |
| Design fit | re-derives a grid (mild tension with the pass-through principle) | pure pass-through |

Net: #299 minimizes the upstream payload via a memoized bounded probe at the cost of re-implementing planning; this PR is simpler and strictly more faithful, at the cost of one (cheap, per-open) forwarded RPC. `get_flight_info` is per-tensor-open, not per-chunk, and the proxy already round-trips to the upstream for every `do_get`.

## Tests
`remote_tensor_adapter_test.py` (40 pass, incl. the existing big-endian / scaled-read / end-to-end proxy tests unchanged):
- `test_get_read_plan_forwards_upstream_native_grid` — empty seed ⇒ plan on the upstream's `[1,40,50]` grid (3 endpoints), local `chunk_id`s.
- `test_get_read_plan_falls_back_when_upstream_unreachable` — failed upstream ⇒ local planner, no raise.

Pick one of #299 / this to merge; close the other.

author: mikepapadim
body:
## Description

This PR introduces the **Hybrid API**: native library tasks that let a `TaskGraph` mix JIT-compiled Java tasks with calls into vendor libraries (NVIDIA cuBLAS, cuBLASLt, cuFFT), sharing TornadoVM-managed device buffers and the backend's CUDA stream — no extra copies, no host synchronization, correct dependencies from the standard `Access[]`-driven data-flow graph.

```java
TaskGraph taskGraph = new TaskGraph("cuBLAS")
    .transferToDevice(DataTransferMode.EVERY_EXECUTION, matrix, vector)
    .task("preprocess", MyClass::preprocess, matrix)                  // JIT-compiled kernel
    .libraryTask("sgemv", CuBlas::cublasSgemv,                        // native cuBLAS call
            CuBlasOperation.CUBLAS_OP_T.operation(),
            m, n, alpha, matrix, lda, vector, incx, beta, output, incy)
    .task("postprocess", MyClass::postprocess, output)                // JIT-compiled kernel
    .transferToHost(DataTransferMode.EVERY_EXECUTION, output);
```

### Architecture

- **Runtime SPI** (`tornado-runtime/.../library/spi`): `TornadoLibraryProvider` discovered via `ServiceLoader` — adding a library requires **zero core-runtime changes** (a self-contained module pair + `provides` in its module descriptor). Providers get per-(device, execution-plan) contexts, a `prepare()` hook invoked before CUDA graph capture (for native plans that allocate device memory), and arguments resolved to raw device pointers of TornadoVM buffers.
- **No new bytecodes or graph nodes**: `LibraryTask` is a sketch-free `SchedulableTask` (like `PrebuiltTask`) riding the existing ALLOC/TRANSFER/LAUNCH pipeline; the interpreter dispatches to the provider instead of launching a kernel.
- **CUDA integration**: the CUDA backend exposes its raw `CUstream`/`CUcontext` (`TornadoNativeStreamSupport`); library handles are bound with `cublasSetStream`/`cufftSetStream`, so library calls are ordered with kernels/transfers and are **CUDA-Graph capturable/replayable** under `withCUDAGraph()`. Profiler reports `TASK_KERNEL_TIME` for library calls.

### Modules in this PR

| Module | Provides |
|---|---|
| `tornado-cublas` (+ `cublas-jni`) | `cublasSgemv`/`cublasSgemm` FP32 (incl. `beta != 0` READ_WRITE semantics), TF32 math mode, `cublasGemmEx` FP16, strided-batched GEMM, per-call tuning (`CuBlasOptions` via `withTuning`), workspace control; **cuBLASLt** second provider with plan caching and fused `BIAS`/`GELU_BIAS` epilogues |
| `tornado-cufft` (+ `cufft-jni`) | 1D C2C fwd/inv, **R2C/C2R**, **Z2Z (FP64)**, **2D C2C**; plans created capture-safely in `prepare()` |

### Tests

JUnit suites in `tornado-unittests`, registered in `tornado-test`, auto-skip as `[UNSUPPORTED]` on non-CUDA backends or missing native libs: `cublas.TestCuBlas` (11 — incl. mixed pre/post-task graphs, shared buffers across task graphs via `persistOnDevice`/`consumeFromDevice`, CUDA-graph capture), `cublas.TestCuBlasLt` (5), `cufft.TestCuFft` (8 — incl. FFT→IFFT→JIT-normalize round trips and a CUDA-graph pipeline). All validate element-wise against sequential Java references.

### Benchmarks (RTX 4090, CUDA 12.6, cross-validated)

| Benchmark | TornadoVM kernel | Library task | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| SGEMM 4096² FP32/TF32/FP16 | 5.8 TFLOP/s (tiled KernelContext) | 57 / 81 / **160.6 TFLOP/s** | up to **27×** |
| Fused MLP `GELU(A·B+bias)` FP16 | GemmEx + JIT epilogue | cuBLASLt fused | 1.68× (1024²) |
| SGEMV 8192×2048 | 410 GB/s (KernelContext) | 578 GB/s | 1.4× (74× vs Java) |
| FFT n=65536 | 63.4 ms (JIT DFT kernel) | **0.080 ms** | **793×** |

### Docs

`docs/source/hybrid-api.rst` (architecture + "add a new library" guide), `tornado-cublas/README.md` + `ROADMAP.md`, `tornado-cufft/README.md`, `HYBRID_API_BRANCHES.md`.

Also includes a standalone build fix: the JNI CMake builds now prefer `/usr/local/cuda` over an older apt toolkit, fixing NVRTC/header version mismatches that broke runtime kernel compilation.

**Related:** #888 stacks the cuDNN provider (incl. fused flash attention) on top of this PR.

### Backend/s tested

Verified on the CUDA backend (`make BACKEND=cuda`), RTX 4090; suites skip cleanly on OpenCL/PTX/SPIR-V/Metal.

author: xandeq
body:
## Contexto

Auditoria dos providers de IA de imagem/vídeo encontrou 3 bugs reais e 4 gaps de design. Este PR corrige todos.

## Bugs corrigidos

### 1. Persistência de imagens geradas nunca acontecia de forma confiável 🔴
- \`GeneratedImageRepository.AddAsync\`/\`UpdateAsync\` só fazem *stage* — **nenhum SaveChanges existia no fluxo**. A persistência acontecia como efeito colateral do \`SaveChanges\` do usage-tracking, dentro de um \`Task.Run\` fire-and-forget usando DbContext scoped (race com o dispose do request).
- Base64 do Gemini/HuggingFace (sempre base64) estourava \`storage_url nvarchar(1000)\` → SqlException engolida → histórico silenciosamente vazio e projeto preso em "Processing".
- **Fix**: \`SaveChangesAsync\` explícito via \`IUnitOfWork\` (best-effort: falha de DB não descarta geração já paga) + novo \`GeneratedMediaStorageService\` que salva o binário em \`wwwroot/generated-media\` (mesmo padrão do EmailImageStorageService) e grava URL durável curta. URLs de provider (DALL·E/FAL) expiram em horas — agora baixamos e hospedamos.

### 2. VideoProviderSeeder criava só lixo
Rodava depois do AiDataSeeder e pulava os providers reais (já existiam); sobrava criar \`fal-ai\` (duplicata de \`falai\` — **nenhum client atende por essa key**), \`pika\` e \`kling\` (sem clients — funcionam via \`falai\`). Seeder removido + migration \`RemoveOrphanVideoProviders\` (data-only, idempotente, com fallback: se alguma FK não mapeada impedir o DELETE, apenas desabilita os providers para não quebrar o startup).

### 3. Gemini API key na query string
Movida para o header \`x-goog-api-key\` (não vaza mais em logs de URL).

## Melhorias

- **Fallback automático entre providers** (regra "nunca parar de gerar"): em erro transitório (quota, rate limit, timeout, 5xx, auth, modelo removido) o serviço tenta o próximo provider com chave configurada, modelo habilitado com a capability certa e **acesso RBAC do usuário**. Ordem imagem: \`gemini → grok → falai → openai → openrouter → huggingface\`; vídeo: \`falai → huggingface → replicate\` (runway fora — exige imagem de referência; shotstack fora — é composição). Com imagem de referência, só considera clients com img2img/img2video. Opt-out via \`allowFallback: false\`. Response expõe \`fallbackOccurred\`/\`attemptedProviders\` e a UI mostra badge \`fallback: gemini → grok\`.
- **Quota para imagens** (antes só vídeo) — checada antes de gastar a chamada; quota local esgotada também dispara fallback.
- **Tracking awaited** — fim dos \`Task.Run\` com DbContext scoped nos dois serviços.
- **Validações**: NumberOfImages 1–4, dimensões 256–4096, vídeo exige prompt ou imagem de referência.
- Logging estruturado de cada tentativa/hop de fallback com categoria de erro.

## Testes

- **458/458 passando** (20 novos: \`AiMediaFallbackPolicyTests\` + \`GeneratedMediaStorageServiceTests\`)
- \`tsc --noEmit\` limpo no crm-web

## Pós-merge (auto-deploy + auto-migrate cuidam do resto)

1. Migration \`RemoveOrphanVideoProviders\` roda no boot (limpa fal-ai/pika/kling)
2. Smoke: gerar 1 imagem com \`gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-image\` e conferir galeria/histórico persistido + arquivo em \`/generated-media/\`

body:
## Summary

Implements the fix proposed in #3462. `isPM`, `isAM`, and the suffix-strip regex in `parseTimeInput` all accept optional dots, but `hasMeridiem` used its own regex without them. For `"2:30 p.m."` the suffix was stripped and `isPM` was true, yet `hasMeridiem` stayed false, so the 12h-to-24h conversion was skipped and the input was silently accepted as `02:30`; `"12 a.m."` parsed as noon. This flowed into TimeInput and DateTimeInput, which commit user-typed text through `parseTimeInput` on blur/Enter.

Rather than aligning a fourth regex, `hasMeridiem` is now derived as `isPM || isAM`, so the detection can never drift from the conversion logic again. A side effect that falls out for free: `"14:30 p.m."` is now rejected exactly like `"14:30 pm"` already was, instead of being accepted as 14:30.

Fixes #3462

## Test plan

- New `parses dotted meridiems (a.m./p.m.)` block in `timeParser.test.ts`: `2:30 p.m.` / `2:30 P.M.` / `2:30 p.m` all parse to `14:30`, `12 a.m.` to `00:00`, `12 p.m.` to `12:00`, `2 p.m.` to `14:00`; plus `13:00 p.m.` is rejected like `13:00 PM`.
- Full runs of `timeParser.test.ts` (26), `TimeInput.test.tsx` (18), and `DateTimeInput.test.tsx` (48) all pass.
- `node scripts/check-changesets.mjs` passes.

## Homeowner new-booking ("Request a cleaning") flow

Replaces the legacy `RequestAppointmentModal` (off-system yellow) with a phone-first, on-brand flow built entirely from the design system. This is the last major legacy surface a homeowner touches and the actual booking-creation path.

Designed with you via the browser companion (spec + plan committed): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-02-homeowner-new-booking-flow-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-02-homeowner-new-booking-flow.md`.

### The flow (Flow C: hybrid)
- **Picks page** , Home and Service are tappable rows that open picker sheets; up to 3 preferred times as chips, each added through a focused **calendar sheet** (`ui/calendar`); optional notes.
- **Review & send** , summary, payment method (a brand card picker reusing the Slice 4 components), and a fee-aware total ("$80 base to $82.70 with the card fee", "No upfront hold, charged when the job is completed").
- **Request sent** success, then it lands under Cleanings as a pending "Requested".
- **Book again** on a completed cleaning opens the flow prefilled with the same home + service.

### Reuse (no new backend)
- Submits via `POST /api/appointments/request` **unchanged** (creates a pending `homeowner_request` appointment + its offered slots). **No migration, no new route, no RLS change.**
- Reuses the slot rules, the method-aware fee math (`processingFee`), `useHomeownerRequests`, and the Slice 4 brand card components. The legacy modal / `HomeownerCardPicker` / `AddPaymentMethodPanel` are logic-only references; all presentation is rebuilt from the design system.
- Every "Request a cleaning" button + the Home FAB + a service's "Request this cleaning" now route into this flow via `useOpenBooking()`.

### Quality
- **Independent adversarial review: SPEC-COMPLIANT.** All 7 binding constraints verified against the real code (payload correctness, card-required-when-payments-on gating, fee round-trip, no `supabase-admin` in client code, no legacy yellow, no em dashes / "operator", correct invalidation). The one Important (the card sheet was dismissable mid-3DS) is fixed, plus two minors (hour pluralization; drop a stale prefill so Book-again on a since-deactivated service falls back to unselected).
- **ui-ux-pro-max conformance: clean** (no raw hex / `primary-<number>` / `#F7C41E` / em dashes / "operator"; 44px+ tap targets; reused primitives).
- **795 unit tests pass** (incl. 15 new: `deriveBooking`, `useSubmitBookingRequest` payload, `time-options`, `useOpenBooking`). tsc + lint clean on touched files.
- **Verified end to end on a phone viewport** (dev, John Doe): open from every entry point, pick home/service/time, review with a card, send, success, and the new request appears under Cleanings; plus Book again prefill and the payments-off path. Screenshots shared in the thread. (A real pending request was created on dev during verification.)

### Deliberate deferral
- "Book again" ships on the cleaning **detail** (reached by tapping the recent-cleaning card), not as a nested button on the card itself, to avoid an invalid/inaccessible button-inside-button. A card-level shortcut can follow up if wanted.

### Constraints honored
No migration/route/RLS change; no em dashes; no "operator" in homeowner copy; no legacy yellow; no client-side `supabase-admin`; implemented from the design system.

body:
## Summary

Two new self-contained Python components (auto-discovered by the existing CI/test/build pipelines):

### 1. `qanary-component-RD-Python-PredicateIdentifier`

Given a resource already identified in the Qanary triplestore (`qa:AnnotationOfInstance` / `qa:AnnotationOfEntity`), it identifies the **most probable predicate** answering the question and stores it as `qa:AnnotationOfRelation`.

- Fetches the resource's *actual* predicates from any configured SPARQL endpoint (`KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_ENDPOINT`) — only predicates the resource really has can be proposed — and ranks them against the question (camelCase/snake_case-aware tokenisation, stop-word filtering, character-level similarity, ontology-namespace tie-break: `dbo:capital` beats `dbp:capital`).
- Resolves opaque Wikidata property labels (`wdt:P36` → "capital") via `wikibase:directClaim`.
- Example (verified live): *"What is the capital of Germany?"* + `dbr:Germany` → `dbo:capital`.
- **Tests (offline, deterministic):** unit suite + four data-driven suites over committed 100-resource subsets of **DBpedia, Wikidata, MusicBrainz, GeoNames** (≥3 cases per resource, ~1600 cases; committed generator documented in `tests/kg_fixtures/`).

### 2. `qanary-component-QB-Python-RuleBasedQueryBuilder`

Rule-based query builder: from 1–2 annotated entities and 1–2 annotated predicates it generates the answering SPARQL query and stores ranked candidates as `qa:AnnotationOfAnswerSPARQL`.

- Pattern rules derived from a committed **QALD-10 / LC-QuAD analysis**: forward/backward, `ASK` (both orientations), `COUNT`, two-hop chains, intersections, shared-predicate intersections, **superlatives** (`ORDER BY … LIMIT 1`, e.g. "highest mountain") and **SUM/AVG aggregation**.
- **Automatic pattern search:** each candidate is probed with an `ASK` against the knowledge-graph endpoint (rate-limit aware, with retries); matching patterns rank first; degrades gracefully to the deterministic rule order offline.
- **Offline E2E pipeline:** 124 benchmark-inspired questions exercise the full component (HTTP round trips against a local rdflib-backed SPARQL server standing in for the Qanary triplestore *and* the knowledge graph); generated queries are executed and compared with gold answers.
- **Opt-in live quality suite (QALD-9 test set):** gold and generated queries are both executed on live DBpedia and compared per question. Measured 2026-07-02: **55/83 exact matches, macro-F1 0.663** (extensive per-question comparison report written to a temp file). Disabled by default (`QALD9_LIVE_TEST_ACTIVE=true`), so CI stays offline.
- Every test run writes a complete report to a temporary file; `pytest -v` prints one line per case (inputs → generated query, ✔/✘).

## Test plan

- [x] RD: 1612 tests green (unit + 4 KG suites), component module 88% coverage
- [x] QB: 149 tests green offline (unit + 124-question E2E), component module 97% coverage

author: qwinndev
body:
## Summary

Historical liquidation rows/tooltips in Trade History reconstructed **Minimum required margin** and the max-leverage context from `tradeAction.marketInfo.minCollateralFactorForLiquidation` — the *current* market config. For markets that switch risk parameters (e.g. RWA/commodity markets toggling off-hours vs on-hours), this renders a misleading historical value.

This change reads the **block-time** `minCollateralFactorForLiquidation` now indexed on `TradeAction` (Subsquid slot `6230c4`) and uses it for the liquidation tooltip, so a past liquidation is explained with the config that applied at its block. It falls back to the current market config only when the historical value is unavailable (old data).

Example (WTIOIL/USD): renders the historical off-hours `1%` factor → `$9,526.02` minimum required margin instead of the later on-hours `0.5%` → `$4,763.01`.

## Changes

- **Subsquid**: point all chains except Fuji at slot `6230c4` (which indexes `TradeAction.minCollateralFactorForLiquidation`); bump the codegen source URL.
- **SDK**: add `minCollateralFactorForLiquidation` to the generated `TradeAction` type, both trade-history GraphQL queries, the raw→domain transformer, and `PositionTradeAction`.
- **UI**: `formatPositionMessage` liquidation branch uses the event-time factor (with fallback) for max leverage and minimum required margin.
- **Tests**: regression coverage for a liquidation whose factor changes after the execution block, plus the missing-value fallback.

## Summary

Fixes the globe being cut off during the scroll zoom: clipped on the sides on desktop, clipped top/bottom on mobile.

**Cause** — the globe canvas was sized as a square of `min(width, height)` of its container. Once the scroll zoom grew the sphere past its base radius, drawing was clipped at the square canvas edges, which were visible inside the viewport.

- In focus mode, size the canvas to the **full container surface** (whole viewport) and center the projection on the real viewport center, so the zoomed sphere extends past the screen edges instead of being clipped

author: fiddur
body:
## Problem

Only `Create` was federated (on share). Editing a shared post's metric selection/visibility, or unsharing it, left the post stale in followers' timelines.

## Change

Propagate the full feed-post lifecycle:

- **`deliver.ts`**: `buildFeedUpdate`/`deliverFeedUpdate` (`Update{Note}`) and `buildFeedDelete`/`deliverFeedDelete` (`Delete{Tombstone}`). Both reuse the same `getObjectUri`-derived `Note` id, so an `Update` replaces exactly the object that was delivered and a `Delete` retracts it by that id. `buildFeedDelete` needs no activity/scalar resolution, so it stays synchronous and works even after the row is gone.
- **Hook shape**: generalised `FeedDeliver` from a single function to a `{ created, updated, deleted }` interface (one fire-and-forget hook per lifecycle event). Wired `updated`/`deleted` into both the REST feed router (`PATCH`/`DELETE`) and the MCP tools (`update_feed_post`/`delete_feed_post`), so a post edited/deleted via either transport federates identically. The `DELETE` route now reads the post before removing it so the `Delete` can be addressed by its original visibility.

## Tests

- Unit: `buildFeedDelete` → `Delete` wrapping a `Tombstone` at the object id, with correct visibility addressing (public → Public/followers; followers-only → followers, never Public).
- Integration: `buildFeedUpdate` wraps the post's `Note` in an `Update` at its canonical id.

All green + `pnpm --filter aurboda-backend check` clean.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

Serving a `410 Tombstone` on a GET of a deleted object needs persistence (feed_posts are hard-deleted); the pushed `Delete` is what retracts from followers' timelines.

author: andrebrait
body:
Fixes #720.

Two test-masked production correctness bugs in `pfb_unbound.py`, each landed as its own commit with red→green coverage (all six pinning tests verified failing against the pre-fix source).

## 1. TLD-Allow / HSTS compare was case-sensitive against the raw wire case (RFC 4343)

`operate()` lowercases the names it evaluates, but the non-CNAME `tld` came from `get_tld()` = `qname_list[-2]` in the client's original case — so a mixed-case query (dns0x20-style or case-preserving clients) failed the lowercase-only membership tests: a name whose TLD **is** in the TLD-Allow list was falsely blocked, and an HSTS-TLD name missed the NULL override (VIP instead of NULL → cert error on the block page). Fixed at the source: `get_tld()` and `get_tld_from_name()` now return the lowercased label, covering both membership sites. Tests: unit (mixed-case label → lowercase) plus path-level TLD-Allow and HSTS cases asserting the mixed-case query gets the identical verdict to its lowercase form (before-state asserted first).

## 2. ADR-08: a digits/hyphen-only label was flagged; the contract says legitimate

`severity_of()` returned `flagged` for any empty script set, but ADR-08 §2 lists Common-only mixes (digits/hyphen) under "Legitimate (no action) — must never be touched in Confusable mode" (and the Phase-1 instrument encoded exactly that). With the opt-in `escalate_suspicious`, a legitimate name containing a purely numeric label was **blocked**. Fixed with the narrow carve-out that reconciles the ADR contract with the Phase-2 spec's documented borderline call: a scriptless label whose characters are all ASCII digits/hyphen → `legit`; every other scriptless label (empty/control/emoji/marks-only) **stays** `flagged`, and decode errors are untouched. The decision-table `_meta`, the golden row (`12-21` → legit/none), and the Phase-2 oracle were updated in lockstep so spec and analyzer agree; a contrast test pins that the carve-out is narrow (emoji label still flagged), and the escalate-ON branch is asserted not to promote a digit label.

## Verification

- Full suite 2000 passed (re-run after rebasing onto the live `devel` tip); `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `mypy tests/` clean.
- Red→green proven independently by the orchestrator: all 6 pinning tests fail against the `origin/devel` source for the exact reported reasons.
- Both features are opt-in (`python_tld` / ADR-08 Confusable mode); no `www/` change (no UI tier required); no manifest/swap/hook surface touched.

body: The cost explorer's "Breakdown by" control mixed the organizational breakdowns (Division, Department, User, …) with the Claude attribution cuts (MCP Server/Tool, Skill, Subagent). Those cuts group a different dataset — api_request attribution rows — and don't roll up to the same total as the org breakdowns, so selecting one made the totals jump and read as a broken breakdown rather than a re-grouping of the same data. This moves the attribution cuts out of "Breakdown by" and into a dedicated **MCP breakdown** dropdown next to the time-range picker. Both dropdowns drive the same underlying axis state, so only one is ever active at a time — the inactive one shows its category placeholder. The "skills run outside a subagent" caveat tooltip moves alongside the new dropdown, and the MCP dropdown is hidden entirely for orgs with no attribution data (so their view is unchanged). Scoped as a short-term UX fix per the DNO-392 discussion. ## Changes - `CostsExplorer.tsx`: partition pivot options into org breakdowns (main dropdown) and attribution cuts (`mcpAxisOptions`), sharing `axisValue`/`onAxisChange`. - `EntityProfile.tsx`: render the MCP breakdown `Select` in the top-right header next to the range picker; relocate the axis-hint tooltip there; add a placeholder to the main dropdown for when an MCP breakdown is active. --- ## Summary by cubic Split Claude attribution breakdowns into a separate “Agent activity” dropdown beside the date range, leaving org breakdowns in “Breakdown by.” This prevents confusing total jumps and aligns with DNO-392. - **New Features** - Org pivots + Sessions stay in the main dropdown; MCP Server/Tool, Skill, and Subagent move to the Agent activity dropdown. - Both dropdowns share the same axis state; the inactive one shows a placeholder. Agent activity hides when there’s no attribution data. Moved the Skill caveat tooltip next to it. - **Dependencies** - Added changeset for a `dashboard` patch release. Written for commit 38cad052d3d4a3e8ee12f9bce26679c8b549b8ee. Summary will update on new commits.

author: fcostaoliveira
body:
## Summary

The two flat `counts[]` percentile scans (`getValueFromIdxUpToCount` used by `ValueAtPercentile`,
and the `ValueAtPercentiles` batch loop, both from #57/#58) iterated with an `int32` index and read
`counts[idx]` — which Go bounds-checks on **every** element of the hot prefix-sum loop. Iterating with
`for idx, c := range h.counts` hands the element to the loop directly (and `len(counts) == countsLen`),
so the compiler elides the per-element bounds check. Results are unchanged.

## Benchmark

`gnr1` (Intel Granite Rapids), single core, same-session A/B (base = current master):

| | before | after | Δ |
|-|--------|-------|---|
| `ValueAtPercentile` (Mq/s) | 0.1067 | **0.1833** | **+71.8%** (9.4 → 5.5 µs/query) |
| `ValueAtPercentiles` batch (calls/s) | 58,779 | **70,237** | **+19.5%** |
| `RecordValue` (control) | 322.9 M/s | 321.6 M/s | flat |

Percentile results byte-identical (verified via a stable cross-sum, unchanged). `go test ./...` green.
This closes most of the remaining gap to the SIMD C implementation for the scalar scan.

author: sroussey
body:
## Summary

Adds per-port backpressure gating to the no-accumulation passthrough streaming path, enabling fine-grained pacing of producers to match consumer read rates on individual ports. Previously, passthrough edges had no pacing mechanism; producers could race ahead unbounded. This change introduces `BackpressureGate` coordination between producer and consumer streams, with separate gates per source port feeding independent consumers.

## Key Changes

- **Per-port edge gates** (`EdgeGateState`): `StreamPump` now builds a `BackpressureGate` for each source port that feeds a no-accumulation passthrough edge. Gates track pending event costs in a FIFO and coordinate producer/consumer pacing.

- **Producer-side pacing**: `StreamProcessor` receives an `edgeBackpressure` callback from the graph runner. After emitting each delta, the processor awaits the gate for that port, parking until the consumer has read enough to bring buffered bytes below the high-water mark.

- **Consumer-side credit**: The passthrough stream's reader charges the gate as events are enqueued and credits it as the consumer reads, using `streamEventCost` to measure bytes per event.

- **Safety cleanup**: If a passthrough consumer reaches a terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, DISABLED, ABORTING) without fully reading its stream, the gate is closed to release any parked producer; every edge-stream teardown path (stream end, terminal producer status, reader cancel) also closes the gate.

- **Deadlock liveness guard**: a gate is built only when the consumer can make read progress while the producer is parked — if any other edge into the consumer is sourced from the producer or one of its DAG descendants (drained, mode-mismatched, or static edges), that edge settles only after the producer finishes, so gating would deadlock the pair. Such consumers keep the ungated passthrough (correct, just unpaced).

- **Stream-fed consumers run uncached**: a run consuming a live stream at an unsettled input port computes its cache key without the streamed content, so caching is disabled (`kind: "none"`) for that run — preventing stale hits and poisoned rows when two runs differ only in stream payload. Drained edges keep caching.

- **Producer failure propagates in-stream**: a producer failure enqueues an in-stream error event before edge streams close, so an early-dispatched consumer fails instead of completing (and caching) on truncated input; abort keeps the graceful close.

- **Mixed-mode and fan-out test coverage**: Two new comprehensive test suites validate the gating behavior:
  - `StreamMixedModeFanout.test.ts`: One source with separate `append` and `object` ports, each feeding its own passthrough consumer with independent gates; also tests fan-out (one port → two consumers) which correctly falls back to tee'd drain without a gate.
  - `StreamBackpressureEngaged.test.ts`: Fast append producer feeding a slow consumer over a small high-water mark; verifies producer is parked and peak lead stays bounded.

- **Cache hit replay pacing**: `CacheCoordinator` now accepts `edgeBackpressure` in `CacheReplayContext`, allowing cache-hit replay to respect the same per-port gates as fresh runs so slow consumers pace both paths identically; append/object logs decode in a single pass instead of buffering the whole byte log.

- **Validation and schema improvements**:
  - Added `isDeltaStreamMode()` helper to identify modes that can be encoded to byte streams (`append`, `object`, `binary`).
  - Added `portForcesStreamValidation()` to read the `x-validate-stream` opt-in, allowing ports to opt out of both validation exemption and passthrough pacing.
  - Updated `TaskRegistry` to validate binary format on both input and output ports.
  - `AiTask` / `ImageEditTask` / `ImageGenerateTask` forward the `validateInput` skip-ports parameter.

- **Instance schema support**: `CacheCoordinator` and `TaskRunner` now use instance schemas (via `task.inputSchema()` / `task.outputSchema()`) instead of static schemas, enabling dynamic-schema tasks to add ports at runtime without breaking cache key normalization, sink setup, or cache-hit replay.

- **Streaming output hydration**: `resolveJobOutput` now adapts inline append/object values to byte streams (UTF-8 text, NDJSON) for consistent caller behavior whether the value came from a ref or inline; input-ref hydration decodes append/object refs through their stream codecs (string / folded object) instead of handing byte Blobs to string ports.

- **Cycle detection in ref resolution**: `resolveOutput` now detects cyclic values and uses memoization for acyclic ones, ensuring shared subtrees resolve once and both slots receive the same resolved copy.

- **File write robustness**: `FsFolderTaskOutputRepository` now loops on partial writes to ensure the full chunk reaches disk before returning the size stamped into the `CacheRef`, and opens stream reads eagerly so a pruned blob reports a clean cache miss instead of throwing ENOENT mid-iteration.

- **Orphan-blob cleanup**: covers all delta modes (was binary-only); a stream ending without a finish event fails its cache sinks so truncated blobs are discarded, not published. (The run-private tier does not build streaming sinks after the run-scoping reconciliation from main — it falls back to accumulation — so no orphan refs can arise there.)

## Notable Implementation Details

- Gates are installed only for edges that satisfy `isNoAccumulationPassthroughEdge()`: single consumer, same mode on both ends, consumer is a streamable non-subgraph task, no validation opt-in — plus the liveness guard above.
- The `edgeBackpressure` callback is threaded through `IRunConfig` → `StreamProcessor` → task's `IExecuteContext` `backpressure()` hook, allowing both direct emitters and `StreamProcessor`-routed deltas to respect pacing.
- Passthrough streams are never tee'd (no materialize copy), avoiding the accumulation the passthrough exists to prevent; the edge keeps the same stream reference so "this edge is streaming" checks still hold.
- Non-qualifying edges (transforms, mode mismatch, fan-out, `*` edges, non-streamable or subgraph targets) fall back to the existing drain path — correct, just without the memory and pacing win. With `noAccumulation` off, behavior is unchanged.
- The branch merges `claude/relaxed-faraday-ql3olr` after its reconciliation with `main` (run-scoped private cache, degrade-to-miss cache decode, edge-stream reader-cancel teardown); conflict resolutions combine both sides — see the merge commit message for details.

## Verification (post-merge head)

- `bun scripts/test.ts graph vitest` green (962 tests); `bun scripts/test.ts task vitest` green (1119, 24 skipped); job-queue + FsFolder storage spot suites green
- `npx tsc -p packages/task-graph/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; `bun run build:types` clean across all 36 packages
- Policy-OFF runs identical to pre-change behavior (explicit assertions in test files)

author: robzolkos
body: ## Summary Documentation-only change addressing #459, where `basecamp comment` posted a comment with a stray leading `$`. ## Root cause Not a CLI bug — a shell quoting issue. The reporter used bash ANSI-C quoting: ```bash basecamp comment 9802493119 $'海报 mockup 方向稿：\n\n' --in ... --json ``` `$'...'` is a **bash/zsh extension**, not POSIX. Under a POSIX `/bin/sh` (dash, busybox-ash — the default in most Linux sandboxes and "agent workflow" shells), `$'...'` is parsed as a literal `$` followed by an ordinary single-quoted string. The CLI then faithfully posts exactly what the shell handed it. The smoking gun is in the issue's own output: the posted HTML contains **both** the literal `$` **and** literal `\n\n` (backslash-n, not real newlines). If bash had interpreted `$'...'`, the `\n` would have become real newlines and the `$`/quotes consumed. Their survival proves a POSIX `sh` ran the command. ## Why not "fix" it in the CLI The issue floated stripping the `$'...'` wrapper inside the CLI. Rejected: `$` and `'` are legitimate content characters (prices, code, apostrophes), and the app can't know a leading `$` was an unintended quote wrapper. Guessing at shell intent would silently corrupt real content. The safe alternative — stdin via `-`, bare pipe, and `--edit` — already exists. This PR just documents it. ## Changes - `comments create` / `comments update` help text: warn against `$'...'` for multiline/non-ASCII content, recommend the stdin (`-`) pattern. - `skills/basecamp/SKILL.md`: same guidance in the content-fields section, extending the existing `printf %q` quoting advice. ## Note `bin/ci` currently fails on this branch's base due to a **pre-existing, unrelated** build breakage in `internal/commands/cards.go` (the SDK's `CardColumns.EnableOnHold/DisableOnHold/SetColor` gained a `columnID` parameter that `cards.go` hasn't been updated for). It exists on the clean base independent of this change; this PR only touches help-text strings and Markdown (gofmt-clean). --- ## Summary by cubic Warns against using bash ANSI-C quoting `$'...'` for multiline or non-ASCII comment content, which under POSIX `/bin/sh` posts a stray `$` and keeps `\n` literally. Updates the `basecamp comments create`/`update` help to recommend stdin with `-`, and adds the same guidance to `skills/basecamp/SKILL.md` (addresses #459). Written for commit 471fdc7dec058da76ef31ab416448246471e043a. Summary will update on new commits.

author: felipesauer
body:
## Contexto

Auditoria do projeto + investigação do modo `soap` (STATUS_SOURCE=soap com certificado A1), que "não funcionava". A investigação revelou **dois bugs encadeados** — corrigidos e validados contra a SEFAZ real — além de correções de auditoria (rota e docs).

## Bugs corrigidos

### 1. A API não carregava o `.env` (causa raiz do modo soap)
A API lia toda a config de `process.env`, mas **nada carregava o arquivo `.env`** (`dotenv` não era dependência, nenhum `--env-file`). Com `pnpm dev`, o `.env` era ignorado: `STATUS_SOURCE` caía no default `hybrid` e `SEFAZ_CERT_PATH` ficava vazio → o modo `soap` **nunca ativava**.

**Correção:** `loadDotEnv()` no topo de `main()` usando `process.loadEnvFile()` (nativo do Node ≥20.12, sem dependência nova). Procura o `.env` na raiz do monorepo e cai para o cwd; variáveis já no ambiente têm precedência.

### 2. Endpoints SOAP desatualizados
Com o `.env` carregando, o SOAP finalmente rodou e expôs endpoints quebrados. Uma varredura das **27 UFs × 5 documentos** com cert A1 achou **7 endpoints únicos** retornando 404/HTML ou com DNS morto. Todos revalidados (HTTP 200 + XML SOAP):

| Documento | Autorizador | Problema | Correção |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NFe (+NFCe) | SP | `nfestatus.asmx` → 404 | `NFeStatusServico4.asmx` |
| NFe | RS/SVRS/SVCRS | `NfeStatus2.asmx` → 404 | `NfeStatusServico/NfeStatusServico4.asmx` |
| NFe | BA | `NfeStatusServico2` → 404 | `NFeStatusServico4/NFeStatusServico4.asmx` |
| NFe | MS | `ws2/…Servico2.asmx` → 404 | `ws/NFeStatusServico4` |
| NFe | PE | `nfenw.sefaz.pe.gov.br` → DNS morto | `nfe.sefaz.pe.gov.br/nfe-service/…` |
| CTe | RS/SVRS/SVCRS | `CTeStatusServico.asmx` → 404 | `CTeStatusServicoV4/CTeStatusServicoV4.asmx` |
| DCe | SVRS | `dce.svrs.rs.gov.br` → DNS morto | **migrou p/ SEFAZ-PR** `dce.fazenda.pr.gov.br/dce/DCeStatusServico` |

> A DC-e mudou de autorizador: o host do SVRS foi descontinuado e o ambiente nacional passou a ser hospedado pela SEFAZ-PR (confirmado no portal oficial `dfe-portal.svrs.rs.gov.br/Dce`). Corrige produção e homologação.

### 3. Normalização do `document` na rota `/status/:document/:uf`
A rota normalizava a `uf` (`toUpperCase`) mas não o `document`. Como `DocumentType` é case-sensitive (`NFe`), `/status/nfe/sp` gerava o id `nfe:SP` que não casava com o armazenado (`NFe:SP`) → 404 espúrio. Adiciona `normalizeDocument` + teste.

### 4. Docs desatualizados
- README: "15 minutos" → "de hora em hora", alinhado ao cron real do Actions (`17 * * * *`).
- `config.ts`: comentário do `STATUS_SOURCE=hybrid` descrevia o `HybridCollector` antigo; o motor real é o `ConsensusCollector`.

## Validação

- ✅ `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` (todos verdes)
- ✅ API real subida em modo `soap`: `Rodada production [soap]: 135 serviços` — lê o `.env`, carrega o cert A1, coleta e persiste no Redis
- ✅ Os 19 endpoints únicos respondem SOAP (antes: 7 quebrados)

> Nota: com certificado **e-CPF** a maioria das SEFAZ responde `cStat 282 (cert sem CNPJ)`; só GO/BA/PE dão `107`. Status completo via SOAP exige um **A1 de CNPJ** — limitação do certificado, não do código.

author: s243a
body:
## Summary

**Stacked on #3405** (→ #3404 → #3403 → #3402 → #3401). Final PR of the series — the first slice of float support, delivered design-first.

```awk
{ print $2 / 2.0, $2 / 2 }        # 3.5 3 — float vs integer division, explicit
{ print float($2) }               # strtod coercion: "2.5rest" → 2.5, "abc" → 0
{ printf "%.2f;", $2 / 3.0 }      # fixed precision
{ print ($2 + 1) * 0.5 }          # i64 subtrees promote via sitofp
{ print 0.1 + 0.2 }               # 0.3 (correctly rounded literals, %g output)
```

## Design decision

Full awk everything-is-a-double semantics would silently change every existing integer program (`$3 / 2`, `%d` printf, guarded division, END averages) — so this slice makes doubles **explicit and inference-driven**: an expression is double-typed when any operand is a float literal or a `float($N)` coercion; otherwise the established i64 semantics are untouched. `$2 / 2` still truncates; `$2 / 2.0` doesn't.

**Scope boundary (deliberate):** doubles are expression-level only. Scalar slots, guards, and `END` expressions stay `i64`, and assigning a double expression to a scalar is rejected at codegen. Typed double slots — slot types threaded through the ~8 loop/branch/final phi emitters — are the documented follow-up that unlocks `{ sum += $2 * 1.5 }`.

## Interesting bits

- **Exact float literals.** LLVM's textual IR rejects decimal FP constants that aren't exactly representable (`double 0.1` is an error). Instead of a lossy Prolog-float→hex round trip, the parser keeps literals exact as `float_const(Mantissa, 10^k)` and codegen emits `fdiv double 15.0, 10.0` — both operands exactly representable, and one correctly rounded IEEE division yields the same double `strtod` would produce.
- **`float($N)`** lowers to a new `@wam_atom_field_f64_value` runtime helper: `strtod` over a NUL-terminated scratch copy of the field slice (leading number, trailing text ignored, `0.0` for non-numeric/missing — awk's coercion semantics).
- **Emission** is a parallel `plawk_f64_expr_ir` mirroring the i64 emitter (`fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/frem`, `sitofp` promotion of i64 subtrees). Float division is IEEE — no zero-divisor guard, `x/0.0` is `inf` as in awk.
- **Output:** `print` uses a shared `%g` global (integer-valued doubles print as `20`, awk-style); `printf` passes doubles to the vararg call and accepts `%f`/`%g`/`%e` with optional precision.

## Testing (honest exit codes)

- `tests/test_plawk_surface_float_exprs.pl` — 17/17 pass: exact-ratio ASTs, `fdiv`/`sitofp`/`%g` IR shapes, int-vs-float division duality, strtod trailing-text semantics, `0.1 + 0.2` rounding, `%.2f`/`%g`/`%e`, promotion, guard composition
- Full regression: all nine plawk surface suites **plus** the 80-test `test_wam_llvm_target` suite (runtime touched) — all pass

**Merge order for the whole series:** #3401 → #3402 → #3403 → #3404 → #3405 → this. After each merge, retarget the next PR to `main` (or let GitHub do it if the base branch is deleted on merge) — last time the stacked PRs merged into each other's branches instead of `main`, which #3401 repairs.

body:
Findings from a full consistency sweep of `docs/` (every roadmap page read end-to-end; all internal anchors verified against the built site; every issue number cited in docs checked open; docs-stated dependencies cross-checked against GitHub `blocked by` links; docs-cited code line references spot-checked).

Fixes in this PR:

- **roadmap/index.md** — the "which place do I use" intro said "three places" but the table has four rows; two table rows had broken formatting (stray `:` before the pipe, missing spaces) and the "What is already build" typo.
- **metrics-and-leaderboard.md** — "live-forecast scoring (Phase 7 / 8)" referenced the deleted Dagster ML-assets plan's phase numbering; now links to [production monitoring](https://openclimatefix.github.io/nged-substation-forecast/roadmap/live-service/#production-monitoring).
- **delivery-tables.md** — Table 4 (`effective_capacity`) was marked "🚧 MVP in v0.1", but the MVP asset is implemented (`cv_assets.py` — full-history P99, one scalar row per series, exactly as the page describes); flipped to ✅ with the DP upgrade still 🚧. Also retargeted the "(see [scope changes](index.md))" label — no such section exists — to the v2 stretch-goals anchor where the REST API actually lives.
- **switching-events.md** — stage 3's "matching the spirit of v0.5" → v0.6 (the detector's own simple-statistics ethos).

## What's here
- **`custom:oselia-resident`** — a second dynamic strategy, added alongside `custom:oselia` in the same no-build JS module (shared fetch helper).

## Scope (from #20)
- [x] Second, resident-facing dashboard, separate from installer Diagnostics
- [x] Per-Area cards from bound entities (light tiles + native cover cards w/ slider)
- [x] Truthful relay/cover state
- [x] Regenerates from live Areas/bindings

- **11 new HA-free unit tests** (50 total, all green): placeholder-when-empty, heading + light tile + cover tile with `cover-open-close`/`cover-position` features, empty-areas dropped, one-section-per-area, logo-first, all-empty→placeholder.
- **Live against real HA + your own bindings**: cold and warm calls produce a "Home" view with an *Unassigned* section holding your two basement-roller relays.

1. The **lazy bindings store** must be `await`-loaded in the WS handler — a cold request otherwise lists empty and renders a spurious "no rooms yet" placeholder.

Your basement-roller bindings target relay **switches** (relay actions), so they render as light tiles under *Unassigned*. Assign those entities to an HA Area (and/or bind covers) to see them grouped into rooms with cover sliders.

author: acamarata
body:
## Problem

For nested Hasura-style migration layouts (`migrations/<timestamp>_<name>/up.sql`), migration identity was derived via `filepath.Base` — so every migration was keyed `up.sql`. Consequences:

- `nself db migrate status` listed every row as generic `up.sql` instead of real names
- ledger primary-key collisions: `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` silently dropped records, so applied migrations were re-counted as pending
- pending counts were non-deterministic (observed 7 then 12 on back-to-back runs against identical DB state; true count was 0)

Companion to #162 (which makes a version-drifted remote error loudly; this fixes the underlying name collapse in the CLI itself).

## Fix

- New `migrationKey()` is the single identity source for scan ordering, pending computation, status listing, and ledger writes: nested `up.sql` → parent dir name (`002_add_task_approval_system`), flat files → filename.
- `extractMigrationID` (ops-table id / checksum audit) uses the full name instead of first-underscore truncation, so same-day migrations stay distinct.
- Ledger writes: `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (ops table) / erroring INSERT (legacy table) — a PK conflict can only mean the same migration re-recorded, never a silent drop.
- `upgradeLedger()` runs before every applied-set read: idempotently rewrites old prefix-style ops ids in place and renames the single legacy `up.sql` row to its resolved key. No DB schema change.

## Tests

20 new/updated targeted tests (key derivation flat+nested, same-day distinctness, pending determinism + idempotent re-run, never-silent-noop record SQL, legacy upgrade SQL guards, scan ordering) — all green; full `go test ./internal/database/` passes. `gofmt`/`go build`/`go vet` clean.

No version bump.

author: cmungall
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a complementary graph-derived QC metric for source-side gene wiring into the pathograph, alongside the existing phenotype connectivity metric. It also enriches 20 disorder files with gene annotations on pathophysiology nodes to enable the new metric.

## Key Changes

### QC Plugin Infrastructure (`src/dismech/qc_plugins.py`)
- **New `GeneMechanismWiringPlugin`**: Measures whether causal genetic nodes are wired into the mechanism pathograph via `contributes_to` edges to pathophysiology nodes. This is the source-side complement of `PhenotypeConnectivityPlugin`.
- **New `gene_mechanism_wiring_coverage()` function**: Core logic that identifies mechanism-relevant genetic items (excluding BIOMARKER, PROTECTIVE, MODIFIER, DISPUTED, UNKNOWN relationship types) and counts how many are connected to pathophysiology nodes via shared gene keys.
- **New `GENE_WIRING_PREDICATES` constant**: Defines `contributes_to` as the predicate for gene-mechanism edges.
- **Updated module docstring**: Clarifies that both phenotype connectivity (inbound) and gene-to-mechanism wiring (outbound) are now supported.
- **Updated `DEFAULT_PLUGINS`**: Now includes both `PhenotypeConnectivityPlugin` and `GeneMechanismWiringPlugin`.
- **Updated CLI help text**: Reflects dual-metric reporting.
- **Import addition**: Imports `_genetic_item_infers_mechanism_edges` from `dismech.graph` to filter non-causal genetic items.

### Test Coverage (`tests/test_qc_plugins.py`)
- **New test `test_gene_wiring_coverage_identifies_floating_gene()`**: Validates that genes without matching pathophysiology nodes are correctly identified as unwired.
- **New test `test_biomarker_gene_excluded_from_denominator()`**: Confirms that non-causal genetic items (BIOMARKER) are excluded from the denominator.
- **New test `test_gene_wiring_plugin_emits_graded_score()`**: Verifies the plugin emits properly formatted `AggregatedPathScore` records.
- **Helper function `_mendelian()`**: Provides test data with one wired and one floating gene.

### QC Configuration (`conf/qc_config.yaml`)
- **New config section**: Adds `genetic[].mechanism_outlink` metric with weight and min_compliance settings (parallel to `phenotypes[].causal_inlink`). Advisory-only for now (weight 1.5, `min_compliance: null`).

### Disorder Knowledge Base Enrichment
Gene annotations added to pathophysiology nodes across **20** disorder files, targeting the entries with the largest gene-to-mechanism wiring gap. Each gene was mapped to the single mechanism node it drives, reusing verified `hgnc:` ids from the `genetic` block where present and OAK-verifying any fresh lookups; polygenic GWAS/susceptibility loci with no honest single-mechanism node were intentionally left unwired (the metric is advisory and honest partial coverage is the intended outcome).

Fully/near-fully wired (Mendelian): **Fanconi_Anemia** (8→22/22), **Dyskeratosis_Congenita** (0→17/17), **Dystroglycanopathy** (0→17/17), **Joubert_syndrome** (14→35/35), **Primary_Ciliary_Dyskinesia** (2→21/21), **Kawasaki_Disease** (0→20/21), **Meckel_Syndrome** (0→14/15), **Hypertrophic_Cardiomyopathy** (0→24/26).

Substantial gains: **Dilated_Cardiomyopathy** (0→33/48), **Diabetes_Mellitus** (3→15/20), **Rheumatoid_Arthritis** (0→15/23), **Systemic_Lupus_Erythematosus** (0→9/26), **Ulcerative_Colitis** (0→9/18), **Psoriasis** (0→9/24), **Multiple_Sclerosis** (0→8/18), **Schizophrenia** (0→8/14), **Crohn_Disease** (0→7/21), **Amyotrophic_Lateral_Sclerosis** (1→6/21), **Asthma** (3→5/17), **Ankylosing_Spondylitis** (0→4/16).

Aggregate across the 20 files: ~31 → 298 of 440 causal genes wired.

Structural follow-up (genetic nodes whose gene is a multi-word string and needs a `gene_term`, plus continuing the wiring pass down the ranked list) is tracked in #5170.

body:
## What

The code half of `docs/exploration-budget/belief-derived-valuation-design.md` (RATIFIED 2026-07-02, design PR #188) — discharges the two valuation gaps the coherent-injection gate re-run named (#187 §6). The last hand-written numbers at the selection seam become posterior expectations:

- **1a Horizon-completed growth VOI**: `growth_value(Δℓ, n_buf, plateau, H; prior_term, compute_cost)` — canalised (the `net_value` pattern, registered on its linearity audit surface); `H == n_buf` reproduces the window-total score exactly (the nested pin); the prior-Occam charge is one-time, outside plateau AND horizon; `feature_growth_value` is the single home of the Occam composition. Hosts pass declared data (`H` = declared episode length × observed event rate) and never multiply.
- **1b Learned returns-to-growth**: `GrowthReturns` — Gamma(2,1)×Exponential conjugate cells per (op × changed-since-last-fire), conditioned on realised yields (injected posterior mass, incumbent-side read) through Tier-1 `condition`; scored via the new `Reciprocal` TestFunction (exact `β/(α−1)`). The `entropy − log 2` heuristic, the saturation-ordering eligibility gate, and the separate-track fallback all retire; escape ops compete freely and self-extinguish under zero-yield evidence (CONSTITUTION §3.54/§3.55 discharged).
- **1c Metrics amendment (§2c)**: final-window rate co-primary; efficiency gate moves to fixed-reference (steps to half the best compared policy's per-seed total).

## Also in this PR

- **Gate-blocker fix (latent on master)**: `perturb_grammar` could install a subtree referencing another grammar's nonterminal → dangling ref → `compile_expr` crash. Fixed in the shared candidate core (score/transition/signal stay one function); regression test reproduces the crash path.
- **Adversarial self-review batch** (8-angle review, 10 verified findings, 9 fixed — see commit `d538c9c`): incumbent-side yield (no `1−mass` cancellation crash), score==transition on the price coordinate, typed cache keys, attribution gate on the completed score, pool-change context flips, facade/doc/pragma cleanups.
- **Declared depth frontier** (`max_program_depth`): depth-(d→d+1) enumeration is pool-dependent (measured ~7×10⁵ components at 3→4 on the benchmark pool) and the ratified mass-yield observable rewards volume floods at cold start — **the §5 Q1 attention-vs-value wedge, made concrete**. The frontier is task data (conservative default = starting depth; the benchmark declares start+1 so deepen gets its honest probe). Named for the results doc; predictive-delta fidelity is the escalation path.

## Verification

- 57/57 local Julia test files (incl. new `test_growth_returns.jl`, re-baselined `test_grid_world_meta.jl`, the dangling-ref regression in `test_perturb_consumption.jl` §4)
- Skin wire smoke green; lint `apps/` clean + corpus self-test
- Score==transition parity sweep over a (plateau × horizon × cost) grid
- **Dominance gate re-run (20 seeds) in progress** — results commit follows before undraft. Early signal: eu_max seed 0 runs at 17 meta-actions vs ~625 pre-change (claim (i)).

## Notes

- `AgentState` gains `growth_returns` (9th field); snapshot blobs are image-version-scoped per the Move-2 `learning_regime` precedent (no protocol bump).
- The Exponential conjugate guard relaxes to `obs ≥ 0` (zero is in the support and is the modal yield); boundary validation stays the wire's job.

author: ericbfriday
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The lexer contained an O(N^2) time complexity vulnerability when parsing malformed Lua multiline strings/comments (`[===[ ... ]===]`). When checking for string terminators, the inner loop iterated through the full length of expected `=` characters even after encountering a mismatch.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could craft maliciously malformed code with excessively long delimiter sequences that hang the parser, exhausting CPU resources and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) against the host application using `luaparse`.
🔧 Fix: Updated `readLongString` in `luaparse.js` to `break` the inner loop early upon the first character mismatch, reducing the terminator check to O(1) time in failure cases.
✅ Verification: Tested against malicious inputs where parsing dropped from >30s to <10ms. All test suites pass.

author: phil-opp
body:
## Summary

The two `CoordinatorStore` backends disagreed on which param keys they accept:

- `RedbStore::put_node_param` builds a composite string key using `\0` as a separator (`KEY_SEPARATOR`) and rejects any key containing `\0` via `make_param_key`/`check_no_separator`.
- `InMemoryStore::put_node_param` stores the key in a tuple `BTreeMap` and only checked length.

So the same `put_node_param(..., "a\0b", ...)` call returned `Err` on the redb backend but `Ok` on the in-memory backend — a latent inconsistency that would surface if the coordinator switched backends.

## Fix

Move the null-byte rejection into the shared `validate_param_limits`, which both backends already call, so they now accept/reject identical input. The redb-side `check_no_separator` stays as defense in depth. Added an in-memory regression test mirroring the existing redb one (`param_key_with_null_byte_is_rejected`).

## Validation

- `cargo test -p dora-coordinator-store` and `... --features redb-backend` — both new tests pass, all 34 redb tests pass ✅

author: scttbnsn
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4805.

`OpenAITTSService` and `OpenAISTTService` build their `AsyncOpenAI` client with no way to pass HTTP options, so in high-latency environments there's no way to raise the request timeout short of subclassing and replacing `self._client`. `BaseOpenAILLMService` already exposes a public `create_client()` override point for this; the TTS and STT services had nothing.

## What changed

- `OpenAITTSService` accepts an optional `http_client` (`httpx.AsyncClient`) and passes it to `AsyncOpenAI`.
- `BaseWhisperSTTService` accepts the same parameter and passes it through `_create_client()`, so `OpenAISTTService` (and other Whisper-based services like `GroqSTTService`) pick it up via `**kwargs`.
- Default behavior is unchanged: with no `http_client`, the OpenAI SDK builds its default client exactly as before.

Usage, per the scenario in the issue:

```python
import httpx
from openai import DefaultAsyncHttpxClient

tts = OpenAITTSService(
    api_key=...,
    http_client=DefaultAsyncHttpxClient(
        timeout=httpx.Timeout(60.0, connect=10.0),
    ),
)
```

## Verification

- Added `tests/test_openai_http_client.py` covering custom-client pass-through for TTS and STT, plus the `None` default.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -k "openai or whisper or groq"` passes.
- `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check` are clean on the changed files.

author: micio86dev
body:
## Summary

Full security audit of the codebase (auth/authz, injection, secrets/infra,
billing/rate-limit/DoS, frontend) — 5 parallel review passes, cross-checked
against the actual code before fixing. No SQL injection, path traversal,
SSRF, command injection, or committed secrets were found. This PR fixes
everything real that was found: 1 High, 12 Medium, and a batch of Low
hardening items.

### High
- **Guest cost-amplification**: an unauthenticated guest could open a
  private room and stream audio indefinitely — `GUEST_MAX_MINUTES` was
  `None` by default (unlimited) and, even when set, the counter reset on
  every reconnect. Now a cumulative per-IP counter (1h rolling window) with
  a safe default (10 min), so anonymous STT/translation spend is actually
  bounded.

### Medium
- `POST /api/friends/request` let an attacker enumerate registered emails
  and spam friend-request notifications (distinguishable 404 vs 201, no
  rate limit). Now rate-limited per user and returns the same 202 whether
  or not the email is registered.
- Org invite `accept` didn't check the token was redeemed by the invited
  email — anyone holding a leaked token (dashboard URL → referrer/history/
  logs) could join the org at the invited role. Now bound to the invite's
  email.
- The join-time `lang` WS param was interpolated unescaped into the
  Deepgram streaming URL — a crafted value could inject extra query
  parameters into our own paid Deepgram request. Now validated the same
  way the mid-call `set_lang` path already is.
- Stripe webhooks (`checkout.session.completed`) credited without checking
  `payment_status`, so a delayed payment method would get credited before
  the money settles. Now gated on `payment_status == "paid"`, with
  `async_payment_succeeded` handled for the delayed-settlement case.
- `JWT_SECRET` had no strength floor — a short secret is offline
  brute-forceable from any issued token (full account takeover). Startup
  now rejects anything under 32 bytes.
- CORS fell back to `permissive()` in billing-configured (production)
  deployments when `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` was unset. Now fails closed, deriving
  an allowlist from `APP_BASE_URL`/`DASHBOARD_BASE_URL` instead.
- Config structs holding API keys / JWT secret / Stripe keys derived
  `Debug` — a stray `debug!`/`dbg!`/panic would have dumped them straight
  to logs (and Better Stack). Now hand-written `Debug` impls that redact.
- Per-IP rate limits silently collapse onto Cloudflare's edge IP if
  `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` isn't set behind Cloudflare — now warns loudly at
  startup when that misconfiguration is detected.
- Directus↔Supabase DB link had `DB_SSL__REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED: false`
  (MITM-able). Now verifies by default, with an env-gated escape hatch.
- Rate limiter documented as per-instance/in-memory (correct for the
  current single-Railway-instance topology; flagged for a Redis-backed
  swap before any horizontal scale-out).

### Low (hardening)
Constant-time comparisons for the origin-lock and metrics-token secrets;
admin audit rows now record the caller's source IP; Google ID token
verification now requires `email_verified` and checks the issuer; the
transcript-recap email always re-renders from the escaped plain-text body
instead of trusting stored model HTML (closes a prompt-injection→phishing-
link vector); Docker images run as a non-root user; chat attachment and
notification-banner URLs are scheme-checked (`http(s)` only) before hitting
`href`/`src`/`fetch`; the friends call-invite endpoint now sanitizes the
room code like the other invite path does; join-time room/name length caps.

### Deliberately not changed
- **Webhook rate-limiting**: skipped — risks dropping legitimate Stripe
  webhooks (lost payments); the signature already makes forged requests
  harmless, and a shared Cloudflare edge IP would make per-IP throttling
  counterproductive here.
- **JWT in `localStorage`** and **CSP `unsafe-inline`** on the client: the
  real fix (short-lived httpOnly token; nonce-based CSP) needs a live
  browser test to avoid breaking Google Sign-In/hydration — out of scope
  for this pass, flagged for follow-up.

### Related submodule PRs (not yet merged — pointers intentionally unbumped)
- micio86dev/voxtranslate-dashboard#4 — CSP + a self-XSS fix
- micio86dev/voxtranslate-website#2 — drop deprecated `X-XSS-Protection`, add CSP

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (CI-exact invocation) — clean
- [x] `cargo test` on the touched integration suites (config, friends, business_orgs,
      business_members, billing, business_billing, transcripts, admin) against a local
      Postgres — 9/9 binaries, 64/64 tests passing
- [x] `astro check` (client) — 0 errors
- [ ] Manual: sign-in, friend request, org invite accept, and a guest call end-to-end in staging

author: vixitonian
body:
## Summary
Ran a live sweep of all 21 configured AI models (real API calls). This PR acts on the results:

**Removed (needs account funding — real quota/credit walls, not fixable in code):**
- `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.0-flash` — free-tier quota is 0 for these models
- `openai/gpt-4o`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5` — OpenRouter credit shortfall too large to close (needs 16k/32k tokens, account can afford ~3.6k/2.4k)

**Fixed:**
- `nex-agi/nex-n2-pro` — its `:free` route is retired upstream; switched to the plain slug, which works.
- `moonshotai/kimi-k2` — root cause was two-fold: (1) the provider OpenRouter routes it to (Novita) rejects `response_format: json_object` outright, and (2) the 32768 max_tokens budget exceeded what the account could pre-authorize. Fixed by dropping `response_format` and capping this model's `max_tokens` to 12000.
- `openai/gpt-oss-20b:free` — this reasoning model was routing its real answer into a `reasoning` field and leaving `content` null whenever `response_format: json_object` was set. Confirmed dropping the format hint alone fixes it cleanly (verified via raw API call before/after).

**`OpenRouterClient` change:** removed `response_format: json_object` entirely. It was causing outright rejections or empty-content responses on multiple providers; the client already has a lenient JSON-extraction fallback (`ai_lenient_json`) for exactly this kind of response, so the strict format hint was net-negative.

**Removed (broken, unfixable or redundant):**
- `openrouter/owl-alpha` — model doesn't exist on OpenRouter ("no endpoints found")
- `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` — consistently rate-limited upstream (429 on every retry); `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free` already covers this model family and works fine

**Added (free, verified working, good for code/frontend generation):**
- `poolside/laguna-m.1:free` — larger tier of the existing working Laguna family
- `cohere/north-mini-code:free` — code-specialized model, routes through Cohere directly (not the currently-congested Venice provider that several other free models share)

Considered `qwen/qwen3-coder:free` (480B coding-specialized model, 1M context) but it only has one backing provider (Venice) which was persistently rate-limited across multiple retries over several minutes during testing — too unreliable to add right now.

- [x] `php -l` on both changed PHP files
- [x] `node --check` on `app.js`
- [x] Live-tested every model change against the real OpenRouter/NVIDIA/Gemini APIs before and after the fix (not just config review)
- [x] Verified `kimi-k2`, `gpt-oss-20b`, `nex-n2-pro` all succeed end-to-end through the actual `OpenRouterClient` class with the new code
- [ ] Deploy to live server and confirm
