body:
## What this is

The audit found the docs site's parity with chebfun.org had been faked: commits 47bb148/10357da replaced the Python-translated guide/example pages with verbatim chebfun.org HTML and copied 1,193 PNGs byte-for-byte. Separately, CI had been red since March — every run timed out at 6h. This branch restores genuine parity and fixes the underlying library.

## CI status: fully green (first time since March)

Lint 9s · Code quality 16s · Golden refs 16s · Tests+Coverage 9m20s (was: 6h timeout). pytest-timeout + xdist + job limits prevent regressions to the old failure mode.

## Library correctness — 17 real translation bugs fixed

- **Ballfun constructor infinite loop** (the 6h-CI cause; also hid every test collected after it): happiness check rewritten against @ballfun/constructor.m using Chebtech2/Trigtech happiness. Exact for polynomials, ~1e-16 smooth. **Ballfunv** rebuilt (was mis-wired end-to-end); MATLAB norm semantics.
- **Silent under-resolution in division/power/abs** (1/(1+25x²) had 3.7e-2 error) — all quotient/power paths now re-run adaptive construction like MATLAB compose(); abs(f) root-splits.
- **Arithmetic breakpoint-merge** (@chebfun/overlap.m): same-interval operands with different interior breakpoints now merge instead of raising.
- **Chebop.bc property implemented**: `L.bc = 0` used to create a dead attribute and solve with NO boundary conditions (wrong eigenvalues, no warning). Now MATLAB set.bc semantics (numeric/callable/'dirichlet'/'neumann' both ends).
- **AAA Froissart cleanup**: analytic prz residues (deterministic) instead of platform-dependent least-squares residues; sequential support-point removal. Kills the cross-platform conformal2 flake (machine-precision round-trips across perturbation seeds).
- **jacpts(a,b) with a+b=−1** (Chebyshev weight) returned all-NaN — removable 0/0 in the j=1 recurrence coefficient; now exact vs Gauss-Chebyshev.
- **jac2jac** NaN at gam+delta+1=0; **ultracoeffs(λ=1)** skipped the T→U conversion; **chebvals2chebvals(2→1)/chebcoeffs2chebvals/legcoeffs2chebvals(kind=1)** applied corrupting DCT scalings; **diffbarytrig** off by 4^N with a wrong support-point D-matrix.
- **norm(f, ∞)** via minandmax (was max over grid values, missing between-node peaks); **conformal** forward-map pole check (inpolygon semantics); **gallery('zigzag')** was a different function; **imex** stepping ran numpy FFTs per step (GPU sync) — now jnp.

## Docs: genuine parity

Guide chapters **1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 fully redone** (every figure chebfunjax-rendered at the reference pixel geometry, compared numerically + human-reviewed against the MATLAB render, every page snippet executed with real outputs, honest notes where features are missing); **ch.16 figures done** (28/28 genuine; page audit tracked). Tooling: `scripts/compare_plots.py` (flags byte-identical-to-reference figures as NOT_REGENERATED), `scripts/run_page_snippets.py`. Plotting layer: exact-size export, MATLAB ticks, piecewise + dotted jump connectors.

**Remaining chapters** are placeholder-imaged and tracked with precise blockers: ch.5 (complex chebfun support — constructor currently real-casts silently), ch.7 (eigenfunction output/expm/matrix), ch.9 (Unbndfun exists but unwired from the factory), ch.20 (Ballfun calculus ops), ch.11–15/17–19 (unprobed). All 365 example scripts run clean; example-page visual parity is the next workstream.

## Test status

CI full suite green incl. 80% coverage gate; local fast suite 2400+ passed (~3.5 min, xdist); MATLAB golden refs 166 passed; ruff clean repo-wide; new coverage tests for deltafun/transforms/trigutils (which found 6 of the bugs above).

## Summary

Bakes two image-level LAN ingest gateways into the device image so a phone or OBS on the same LAN can publish directly into cerastream without going through the cloud relay. Companion to CeraUI's `feat/trustworthy-experience` PR, which adds the runtime status surface + UI for these gateways.

### What's baked

- `ceralive-rtmp-gateway.service` — pinned MediaMTX `v1.19.2` (`moq: false`), hardcoded publish path `rtmp://<device>:1935/publish/live` matching cerastream's `InputKind::RtmpLocalhost`
- `ceralive-srt-gateway.service` — `srt-live-transmit "srt://:4001?mode=listener" "udp://127.0.0.1:4000"` (from `srt-tools`), rewraps to UDP-TS onto cerastream's `InputKind::SrtIngest` loopback ingest. No SRT passphrase in v1 (tracked in `docs/DEFERRED.md` item 7 follow-up).
- LAN-only ingress firewall (`v2/mkosi/runtime/ingest-firewall/`) — nftables rules dropping :1935 (RTMP) and :4001 (SRT) on modem/WWAN/ppp interface classes, so the gateways are reachable only from the LAN, never from the cellular/WAN uplink
- Host-level smoke tests: ffmpeg RTMP round-trip proof, SRT byte-relay proof
- `docs/DEFERRED.md` item 8: on-device network-ingest relay verification checklist

## Merge order

⚠️ This PR should merge **before** the companion CeraUI PR (`feat/trustworthy-experience`, ceralive/CeraUI#135), since CeraUI's backend probes assume these systemd units exist on the image.

author: paulalbert1
body:
## What

Wrap each destructive delete→repopulate in the small-table ETL modules into **one interactive Prisma transaction** (`$transaction(async (tx) => {…}, { timeout: 120_000, maxWait: 10_000 })`), so a mid-write process kill rolls back to the prior coherent state instead of leaving a table half-empty.

PR-6 of the ETL-hardening effort (`docs/etl-hardening-pr6-pr7-handoff.md`). PR-7 (state-machine tiering) follows next and depends on this — continue-on-failure is only safe once partial writes can't leak.

## Why

Guards (PR-1/PR-3) stop *bad-source* wipes but not *mid-write kills*. A death (OOM/SIGKILL) between `deleteMany` and the batched re-insert leaves the table truncated; Step Functions retries re-run the whole step and widen the window. Concrete hazard: `Coi` dying mid-write → `CoiGap` (next nightly step) fabricates false compliance gaps from the half-empty table.

## Scope

| Module | Tables | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `etl/coi/index.ts` | `coi_activity` | delete + batched insert in one tx |
| `etl/jenzabar/index.ts` | `phd_mentor_relationship` | " (dropped a dead write-only counter) |
| `etl/ed/student-programs.ts` | `student_phd_program` | " |
| `etl/clinical-trials/shared.ts` `replaceAll` | `person_clinical_trial` + `clinical_trial` | both in one tx; children-first delete, parents-first insert |
| `etl/tools/index.ts` | `scholar_tool`; `scholar_family` + `family_entity`/`family_entity_usage` | two txns; entity layer joins the family tx for coherence |

**Out of scope by design:** Reciter `PublicationAuthor` per-PMID path (~500k rows — oversized tx; stays in the abort tier so its partial state is never published) and the ED scholar upsert loop.

Guards (`assertSourceVolume` / `.count()`), reads (`scholar.findMany`), and `etl_run` bookkeeping stay **outside** the tx; every destructive write routes through `tx.*`.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- `eslint` (changed files) clean
- **full `vitest run` — 520 files / 6411 tests passed**, incl. the new `tests/unit/clinical-trials-replace-all.test.ts` (asserts single-tx wrapping, FK-safe ordering, returned counts; the mock exposes only `$transaction` so a stray `db.write.*` escape would throw)
- deterministic grep: no destructive delete/insert remains on `db.write.*`
- 2-lens adversarial review (field-preservation + tx-correctness): no findings

## Deploy

Pure ETL-script change — no CDK / machine-definition change. Activates whenever the `sps-etl-<env>` image next rolls; needs **no** gated `Sps-Etl` deploy (that gate is for PR-7).

author: phil-opp
body:
## Summary

The per-message record path in `binaries/record-node/src/main.rs` allocated and copied the arrow payload **twice**:

```rust
let mut buf = vec[0u8; data_size];                 // alloc #1
arrow_utils::copy_array_into_sample(&mut buf, ...); // copy #1
Some(AVec::from_slice(128, &buf))                   // alloc #2 + copy #2
```

`AVec::from_slice` allocates a new 128-byte-aligned buffer and memcpys `buf` into it, so every recorded message paid for two allocations and two payload-sized copies where one of each suffices.

## Fix

Allocate the aligned `AVec` once (zeroed) and serialize the arrow buffers straight into it, matching the idiom already used in the daemon (`lib.rs`) and runtime:

```rust
let mut buf: AVec<u8, ConstAlign<128>> = AVec::__from_elem(128, 0, data_size);
arrow_utils::copy_array_into_sample(&mut buf, &arrow_data);
Some(buf)
```

Same result type as before. The zeroing is retained because `copy_array_into_sample` leaves alignment-padding gaps between buffers unwritten.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p dora-record-node` ✅
- `cargo clippy -p dora-record-node -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` ✅

author: alex-place
body:
Follow-up to the Tier-1 correctness fixes ([#1888](https://github.com/alex-place/lantern-os/pull/1888)). Implements the backend hot-path, algorithmic, and infra optimizations from the audit. Every change is verified (see below); no behavior change on success paths.

## Tier 2 — hot-path JSONL reads + unbounded seen-Sets (Closes #1889)
- **New `lib/jsonl-cache.js`** — mtime+size keyed parse cache for append-only JSONL/JSON files. Correct by construction: any append bumps mtime/size so the stale key falls through to a fresh read; the collector/file-queue is the only writer. Returned arrays are treated as read-only by all callers.
- Wired into **trading-store** (`_readAll`), **kalshi-stats**, **trading-memory** (`queryRecentTradingRecords`), **convergence-status**, and **`/api/trading/llm-usage`** — these previously re-read + re-parsed the entire growing file on *every* request (UI polls every 5–10s).
- **Bounded `_seenOrders`/`_seenSignals`** (FIFO evict at 10k) — fixes the slow memory leak. `ingestTradingData` now counts newness by pre-checking membership, since size-delta is unreliable once eviction starts.

## Tier 3 — algorithmic hotspots (Closes #1890)
- **`convergence/memory.statistics()`** — single pass; was O(n·sources) (re-scanned all entries once per distinct source).
- **`crypto-collector`** — single pass bucketing by symbol; was N full scans of the ~500-market list.
- **`account_link._latest()`** — scans newest→oldest and returns the first match instead of parsing every line.

## Tier 5 — infra (Closes #1892)
- **`requirements.txt`: `zstandard>=0.22.0`** — CSF now uses the fast codec instead of silently falling back to zlib (~25–30× worse on the JSONL logs).
- **`queue_ledger.replay(auto_compact=True)`** — collapses an oversized (>5 MB) ledger to its live task set, wired into the one-time startup rebuild in `server.py`. Runtime observers (`supervisor.observe_queue`) keep `auto_compact=False` so a frequent poll never rewrites the file under the live writer.

## Tier 4 (#1891) — deferred, left open
The flagged frontend items are either **intentional** (stock-trader 3s poll is a deliberate `#1627` tick-flash choice; kalshi 1s countdown) or **high-risk DOM/swipe-listener rewrites** that can't be responsibly verified without driving the live swipe-deck UI. Kept as an open issue rather than shipped blind.

## Verification
- `node --check` on all 7 JS files; `py_compile` on all 4 Python files.
- jsonl-cache: invalidation-on-append / bad-line-tolerance / missing-file smoke test; trading-store append→read roundtrip through the cache.
- Unit assertions for `memory.statistics`, `account_link._latest`, `queue_ledger` compaction; trading-memory dedup counting.
- `pytest test_account_link + test_convergence_memory` (43 pass), `test_trading_memory` (10 pass); JS `test_trading_memory_js` (16 pass) + `test_account_link` (6 pass).

author: bfollington
body: ## Why Plain clicks in `cf-cell-link`, `cf-profile-badge`, and `cf-render` tiles dispatch the interceptable `cf-navigate` event on `globalThis` — an embedder like Loom can host it and apply its own URL scheme. But **modifier-click** (cmd/ctrl → "open in new tab") did not: each component built a shell URL via `appViewToUrlPath` and called `globalThis.open()` directly, dispatching nothing. That makes the new-tab path **un-interceptable** and a **guaranteed 404 on any non-shell origin**. Loom is shipping a server-side redirect as a stopgap (commontoolsinc/loom#3627); the right fix is upstream — make new-tab navigation interceptable the same way in-place navigation already is. ## What - **New `openInNewTab(command)` helper** next to `navigate()` in `packages/shell/shared/navigate.ts` (re-exported through `@commonfabric/shell/shared`, where all three components already import `navigate`). It dispatches a **cancellable `cf-open-external`** event on `globalThis` (matching where `cf-navigate` is dispatched) carrying the same `AppView` detail (`{spaceDid|spaceName, pieceId}`) **before** URL construction. - A host cancels via `preventDefault()` and owns the navigation. - If not cancelled, the shell default runs: today's `appViewToUrlPath` + `globalThis.open` — **shell behavior unchanged, zero callback plumbing**. - **All three components** (`cf-cell-link`, `cf-profile-badge`, `cf-render`) now call the one helper — no three copies of the URL-building logic. Their modifier-click branches collapse to `openInNewTab(view)`. - **Event typing** mirrors the existing `cf-navigate` idiom: a `CustomEvent` subclass (`OpenExternalEvent`), consistent with `NavigationEvent`/`ReplaceNavigationEvent`. (The repo does not use a `WindowEventMap`/`HTMLElementEventMap` augmentation for these — the pattern is a typed `CustomEvent` subclass + cast on the listener.) ### Event contract - **Name:** `cf-open-external` - **Detail:** `NavigationCommand` (= `AppView`, e.g. `{spaceDid, pieceId}`) — same shape as `cf-navigate` - **Dispatch target:** `globalThis` (same as `cf-navigate`) - **Cancelable:** yes — `preventDefault()` suppresses the default `globalThis.open` ### Deliberate unification `cf-profile-badge` already passed `"noopener"` to `globalThis.open`; `cf-cell-link` and `cf-render` did not. The unified helper uses `globalThis.open(url, "_blank", "noopener")` for all three — `"noopener"` is strictly safer for externally-opened tabs. ## Tests - `packages/shell/test/navigate.test.ts` (new) — covers the helper directly: dispatches a cancellable `cf-open-external` with the right detail; falls through to `globalThis.open` with `_blank` + `noopener` and the expected URL when not cancelled; `preventDefault()` suppresses `globalThis.open`. - `packages/ui/src/v2/components/cf-profile-badge/cf-profile-badge.test.ts` — added two tests following the existing `cf-navigate`-contract idiom: modifier-click dispatches cancellable `cf-open-external` with the right detail; `preventDefault()` suppresses `globalThis.open`. The pre-existing new-tab test (default URL unchanged) still passes. `deno fmt`, `deno lint`, `deno check`, and the touched-package tests all pass. Linear: CT-1830 Loom stopgap: https://github.com/commontoolsinc/loom/pull/3627 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Make modifier-click “open in new tab” interceptable by dispatching a cancellable `cf-open-external` event, preventing 404s on non-shell origins. Default shell behavior stays the same; addresses Linear CT-1830. - **New Features** - Added `openInNewTab(command)` in `packages/shell/shared/navigate.ts` (re-exported via `@commonfabric/shell/shared`). It dispatches cancellable `cf-open-external` on `globalThis` with `NavigationCommand` detail; hosts can `preventDefault()`. If not cancelled, falls back to `appViewToUrlPath` + `globalThis.open(url, "_blank", "noopener")`. - Updated `cf-cell-link`, `cf-profile-badge`, and `cf-render` to use the helper on cmd/ctrl-click. Unified new-tab opens to include `"noopener"` for all. Written for commit 44508f545bd871a1ee4aab21430eb9936036b036. Summary will update on new commits.

author: luchoc-dev
body:
## Resumen

Fixes #13

Arregla las dos causas raíz del bug F4 (dashboard mostrando `claude-sonnet-5` con 362 sesiones y \$0.00), diagnosticadas en el spike de storage (`docs/research/storage.md` §5):

1. **Pricing $0 para modelos nuevos** — `calculate_cost()` solo tenía precios hardcodeados para Opus 4 y Sonnet 4 (substrings `opus-4` / `sonnet-4`). Se reemplazó por una tabla de reglas ordenada de más específica a más general (`PRICING_RULES`), cubriendo:
   - **Confirmados contra la doc oficial** (skill `claude-api`): Fable 5 / Mythos 5 ($10/$50), Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6 ($5/$25), Sonnet 5 ($3/$15), Sonnet 4.6 ($3/$15), Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5).
   - **Sin confirmar, fallback a precio de la misma familia**: Opus 4.5/4.1/4.0 (usan precio de "opus-4" genérico: $15/$75) y Sonnet 4.5/4.0 (usan precio de "sonnet-4" genérico: $3/$15).
   - **Modelo totalmente desconocido**: fallback a precio de Sonnet 4 ($3/$15) en vez de $0.
   - Cache write/read se derivan del precio de input con la razón estándar de Anthropic (write = input×1.25, read = input×0.1) — se verificó que esta razón coincide exactamente con las constantes que traía el archivo para Opus 4 y Sonnet 4.

2. **`session_count` contaba entradas, no sesiones** — se incrementaba una vez por cada `UsageEntry` (mensaje con tokens), no por sesión única. Se cambió a `HashMap<String, HashSet<String>>` (modelo → session_ids únicos) en **ambas** funciones (`get_usage_stats` y `get_usage_by_date_range`), y `total_sessions` global también se corrigió para usar sesiones únicas (antes era `filtered_entries.len()`).

## Fuera de alcance (detectado, no corregido — mismo patrón)

Por instrucción explícita se limitó el alcance a `usage.rs` sin tocar el resto del dashboard/frontend. Se detectó que el mismo patrón roto (contar entradas en vez de sesiones) también afecta:
- `project_stat.session_count` en ambas funciones.
- El conteo en `get_session_stats` (línea ~693), aunque ahí `session_count` está documentado como "entradas por sesión", no sesiones — su semántica es distinta y probablemente correcta como está.

Quedan anotados para un fix futuro si se decide expandir el alcance.

## Verificación
- `bun run build` (genera `dist/`) + `cargo check` desde PowerShell: **verde**, sin errores nuevos (solo warnings preexistentes no relacionados).
- **Test manual pendiente para el usuario**: correr `bun run tauri dev`, abrir el Usage Dashboard y verificar que `claude-sonnet-5` (u otro modelo reciente) muestre costo > 0 acorde a sus tokens, y que el número de sesiones por modelo sea plausible (no igual a la cantidad de mensajes).

author: natanai
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a small, dependency-free web app that teachers can use to generate printable analog clock cards for classroom visual schedules. 
- Ensure every clock is drawn programmatically as precise SVG geometry so printed cards are predictable, high-contrast, and accurate at small sizes.

### Description
- Add a single-page app with controls and preview in `index.html`, styles and print rules in `styles.css`, and the app logic in `app.js` that implements parsing, settings persistence, and card generation; add a simple vector `favicon.svg` and an expanded `README.md` with usage and deployment notes.
- Implement schedule parsing with `parseScheduleInput` / `parseLine` / `parseTime`, producing items like `{ activity, rawTime, displayTime, hour, minute, hasAmPm, amPm }` and generating clear inline parse errors for invalid lines.
- Draw clocks entirely with SVG in `createClockSvg` using the exact geometry formulas `minuteAngleDegrees = minute * 6` and `hourAngleDegrees = ((hour % 12) + minute / 60) * 30`, plus numerals, 60 ticks (thicker every 5 minutes), two hands with suggested stroke widths, and a center dot.
- Expose user settings (card size, columns, clock size, layout, toggles for activity labels, borders, cut lines, ticks, numerals, AM/PM options) wired to `localStorage`, applied to CSS variables (`--card-width`, `--card-height`, `--clock-size`, `--columns`), and used when rendering the preview and print output.

### Testing
- `node --check app.js` to validate JavaScript syntax: passed.
- Served the site with `python3 -m http.server 8000` and fetched `/`, `/styles.css`, and `/app.js` to confirm files are served: passed.
- Verified the clock-hand angle math for the acceptance cases with a Python check of the formulas (7:00, 8:30, 9:15, 9:45, 10:20, 10:30, 11:30, 12:00, 2:45, 4:15, 5:00): passed.
- Attempted a headless browser screenshot step but no headless browser was available in the environment, so the screenshot step was not performed (non-blocking).

Files added/updated: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.js`, `README.md`, and `favicon.svg`.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent tap-to-play from reselecting the already-playing station when the user taps another location while preserving globe rotation, beacon animation, and existing playback selection flow.
- Ensure touch/drag/pinch gestures do not accidentally trigger playback by scoping dragging per pointer and invalidating multi-touch tap candidates.

### Description
- Add an `activeStationKeyProvider` option to `AtlasInteractionEngine` and wire `BlueMarbleGlobe` to pass the current active key as `station.station_uuid || station.id` via a ref to avoid stale closures.
- Update `rankPlayableAtlasStationsInCountry` to accept an optional `activeStationKey`, keep distance-first sorting (avoid `Infinity - Infinity` issues with a stable comparator), exclude the active station when other playable stations exist, and fallback with `only-active-station-in-country` when it is the only playable candidate. 
- Make tap candidate handling multi-touch-safe by scoping dragging to the pointer candidate, rejecting multi-touch taps, and invalidating candidates on pointer cancel so drag/pinch gestures don't trigger selection. 
- Surface developer diagnostics (dev-only) in the globe click logger including `activeStationKey`, `excludedActiveStation`, `candidateCountBeforeExclusion`, `candidateCountAfterExclusion`, `selectedStation`, `selectedStationDistanceKm`, and `fallbackReason`, while preserving the existing `onStationSelect` playback/focus flow. 
- Use a `getGlobeGeometryRef` in `BlueMarbleGlobe` so the interaction engine reads current geometry without capturing a stale `getGlobeGeometry` closure.

author: hitoshiichikawa
body:
Closes #473

## 概要

`install.sh`（1,492 行）の内部を機能単位に再構成し、見通しを改善する。**CLI 契約
（フラグ / 冪等性 / NEW・OVERWRITE・SKIP・BACKUP 挙動 / 出力文言）は完全不変**。

## 事前判断: 案A（install-lib.sh 分離）を採用

`setup.sh`（curl | bash bootstrap）は `install.sh` を**単体で** curl 取得することはなく、
必ず `git clone --depth 1` で repo 全体を取得してから `exec bash "$IDD_CLAUDE_DIR/install.sh" "$@"`
で起動する（setup.sh:108-134）。手動導入も `git clone` 前提。よって install.sh が
curl | bash の単体取得経路に載ることはなく、**案A（install-lib.sh へ分離し BASH_SOURCE 相対で
source）を採用**。install.sh は既に `SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"`
を使っており、相対 source の土台が既にあった。

## 実施内容

1. **install-lib.sh を新設**し、以下を機械移動:
   - 配置ヘルパー 13 関数（`log_action` / `classify_action` / `copy_template_file` /
     `copy_with_hybrid_overwrite` / `copy_claude_md_with_org` 等、全 533 行）
   - ラベル自動セットアップ 4 関数（Issue #85、全 164 行）
   - 履歴持ち込み検出 9 関数 + 2 グローバル（Issue #115、全 381 行）
   - 上記 26 関数は**全て verbatim 移動**（本文 1 文字も変更なし。Python アンカースクリプトで
     元ファイルの行範囲を機械抽出し、再構成後に非コメント行の内容差分ゼロを確認）
2. 加えて、Issue 本文の指示（「引数 parse / repo-template 配置 / local-watcher 配置 / cron 案内 /
   doctor を install-lib.sh へ移動、install.sh は main フローのみに」）を full に満たすため、
   従来 install.sh にインラインだった 3 ブロックを **新規関数として** install-lib.sh に追加:
   - `parse_install_args "$@"` ← 引数パース while ループ（48 行、無改変で関数化）
   - `run_repo_install` ← repo-template 配置フロー（106 行、`if $INSTALL_REPO; then` の中身を
     無改変で関数化）
   - `run_local_install` ← local-watcher 配置 + cron/launchd 案内 + 前提ツールチェック（doctor）
     （142 行、`if $INSTALL_LOCAL; then` の中身を無改変で関数化）
   - この 3 関数は bash の「関数内グローバル代入は呼び出し元スコープに伝播する」性質と
     `exit` がネストに関係なくプロセス終了する性質により、**挙動を変えずに関数化可能**と判断。
     install.sh 側は `if $INSTALL_REPO; then run_repo_install; fi` のように、元の `if/fi` 骨格を
     main フローとして残し、中身だけ呼び出しに置換した。
3. **install.sh は 1,492 → 119 行**に縮小（sudo ガード / SCRIPT_DIR 解決 / source /
   フラグ既定値 / 3 関数への call site のみ）。install-lib.sh は 1,441 行。
4. cross-file 変数可視性喪失による SC2034 false-positive（`REPO_TEMPLATE_DIR` /
   `DRY_RUN` 等が install.sh 側、`INSTALL_LOCAL` / `INSTALL_REPO` が install-lib.sh 側）を
   #464/#469 と同じパターンで file-wide `# shellcheck disable=SC2034` + 根拠コメントで抑止
   （dead code ではなく cross-file 参照であることを明記）。

## 検証結果

```
$ bash -n install.sh && bash -n install-lib.sh
syntax OK（両ファイル）

$ shellcheck local-watcher/bin/*.sh local-watcher/bin/modules/*.sh install.sh install-lib.sh setup.sh .github/scripts/*.sh
（出力なし = warning ゼロ）

$ 29 関数（既存26 + 新規3）が install.sh / install-lib.sh / setup.sh 全体で重複定義なし（各 1 箇所）を確認
```

**冪等性 smoke（/tmp scratch repo）**:
- `--help` → 使い方表示 OK
- `--dry-run --repo .` （初回）→ 全ファイル `[DRY-RUN] NEW`
- `--repo .` 実行 → 全ファイル `[INSTALL] NEW`（20 件）
- 再実行 → 全 20 件 `SKIP`（完全冪等）
- テンプレファイル手動編集後 `--force` → `BACKUP` (`.bak` 生成) + `OVERWRITE`
- 既存 CLAUDE.md 編集後の通常再実行 → CLAUDE.md は `SKIP`（据え置き）+ `CLAUDE.md.org` を `NEW`
- `--force-claude-md` → CLAUDE.md を `BACKUP` + `OVERWRITE`
- `--local`（scratch `$HOME`）→ 54 件 `NEW`（issue-watcher.sh / watcher-config.sh / modules 43 本含む）
- `--local` 再実行 → 54 件 `SKIP`（完全冪等）
- 未知オプション `--bogus-flag` → エラーメッセージ + `exit 1`
- 疑似 `docs/specs/999-.../` 配置後 → inherited 検出 WARNING が正しく発火

**root 実行検知（sudo 禁止ガード）**: コードは install.sh 冒頭に無改変で残置（`SCRIPT_DIR` 解決・
source より前に配置し、install-lib.sh を読み込む前に安全側で停止できる構成を維持）。
ロジック自体は 1 文字も変更していないため、既存の sudo 検知動作は引き続き機能する。

**内容不変性の機械確認**: 元 install.sh と 新 install.sh+install-lib.sh を結合したものから
コメント/空行を除去して diff した結果、差分は「if/while ブロック境界 → 関数境界への構文置換」
（3 関数化 + 4 個の新規呼び出し行 + 1 個の source 行）のみで、case 分岐・文字列・ロジックの
変更は一切ないことを確認済み。

## README 更新

ディレクトリ構成ツリーに `install-lib.sh` を追加。install.sh の使い方・フラグ説明を含む
他の README 記述は CLI 契約が不変のため変更不要（`install.sh --local` 等の利用手順はそのまま）。

## 確認事項（レビュワー判断ポイント）

- Issue 本文の列挙（引数 parse / repo-template 配置 / local-watcher 配置 / cron 案内 / doctor）を
  忠実に反映するため、`run_local_install` は「local-watcher 配置」「cron 案内」「doctor」を
  **1 関数にまとめて**実装した（3 関数に細分化していない）。細分化は「どの境界で切るか」という
  新たな設計判断を伴うため、機械的移動の原則に沿って粒度を最小限（呼び出し元ブロック単位）に
  留めた。より細かい分割が必要であれば追加 Issue で対応可能。
- `parse_install_args` の内部（`while`/`done`）は元のインデント（0 起点）のまま関数でラップしており、
  関数本体としては先頭 2 マス下げになっていない（他の関数とスタイルがわずかに不揃い）。
  内容を 1 文字も変えない方針を優先したため意図的に残した。

## スタック運用について

本 PR は #455 tracking issue の子 issue 群の一部として、base を `main` ではなく
`claude/issue-472-promote-pipeline-family`（直前 issue #472 のブランチ）にしている。
先行 PR が `main` に merge され次第、base を付け替える。

body:
## Summary

Introduces the **Architect Council** pattern as a specialized decomposition procedure for the orchestrator skill. This pattern delegates complex or ambiguous requirement analysis to two sub-agents (brainstorm architect for analysis/design, grill architect for validation) before task derivation, enforcing the design-first principle from CLAUDE.md at the swarm decomposition stage.

## Key Changes

- **New reference document** (`architect-council.md`): Comprehensive guide for the architect council pattern
  - Defines when to invoke the council (complex/ambiguous requirements vs. simple fan-out)
  - Specifies roles: brainstorm architect (diverge→converge analysis) and grill architect (interrogation/validation)
  - Documents the council loop with max rounds budget and escalation rules
  - Establishes task output contract (id, scope, files, dependencies, risk, verification criteria, DB touch flag)
  - Enforces model policy: fable tier floor for architects, ceiling for all other roles
  - Lists antipatterns and validation checklist

- **Updated `autonomous-driving.md`**: Integrates architect council into main orchestrator loop
  - Decompose step now references architect council for complex requirements
  - Decision log now includes council outputs
  - Added DBA agent as conditional gate for DB-touching tasks (schema, migration, query, ORM changes)
  - Clarified fable distribution policy as fixed constraint (not heuristic)
  - Updated gate rules: reviewer + QA + (conditional) DBA all pass before merge

- **Updated `SKILL.md`**: Reflects architect council in orchestrator workflow
  - Step 1 (Decompose) now mentions council delegation for complex/ambiguous work
  - Step 6 (Gate) now includes DBA agent for DB-touching tasks
  - Added reference to architect-council.md in documentation index
  - Clarified model distribution policy envelope

- **Updated `delegation-patterns.md`**: Formalizes fable distribution policy
  - Added model tier table entry for requirement decomposition/design interrogation
  - New section "fable 배분 정책" defining fixed envelope:
    - **Floor**: Architect council (brainstorm/grill) maintains fable/opus tier
    - **Ceiling**: All non-council roles (implementation, review, QA, DBA) forbidden from fable tier
  - Clarifies that envelope is policy constraint, not heuristic—no re-evaluation within bounds

- **Updated `spec-driven-review.md`**: Minor clarification on DBA gate applicability

## Implementation Details

- **Council loop contract**: Brainstorm→grill→(if reject) brainstorm again, max `max_council_rounds` iterations before hard stop + escalation
- **Task output format**: Mandatory fields ensure dispatch prompt has complete context (dependencies, risk, verification criteria, DB touch flag)
- **Skill adaptation**: Brainstorm/grill skills auto-adapt from user conversation to codebase exploration + explicit assumptions + escalation for domain decisions
- **Context isolation**: Council full output goes to decision log; main retains only task list + assumptions/escalation summary
- **DBA gate trigger**: Dual detection—task flag from council + file change inspection (migrations, .sql, schema, ORM, query builder calls)
- **Model policy enforcement**: Parent session with fable model must explicitly specify `model` for non-council dispatch to avoid inheritance ceiling violation

## Rationale

Enforces CLAUDE.md's design-first principle (requirements → side-effect investigation → design) at the swarm decomposition stage. Prevents main agent from being overwhelmed by analysis while ensuring decomposition quality (which bounds all downstream work) is validated before dispatch. Fable distribution policy ensures highest-tier reasoning is reserved for decisions that determine swarm direction, not execution.

author: isaacaryeepah-beep
body:
## Why offline login was failing in practice

The previous offline-login work passed in clean lab conditions but broke in the field. Three concrete, reproduced gaps:

### 1. App shell couldn't boot offline after any service-worker update
`index.html` loads every script with a cache-busting query string (`/js/app.js?v=...`), but the SW pre-cached only 4 bare paths and matched the cache by **exact URL** — so the versioned requests never hit the pre-cache. Runtime caching papered over this only until the next SW version bump, which wipes **all** caches on `activate` (we shipped five bumps in one day). In that window, an offline app open served `index.html` with no scripts at all — a dead page, so login couldn't even run.

**Fix**: the SW now pre-caches the full shell (all `pages-*`, `faq-*`, `manager-portal`, vendored Chart.js, icon, manifest — 20 files total), stores runtime-cached entries under their bare path, and matches JS/CSS/navigation fallbacks with `ignoreSearch`, so versioned requests are always served offline immediately after any update. Cache bumped to `dikly-v12`.

### 2. Login dead-ended on "Network error" when the device lied about being online
`isOnlineAsync()` caches its reachability probe for 8s, and iOS often keeps `navigator.onLine === true` right after airplane mode. When that happened, the online login path ran, the request failed at the network layer, and the catch block just showed "Network error" — it never consulted the offline profile store.

**Fix**: new `loginOnlineWithOfflineFallback()` — all five login handlers (admin, lecturer, HOD, employee, student) now detect network-type failures mid-login and retry against the offline profiles instead of surfacing a dead end.

### 3. Offline app open could log the user out for the same reason
The boot-restore path trusted the same stale reachability probe, so a network-failed `/api/auth/me` fell through to a token wipe instead of restoring the cached session.

**Fix**: a network-type `/auth/me` failure now counts as offline evidence and restores the cached session snapshot.

## Verification (Playwright, live stack)

- Fresh SW install pre-caches 20 shell entries including all page scripts
- Offline **cold open in a brand-new tab** (simulating force-quit/reopen) boots fully from cache — versioned script URLs served, `handleAdminLogin`/`attemptOfflineLogin` present
- Boot-restore lands straight on the dashboard offline
- Logged-out offline login via the real form works end-to-end
- Wrong password still correctly rejected offline
- 🔍 Stale-online simulation (forced `navigator.onLine = true` + primed reachability cache + actual network cut) — both **login** and **boot-restore** correctly fall back instead of dead-ending
- Reconnect restores live API access via token refresh

author: jonastemplestein
body:
Follow-up to #1589 — CI speed/reliability wins, plus the Depot CI usage doc.

## What's in this PR

- **Warm the OAuth path** (validated ✅) — the preview warms the cold OAuth callback (OS callback handler + the auth worker, origin derived from the `/login` redirect) before the specs. `signup.spec` went from **3 cold-callback timeouts (~33s each) to passing in ~4s**; `create-project` passes too.
- **Fail-fast** — Playwright `retries` 2→1 (one retry is enough); itx-client WS `handshakeTimeout` 30s→15s (post-#1601 connects are fast).
- **Raise e2e concurrency** — restore `sequence.concurrent` + `maxConcurrency: 3` (up from the reliability-pinned 2), now that #1601 fixed the cold-create latency. `4` (peak ~16) still overloaded a *very* cold slot (161s deploy → DO-storage-timeout fails that survived retry), so 3 (peak ~12) is the reliable ceiling. Going higher wants the itx-monolith split (`tasks/raise-e2e-maxconcurrency.md`).
- **`docs/depot-ci.md`** — README-discoverable (one hop): how our Depot CI works, the commands (run/status/logs/dispatch/metrics/secrets), gotchas, and links.

## "Move all CI to Depot" — designed, not landed here (on purpose)

I prototyped the full migration (generator routing `.github/workflows/` → `.depot/workflows/` for everything except `claude-assistant`) and **reverted it**, because doing it *right* is an infra task that shouldn't be rushed:

- **One secret is real** — Depot only needs `DOPPLER_TOKEN`: deploys/test already `doppler run`, `slack.ts` already falls back to Doppler for the Slack token, and `ITERATE_BOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` resolves from Doppler too. Verified both tokens resolve from `_shared/prd`.
- **But Doppler must be baked into the Depot image** (not `curl | sh`'d per run, per review), and **moving the prod-deploy workflows needs deliberate validation** (high blast radius).

The full runbook (Doppler-in-image → generator routing → one-secret → validate deploys) is in `tasks/move-all-ci-to-depot.md`.

> Note: `depot ci secrets` currently holds an interim *personal* `DOPPLER_TOKEN`; swap it for the CI Doppler service token before relying on the migration.

author: kroperuk
body:
Closes #74. Builds on the #67 diagnostics probe to actually surface per-device data as sensors.

## Problem
The coordinator only polls **plant-level** realtime, so devices whose data isn't aggregated at the plant level — EV chargers, meters, secondary batteries — never become sensors even though they show in the iSolarCloud app and diagnostics.

## What this adds
- **New option "Create per-device sensors"** (off by default — avoids extra API calls / entity clutter). Configure → toggle on.
- **Discover all devices**: `__init__` now fetches the full device list (not just inverter/ESS) and passes it to the coordinator. `select_dispatch_device` is tightened to only pick an **inverter/ESS** so the broader discovery can't accidentally attach dispatch controls to a meter or charger.
- **Coordinator per-device polling**: when enabled, best-effort `async_get_device_realtime` per distinct device type (forwarding your **extra measure points**) into `coordinator.device_data`. A device type whose endpoint errors is skipped without failing the update.
- **`SungrowDeviceSensor`**: reads per-device data and is grouped under its own device card, linked to the plant via `via_device`. `SungrowSensor` was refactored so both share point naming/classification.
- **Dedup**: device points already present at the plant level are skipped, so enabling the option doesn't just duplicate every plant sensor under the inverter — you get the genuinely device-specific points (charger/meter).

## Using it for an EV charger (the #18 case)
1. Get the charger's point IDs from a diagnostics dump (`all_devices` / `device_realtime`).
2. Add them under **Extra measure points** (`<id>=ev_charger_power`).
3. Enable **Create per-device sensors** → the charger appears as its own device with sensors.

## Tests
Coordinator fetch (enabled/disabled/best-effort/dedupe), device-sensor creation + plant-duplicate skip + `via_device` grouping + value read-through, and `select_dispatch_device` ignoring non-dispatch devices. Suite green (**138**), `sensor.py` at **100%**, docs updated.

author: milosdjakovic-vicert
body:
## What it does

rx-history automates Surescripts medication history for upcoming appointments and surfaces it in the chart. Two daily cron tasks send Surescripts eligibility and medication history requests for patients with appointments 1 and 7 days out. A chart action button in the medications section opens a side panel that groups the returned history by drug, flags each row as matched or unmatched against the active medication list, and lets the provider add a missing medication to the open note or dismiss a row. A provider menu application opens a bulk requests page where staff trigger eligibility and medication history requests for any patient set inside a date range.

## Problem it solves

At the point of care a provider often lacks a complete picture of what a patient is actually filling at the pharmacy. Surescripts holds that dispensed history, but pulling it by hand for each upcoming visit is slow and easy to forget. The plugin sends the requests automatically ahead of the appointment and lays the returned history next to the active medication list, so reconciliation gaps surface before the patient is in the room.

## How it works

The two cron tasks run daily and fan out one request per eligible patient. The chart action button renders the comparison panel server side on click, so the panel does not wait on a fetch. The bulk page and the panel actions are backed by SimpleAPI endpoints under staff session auth. Adding a medication from the panel originates a MedicationStatementCommand on the open note. Each Surescripts row is matched against the active medication list by drug code rather than name, checking RxNorm CUI, then NDC on the digits only form, then an NDC to RxNorm cross reference through the FDB ontologies service. Matching flags a row but never suppresses it.

## Configuration

The plugin owns the vicert__rx_history custom data namespace for its dismissal store. Set the namespace_read_write_access_key secret to the read and write key that Canvas generates when the plugin first installs. Manual and bulk requests are blocked unless the patient has a non cancelled appointment within a 7 day care event window.

## Testing

The plugin ships a pytest suite covering the cron tasks, the action button and modal, the modal and bulk SimpleAPI endpoints, the dismissal store, and the static asset endpoint. All 109 tests pass and mypy is clean across 15 source files.

body: ## Same site: www.giga3ai.com PWA Production already had v35 deployed, but chat **still used Convex websocket mutations** to send messages. body:
## 概要

PIIスキャナ（scripts/pii-check.sh）のcanaryセルフテストを拡張し、スキャナ自体の故障をCIが両方向から自動検知できるようにする。

### canaryセルフテストの仕組み

CIは本スキャンの**前**に \`pii-check.sh --self-test\` を毎回実行する:

- **真陽性検証（既存）**: 架空の疑似PII（疑似人名+敬称・疑似電話番号・疑似メール・疑似住所）を含む一時fixtureを生成してスキャンし、**検知されること**を確認。検知されなければ「スキャナ故障」としてCIを赤にする
- **真陰性検証（本PRで追加）**: 匿名化済みのクリーンなfixture（スタッフA等の匿名表記のみ）が**素通りすること**を確認。誤検知過多への振れ戻りを検知する

fixtureは実行時にmktempで生成しtrapで削除する（リポジトリにコミットしない）。文字列はすべて架空で、スクリプト内ではエスケープ・連結で組み立てて自家中毒（スキャナが自スクリプトを検知）を防いでいる。

### 変更内容

| ファイル | 変更 |
|---------|------|
| \`scripts/pii-check.sh\` | \`--self-test\` に真陰性検証を追加（真陽性のみ→両方向） |
| \`.gitattributes\` | 新設。\`scripts/*.txt\` \`scripts/*.sh\` にLF強制。CRLF混入によるパターン全滅故障を根本から封じる |
| \`README.md\` | PIIスキャンとcanaryの仕組み・SELF-TEST FAILED時の対処手順を記載 |

## 検証結果（3点セット）

### 1. 真陽性検証 ✅

ローカルで \`bash scripts/pii-check.sh --self-test\` を実行。疑似PII 4カテゴリすべて＋姓ブロックリストが検知され、\`true positive OK\` を確認（exit 0）。

### 2. 真陰性検証 ✅

同セルフテスト内でクリーンfixtureが誤検知ゼロで素通りし、\`true negative OK\` を確認。またCI相当の全ファイルスキャン（\`git ls-files ... | xargs bash scripts/pii-check.sh\`）もローカルでPASS。

### 3. 故意破壊テスト ✅（壊すと赤・直すと緑）

スキャナのパターン定義・ブロックリスト参照先を存在しないファイルに変えた破壊コミットをpushし、canaryステップでCIが**赤**になることを確認後、revertで**緑**に復帰することを確認した。

| コミット | 状態 | CI結果 |
|---------|------|--------|
| 844f55f（実装） | 正常 | ✅ success — https://github.com/kumagoro1202/clinic-shift-scheduler/actions/runs/28628475725 |
| 212fbc7（故意破壊） | スキャナ故障 | ❌ **failure**（canaryステップで \`SELF-TEST FAILED ... Scanner is broken.\` → exit 1）— https://github.com/kumagoro1202/clinic-shift-scheduler/actions/runs/28628501622 |
| 0cae7fc（revert） | 正常 | ✅ success — https://github.com/kumagoro1202/clinic-shift-scheduler/actions/runs/28628541268 |

補足: 当初の故障事例（パターン定義のCRLF化）は、本PRの \`.gitattributes\` によりコミット時点でLFへ正規化されるため再現不能になった（防御が機能している証左）。そのため破壊テストは同型の「パターン喪失」故障で実施した。

CodeQL flagged insecure temporary file creation in `scripts/prepare-objective-impact-safe-output-evaluations.cjs`. During review, this script was confirmed to be live code used by the active `objective-impact-report` workflow, so the fix keeps the behavior and removes the unsafe temp-file pattern.

- **Security fix**
  - Replaced the ad hoc temp-file naming logic with a private temp directory created via `fs.mkdtempSync(...)`.
  - Writes now occur inside that temp directory and are finalized with `renameSync`, avoiding predictable temp paths and reducing TOCTOU/symlink risk.

- **Script cleanup**
  - Removed the now-unused `crypto` import.
  - Kept the helper scoped to the existing atomic-write path rather than changing surrounding workflow behavior.

- **Failure diagnostics**
  - Split write and rename failure handling so errors identify which atomic-write step failed.

```js
const tmpDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(parentDir, `.${baseName}.tmp-`));
const tmpFile = path.join(tmpDir, baseName);

fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, content);
fs.renameSync(tmpFile, filePath);
```

author: michel-az-de
body:
Primeira fatia da **Fase C**. Torna a arquitetura de eventos real: os eventos de domínio que já eram levantados (`ArtigoPublicado`, `ComentarioCriado`, `ComentarioAprovado`) e **descartados** agora vão a um Outbox transacional e um relay os publica no RabbitMQ para o **Hiram** consumir. Isso já entrega a notificação de comentário pendente (C3).

## Decisões (spike C0, com o Felipe)
- **Mecanismo:** hand-rolled + Change Streams (sem framework). O core do Wolverine virou **MIT/grátis** — não é mais armadilha de licença —, mas não foi adotado (mudaria o estilo de handlers-diretos; outbox dele com Mongo é não-validado). `mapa-tecnico` atualizado; GAP-F resolvido.
- **Contrato Hiram (GAP-I):** envelope JSON versionado provisório em [`docs/adr/0001`](docs/adr/0001-outbox-envelope-hiram.md); o Felipe alinha o Hiram.

## O que entra
- **`GravadorDeAgregadoMongo`**: grava agregado + eventos na **mesma transação**. Detecta suporte no boot (replica set) e **degrada para escrita sequencial** best-effort no single-node — então as fixtures atuais e o dev local seguem funcionando sem replica set. Só `ArtigoRepository` e `ComentarioRepository` passam a rotear por ele.
- **`RelayDeOutbox`** (`BackgroundService`): fila com **delete-após-publicar**; Change Stream na collection `outbox` + **sweep** de recuperação no start → **at-least-once** (consumidor deduplica por `eventId`). Publisher RabbitMQ (exchange topic durável `levante.eventos`, routing key = tipo, mensagens persistentes). Registrado **só quando `Outbox:RelayHabilitado`** (default off em teste/dev).
- Envelope: `{ eventId, tipo, versao, ocorridoEm, dados }` (JSON limpo — Guid como string).
- Pacotes: `RabbitMQ.Client` 7.2.1 (MPL-2.0/Apache-2.0), `Testcontainers.RabbitMq` 4.12.0. `appsettings`/README/user-secrets documentados.

## Testes
- **`OutboxRelayFixture`**: Mongo em **replica set** (`WithReplicaSet`) + RabbitMQ Testcontainers, relay ligado. `OutboxRelayEndpointTests`: publicar artigo → evento gravado na mesma transação → relay publica → um consumidor de teste recebe o envelope com `tipo="ArtigoPublicado"` e `dados.slug`.
- Fixtures single-node **inalteradas** (fallback sequencial) → os 17 testes de integração e 193 unit tests atuais seguem verdes.

## Risco conhecido (honesto)
O caminho transacional + relay **só valida no CI** (a máquina local não tem Docker). O combo Mongo replica set + Testcontainers pode precisar de 1–2 iterações de push até estabilizar (gotcha driver 3.x + replica set). Se instabilizar, fica isolado na `OutboxRelayFixture`; as demais suítes não são afetadas.

Próximo: **C2 — Audiência (newsletter double opt-in)**, que usa este outbox (o e-mail de confirmação sai como evento → Hiram).

author: erikunha
body:
## Summary

Closes the CI gap that caused the #169/#170 production incident.

- **Root cause:** the `detect-changes` `ai` category (which gates the real-Gateway `ai-eval` job) matched only ask **code** paths and deliberately excluded `package.json`/`pnpm-lock.yaml` (to avoid burning Gateway credits on routine dep churn). So dependabot **#169** bumped `ai` 6→7 as a **deps-only** change, `ai-eval` **skipped**, and it merged green while shipping v7 package + v6 route code — breaking prod `/api/ask` (0-byte stream, hotfix'd in #170).
- **Fix:** `scripts/detect-changes.mjs` now reads the `ai` **major** at BASE vs HEAD (`aiMajor` slice, mirroring the existing `ui` browserslist/pnpm render-slice) and ORs `aiMajorChanged` into the `ai` output. A **major** `ai` bump runs `ai-eval`; minor/patch bumps stay credit-cheap.
- **Precedence** `pnpm.overrides.ai` → `dependencies.ai` → `devDependencies.ai`: an override *forces* the resolved version, so it must win — else a PR forcing `ai` v7 via `pnpm.overrides` while leaving the declared range at `^6` would bypass the re-arm (the repo uses overrides elsewhere). This bypass was caught by the adversarial review and closed with a test.
- **Fail-safe:** an absent/unparseable specifier or git-read error yields `null`, which (differing from the other ref's number) **over-arms** `ai-eval` rather than skipping.

## Type of change

- [x] `chore` / `ci` / `docs` — CI merge-gate hardening
- [ ] `feat` · `fix` · `refactor` · `perf`

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm test --run` → **1088 passed, 2 skipped** · `pnpm check` (Biome) clean · `pnpm check:doc-drift` 0 stale · `pnpm check:detect-changes-paths` OK.
- [x] **TDD:** `aiMajor` unit cases (caret/tilde/range/exact specifiers, devDeps, `pnpm.overrides` precedence/bypass, `null` on `workspace:`/`latest`/malformed) + `computeCategories` re-arm cases + a **real-git end-to-end test** proving the exact incident (a repo whose only diff is `ai` `^6`→`^7` in package.json → `ai=true app=true ui=false`).
- [x] 5-agent battery, two rounds: round 1 caught an Important `pnpm.overrides` bypass; round 2 (post-fix) CLEAN on all five.

## Visual changes

None — CI scripts/config + tests + docs only.

## Checklist

- [x] No hardcoded hex / magic numbers — N/A
- [x] No `use client` — N/A
- [x] Bundle size — N/A (CI only, no production/client code)
- [x] A11y — N/A
- [x] ADR added to `DECISIONS.md`

## Notes

- Residual **Minor** (non-blocking, documented): the `ai` specifier parser reads the first digit-run major (a `6.0.0 || 7.0.0` OR-combinator would read only the first token) and the override lookup checks the direct `pnpm.overrides.ai` key only (not nested `pkg>ai` syntax). Neither is reachable under the repo's caret-pin + top-level-override style; comments note the assumptions.
- This is the systemic follow-up to the #170 hotfix — it makes the incident class (a breaking `ai` bump skipping `ai-eval`) impossible to recur.

author: mmarmol
body:
Second-round E2E caught it immediately: the bot token validated ✓ but the app token always failed with a raw `TypeError`.

**Cause**: `slack_sdk`'s `apps_connections_open()` requires the app-level token as an explicit keyword (`app_token=...`) — the client-constructor token is not used for that endpoint. The call raised `TypeError` before ever reaching Slack.

**Why tests missed it**: the test fake's `apps_connections_open()` accepted a no-arg call. Its signature now mirrors the SDK (`*, app_token: str` required) so this class of drift fails in CI.

Full suite green; 57 slack-related tests pass.

body:
## Bug

Em `/admin/assinantes/[lojaId]/configuracao`, salvar/remover a **logo** falhava com toast genérico. A seção de logo do `PerfilClient` reusado caía nas actions do **lojista** (`salvarLogoLoja`/`removerLogoLoja`, hardcoded em `UploadLogoLoja`), que derivam a loja de `buscarLojaDoDono(auth)` — o admin não é dono da loja-alvo → "Não autorizado".

**Agravante (por isso crítico):** como o admin é dono de loja própria, a logo seria gravada **na loja do admin**, não na loja-alvo — escrita cross-tenant errada e silenciosa.

## Fix (issues 116–119, spec `specs/arquivo/fix-logo-admin-cross-tenant.md`)

- **`admin-logo.ts` (novo):** `salvarLogoAdmin`/`removerLogoAdmin` sob `service_role`, padrão admin: `validarLojaIdAdmin` antes de tudo → `prepararContextoAdmin` **fora do try** (fail-closed) → `validarBlobImagem` após a prova → path server-side `${lojaId}/logo/${uuid}.${ext}` → `schemaStorageUrl` antes do UPDATE → `escopo.atualizarLoja({ logo_url })`.
- **`UploadLogoLoja`:** props opcionais `onSalvar`/`onRemover` (default = actions do lojista — painel intocado; mesmo padrão do `UploadQrPix`).
- **`PerfilClient`:** repasse puro `onSalvarLogo`/`onRemoverLogo`.
- **`ConfiguracaoAdminClient`:** injeta as actions admin com `lojaId` fixado por closure (sobrescreve `loja_id` hostil no FormData).

## Qualidade

- TDD red-first nas críticas (116, 119): FAIL capturado antes, GREEN depois (evidências nas issues).
- Suíte completa: **1906 testes / 124 arquivos verdes** (17 novos). `next build` verde. Enforcement estático de escopo admin auto-descobriu e aprovou a action nova.
- Auditoria de segurança: **0 findings MÉDIA+** (1 BAIXA de robustez opcional; 1 informativo já rastreado em tasks/115).
- Sem migration, sem RLS nova, sem mudança de `references/`.

## Pendência

Verificação visual humana em produção (`tasks/120-verificacao-humana-logo-admin.md`) — conta admin é Google OAuth, sem senha para login automatizado.

author: bioedca
body:
## Summary

First M3 (Corrections) PR: a native, headless **Bayesian single-step photobleach detector**, run per channel, plus the per-trace **analysis-window auto-default** (trace-start → first bleach of the *summed* donor+acceptor intensity), layered under the existing manual `-`/`=`/`[`/`]` window override.

### What lands

- **`tether.fret.photobleach`** — vectorized `O(T)` reimplementation of tMAVEN's single-step model (signal → `N(0)` change point; conjugate NIG priors `a=b=β=1`, `μ=1000`, the frozen §11.2 values as named `PB_PRIOR_*` constants):
  - `point_pbtime` ≙ `get_point_pbtime` (MAP change point; `== T` ⇒ no bleach within the trace)
  - `ensemble_pbtime` ≙ `pb_ensemble` (two-pass exponential-lifetime prior, first pass truncated to `int64` exactly as the reference)
  - `detect_photobleach` → per-channel donor/acceptor first-bleach frames, active masks, and the `(0, sum_pb)` window
- **`tether.project.compute_photobleach`** — runs the detector over a project's `corrected` traces and writes into the **already-frozen** `/molecules` `bleach_frames` + `analysis_window` fields. **No schema change** (`schema-guard` green). Auto-window overwrites `analysis_window` only where it still equals the extraction default → **manual override wins**; the three existing window readers are untouched.
- **ADR-0026** — homes the §7.2 / Appendix B decision and records the `pacc`/`pdon` reframe (below).

### Validation

- **Reference parity** — the vectorized likelihood / point / ensemble are asserted equal to a direct in-test transcription of the tMAVEN formulas.
- **Synthetic ground truth** — injected `N(μ,σ)→N(0,σ)` steps recovered within the **§11.2 ±2-frame** tolerance across positions and SNRs.
- **Store integration** — stored `bleach_frames`/`analysis_window` match the headless detector exactly; manual-window precedence; a `no-new-groups` schema-guard test.

### Data-gap finding (reframe, not a fabrication)

The §9-M3 acceptance cites "±2 frames of `.mat` `pacc`/`pdon`". Empirically that Deep-LASI export's `pacc`/`pdon` is a **uniform constant 60 for all 250 molecules**, whose corrected traces demonstrably bleach at ≈97…1693 — i.e. a **global acquisition marker, not a per-molecule bleach oracle**. Gating against it would force a wrong detector, so per the working agreement it is **reframed** (ADR-0026) to synthetic-known-step + reference-parity validation, not fabricated. A real per-molecule oracle, if later sourced, can be added as a `@pytest.mark.large` check.

### Gates

- **context7**: `scipy.special.gammaln` (vectorized real-input log-gamma, scipy 1.18) — no new dependency (pure numpy + scipy).
- **Consensus**: Bayesian MAP change-point photobleaching-step detection validated vs ground truth (Tsekouras 2016, Garry 2020, Mattamira 2025).
- Full base suite green headless (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`): **889 passed** (887 pre-existing + new), ruff clean, REUSE 186/186.

### Deferred (follow-up)

The GUI `P`-key trigger and the manual window-nudge handlers (bound but no-op since M2) are **not** wired here — this PR is the headless detection + storage substrate; the GUI wiring gets its own computer-use live-smoke + `pytest-qt` coverage.

## Self-review checklist (§12.4)

- [x] **Schema freeze respected** — only frozen `/molecules` fields populated; `no-new-groups` test; `schema-guard` target green.
- [x] **conda-lock** unchanged — pure numpy + `scipy.special.gammaln`, both already in the base lock.
- [x] New tunables already registered in **PRD §11.2** (rows 813/816/819/821); named `PB_PRIOR_*` constants, not hardcoded.
- [x] Tests added (`test_fret_photobleach.py`, `test_project_photobleach.py`); reference-parity + synthetic ±2 + store integration.
- [x] SPDX `GPL-3.0-or-later` on every new file; `reuse lint` green (186/186).
- [x] Resolved PRD decision homed as **ADR-0026** in the same PR.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added automatic photobleach detection for donor, acceptor, and combined signal traces.
  * Analysis windows can now default to the first detected bleach frame, while preserving any manual window adjustments.
  * Detected bleach-frame results are written back into existing molecule records.

* **Documentation**
  * Added a new architecture note describing the photobleach detection behavior and updated the ADR index.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of traces with no detected bleaching and short or edge-case traces.

body:
## 概要
kb-bot 逆輸入 1/4（#81）。保存済みモデルの退役（404）でレビュー/改稿が失敗し続ける事故に対し、現存モデルへのフォールバックで完走させる。

Closes #81

## 設計
- **`src/ai/modelFallback.ts`（新規）**
  - `isModelNotFoundError`: `providers.ts` が投げる `LLM <url> failed: 404 <body>` を第一義に、プロバイダのエラー本文（`not_found_error` / `model_not_found` / "does not exist"）と SDK 形式（`status`/`code`）を保険に判定。エンドポイントは固定なので converse の 404 ≒ モデル不明。
  - `pickFallbackModel`: **既定モデルのハードコードなし**（モデル ID は動的情報＝リポジトリの「バージョン識別子を記憶で書かない」原則に整合）。本人のキーで `listModels` を引き、**退役モデルと最長共通接頭辞の現存モデル**を選ぶ（同系統・同ファミリー優先）。同点は短い id（派生より基準）、embedding/tts 等の非チャット系は除外、共通接頭辞 3 文字未満しか無ければ null → 元エラーのまま失敗させ設定し直しを促す。
  - `runReviewAgentWithModelFallback`: 404/退役のときだけ一度だけ再試行。他のエラー（429/500 等）は一覧取得すらせずそのまま投げる。
- **適用箇所**: レビュー（SSE/JSON 両方）・レビューのスレッド化・改稿の 4 実行部すべて。
- **記録**: 履歴（reviews/revisions.model）と応答（`model` + `fellBack`）は実際に使ったモデル。content-free の運用イベント `model_fallback` を追記（メトリクスは action 名フィルタなので追加は無害）。AiReviewPanel の履歴表示は保存された model を出すため、画面からもフォールバックに気づける。

## kb-bot からの差分
kb-bot は各プロバイダ固定の `defaultModel` へフォールバックするが、mdcollab は BYO-key・ユーザー選択モデルなので「本人が選んでいたものに最も近い現存モデル」を動的に選ぶ方式にした（コスト・挙動のサプライズを最小化）。

## 検証
- `bun run test` 217 件緑（判定・選定のユニット 7 件＋ルート統合 4 件を追加: 退役→近縁で完走・現役はそのまま・近縁なしは元エラー・500 はフォールバックしない）
- `bun run typecheck` 緑

## Summary

Completes Phase 5 by porting `useShoppingListStore` from a Decision 015 stub (throwing on all actions) to a real SQLite-backed Zustand store, and wires the mount-time hydration/advance/reset logic in `app/shopping.tsx` that was previously omitted. The shopping screen now persists recurring lists, templates, and automatic monthly resets.

## Key Changes

### `store/useShoppingListStore.ts` (stub → real implementation)
- **Ported verbatim** from the old app's store logic: `load()` (with `backfillOrphanedItems()` self-heal for pre-migration orphaned items), `add()`, `update()`, `remove()`, `rename()`, `setRecurring()`, `toggleLocked()`, `currentList()`, `advanceRecurringLists()` (closed-form period jump + `copyOpenItemsToList()`), `saveAsTemplate()`, `instantiateTemplate()`.
- **Widened `ShoppingList` type** (additive): adds `isCustomName`, `sortOrder`, `createdAt`; makes `recurrenceIntervalWeeks` required. No consumer constructs a `ShoppingList` literal — all read it as a prop type only — so the widening is safe and requires no consumer changes.

author: galligan
body:
## Context

A running `dispatchd` can keep serving an older op registry after the CLI has been upgraded. The live symptom after `dispatch query` landed was `unknown op 'query'` until the daemon was restarted. This makes that stale-daemon case self-healing when safe and explicit when not.

Closes DIS-28.

## What changed

- Adds a private control metadata method with protocol version, package version, and supported ops.
- Detects `method not found` for ops that exist in the current CLI registry as likely daemon/client skew.
- Reads daemon status before self-healing.
- Restarts and retries once only when the daemon is idle.
- Refuses automatic restart when the daemon is busy, waiting/active, or activity is unclear, with an explicit `dispatch down && dispatch up` recovery.
- Adds active/waiting-approval counts to `dispatch daemon status`.
- Updates operator docs and the Dispatch skill.
- Adds a goal packet/retro for the work.

## Guardrails

- Unknown op typos are not treated as skew unless the op exists in the current CLI registry.
- Retry is bounded to one restart attempt.
- Busy or uncertain daemons are not restarted silently.
- Lifecycle still uses existing pidfile/socket liveness checks; no launchd policy changes.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/surfaces/test_cli_daemon_skew.py tests/daemon/test_control.py tests/core/test_handlers.py::test_status_and_log_reflect_activity tests/core/test_examples.py::test_examples -q`
- `just check`
  - ruff passed
  - format check passed
  - mypy strict passed
  - pytest `403 passed / 9 deselected`
  - package build/content check passed
- `uv run dispatch down && uv run dispatch up && uv run dispatch daemon status --json`
- `uv run dispatch query --type tool --limit 1 --json`
- Local review: `.agents/goals/2026-07-02-daemon-skew-self-heal/tmp/reviews/codex/round-1.json`, 5/5, no open P0/P1/P2

## Risk

The live smoke validates the refreshed daemon path. The actual stale-daemon restart/retry path is covered by deterministic unit tests rather than forcing an old live binary.

author: mikeldking
body:
# REST API: Assign annotation configs to projects

Closes #14016 (parent: #11985).

## What changed

Annotation configs already had full CRUD over REST, but there was **no REST surface for
assigning a config to a project** — the `project_annotation_configs` association was only
reachable via GraphQL. This PR closes that gap by exposing the project ↔ annotation-config
membership as an idempotent sub-collection under the project.

New endpoints (added to `src/phoenix/server/api/routers/v1/annotation_configs.py`):

| Method & path | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/projects/{project_identifier}/annotation_configs` | Paginated list of the configs assigned to the project (same item shape / discriminated union as `GET /annotation_configs`). |
| `PUT /v1/projects/{project_identifier}/annotation_configs/{config_identifier}` | Assign a config to the project. **Idempotent** — re-assigning an already-assigned config is a `200` no-op (the duplicate `409` from the GraphQL `add` mutation is intentionally swallowed). Returns the assigned config. |
| `DELETE /v1/projects/{project_identifier}/annotation_configs/{config_identifier}` | Unassign a config from the project. `204 No Content`. Idempotent — unassigning a config that is not assigned is a no-op (the underlying config is never deleted). |
| `PUT /v1/projects/{project_identifier}/annotation_configs` | **Replace** the project's entire config set. The server diffs desired vs. current in one transaction (adds missing, removes extra). An empty array clears all assignments. Returns the resulting set. |

### Conventions

- `{project_identifier}` accepts a project **name or ID** — reuses `get_project_by_identifier()`.
- `{config_identifier}` accepts an annotation-config **name or GlobalID** (polymorphic
  `Categorical`/`Continuous`/`Freeform` prefixes) — reuses the existing resolver.
- **Reads:** all authenticated. **Writes:** MEMBER+ (VIEWER / read-only rejected automatically at
  the router level via `restrict_access_by_viewers`). Write endpoints (both `PUT`s) also use
  `Depends(is_not_locked)`; `DELETE` does not, since it frees rather than consumes storage.
- **Not found:** a missing project or path config → `404`. For the bulk `PUT`, an invalid or
  unknown config GlobalID in the body is a **`422`** (the ids are payload values, not path
  resources).
- Responses reuse `db_to_api_annotation_config()` for serialization, so no follow-up `GET` is
  needed.

## Why this shape

The join table carries no attributes (no `enabled`, ordering, or `assigned_by`), so the
assignment is modeled as an idempotent membership sub-collection rather than a standalone
association resource. `PUT` on the pair is the workhorse for infra-as-code re-applies; the
collection `PUT` fits a checkbox/settings screen; `DELETE` cleans up a deprecated rubric without
deleting the shared config. See the issue for the full rationale.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`tests/unit/server/api/routers/v1/test_annotation_configs.py`, in-process, no auth):
  assign + idempotent re-assign + list, assign/list by name, unassign + idempotent
  unassign-missing, bulk replace (add + remove, then clear), `404` for missing project/config,
  `422` for malformed and unknown bulk ids.
- **Integration** (`tests/integration/annotation_configs/`, real subprocess with auth): the same
  behaviors end-to-end plus **VIEWER is forbidden (`403`)** from all three write endpoints.
- Registered all four routes in the endpoint-coverage constants in
  `tests/integration/_helpers.py` (`_COMMON_RESOURCE_ENDPOINTS` /
  `_VIEWER_BLOCKED_WRITE_OPERATIONS`) so `_ensure_endpoint_coverage_is_exhaustive()` stays green.

## Docs

Added the four Mintlify OpenAPI wrapper pages under
`docs/phoenix/sdk-api-reference/rest-api/api-reference/annotation-configs/` and registered them in
`docs.json`.

## How to verify

```bash
# assign (idempotent)
curl -XPUT $PHOENIX/v1/projects/my-project/annotation_configs/helpfulness
# list
curl $PHOENIX/v1/projects/my-project/annotation_configs
# replace the whole set
curl -XPUT $PHOENIX/v1/projects/my-project/annotation_configs \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"annotation_config_ids": ["<cfg GlobalID 1>", "<cfg GlobalID 2>"]}'
# unassign
curl -XDELETE $PHOENIX/v1/projects/my-project/annotation_configs/helpfulness
```

Then run `make test-python` (unit + integration) and `make lint-python`.

## ⚠️ Follow-up required in CI (toolchain unavailable in this sandbox)

`uv` is not installed in the environment this change was authored in, so the generated artifacts
could **not** be regenerated here. Before/at merge, run **`make openapi`** to regenerate and commit:

- `schemas/openapi.json` and `docs/openapi.json`
- `packages/phoenix-client/src/phoenix/client/__generated__/v1/__init__.py`
- `js/packages/phoenix-client/src/__generated__/api/v1.ts`
- `app/src/api/__generated__/v1.ts`

The new Mintlify doc pages reference these operations by method + path and will render once the
schema is regenerated. Also run `make lint-python` / `make format-python` and `make test-python`;
they could not be executed locally for the same reason. No `js/` package source was modified by
hand, so no changeset is required.

body: The reviewer showed a blank image in dev: `signedHomeworkReadUrl` returned a bare filesystem path (`` can't load it) and no HTTP route served the local blob. Prod on Azure works via SAS. **Adds a filesystem-backed image endpoint:** - `GET /api/v1/storage/homework-image?token=…` (`@Public`, `@ApiExcludeEndpoint`): the token is a short-lived HMAC capability (signed with `STAFF_JWT_SECRET`) encoding the storage key — SAS-equivalent, so a cross-origin `` needs no cookie. Streams bytes via `storage.readBinary` as `image/webp`. Excluded from OpenAPI (binary capability URL, not part of the typed JSON contract → no contract drift). - `signedHomeworkReadUrl`'s non-Azure branch returns that URL, built from `PUBLIC_API_URL` (new; default `http://localhost:${PORT}/api/v1`). Azure path unchanged (SAS). Verified end-to-end: valid token → `200 image/webp`, tampered/expired → `404`. 150 backend tests pass; `openapi.json` unchanged.
